paras.en: [[10:7|And going, preach, saying: The kingdom of heaven is at hand|Euntes autem prædicate, dicentes: Quia appropinquavit regnum cœlorum]], that is, the glory of the heavenly kingdom, because by the incarnation and merit of Christ the entrance to the kingdom of heaven lies open. For men are put far off and away from the heavenly kingdom and true happiness by guilt. Since, then, Christ came to take away the sins of the world[[John 1:29||]], from the time of His coming this kingdom drew near, and men began to be disposed to obtain it. Yet no one could enter it before the passion.

paras.t: Consequenter Salvator donat Apostolis congrua proportionataque argumenta probandi doctrinam evangelicam. Infirmos curate, miraculose et instrumentaliter, divinam potentiam atque clementiam invocando; mortuos suscitate. Non leguntur Apostoli ante passionem mortuos suscitasse, sed postea. Leprosos mundate, orando pro curatione eorum; dæmones ejicite. Gratis, id est sine pretio vestro ac merito, accepistis a me dona Spiritus Sancti, videlicet gratias gratis datas, et gratiam gratum facientem: alioqui gratia non esset gratia; gratis, id est pure propter Deum, date, id est, aliis communicate spiritualia vobis concessa, sacramenta Ecclesiæ, beneficia sanitatum, sapientiam et scientiam, et ceteros actus spirituales: pro quibus nihil sumendum est per modum pretii, ne spiritualia temporalibus comparentur; quamvis aliquid accipi possit tanquam stipendium vitæ. Hoc et Petrus in prima sua hortatur Canonica, dicens: Unusquisque sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administrantes, sicut boni dispensatores multiformis gratiæ Dei.
paras.en: Next the Saviour gives the Apostles fitting and proportioned arguments for proving the Gospel teaching. [[10:8|Heal the sick|Infirmos curate]], miraculously and instrumentally, calling upon the divine power and mercy; [[10:8|raise the dead|mortuos suscitate]]. The Apostles are not read to have raised the dead before the passion, but afterwards[[Acts 9:40||]][[Acts 20:10||]]. [[10:8|cleanse the lepers|Leprosos mundate]], by praying for their cure; [[10:8|cast out devils|dæmones ejicite]]. [[10:8|freely have you received|Gratis, id est sine pretio vestro ac merito, accepistis]], that is, without price or merit of yours you have received from Me the gifts of the Holy Ghost, namely the graces freely given and the grace that makes pleasing [gratiæ gratis datæ, gifts such as miracles given for others' good, and gratia gratum faciens, the sanctifying grace that makes the soul pleasing to God]; [[Rom 11:6|otherwise grace is no more grace|alioqui gratia non esset gratia]]. [[10:8|freely give|gratis, id est pure propter Deum, date]], that is, purely for God's sake, give, that is, share with others the spiritual things granted you: the sacraments of the Church, the benefits of healing, wisdom and knowledge, and the other spiritual acts. For these nothing is to be taken by way of price, lest spiritual things be set level with temporal ones; though something may be accepted as a livelihood. Peter too urges this in his first canonical epistle, saying: [[1 Pet 4:10|As every man hath received grace, ministering the same one to another: as good stewards of the manifold grace of God|Unusquisque sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administrantes, sicut boni dispensatores multiformis gratiæ Dei]].

paras.t: Nolite possidere aurum, neque argentum, neque pecuniam in zonis vestris, id est in bursis ad zonas pendentibus. Quid mirum si hoc dicatur ad discipulos, quibus et dixit, Qui non renuntiaverit omnibus quæ possidet, non potest meus esse discipulus? Apostoli namque esse debuerant ceteris omnibus, maxime prædicatoribus, exemplum perfectionis, videlicet paupertatis et plenæ spei in Deo, non cogitando de crastino, itemque de libertatis perfectione, sola futuri sæculi bona quærendo. Denique, non solum prohibuit Christus Apostolis nil horum possidere, sed etiam nihil secum portare. Unde apud Lucam: Nihil, inquit, tuleritis in via, etc. Temporalium namque possessio parit solicitudinem, et impedit animi libertatem, sicque efficit hominem minus expeditum ad infatigabile prædicationis officium. Non peram, id est repositorium victualium, in via prædicationis, possideatis aut circumferatis.
paras.en: [[10:9|Do not possess gold, nor silver, nor money in your purses|Nolite possidere aurum, neque argentum, neque pecuniam in zonis vestris]], that is, in pouches hanging from your belts. What wonder if this is said to the disciples, to whom He also said: [[Luke 14:33|every one of you that doth not renounce all that he possesseth cannot be my disciple|Qui non renuntiaverit omnibus quæ possidet, non potest meus esse discipulus?]]? For the Apostles were to be an example of perfection to all others, above all to preachers: namely of poverty and of full hope in God, not taking thought for the morrow[[Matt 6:34||]], and likewise of perfect freedom, seeking only the goods of the world to come. Moreover, Christ forbade the Apostles not only to possess any of these things, but even to carry anything with them. Whence in Luke He says: [[Luke 9:3|Take nothing for your journey|Nihil, inquit, tuleritis in via]], etc. For the possession of temporal things breeds anxiety and hinders freedom of mind, and so makes a man less ready for the untiring office of preaching. [[10:10|Nor scrip for your journey|non peram in via]], that is, a store for food, on the way of preaching, should you possess or carry about.

paras.t: Videtur contrarium quod ait Salvator: Quando misi vos sine sacculo et pera, numquid aliquid defuit vobis? sed nunc qui habet sacculum, tollat; similiter et peram. Sed et ipse Salvator aliquid tulit in via, videlicet sacculum, peram, pecuniam, quorum Judas custos fuit. Nam quum in cœna Christus ei dixisset, Quod facis, fac citius; putabant Apostoli quod dixisset ei: Eme nobis qua ad diem festum necessaria sunt. Discipuli quoque ejus intraverunt civitatem Samaritanorum emere cibos. Et respondendum ad primum, quod Christus secundum congruentiam loci ac temporis, convenientia dedit præcepta. In legatione igitur Apostolorum quæ facta est ante passionem, præcepit ne quid tollerent in via, quia tunc mittebantur ad notos, nec prædicabant mirabilia aut supernaturalia de Christo, sicut post passionem; unde et tunc persecutionem perpessi non sunt, ut postea, sed satis provisum est eis ab his quibus prædicaverunt: ideo jussi sunt pro tunc nihil secum portare. Post passionem vero, cœperunt mirabilia prædicare de Christo, et hominum vitia ac idola publice reprobare: ideirco tunc permissi sunt secum ferre necessaria vitæ. Quod autem Apostoli post passionem hoc egerint, innotescit ex eo quod ad Corinthios dicit Apostolus: Numquid non habemus potestatem mulierem sororem circumducendi, sicut et ceteri Apostoli, et fratres Domini, et Cephas? Ad secundum dicendum, quod Christus tulit et habuit talia pro communitate sui gregis, et pro necessitate egenorum, non quasi privata et propria bona. Neque duas tunicas superiores, seu tales quarum una dumtaxat necessaria est, id est, non habete vestes superfluas. Juxta quem sensum ait Joannes Baptista: Qui habet duas tunicas, det non habenti. Hoc ergo intelligendum est, secundum qualitatem locorum ac temporum: quia in uno loco et tempore pauciora vestimenta sufficiunt, quam in alio.
paras.en: What the Saviour says seems contrary to this: [[Luke 22:35|When I sent you without purse and scrip|Quando misi vos sine sacculo et pera]], [[Luke 22:35|did you want anything?|numquid aliquid defuit vobis?]] [[Luke 22:36|But now he that hath a purse, let him take it, and likewise a scrip|sed nunc qui habet sacculum, tollat; similiter et peram]]. And the Saviour Himself also carried something on the way, namely a purse, a scrip and money, of which Judas was the keeper. For when at the Supper Christ had said to him, [[John 13:27|That which thou dost, do quickly|Quod facis, fac citius]], the Apostles thought that He had said to him: [[John 13:29|Buy those things which we have need of for the festival day|Eme nobis qua ad diem festum necessaria sunt]]. His disciples too [[John 4:8|were gone into the city to buy meats|intraverunt … civitatem … emere cibos]], the city of the Samaritans. And to the first it must be answered that Christ gave precepts suited to the fitness of place and time. So in the mission of the Apostles that took place before the passion, He commanded that they should take nothing on the way, because they were then sent to people who knew them, nor did they preach wonderful or supernatural things of Christ as they did after the passion; hence they did not then suffer persecution as they did afterwards, but were well provided for by those to whom they preached: therefore they were ordered for that time to carry nothing with them. But after the passion they began to preach wonderful things of Christ, and to condemn publicly the vices and idols of men; therefore they were then allowed to carry with them the necessaries of life. And that the Apostles did this after the passion is known from what the Apostle says to the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 9:5|Have we not power to carry about a woman, a sister as well as the rest of the apostles and the brethren of the Lord and Cephas?|Numquid non habemus potestatem mulierem sororem circumducendi, sicut et ceteri Apostoli, et fratres Domini, et Cephas?]] To the second it must be said that Christ carried and had such things for the community of His flock and for the needs of the poor, not as private goods of His own. [[10:10|nor two coats|Neque duas tunicas]], outer ones, or such that only one of them is necessary; that is, do not have superfluous clothes. In which sense John the Baptist says: [[Luke 3:11|He that hath two coats, let him give to him that hath none|Qui habet duas tunicas, det non habenti]]. This then is to be understood according to the character of places and times, since in one place and time fewer clothes suffice than in another.

paras.t: Neque calceamenta, neque virgam. Marcus refert Christum dixisse: Nihil tuleritis in via, nisi virgam tantum, sed calceati sandaliis. Quomodo ergo nunc dicitur, Neque calceamenta, neque virgam? Et respondendum, quod loquitur de integris calceamentis. Sandalia vero sunt incompleta calceamenta, nec reputantur pro calceis. Quod autem ad Ephesios dicit Apostolus, Calceati pedes in præparatione Evangelii pacis, de spiritualibus calceamentis intelligi potest: de quibus in Canticis scribitur, Quam pulchri sunt gressus tui in calceamentis! Denique non omnia quæ jam jubentur Apostolis, æstimanda sunt omnibus prædicatoribus ad litteram esse præcepta, sed his in quibus eadem ratio invenitur. De virga major est difficultas. Unde sciendum, quod Christus concessit discipulis portare virgam, sumendo virgam ad litteram, quoniam Judæorum consuetudo erat, ut doctores et prædicatores eorum ferrent virgam in signum doctrinæ, et in signum quod hi quibus prædicabant, tenebantur eis de victualibus providere. Sed hoc loco virga accipitur spiritualiter, pro innitentia animi super quamcumque rem temporalem, vel pro re temporali quantumcumque parva et vili, ut sit sensus: Neque virgam, id est, nolite alicui rei temporali inniti, vel rem temporalem quantumcumque minutam, quasi proprium possidere.
paras.en: [[10:10|nor shoes, nor a staff|Neque calceamenta, neque virgam]]. Mark relates that Christ said: [[Mark 6:8|take nothing for the way, but a staff only|Nihil tuleritis in via, nisi virgam tantum]], [[Mark 6:9|But to be shod with sandals|sed calceati sandaliis]]. How then is it said here, Nor shoes, nor a staff? It must be answered that He speaks of complete shoes. Sandals are incomplete shoes, and are not counted as shoes. And what the Apostle says to the Ephesians, [[Eph 6:15|your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace|Calceati pedes in præparatione Evangelii pacis]], can be understood of spiritual shoes, of which it is written in the Canticles: [[Cant 7:1|How beautiful are thy steps in shoes|Quam pulchri sunt gressus tui in calceamentis]]! Moreover, not everything now commanded to the Apostles is to be thought commanded to all preachers according to the letter, but to those in whom the same reason is found. About the staff the difficulty is greater. So it must be known that Christ allowed the disciples to carry a staff, taking 'staff' literally, since it was the custom of the Jews that their teachers and preachers carried a staff as a sign of their teaching, and as a sign that those to whom they preached were bound to provide them with food. But in this place 'staff' is taken spiritually, for the mind's leaning upon any temporal thing, or for a temporal thing however small and mean; so that the sense is: Nor a staff, that is, do not lean upon any temporal thing, nor possess as your own any temporal thing, however tiny.

paras.t: Cur autem nil horum possidendum sive portandum sit prædicatori, subjungitur. Dignus est enim operarius, id est prædicator verbi Dei et minister altaris, seu quilibet spiritualis in templo ministrans, et spiritualia populo exhibens, cibo suo, id est necessariis ad corporis sustentationem. Imo hoc dictat ratio, lexque divina, et jus humanum. Imo hoc ipsum Apostolus pro modico reputans, sic ait: Si nos vobis spiritualia seminavimus, magnum est si vestra carnalia metamus? Ideo iterum loquitur: Communicet autem qui catechizatur ei qui catechizat, in omnibus bonis; itemque, Dominus ordinavit his qui Evangelio deserviunt, de Evangelio vivere.
paras.en: Why the preacher should possess or carry none of these things is then added: [[10:10|for the workman is worthy|Dignus est enim operarius]], that is, the preacher of the word of God and the minister of the altar, or whoever ministers spiritually in the temple and offers spiritual things to the people, [[10:10|of his meat|cibo suo]], that is, of what is necessary for the support of the body. Indeed reason, the divine law and human law all dictate this. Indeed the Apostle, reckoning this very thing as small, says: [[1 Cor 9:11|If we have sown unto you spiritual things, is it a great matter if we reap your carnal things?|Si nos vobis spiritualia seminavimus, magnum est si vestra carnalia metamus?]] So again he says: [[Gal 6:6|let him that is instructed in the word communicate to him that instructeth him, in all good things|Communicet autem qui catechizatur ei qui catechizat, in omnibus bonis]]; and likewise: [[1 Cor 9:14|the Lord ordained that they who preach the gospel should live by the gospel|Dominus ordinavit his qui Evangelio deserviunt, de Evangelio vivere]].

paras.t: Mystice, per aurum hoc loco prohibitum, intelligitur sapientia sæcularis; per argentum, sermo coloratus; per pecuniam autem, cupiditas; per duas tunicas, duplicitas animi, vel sanctitas simulata; per virgam, rigor vindictæ; per peram, thesauri impietatis. Omnia igitur hæc abjicienda sunt prædicatoribus atque doctoribus Christi, quia ut ait Apostolus: Prudentia carnis, mors est; et rursus, Sermo (inquit) meus non fuit in persuasibilibus humana sapientiæ verbis. Jacobus quoque hortatur: Purificate corda, duplices animo.
paras.en: Mystically, by the gold forbidden in this place is understood worldly wisdom; by silver, ornate speech; by money, covetousness; by the two coats, doubleness of mind, or feigned holiness; by the staff, the severity of vengeance; by the scrip, the treasures of wickedness. All these, then, must be cast away by the preachers and teachers of Christ, because, as the Apostle says: [[Rom 8:6|the wisdom of the flesh is death|Prudentia carnis, mors est]]; and again: My speech, he says, [[1 Cor 2:4|was not in the persuasive words of human wisdom|non fuit in persuasibilibus humanæ sapientiæ verbis]]. James also exhorts: [[Jas 4:8|purify your hearts, ye double minded|Purificate corda, duplices animo]].

paras.t: In quamcumque autem civitatem, id est locum majorem, vel castellum, id est locum minorem, intraveritis, gratia prædicandi, vescendi, vel hospitandi, interrogate, id est, ab hominibus locorum illorum diligenter inquirite, quis habitator, in ea civitate, id est tali vel tali loco, dignus sit vestro introitu seu hospitatione: id est, ad quemlibet indifferenter non intretis ad vescendum vel quiescendum, sed ad aliquem bonas fame, ac vitæ laudabilis, ne ex diffamia et peccatis hospitis vos recipientis, incurratis diffamiam vel suspicionem malam, et ne alios scandalizetis, vestraque doctrina vilipendatur ab aliis. Sed huic documento videtur contrarium, quod ipsemet Christus ad publicanos et peccatores ingressus est, convescens cum eis. Porro Apostoli et successores eorum, quum sint medici animarum, videntur potissimum ingredi debuisse domus peccatorum, non justorum. Et respondendum, quod peccatores ad quos Christus declinavit, veraciter pœnituerunt, et tales a prædicatore sunt visitandi; qui vero indurati atque infames sunt, non sunt visitandi a prædicatoribus: sicut nec medicus visitat languidos omnem medicinam et sanitatis consilium respuentes.
paras.en: [[10:11|And into whatsoever city|In quamcumque autem civitatem]], that is, a larger place, [[10:11|or town|vel castellum]], that is, a smaller place, [[10:11|you shall enter|intraveritis]], to preach, to eat or to lodge, [[10:11|inquire|interrogate]], that is, ask carefully of the people of those places, [[10:11|who in it is worthy|quis … in ea … dignus sit]], who dwelling in that city, that is, in this place or that, is worthy of your coming in or of lodging you: that is, do not go in to just anyone indiscriminately to eat or to rest, but to someone of good name and praiseworthy life, lest from the ill fame and sins of the host who receives you, you incur ill fame or evil suspicion, and lest you scandalize others and your teaching be despised by others. But what seems contrary to this instruction is that Christ Himself went in to publicans and sinners, eating with them[[Matt 9:10||]]. Moreover the Apostles and their successors, being physicians of souls, seem above all to have been bound to enter the houses of sinners, not of the just. And it must be answered that the sinners to whom Christ turned aside truly repented, and such are to be visited by the preacher; but those who are hardened and of evil repute are not to be visited by preachers, just as a physician does not visit sick men who spurn all medicine and all advice for their health.

paras.t: Et ibi, id est in tali hospitio, manete donec exeatis, id est tamdiu quousque occurrat vobis rationabilis causa egrediendi de domo illa, videlicet, ut alibi prædicetis vel aliquid boni alibi efficiatis. Vult itaque Christus ne prædicator, more gyrovagi et hominis vani, currat de domo ad domum et locum sine profectu frequenter transmutet: quia ut Salomon profitetur, Sicut avis transvolans de nido suo, sic homo qui relinquit locum suum. Sed actu prædicationis et corporalis necessitatis cessante convertatur ad Deum, orationi, compunctioni, et contemplationi vacando, quatenus illic sibi Deus infundat quod aliis postmodum affectuose proponat. Qui autem non valet corpus suum stabilire in loco, quomodo poterit cor suum stabilire in Deo?
paras.en: [[10:11|and there abide|et ibi manete]], that is, in such a lodging, [[10:11|till you go thence|donec exeatis]], that is, until a reasonable cause comes up for you to leave that house, namely, to preach elsewhere or to do some good elsewhere. So Christ wills that the preacher should not, like a gyrovague [a wandering monk who drifts from house to house] and a vain man, run from house to house and change his place often without profit; because, as Solomon declares, [[Prov 27:8|As a bird that wandereth from her nest, so is a man that leaveth his place|Sicut avis transvolans de nido suo, sic homo qui relinquit locum suum]]. But when the act of preaching and of bodily necessity is over, let him turn to God, giving his time to prayer, compunction and contemplation, so that there God may pour into him what he may afterwards set before others with feeling. For he who cannot settle his body in one place, how will he be able to settle his heart in God?

paras.t: Intrantes autem in domum talem, salutate eam, dicentes, id est, veram salutem seu felicitatem optate, et dicite habitantibus et exsistentibus in ea: Pax exterior, scilicet quies ab hostium impugnatione, paxque interior, puta tranquillitas mentis, sit huic domui. Quid enim Christus pax nostra, aptius quam pacem mandaret? Est tamen pax quadam carnalis et vitiosa, quam habuit Adam et Eva, quam etiam habet ratio impii cum sensualitate. Hanc Christus non mandat, juxta illud: Non veni pacem mittere, sed gladium. Et si quidem fuerit domus illa digna: id est, si exsistentes in ea fuerint capaces pacis, se disponendo ad gratiam a vobis eis petitam, vel si fuerint præordinati ad pacem Christi, quæ omnem sensum exsuperat, et prædestinati; veniet pax vestra super eam, id est, pax quam eis optastis præstabitur ipsis, et oratio vestra pro illis exaudietur: si autem non fuerit digna, id est capax seu prædestinata, sed obicem ponens et reproba, pax vestra ad vos revertetur, id est, sermo quo eis pacem petistis, vobis meritorius erit, et salutarem in vobis sortietur effectum in presenti et in futuro. Juxta quem sensum ait Psalmista: Oratio mea in sinu meo convertetur.
paras.en: [[10:12|And when you come into the house|Intrantes autem in domum]] of such a kind, [[10:12|salute it, saying|salutate eam, dicentes]], that is, wish it true salvation or happiness, and say to those who dwell and are in it: [[10:12|Peace|Pax]] outward, namely rest from the attacks of enemies, and inward peace, namely tranquillity of mind, [[10:12|be to this house|sit huic domui]]. For what could Christ, [[Eph 2:14|our peace|pax nostra]], more fittingly command than peace? Yet there is a certain carnal and sinful peace, which Adam and Eve had, and which the reason of the wicked man also has with sensuality. This peace Christ does not command, according to that saying: [[Matt 10:34|I came not to send peace, but the sword|Non veni pacem mittere, sed gladium]]. [[10:13|And if that house be worthy|Et si quidem fuerit domus illa digna]]: that is, if those in it are capable of peace, disposing themselves for the grace you ask for them, or if they are foreordained to the peace of Christ, [[Phil 4:7|which surpasseth all understanding|quæ omnem sensum exsuperat]], and predestined, [[10:13|your peace shall come upon it|veniet pax vestra super eam]], that is, the peace you wished them will be granted them, and your prayer for them will be heard; [[10:13|but if it be not worthy|si autem non fuerit digna]], that is, capable, or predestined, but putting an obstacle and reprobate, [[10:13|your peace shall return to you|pax vestra ad vos revertetur]], that is, the word with which you asked peace for them will be meritorious for you, and will have a saving effect in you, in the present and in the future. In which sense the Psalmist says: [[Ps 34:13|my prayer shall be turned into my bosom|Oratio mea in sinu meo convertetur]].

paras.t: Et quicumque non receperit vos, negando vobis hospitium, neque audierit auribus cordis sermones vestros, vestris exhortationibus obtemperando; exeuntes foras de domo vel civitate non recipientium vos, excutite pulverem de pedibus vestris, id est, minutias terræ pedibus vestris adhærentes removete, et in loca illorum rejicite, in signum damnationis eorum: ut excussio illa significet illos in infernum excutiendos, et item quod vos nil temporale ab ipsis quæsistis.
paras.en: [[10:14|And whosoever shall not receive you|Et quicumque non receperit vos]], refusing you lodging, [[10:14|nor hear your words|neque audierit auribus cordis sermones vestros]] with the ears of the heart, by complying with your exhortations: [[10:14|going forth out of that house or city|exeuntes foras de domo vel civitate]] of those who do not receive you, [[10:14|shake off the dust from your feet|excutite pulverem de pedibus vestris]], that is, remove the specks of earth clinging to your feet, and throw them back into their places, as a sign of their damnation: so that this shaking off may signify that they are to be shaken off into hell, and also that you have sought nothing temporal from them.

paras.t: Amen dico vobis, tolerabilius, id est minor pœna, erit terra, id est populo, Sodomorum et Gomorrhæorum, et per consequens, aliarum trium urbium cum illis mersarum, videlicet Seboim, Adama, et Segor, in die judicii, quam illi civitati, id est populo civitatis vos non hospitanti nec audienti. An hoc intelligendum sit absolute, ita quod simpliciter omnibus consideratis, major erit damnatio horum, quam Sodomitarum, difficile est determinare. Videtur enim quod sic, quoniam ceteris paribus, major est damnatio malorum fidelium, quam infidelium, et tanto gravius est peccatum, quo major gratia offertur ac spernitur. Sodomitæ autem non viderunt miracula, nec prædicationem tam efficacem, ut fuit sermocinatio Apostolorum. Oppositum vero hujus apparet ex eo quod in Genesi legitur, quemadmodum homines Sodomitæ pessimi erant, et peccatores nimis coram Domino. Lyra ergo respondet, quod comparatio ista intelligenda sit solum quantum ad aliquid, hoc est quoad peccatum inhospitalitatis et immisericordiæ Sodomorum, non quoad peccata eorum contra naturam, ita quod Sodomitis remissius erit in die judicii, quam istis, non simpliciter, sed quoad hoc, quod minus peecaverunt non exercendo opera misericordiæ in suos, quam isti, qui non rcœperunt Apostolos. Sed huic solutioni videtur obstare, quod Christus simpliciter loquitur. Item, qui non rcœperunt Apostolos, non videntur minus peccasse quam Judæi tempore Ezechielis: et tamen de illis ait Ezechiel, quod Sodoma non peccavit dimidium peccatorum illorum. Rursus, Sodomitæ transgressi sunt legem naturalem dumtaxat, isti vero legem naturalem atque divinam seu scriptam. Hæc tangendo, sic dixerim: quoniam determinare nil audeo. Certum est tamen quorumdam Judæorum, eorum videlicet qui Christum occiderunt, et forte eorum qui occiderunt ejus discipulos, peccata esse graviora sceleribus Sodomorum.
paras.en: [[10:15|Amen I say to you, it shall be more tolerable|Amen dico vobis: Tolerabilius erit]], that is, the punishment will be less, [[10:15|for the land of Sodom and Gomorrha|terra, id est populo, Sodomorum et Gomorrhæorum]], that is, for the people, and consequently for the other three cities sunk with them, namely Seboim, Adama and Segor[[Deut 29:23||]], [[10:15|in the day of judgment, than for that city|in die judicii, quam illi civitati]], that is, for the people of the city that neither lodged nor heard you. Whether this is to be understood absolutely, so that, all things considered, the damnation of these will simply be greater than that of the Sodomites, is hard to determine. For it seems that it is so, since, other things being equal, the damnation of wicked believers is greater than that of unbelievers, and sin is the graver the greater the grace that is offered and spurned; and the Sodomites did not see miracles, nor preaching as effective as the preaching of the Apostles was. But the opposite appears from what we read in Genesis, how [[Gen 13:13|the men of Sodom were very wicked, and sinners before the face of the Lord beyond measure|homines Sodomitæ pessimi erant, et peccatores nimis coram Domino]][[Gen 18:20||]]. So Lyra answers that this comparison is to be understood only in a certain respect, that is, as to the sin of inhospitality and lack of mercy of the Sodomites, not as to their sins against nature: so that it will go more lightly for the Sodomites in the day of judgement than for these, not simply, but in this respect, that they sinned less by not doing works of mercy to their own than these did who did not receive the Apostles. But what seems to stand against this solution is that Christ speaks without qualification. Again, those who did not receive the Apostles do not seem to have sinned less than the Jews in the time of Ezechiel; and yet of them Ezechiel says that Sodom did not sin half their sins[[Ezech 16:48||]] [the words are those of Ezech 16:51, where they are said of Samaria; of Sodom Ezechiel says (16:48) that she did not do as Jerusalem did]. Further, the Sodomites transgressed the natural law only, but these both the natural law and the divine or written law. Touching on these things, I would put it thus, for I dare determine nothing: yet it is certain that the sins of certain Jews, namely of those who killed Christ, and perhaps of those who killed His disciples, are graver than the crimes of the Sodomites.

10.title: Explanatio residuæ partis hujus capituli: Ecce ego mitto vos
10.title_en: Explanation of the rest of this chapter: “Behold I send you”

paras.t: Nam Salvator docet discipulos omnesque prædicatores, ad veram prudentiam, ad invictam atque fortissimam patientiam, ad plenam quoque habendam in Deo fiduciam. Ecce ego mitto vos ad prædicandum, sicut oves in medio luporum, id est, sicut mittuntur homines pii, innocentes ac simplices, qui ovibus comparantur, inter rapaces, voraces crudelesque homines, qui more luporum opprimunt innocentes, juxta illud Isaiæ prophetæ: Quare atteritis populum meum, et facies pauperum commolitis? Tales fuerunt sacerdotes, Scribæ et Pharisæi Judæorum, qui Christum et ejus discipulos dilaniare conati sunt.
paras.en: For the Saviour teaches the disciples and all preachers true prudence, unconquered and most steadfast patience, and full confidence to be had in God. [[10:16|Behold I send you|Ecce ego mitto vos]] to preach, [[10:16|as sheep in the midst of wolves|sicut oves in medio luporum]]: that is, as godly, innocent and simple men, who are compared to sheep, are sent among rapacious, greedy and cruel men, who like wolves oppress the innocent, according to that saying of the prophet Isaias: [[Is 3:15|Why do you consume my people, and grind the faces of the poor?|Quare atteritis populum meum, et facies pauperum commolitis?]] Such were the priests, scribes and Pharisees of the Jews, who tried to tear Christ and His disciples to pieces.

paras.t: Estote ergo prudentes, id est circumspecti, cauti ac providi, ne a lupis fallamini, sicut serpentes, qui obturant aures suas, ne audiant incantantem, et toto corpore caput suum, in quo vita consistit, occultant et protegunt. Sie nos aures obturemus, ne verba nociva, detractoria, aut deceptoria audiamus, quemadmodum Sapiens nos hortatur: Sepi aures tuas spinis, et noli audire linguam nequam. Et simplices, id est sine felle amaritudinis, sine simulatione ac duplicitate, estote sicut columbæ. Non enim est sensus, ubi abundat amaritudo; et væ duplici corde. Ecce ordinata temperies, ut prudentia nostra sit simplex, non vulpina, aut versipellis. Callidi namque provocant iram Dei, et vir versutus odiosus est, ut in Proverbiis dicitur. Simplicitas quoque nostra non sit rudis, indocta, aut indiscreta. De hac sancta simplicitate Salomon ait: Simplicitas justorum diriget eos, et justitia simplicis diriget viam ejus; et alibi: Cum simplicibus sermocinatio ejus. Qui itaque inter perversos et persecutores mittitur, vivit et conversatur, maxima eget prudentia, ne aliquo modo pervertatur, aut mente lædatur ab ipsis. Idcirco Sapiens inquit: Dic sapientiæ, Soror mea es; et prudentiam voca amicam.
paras.en: [[10:16|Be ye therefore wise|Estote ergo prudentes]], that is, circumspect, cautious and provident, lest you be deceived by the wolves, [[10:16|as serpents|sicut serpentes]], which stop their ears so as not to hear the charmer[[Ps 57:5||]], and with their whole body hide and protect their head, in which their life lies. So let us stop our ears, so as not to hear harmful, detracting or deceiving words, as the Wise Man exhorts us: [[Ecclus 28:28|Hedge in thy ears with thorns, hear not a wicked tongue|Sepi aures tuas spinis, et noli audire linguam nequam]]. [[10:16|and simple|Et simplices]], that is, without the gall of bitterness, without pretence or doubleness, [[10:16|as doves|estote sicut columbæ]]. For [[Ecclus 21:15|there is no understanding where there is bitterness|Non enim est sensus, ubi abundat amaritudo]]; and [[Ecclus 2:14|Woe to them that are of a double heart|væ duplici corde]] [the margin's reference is misread; the words are those of Ecclus 2:14]. See the ordered tempering: that our prudence be simple, not fox-like or shifty. For [[Job 36:13|Dissemblers and crafty men prove the wrath of God|Callidi namque provocant iram Dei]], and [[Prov 14:17|the crafty man is hateful|vir versutus odiosus est]], as is said in Proverbs. And let our simplicity not be crude, untaught or indiscreet. Of this holy simplicity Solomon says: [[Prov 11:3|The simplicity of the just shall guide them|Simplicitas justorum diriget eos]], and [[Prov 11:5|The justice of the upright shall make his way prosperous|justitia simplicis diriget viam ejus]]; and elsewhere: [[Prov 3:32|his communication is with the simple|Cum simplicibus sermocinatio ejus]]. So he who is sent among the perverse and persecutors, and lives and moves among them, needs the greatest prudence, lest he be in any way perverted or hurt in mind by them. Therefore the Wise Man says: [[Prov 7:4|Say to wisdom: Thou art my sister: and call prudence thy friend|Dic sapientiæ, Soror mea es; et prudentiam voca amicam]].

paras.t: Cavete autem, id est, vos ipsos observate et custodite, ab hominibus, ne detrimentum salutis et gratiæ inferant vobis, terrendo aut blandiendo. Unde in Ecclesiastico scriptum est: A filiis tuis cave, et a domesticis tuis attende. Et Jeremias: Unusquisque, ait, a proximo se custodiat, et in omni fratre suo non habeat fiduciam. Et certe multum perfectus atque beatus est, qui se ita ab hominibus cavet, quod nullus sit sibi peccati occasio. Tradent enim, id est adducent, vos in conciliis, id est ad loca secreta conciliorum, seu inter se ipsos contra vos concilia celebrantes; et in synagogis suis, id est publicis locis seu congregationibus, flagellabunt vos. Hæc atque sequentia non leguntur illata Apostolis seu discipulis Christi ante ipsius passionem, sed postea frequenter et copiose, ut patet in Actibus Apostolorum. Et ad præsides, id est judices substitutos: quales fuerunt Festus et Felix, ante quos ductus est Paulus; et ad reges: qualis fuit Herodes, qui Jacobum occidit, et Petrum incarceravit, volens post Pascha producere cum populo: ducemini propter me, id est ob constantem prædicationem fidei meæ, et nominis mei cultum atque amorem, in testimonium illis, et gentibus, id est in testimonium damnationis tam regum et judicum vos condemnantium, quam gentium eis consentientium, vel vos eis præsentantium: ita quod vestra innocens adductio, vera confessio, libera prædicatio, injustaque passio, testimonium perhibebit, et declarabit illos esse damnabiles, qui credere noluerunt, et vos persecuti sunt. Vel, In testimonium illis, id est, ut testimonium perhibeatis de me coram ipsis, vel, ut ipsi testimonium ferant adversum vos,
paras.en: [[10:17|But beware of men|Cavete autem ab hominibus]], that is, watch and guard yourselves, lest they bring loss of salvation and grace upon you by terrifying or flattering you. Whence it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 32:26|beware of thy own children, and take heed of them of thy household|A filiis tuis cave, et a domesticis tuis attende]]. And Jeremias: [[Jer 9:4|Let every man take heed of his neighbour, and let him not trust in any brother of his|Unusquisque … a proximo se custodiat … non habeat fiduciam]]. And surely he is very perfect and blessed who so guards himself against men that no one is an occasion of sin to him. [[10:17|For they will deliver you up in councils|Tradent enim vos in conciliis]], that is, will bring you to the secret places of councils, or holding councils among themselves against you; [[10:17|and they will scourge you in their synagogues|et in synagogis suis flagellabunt vos]], that is, in public places or assemblies. These and the following things are not read to have been inflicted on the Apostles or disciples of Christ before His passion, but afterwards, often and abundantly, as is clear in the Acts of the Apostles[[Acts 4:5||]][[Acts 5:27||]]. [[10:18|And you shall be brought before governors|et ad præsides, et ad reges ducemini]], that is, deputy judges[[Acts 16:19||]], such as were Festus and Felix, before whom Paul was brought[[Acts 23:33||]][[Acts 25:6||]]; [[10:18|and before kings|et ad reges]], such as was Herod, who killed James and imprisoned Peter, meaning to bring him out to the people after the Pasch[[Acts 12:1||]][[Acts 12:4||]], [[10:18|for my sake|propter me]], that is, for the steadfast preaching of My faith and for the worship and love of My name, [[10:18|for a testimony to them and to the Gentiles|in testimonium illis, et gentibus]]: that is, as a testimony to the damnation both of the kings and judges who condemn you and of the Gentiles who consent with them or bring you before them; so that your innocent arraignment, your true confession, your free preaching and your unjust suffering will bear witness and declare that those who would not believe and who persecuted you are worthy of damnation. Or, 'for a testimony to them', that is, so that you may bear witness of Me before them; or that they themselves may bear witness against you.

paras.t: Quum autem tradent vos ante conspectum regum et judicum, nolite cogitare, id est anxie premeditari, et cum sollicitudine quadam inquirere, quomodo aut quid loquamini, id est per quem modum, vel quam rationem seu responsionem detis ad objecta vel interrogata. Non prohibetur per hoc, quin homo possit facere quod in se est, sagaciter considerando quid et quam constanter ac sapienter respondere oporteat (præsertim quum princeps Apostolorum dicat: Parati semper ad satisfactionem omni poscenti vos rationem de ea quæ in vobis est fide et spe), sed ne homo in sua præmeditatione, inquisitione, vel eruditione confidat, aut turbetur et metuat si tempus præmeditandi non habeat. Hujus insuper efficax ratio assignatur: Dabitur enim vobis in illa hora traditionis vestræ, quid loquamini, id est divinitus mentibus vestris infundetur ac revelabitur apta responsio. Tunc enim potissimum adimpletur quod Dominus loquitur: Aperi (seu dilata) os tuum, et implebo illud. Cujus annectitur ratio: Non enim vos estis qui loquimini, quasi principales locutores, vel ex proprio ingenio respondentes, sed Spiritus Patris vestri, id est Spiritus Sanctus a Patre æterno procedens, est qui loquitur in vobis, id est in anima vestra, per inspirationem internam, docendo vos: juxta illud, Audiam quid loquatur in me Dominus Deus. Propter quod dicit Salvator: Paracletus Spiritus Sanctus docebit vos omnia, et suggeret vobis omnia quæcumque dixero vobis. Vel, Loquitur in vobis, id est per os vestrum, tanquam principalis locutor: prout in Actibus de Stephano scribitur, quod Judæi non poterant resistere sapientiæ et Spiritui qui loquebatur.
paras.en: [[10:19|But when they shall deliver you up|Quum autem tradent vos]] before the face of kings and judges, [[10:19|take no thought|nolite cogitare]], that is, do not anxiously think beforehand and inquire with a certain solicitude, [[10:19|how or what to speak|quomodo aut quid loquamini]], that is, in what manner, or what reason or answer you are to give to what is objected or asked. This does not forbid a man to do what is in him, considering shrewdly what he ought to answer and how steadfastly and wisely (especially since the prince of the Apostles says: [[1 Pet 3:15|being ready always to satisfy every one that asketh you a reason of that hope which is in you|Parati semper ad satisfactionem omni poscenti vos rationem de ea quæ in vobis est]]), but that a man should not trust in his own forethought, inquiry or learning, nor be troubled and afraid if he has no time to think beforehand. And an effective reason for this is given: [[10:19|for it shall be given you in that hour what to speak|Dabitur enim vobis in illa hora traditionis vestræ, quid loquamini]], the hour of your being delivered up: that is, a fitting answer will be poured into your minds and revealed by God. For then above all is fulfilled what the Lord says: [[Ps 80:11|open thy mouth wide, and I will fill it|Aperi (seu dilata) os tuum, et implebo illud]]. The reason for this is added: [[10:20|For it is not you that speak|Non enim vos estis qui loquimini]], as principal speakers, or answering from your own wit, [[10:20|but the spirit of your Father|sed Spiritus Patris vestri]], that is, the Holy Ghost proceeding from the eternal Father, [[10:20|that speaketh in you|est qui loquitur in vobis]], that is, in your soul, by inward inspiration, teaching you; according to that saying: [[Ps 84:9|I will hear what the Lord God will speak in me|Audiam quid loquatur in me Dominus Deus]]. Hence the Saviour says: [[John 14:26|the Paraclete, the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things and bring all things to your mind, whatsoever I shall have said to you|Paracletus Spiritus Sanctus docebit vos omnia, et suggeret vobis omnia quæcumque dixero vobis]]. Or, 'speaketh in you', that is, through your mouth, as principal speaker: as is written in the Acts of Stephen, that the Jews [[Acts 6:10|were not able to resist the wisdom and the spirit that spoke|non poterant resistere sapientiæ et Spiritui qui loquebatur]].

paras.t: Tradet autem frater infidelis fratrem fidelem in mortem martyrii, et pater infidelis filium fidelem; et insurgent filii infideles, in parentes fideles, et morte eos afficient. Hæc omnia frequenter contigisse in sanctis martyribus, multæ testantur historiæ. Et eritis odio omnibus, id est aliquibus de omni genere hominum, puta cunctis perversis: de quibus dicit Apostolus, Si hominibus placerem, Christi ser; vus non essem; propter nomen meum, id est propter me, et propter fidem, spem et caritatem, conversationem et prædicationem quam habetis in me. Veritas enim generat odium. Hinc Christus inquit: Si de mundo essetis, mundus quod suum erat diligeret; quia vero de mundo non estis, sed ego elegi vos de mundo, propterea odit vos mundus. Et Joannes: Nolite, inquit, mirari si odit vos mundus. Qui autem perseveraverit in fide, caritate et opere, usque in finem vitæ præsentis inclusive, hic salvus erit, beatitudinem patriæ consequendo. In quacumque enim hora justus recesserit a justitia, omnes justitiæ ejus oblivioni tradentur, ut ait Ezechiel. Et in ea affectione anima æternaliter manet, in qua separatur a corpore, prout Salomon asserit: Si ceciderit, inquit, lignum ad austrum, aut ad aquilonem, in quocumque loco ceciderit, ibi erit. Sola ergo perseverantia coronatur; nec inchoasse, sed consummasse, virtutis est. Hanc vocem, Qui perseveraverit, non audiunt nisi oves.
paras.en: [[10:21|The brother also shall deliver up the brother to death|Tradet autem frater fratrem in mortem]], the unbelieving brother the faithful brother, to the death of martyrdom, [[10:21|and the father the son|et pater infidelis filium]], the unbelieving father the faithful son; [[10:21|and the children shall rise up against their parents|et insurgent filii infideles, in parentes]], unbelieving children against faithful parents, [[10:21|and shall put them to death|et morte eos afficient]]. Many histories testify that all these things often happened among the holy martyrs. [[10:22|And you shall be hated by all men|Et eritis odio omnibus]], that is, by some of every kind of men, namely by all the perverse, of whom the Apostle says: [[Gal 1:10|If I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ|Si hominibus placerem, Christi servus non essem]]; [[10:22|for my name's sake|propter nomen meum]], that is, for My sake, and for the faith, hope and charity, the way of life and the preaching that you have in Me. For truth begets hatred. Hence Christ says: [[John 15:19|If you had been of the world, the world would love its own: but because you are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you|Si de mundo essetis, mundus quod suum erat diligeret; quia vero de mundo non estis, sed ego elegi vos de mundo, propterea odit vos mundus]]. And John: [[1 John 3:13|Wonder not, brethren, if the world hate you|Nolite, inquit, mirari si odit vos mundus]]. [[10:22|but he that shall persevere unto the end|qui autem perseveraverit usque in finem]], in faith, charity and works, up to and including the end of the present life, [[10:22|he shall be saved|hic salvus erit]], by attaining the happiness of the fatherland. For in whatever hour the just man turns away from justice, all his justices shall be given over to oblivion, as Ezechiel says[[Ezech 18:24||]][[Ezech 33:13||]]. And the soul remains for ever in the disposition in which it is separated from the body, as Solomon asserts: [[Eccles 11:3|If the tree fall to the south, or to the north, in what place soever it shall fall, there shall it be|Si ceciderit … lignum ad austrum … ibi erit]]. Perseverance alone, then, is crowned; nor is it of virtue to have begun, but to have finished. This saying, 'he that shall persevere', none hear but the sheep[[John 10:3||]].

paras.t: Quum autem persequentur vos in civitate ista, in qua principaliter estis, fugite in aliam. Sic enim Christus fugit in Ægyptum, et sæpius abiit et abscondit se. Petrus quoque de carcere ab angelo liberatus, relicta Jerosolyma, fugit in alium locum. Sie et Paulus a Damasco fugit. Et Stephano lapidato, fideles qui erant Jerosolymis, dispersi sunt per regiones Judææ præter Apostolos. Quæ omnia in Actibus recitantur. Sed videtur huic contrarium, quod apud Joannem scriptum est: Mercenarius videt lupum venientem, et fugit. Et respondendum, quod ista admonitio de fuga non est universaliter intelligenda, nec per modum præcepti communiter data. Quando enim ex fuga alicujus alii graviter scandalizarentur, fides irrideretur, justitia opprimeretur, subditi periclitarentur, nequaquam est fugiendum, presertim prælato, superiori vel doctori, nisi omnes simul fugere possint. Porro, quum ex fuga alicujus non immineat tale periculum, sed potius aliquod commodum, scilicet: quia non expediret Ecclesiæ tali pastore seu membro privari, propter futurum profectum; et quia qui fugit, potest alibi fructificare, et in loco a quo fugit, alium idoneum loco sui relinquere: tunc fugere licet. Fugere autem ex timore ruinæ, propter propriam infirmitatem, non semper est illicitum, quamvis sit imperfectum. Sed et multi Sanctorum ex fervore fidei, etiam non requisiti, obtulerunt se ipsos ad martyrium.
paras.en: [[10:23|And when they shall persecute you in this city|Quum autem persequentur vos in civitate ista]], in which you chiefly are, [[10:23|flee into another|fugite in aliam]]. For so Christ fled into Egypt[[Matt 2:13||]], and often went away and hid Himself[[Luke 4:30||]][[John 8:59||]][[John 12:36||]]. Peter too, freed from prison by the angel[[Acts 12:7||]], left Jerusalem and fled to another place[[Acts 12:17||]]. So too Paul fled from Damascus[[Acts 9:25||]]. And when Stephen had been stoned, the faithful who were in Jerusalem were scattered through the regions of Judea, except the Apostles[[Acts 8:1||]]. All this is told in the Acts. But what is written in John seems contrary to this: the hireling [[John 10:12|seeth the wolf coming|videt lupum venientem]], [[John 10:12|and flieth|et fugit]]. And it must be answered that this counsel about flight is not to be understood universally, nor given in general by way of precept. For when by someone's flight others would be gravely scandalized, the faith mocked, justice oppressed, or subjects endangered, there must be no flight at all, especially for a prelate, a superior or a teacher, unless all can flee together. But when no such danger threatens from someone's flight, but rather some advantage, namely because it would not be expedient for the Church to be deprived of such a pastor or member, on account of the good he will do later, and because he who flees can bear fruit elsewhere, and leave someone suitable in his place where he flees from: then it is lawful to flee. And to flee from fear of falling, because of one's own weakness, is not always unlawful, though it is imperfect. But many of the Saints, from fervour of faith, offered themselves to martyrdom even when they were not sought.

paras.t: Et quasi Apostoli quærerent, Quamdiu fugiemus? respondet: Amen dico vobis, non consummabitis, id est, perfecte non perambulabitis, nec prædicando circuietis, civitates Israel, id est populi Judæorum, donec, id est antequam, veniat Filius hominis, id est, post resurrectionem ad vos revertatur: quemadmodum apud Joannem scriptum est, Non vos relinquam orphanos, vado, et venio ad vos; et rursus, Iterum autem videbo vos. Tempus quippe prædicationis Apostolorum in Judæa ante passionem, modicum fuit, nec in eo poterant omnes civitates Israel consummare. Vel sic: Non consummabitis, id est, non convertetis ad fidem, civitates Israel, id est totum populum Judæorum, vos et successores vestri, donec veniat Filius hominis ad judicium universale. Non enim generaliter convertentur, nisi in fine sæculi, instante secundo Christi adventu.
paras.en: And as though the Apostles asked, How long shall we flee? He answers: [[10:23|Amen I say to you, you shall not finish all the cities of Israel|Amen dico vobis, non consummabitis civitates Israël]], that is, you will not go through perfectly, nor go round preaching in, the cities of Israel, that is, of the people of the Jews, [[10:23|till|donec]], that is, before, [[10:23|the Son of man come|veniat Filius hominis]], that is, comes back to you after the resurrection; as is written in John: [[John 14:18|I will not leave you orphans|Non vos relinquam orphanos]]; [[John 14:28|I go away, and I come unto you|vado, et venio ad vos]]; and again: [[John 16:22|I will see you again|Iterum autem videbo vos]]. For the time of the Apostles' preaching in Judea before the passion was short, nor could they finish all the cities of Israel in it. Or thus: 'you shall not finish', that is, you will not convert to the faith, 'the cities of Israel', that is, the whole people of the Jews, you and your successors, until the Son of man comes to the universal judgement. For they will not be converted generally except at the end of the world, when the second coming of Christ is at hand.

paras.t: Non est discipulus super magistrum, nec servus super dominum suum. Si per magistrum et dominum, determinate intelligamus Christum, certum est nullum Christianum hoc magistro ac domino esse majorem vel parem. Si vero per magistrum et dominum, intelligatur indeterminate quicumque magister et dominus, intelligendum est verbum hoc formaliter, ut sit sensus: Non est discipulus, in quantum discipulus, super magistrum, id est major aut doctior eo, nec servus, secundum quod talis est, super dominum suum, id est major ac dignior eo. Sufficit discipulo, ut sit sicut magister ejus, id est, ei assimiletur: si tamen ille perfectus sit. Alioqui æmulari oportet charismata meliora, et magis proficere, presertim quum dicat Propheta: Super omnes docentes me intellexi. Si vero per magistrum, Christus specialiter designetur, tunc omnino sufficit discipulo, id est cuilibet Christiano, ut sit similis Christo, qui omnis perfectionis ac sanctitatis exemplar est, cui nullus æquari valet seu parificari. Debet tamen ejus sequi vestigia, juxta illud: Qui se dicit in Christo manere, debet sicut ille ambulavit, et ipse ambulare. Et servus debet esse contentus, vel servo sufficere debet, ut sit sicut dominus ejus, id est, domino suo conformetur ut decet. Hac Salvator ait, quatenus sui ipsius exemplo provocet discipulos suos et omnes fideles ad patientiam inconcussam. Unde prædicta applicans ad se ipsum, adjecit:
paras.en: [[10:24|The disciple is not above the master, nor the servant above his lord|Non est discipulus super magistrum, nec servus super dominum suum]]. If by 'master' and 'lord' we understand Christ definitely, it is certain that no Christian is greater than or equal to this Master and Lord. But if by 'master' and 'lord' is understood indefinitely any master and lord, this saying is to be understood formally, so that the sense is: The disciple, as disciple, is not above the master, that is, greater or more learned than he, nor the servant, as such, above his lord, that is, greater or worthier than he. [[10:25|It is enough for the disciple that he be as his master|Sufficit discipulo, ut sit sicut magister ejus]], that is, that he be made like him, if indeed the master is perfect. Otherwise one must [[1 Cor 12:31|be zealous for the better gifts|æmulari oportet charismata meliora]] and make more progress, especially since the Prophet says: [[Ps 118:99|I have understood more than all my teachers|Super omnes docentes me intellexi]]. But if by 'master' Christ in particular is meant, then it is wholly enough for the disciple, that is, for any Christian, that he be like Christ, who is the exemplar of all perfection and holiness, to whom no one can be equalled or made level. Yet he ought to follow His footsteps[[1 Pet 2:21||]], according to that saying: [[1 John 2:6|He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also to walk even as he walked|Qui se dicit in Christo manere, debet sicut ille ambulavit, et ipse ambulare]]. [[10:25|and the servant as his lord|Et servus]] ought to be content, or it ought to be enough for the servant, that he be as his lord, that is, conformed to his lord as is fitting. The Saviour says this so that by His own example He may rouse His disciples and all the faithful to unshaken patience. Whence, applying what He had said to Himself, He added:

paras.t: Si, pro quia, patremfamilias, id est me Christum, ecclesiasticæ familiæ patrem, Beelzebub, id est dæmonem seu dæmoniacum, vocaverunt Judei, dicendo: In Beelzebub principe dæmoniorum ejicit dæmonia, quanto magis, id est multo amplius, domesticos ejus, id est discipulos meos, filios domus meæ, qua est Ecclesia, appellabunt Beelzebub, adscribendo verba, facta et signa eorum principi dæmoniorum? Dicitur autem aliquis demon dupliciter, videlicet per naturam, et per participationem seu imitationem diabolicæ pravitatis: et hoc secundo modo vocaverunt Judæi Christum Beelzebub; sicque Christus ait de Juda, Nonne vos duodecim ego elegi, et unus ex vobis diabolus est!
paras.en: [[10:25|If they have called the good man of the house Beelzebub|Si … patremfamilias … Beelzebub … vocaverunt]] ('if' for 'since'), that is, Me, Christ, the father of the Church's household, the Jews called Beelzebub, that is, a demon or one possessed, saying: [[Luke 11:15|He casteth out devils by Beelzebub, the prince of devils|In Beelzebub principe dæmoniorum ejicit dæmonia]]; [[10:25|how much more them of his household|quanto magis domesticos ejus?]], that is, much more, My disciples, the sons of My house, which is the Church, will they call Beelzebub, ascribing their words, deeds and signs to the prince of demons? Now someone is called a demon in two ways, namely by nature, and by sharing in or imitating the devil's wickedness; and in this second way the Jews called Christ Beelzebub; and so Christ says of Judas: [[John 6:71|Have not I chosen you twelve? And one of you is a devil.|Nonne vos duodecim ego elegi, et unus ex vobis diabolus est!]]

paras.t: Ne ergo timueritis eos, propter injurias et contumelias quas vobis possunt infligere, sed potius exsultate in omni adversitate quam ab eis patimini: considerantes quid passus sim ego, et gloriantes in hoc, quod domino vestro ac magistro conformari meruistis, quum hoc sit beneficium ingens. Quid enim tam gloriosum est servo, quam ut domino suo assimiletur! Sæpe contingit ut aliquis injuriam passus doleat, et ulcisci se cupiat. Si vero conspexerit alium multo sublimiorem, eadem vel graviora perpessum, et tamen servare patientiam, incipit consolari, et ab ira cessare, dicens in se: Si ille tantus talia patitur, quanto magis ego? Ita et nos, si Christi passionem patientiamque pensamus, patientiam discimus, et cum Apostolo in tribulationibus jucundamur. Cui vero hi impii metuendi non sint, subditur:
paras.en: [[10:26|Therefore fear them not|Ne ergo timueritis eos]] for the injuries and insults they can inflict on you, but rather rejoice in every adversity you suffer from them, considering what I have suffered, and glorying in this, that you have been found worthy to be conformed to your Lord and Master, since this is a great benefit. For what is so glorious for a servant as to be made like his lord? It often happens that someone who has suffered an injury grieves and wants to avenge himself; but if he sees another far higher who has suffered the same or worse and yet keeps patience, he begins to be consoled and to cease from anger, saying within himself: If so great a man suffers such things, how much more I? So we too, if we weigh Christ's passion and patience, learn patience, and with the Apostle are glad in tribulations[[Rom 5:3||]][[2 Cor 7:4||]]. Why these wicked men are not to be feared is then added:

paras.t: Nihil enim opertum, id est, nullum opus est jam ita absconditum et ignotum, quod non revelabitur, id est, manifestum erit cunctis et singulis in die judicii, quatenus omnes sciant justum esse judicium Dei; et occultum, id est, nullum propositum, consilium, desiderium, vel cogitamen, est nunc ita secretum, quod non scietur ab omnibus in die novissimo, quando, secundum Apostolum, adveniet Dominus, qui illuminabit abscondita tenebrarum, et manifestabit consilia cordium. Quasi dicat: Non curetis quid nunc patiamini propter me, quoniam veniet hora in qua et vestra patientia, et illorum perversitas, dignam ac justam sortietur mercedem: secundum illud Joannis in Apocalypsi, Ecce venio cito, et merces mea mecum est, dare unicuique secundum opera sua.
paras.en: [[10:26|For nothing is covered|Nihil enim opertum]], that is, no work is now so hidden and unknown, [[10:26|that shall not be revealed|quod non revelabitur]], that is, will be made manifest to each and all on the day of judgement, so that all may know that the judgement of God is just; [[10:26|nor hid|et occultum]], that is, no purpose, counsel, desire or thought is now so secret, [[10:26|that shall not be known|quod non scietur]] by all on the last day, when, according to the Apostle, [[1 Cor 4:5|the Lord come, who both will bring to light the hidden things of darkness and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts|adveniet Dominus, qui illuminabit abscondita tenebrarum, et manifestabit consilia cordium]]. As if to say: Do not care what you suffer now for My sake, since the hour will come in which both your patience and their perversity will receive a worthy and just reward; according to that word of John in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 22:12|Behold, I come quickly: and my reward is with me, to render to every, man according to his works|Ecce venio cito, et merces mea mecum est, dare unicuique secundum opera sua]].

paras.t: Quod dico vobis in tenebris, hoc est in locis secretis; vel, In tenebris, id est in parabolis, mysteriis et figuris, de his quæ evangelicam veritatem concernunt; dicite aliis in lumine, hoc est publice coram omnibus. Et quod in aure, id est secrete, et quasi silenter, auditis a me de finali omnium retributione, et ceteris fidei documentis, prædicate super tecta, id est stando in locis elevatis atque patentibus: prout Isaias inquit, Clama, quasi tuba exalta vocem tuam; et alibi, Super montem excelsum ascende, tu qui evangelizas Sion. Ad litteram, per tecta, intelligi possunt deambulatoria templi, super qua ascendebant doctores Hebræorum prædicaturi populo, vel tecta domorum in Palestina, quæ plana erant, et apta ut super ea staret prædicans populo.
paras.en: [[10:27|That which I tell you in the dark|Quod dico vobis in tenebris]], that is, in secret places; or, 'in the dark', that is, in parables, mysteries and figures, about the things that concern the truth of the Gospel, [[10:27|speak ye in the light|dicite aliis in lumine]] to others, that is, publicly before all. [[10:27|and that which you hear in the ear|et quod in aure auditis]], that is, secretly and as if silently, from Me, about the final retribution of all and the other teachings of the faith, [[10:27|preach ye upon the housetops|prædicate super tecta]], that is, standing in high and open places; as Isaias says: [[Is 58:1|lift up thy voice like a trumpet|quasi tuba exalta vocem tuam]]; and elsewhere: [[Is 40:9|Get thee up upon a high mountain, thou that bringest good tidings to Sion|Super montem excelsum ascende, tu qui evangelizas Sion]]. Literally, by the housetops may be understood the walks of the temple, on which the teachers of the Hebrews went up to preach to the people, or the roofs of the houses in Palestine, which were flat and fit for one to stand on them preaching to the people.

paras.t: Et nolite timere timore carnali et inordinato, eos qui occidunt corpus, hoc est tyrannos et persecutores, animam autem rationalem non possunt occidere, quum sit immortalis. Non ergo possunt ei auferre vitam naturæ, nec etiam vitam gratiæ, compellendo eam ad culpam, quum libera sit. Ideo dicit Scriptura: Qui timet hominem, cito corruet; et Isaias: Nolite, inquit, timere opprobrium hominum, et blasphemias eorum: quis tu, ut timeas ab homine mortali, et a filio hominis qui quasi fœnum arescet? Non itaque cessemus ab opere bono propter tormenta quæ reprobi infligere possunt, ne simus de eorum collegio, de quibus fertur in Psalmo: Deum non invocaverunt; illic trepidaverunt timore, ubi non erat timor. Unde rursus ait Psalmista: Non timebo millia populi circumdantis me, etc.; et, Si consistant adversum me castra, non timebit cor meum. Et Job: Si expavi, inquit, ad multitudinem nimiam. Si autem pensemus hujus vitæ brevissimam umbram, instabilem fluxum, et infinitam calamitatem, atque futuræ beatitudinis, quæ pro temporali passione momentanea redditur, merces in æternum mansura, non solum non timebimus, sed et affectabimus mori pro Christo. Quoniam tamen hoc ipsum magna perfectio est, et donum Dei, orare debemus cum Psalmista, A timore inimici eripe animam meam: videlicet, ne timeat persequentem. Verumtamen naturalis timor mortis, qui etiam fuit in Christo, non reprobatur; sed per rationem frenandus est, ne immoderatus consistat: quinimo, ut cesset.
paras.en: [[10:28|And fear ye not|Et nolite timere]] with a carnal and disordered fear [[10:28|them that kill the body|eos qui occidunt corpus]], that is, tyrants and persecutors, [[10:28|and are not able to kill the soul|animam autem rationalem non possunt occidere]], the rational soul, since it is immortal. So they cannot take from it the life of nature, nor even the life of grace by forcing it to sin, since it is free. Therefore Scripture says: [[Prov 29:25|He that feareth man shall quickly fall|Qui timet hominem, cito corruet]]; and Isaias: [[Is 51:7|fear ye not the reproach of men, and be not afraid of their blasphemies|Nolite, inquit, timere opprobrium hominum, et blasphemias eorum]]; [[Is 51:12|who art thou, that thou shouldst be afraid of a mortal man, and of the son of man, who shall wither away like grass?|quis tu, ut timeas ab homine mortali, et a filio hominis qui quasi fœnum arescet?]] Let us not, then, cease from good works because of the torments the reprobate can inflict, lest we be of their company of whom it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 13:5|They have not called upon the Lord: there have they trembled for fear, where there was no fear|Deum non invocaverunt; illic trepidaverunt timore, ubi non erat timor]][[Ps 52:6||]]. Whence again the Psalmist says: [[Ps 3:7|I will not fear thousands of the people surrounding me|Non timebo millia populi circumdantis me]], etc.; and: [[Ps 26:3|If armies in camp should stand together against me, my heart shall not fear|Si consistant adversum me castra, non timebit cor meum]]. And Job: [[Job 31:34|If I have been afraid at a very great multitude|Si expavi, inquit, ad multitudinem nimiam]]. But if we weigh the most brief shadow of this life, its unstable flow and its endless misery, and the reward of future happiness, which is given for momentary temporal suffering[[2 Cor 4:17||]] and will last for ever, we shall not only not fear, but shall even long to die for Christ. Yet since this is itself great perfection and a gift of God, we ought to pray with the Psalmist: [[Ps 63:2|deliver my soul from the fear of the enemy|A timore inimici eripe animam meam]], namely, that it may not fear the persecutor. Nevertheless the natural fear of death, which was in Christ too, is not condemned; but it must be bridled by reason, lest it be immoderate, nay rather, so that it may cease.

paras.t: Sed potius eum timete, qui potest et animam et corpus perdere in gehennam, hoc est damnare atque projicere in infernum: videlicet Deum, qui tanto amplius metuendus est omni persecutore et impio homine, quanto pœnalior ac diuturnior est pœna inferni, quam pœna hujus mundi, temporalisque mortis. Ideo Propheta: Magnus es tu, inquit, et magnum nomen tuum in fortitudine: quis non te timebit, o Rex gentium? Et sanctus Job ait: A facie ejus turbatus sum, et considerans eum, timore sollicitor. Salomon quoque in Proverbiis: In timore (inquit) Domini esto tota die, et habebis spem in novissimo.
paras.en: [[10:28|but rather fear him that can destroy both soul and body in hell|Sed potius eum timete, qui potest et animam et corpus perdere in gehennam]], that is, damn and cast into hell: namely God, who is so much more to be feared than every persecutor and wicked man as the pain of hell is more grievous and lasting than the pain of this world and of temporal death. Therefore the Prophet says: [[Jer 10:6|thou art great, and great is thy name in might|Magnus es tu, inquit, et magnum nomen tuum in fortitudine]]: [[Jer 10:7|Who shall not fear thee, O king of nations?|quis non te timebit, o Rex gentium?]] And holy Job says: [[Job 23:15|I am troubled at his presence, and when I consider him, I am made pensive with fear|A facie ejus turbatus sum, et considerans eum, timore sollicitor]]. Solomon too in the Proverbs: [[Prov 23:17|be thou in the fear of the Lord all the day long|In timore (inquit) Domini esto tota die]], [[Prov 23:18|thou shalt have hope in the latter end|habebis spem in novissimo]].

paras.t: Denique ad habendum cor tam securum ac imperterritum, juxta illud, Justus quasi leo confidens, absque terrore erit, hortatur nos Christus ex consideratione divinæ providentiæ omnia disponentis ac præmiantis dicens: Nonne duo passeres asse veneunt, hoc est, pro nummo sic dicto venduntur. Est enim as, assis, genus nummi parvi valoris. Et unus ex illis passeribus venditis non cadet super terram mactatus, id est, non occidetur, sine Patre vestro, hoc est sine nutu et providentia Patris cœlestis. Unde in alio loco inquit: Nonne quinque passeres veneunt dipondio? et unus ex illis non est in oblivione coram Deo. Est autem dipondium, duplicem valorem assis habens. Vestri autem et capilli capitis omnes numerati sunt: quoniam omnia quantumcumque parva et vilia, distincte et perfectissime cognoscuntur a Deo. Ex his infert Salvator conclusionem intentam: Nolite ergo timere corporum occisores, quasi Deus non attendat, nec curet de persecutione et morte vobis inferenda, nec præmium tribuat. Quod utique ita non est: nam multis passeribus meliores estis vos, quum sitis rationales. Si ergo illorum providentiam habet Deus, nec sine ejus nutu unus illorum occiditur, quanto magis habet curam vestri, et pensat quid pro justitia sustinetis, reddetque præmium copiosum?
paras.en: Further, so that we may have a heart so secure and undaunted, according to that saying, [[Prov 28:1|the just, bold as a lion, shall be without dread|Justus quasi leo confidens, absque terrore erit]], Christ exhorts us from the consideration of the divine providence that orders and rewards all things, saying: [[10:29|Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing?|Nonne duo passeres asse veneunt]], that is, sold for the coin so called. For the as is a kind of coin of small value. [[10:29|and not one of them shall fall on the ground|Et unus ex illis passeribus venditis non cadet super terram]], one of those sparrows sold, killed, that is, will not be killed, [[10:29|without your Father|sine Patre vestro]], that is, without the will and providence of the heavenly Father. Whence in another place He says: [[Luke 12:6|Are not five sparrows sold for two farthings, and not one of them is forgotten before God?|Nonne quinque passeres veneunt dipondio? et unus ex illis non est in oblivione coram Deo]] And a dipondius is worth twice an as. [[10:30|But the very hairs of your head are all numbered|Vestri autem et capilli capitis omnes numerati sunt]]: since all things, however small and mean, are known by God distinctly and most perfectly. From this the Saviour draws the conclusion He intended: [[10:31|Fear not therefore|Nolite ergo timere]] the slayers of bodies, as though God did not attend to or care about the persecution and death to be inflicted on you, nor would give a reward. Which surely is not so: [[10:31|better are you than many sparrows|multis passeribus meliores estis vos]], since you are rational. If, then, God has providence over them, and not one of them is killed without His will, how much more has He care of you, and weighs what you endure for justice, and will render you a plentiful reward?

paras.t: Ostendit præterea Christus, quanta sit merces timentium Deum, non homines persequentes. Omnis ergo qui confitebitur me verbo et opere, seu confessione fidei formata, ac laudis divinæ, coram hominibus, maxime infidelibus, impiis, et tyrannis: quod se fecisse gloriatur Psalmista, dicens, Et loquebar in testimoniis tuis in conspectu regum, et non confundebar; confitebor, hoc est, approbabo, et ad me pertinere affirmabo, eum coram Patre meo, qui in cœlis est, quia quum fuerit meo tribunali præsentatus, judicabo pro eo, et ejus justitiam commemorabo: imo Christus indesinenter confitetur tales pertinere ad se. Qui autem negaverit me coram hominibus, negabo et ego eum, nisi pœnitentiam agens, resipuerit: quemadmodum Petrus, qui post trinam negationem flevit amare, et veniam meruit; coram Patre meo, qui in cœlis est, quia quum fuerit mihi ad judicandum oblatus, pronuntiabo sententiam contra eum, dicamque, Nescio te.
paras.en: Further, Christ shows how great is the reward of those who fear God, not the men who persecute them. [[10:32|Every one therefore that shall confess me before men|Omnis ergo qui confitebitur me coram hominibus]], in word and deed, that is, by the confession of a formed faith [that is, faith informed by charity] and of the divine praise, before men, above all before unbelievers, the wicked and tyrants (which the Psalmist glories that he did, saying: [[Ps 118:46|And I spoke of thy testimonies before kings: and I was not ashamed|Et loquebar in testimoniis tuis in conspectu regum, et non confundebar]]), [[10:32|I will also confess him|confitebor et ego eum]], that is, approve him and declare that he belongs to Me, [[10:32|before my Father who is in heaven|coram Patre meo, qui in cœlis est]]: because when he is presented at My tribunal I will judge in his favour and recall his justice; indeed Christ unceasingly confesses that such belong to Him. [[10:33|But he that shall deny me before men, I will also deny him|Qui autem negaverit me coram hominibus, negabo et ego eum]], unless he repent and come to his senses, as Peter did, who after his threefold denial wept bitterly and obtained pardon[[Matt 26:75||]], [[10:33|before my Father who is in heaven|coram Patre meo, qui in cœlis est]]: because when he is brought before Me to be judged, I will pronounce sentence against him and will say: I know thee not[[Luke 13:27||]].

paras.t: Tripliciter Christus negatur: verbo tantum, ut in his qui timore pœnarum Christum negaverunt; verbo et opere, sed non corde, ut quum malus Christianus dicit et agit contra fidem, quum tamen non dubitet fidem esse veram; opere, sed non verbo, juxta illud Apostoli: Confitentur se nosse Deum, factis autem negant, quum sint abominati et reprobi. Potest etiam addi quartus modus, videlicet, quum quis corde non credit, et tamen se credere asserit vel ostendit. Quælibet harum negationum est peccatum mortale, saltem in casu aliquo. Unde dicit Apostolus: Si negaverimus eum, et ipse negabit nos; et alibi, Noli, inquit, erubescere testimonium Domini nostri Jesu.
paras.en: Christ is denied in three ways: in word only, as in those who denied Christ for fear of punishment; in word and deed but not in heart, as when a bad Christian speaks and acts against the faith, though he does not doubt that the faith is true; in deed but not in word, according to that saying of the Apostle: [[Tit 1:16|They profess that they know God: but in their works they deny him: being abominable|Confitentur se nosse Deum, factis autem negant, quum sint abominati]] and reprobate. A fourth way can also be added, namely when someone does not believe in his heart and yet asserts or shows that he believes. Each of these denials is a mortal sin, at least in some case. Whence the Apostle says: [[2 Tim 2:12|If we deny him, he will also deny us|Si negaverimus eum, et ipse negabit nos]]; and elsewhere: [[2 Tim 1:8|Be not thou therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord|Noli, inquit, erubescere testimonium Domini nostri]] Jesus.

paras.t: Nolite arbitrari quod venerim mittere pacem carnalem, mundanam, et in malo fundatam, in terram, hoc est inter homines. Est igitur pax nociva et inordinata, quæ est concordia seu consensus, vel quietatio aliquorum in malo: quam Paulus sciens esse inter Sadducæos et Pharisæos, ex industria rupit eam, dicens: De spe et resurrectione mortuorum ego judicor hodie. De qua pace dicit Salvator: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, et quidem in hac die quæ ad pacem tibi; et Psalmista, Quia zelavi super iniquos, pacem peccatorum videns. Denique alia est pax vera, spiritualis, interna, quæ est tranquillitas mentis, ex ordinatione interiorum (quam caritas facit) procedens. De qua fertur in Psalmo: Pax multa diligentibus legem tuam; et rursus, Mansueti delectabuntur in multitudine pacis. Ista non convenit pravis, prout in Isaia scriptum est: Non est pax impiis, dicit Dominus. Hanc Christus venit mittere in terram, sicut in Actibus loquitur Petrus: Verbum (inquiens) misit Deus in Israel, pacem annuntians per Jesum. Unde per Prophetam de Christo prædictum est: Et erit iste pax, Assyrius quum venerit, et quum calcaverit in domibus nostris. Et Zacharias dixit: Loquetur pacem gentibus.
paras.en: [[10:34|Do not think that I came to send peace|Nolite arbitrari quod venerim mittere pacem]], carnal, worldly peace founded in evil, [[10:34|upon earth|in terram]], that is, among men. For there is a harmful and disordered peace, which is the agreement or consent, or resting together, of some in evil: which Paul, knowing it to exist between the Sadducees and Pharisees, broke on purpose, saying: [[Acts 23:6|concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question|De spe et resurrectione mortuorum ego judicor]] this day. Of which peace the Saviour says: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, [[Luke 19:42|and that in this thy day, the things that are to thy peace|et quidem in hac die quæ ad pacem tibi]]; and the Psalmist: [[Ps 72:3|Because I had a zeal on occasion of the wicked, seeing the prosperity of sinners|Quia zelavi super iniquos, pacem peccatorum videns]] [pacem peccatorum, literally 'the peace of sinners']. But there is another peace, true, spiritual and inward, which is tranquillity of mind proceeding from the ordering of the inward powers (which charity brings about). Of which it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 118:165|Much peace have they that love thy law|Pax multa diligentibus legem tuam]]; and again: [[Ps 36:11|But the meek shall inherit the land, and shall delight in abundance of peace|Mansueti autem hæreditabunt terram, et delectabuntur in multitudine pacis]]. This does not belong to the wicked, as is written in Isaias: [[Is 48:22|There is no peace to the wicked, saith the Lord|Non est pax impiis, dicit Dominus]]. This peace Christ came to send upon earth, as Peter says in the Acts: [[Acts 10:36|God sent the word to the children of Israel, preaching peace by Jesus|Verbum … misit Deus … pacem annuntians per Jesum]]. Whence it was foretold of Christ through the Prophet: [[Mich 5:5|And this man shall be our peace, when the Assyrian shall come into our land, and when he shall set his foot in our houses|Et erit iste pax, Assyrius quum venerit, et quum calcaverit in domibus nostris]]. And Zacharias said: [[Zach 9:10|he shall speak peace to the Gentiles|Loquetur pacem gentibus]].

paras.t: Consequenter ergo Christus, quasi exponens se ipsum, adjunxit: Non veni pacem jam dictam ac vitiosam mittere, sed gladium, hoc est eradicationem ac separationem hujuscemodi pacis. Potest quoque per gladium accipi rigor perfectionis quam docuit Christus, vel sermo evangelicus: de quo Paulus, Et gladium (inquiens) spiritus, quod est verbum Dei; et in Psalmo, Accingere gladio tuo super femur tuum, potentissime. Hinc in Isaia Christus testatur: Posuit Dominus os meum quasi gladium acutum. Ad litteram autem loquitur Christus potissimum de gladio seu discordia quæ in toto orbe, ex Apostolorum pralicatione secuta est, dum pene in qualibet domo quidam conversi sunt, et quidam in infidelitate manserunt, inter quos dissensio fuit. Propter quod dictum est: Tradet frater fratrem in mortem, et pater filium. Ut enim dicit Hieronymus: Nullus fidus affectus inter eos est, quorum diversa est fides.
paras.en: So then Christ, as though explaining Himself, added: [[10:34|I came not to send peace|non veni pacem mittere]], the sinful peace just spoken of, [[10:34|but the sword|sed gladium]], that is, the rooting out and severing of such peace. By the sword may also be taken the rigour of the perfection that Christ taught, or the word of the Gospel, of which Paul says: [[Eph 6:17|the sword of the Spirit (which is the word of God)|gladium (inquiens) spiritus, quod est verbum Dei]]; and in the Psalm: [[Ps 44:4|Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, O thou most mighty|Accingere gladio tuo super femur tuum, potentissime]]. Hence in Isaias Christ testifies: [[Is 49:2|he hath made my mouth like a sharp sword|Posuit Dominus os meum quasi gladium acutum]]. But literally Christ speaks above all of the sword, that is, the discord, that followed in the whole world from the Apostles' preaching, when in almost every house some were converted and some remained in unbelief, and there was dissension between them. For which reason it was said: [[10:21|The brother also shall deliver up the brother to death, and the father the son|Tradet frater fratrem in mortem, et pater filium]]. For, as Jerome says, there is no faithful affection between those whose faith is different.

paras.t: Veni enim separare hominem adversus patrem suum, hoc est filium a patre dividere, carnalem eorum pacem destruendo, et inordinatam unionem tollendo, ne unanimes sint in peccato, sed altero eorum aversio a me, alius convertatur ad me; et simili modo, veni separare filiam adversus matrem suam, malam amicitiam auferendo, et bonam inimicitiam seu veram dilectionem inducendo, ut evellatur carnalis affectus; et nurum, hoc est conjugem filii, adversus socrum suam, id est matrem mariti. Et inimici hominis patrisfamilias, erunt domestici ejus: quia commorantes secum sibi adversabuntur atque dissentient. Hoc ipsum apud Michæam prophetam legitur: Vir fratrem suum venatur ad mortem; ab ea quæ dormit in sinu tuo custodi claustra oris tui, quia filius contumeliam facit patri, filia consurget adversus matrem, nurus adversus socrum, et inimici hominis domestici ejus. Venit igitur Christus homines quantumcumque propinquos separare ab invicem, dupliciter: Primo, auferendo ab eis unionem carnalis affectionis, et consensum in malo: et hæc est separatio spiritualis, necessaria ad salutem, sine qua nemo potest esse servus vel discipulus Christi.
