And He answers: [[11:16|It is like to children sitting in the market place|Similis est pueris sedentibus in foro]], [[11:17|Who crying|qui clamantes]], that is, singing, [[11:17|to their companions|coæqualibus]], that is, to other children equal in number to themselves, [[11:17|say|dicunt]] with reproach: [[11:17|We have piped to you|Cecinimus vobis]], that is, have sung a song of gladness, [[11:17|and you have not danced|et non saltastis]], that is, you have not rejoiced with us; [[11:17|we have lamented|lamentavimus]], that is, sung you a mournful song, [[11:17|and you have not mourned|et non planxistis]], that is, you were not moved to compassion. To children, then, who neither rejoice with those who rejoice nor grieve with those who grieve, these are likened. The reason for this is added.

paras.t: Venit enim Joannes Baptista neque mmanducans neque bibens, hoc est, socialiter non conversans, nec consueto cibo potuque utens, et frequenter jejunans, sicut de eo prædictum est, Vinum et siceram non bibet; et dicunt homines hujus pessimæ generationis: Dæmonium habet, id est, dæmoniacus est Joannes, et dæmonis operatione sic abstinet, abstracteque vivit. Possessi quippe et arrepticii multa agunt et sustinent, quæ alii agere et pati non valent. Venit Filius hominis, id est Christus, manducans et bibens, hoc est, socialiter vivens, cum hominibus vescens, et filiis suis licentiam manducandi concedens, dicendo, Numquid jejunare possunt filii sponsi, quamdiu cum illis est sponsus? Et dicunt de eo: Ecce homo vorax, instar lupi seu canis famelici, quasi putaret se non posse saturari, et potator vini, tanquam lurco et deliciosus; publicanorum, id est magnorum et manifestorum prævaricatorum, et peccatorum, hoc est aliorum minus malorum, amicus, quia manducat cum eis, non solum amans eorum naturam, sed etiam culpas. Erat utique Christus eorum amicus, amando naturam, non vitia: nam et animam suam pro talibus posuit. Et idcirco cum eis conversari ac vesci dignatus est, ut sua pietate, caritate ac mansuetudine, eos ad pœnitentiam provocaret. Quoniam enim mediator erat Dei ac hominum, reconciliator peccatorum, et medicus infirmorum ac miserorum, tales vitare non debuit, sed benignissime reparare, conversando cum ipsis.
paras.en: [[11:18|For John came neither eating nor drinking|Venit enim Joannes neque manducans, neque bibens]], that is, not living sociably, not using the customary food and drink, and fasting often, as was foretold of him: [[Luke 1:15|shall drink no wine nor strong drink|Vinum et siceram non bibet]]; [[11:18|and they say|et dicunt]], the men of this most wicked generation: [[11:18|He hath a devil|Dæmonium habet]], that is, John is possessed, and abstains so and lives so withdrawn by the working of a demon. For the possessed and the frenzied do and endure many things that others cannot do or bear. [[11:19|The Son of man came eating and drinking|Venit Filius hominis manducans, et bibens]], that is, Christ, living sociably, eating with men, and granting His sons leave to eat, saying: [[Matt 9:15|Can the children of the bridegroom mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with them?|Numquid jejunare possunt filii sponsi, quamdiu cum illis est sponsus?]] [Denis reads 'fast' for 'mourn']. [[11:19|and they say|Et dicunt]] of Him: [[11:19|Behold a man that is a glutton|Ecce homo vorax]], like a wolf or a famished dog, as though He thought He could not be filled, [[11:19|and a wine drinker|et potator vini]], like a guzzler and a man of pleasure; [[11:19|a friend of publicans|publicanorum et peccatorum amicus]], that is, of great and open transgressors, [[11:19|and sinners|et peccatorum]], that is, of others less wicked, because He eats with them, loving not only their nature but also their sins. Christ was indeed their friend, by loving their nature, not their vices: for He even laid down His life for such[[John 10:15||]]. And therefore He deigned to keep company and eat with them, so that by His kindness, charity and gentleness He might call them to repentance. For since He was the [[1 Tim 2:5|mediator of God and men|mediator erat Dei ac hominum]], the reconciler of sinners and the physician of the sick and wretched, He ought not to avoid such, but most kindly to restore them by living among them.

paras.t: Prædictis itaque pueris assimilantur Scribæ et Pharisæi, quia nec Joanni abstinenti, nec Christo manducanti, se conformare vel credere voluerunt, sed utriusque vitam perverse interpretati sunt, et in sua obstinatione pertinaciter permanserunt.
paras.en: To the aforesaid children, then, the scribes and Pharisees are likened, because they would neither conform themselves to nor believe John who abstained, nor Christ who ate, but perversely misinterpreted the life of each, and remained stubbornly in their obstinacy.

paras.t: Referunt quidam, quod Judæi volentes filios suos ad virtutes provehere, assuefecerunt eos ad ludos honestos: ita quod pueri convenerunt in forum, eisque in duas partes æquales divisis, una pars cecinit carmen jucundum, alia lugubre. Et qui cecinit carmen lætitiæ, exprobravit alteri, cur sibi non congauderet; similiter pars cantans canticum triste, exprobravit alteri parti, cur sibi non compateretur. Et ista fiebant ad insinuandam vanitatem lætitiæ, et defectum compassionis ac amicitiæ in hoc mundo. Aliqui per pueros istos intelligunt prædicatores et discipulos Christi, de quibus per Isaiam Christus testatur: Ecce ego et pueri mei, quos dedit mihi Dominus. Hi prædicaverunt Judæis canticum jucunditatis spiritualis, ut delectarentur in Deo; canticum quoque doloris, ut pœniterent: Judæi vero nulli cantico consenserunt. Sed non videtur quod prædictis bonis sanctisque pueris, comparentur Scribæ et Pharisæi. Imo Christus, qui cecinit carmen consolationis et gratiæ, Joannes quoque, canens carmen comminationis ac pœnitentiæ, eis assimilantur. Scribæ autem et Pharisæi his assimilantur qui nec flent cum flentibus, nec gaudent cum gaudentibus. Tales, proh dolor! adhuc multi sunt, qui omnia facta aliorum interpretantur in partem deteriorem, facientes sibi de melle venenum, et bona quæ nequeunt imitari, malunt detrahendo et deridendo vituperare, quam humiliter venerari.
paras.en: Some relate that the Jews, wishing to train their children in virtue, accustomed them to decent games: so that the children met in the market place and, being divided into two equal parts, one part sang a joyful song, the other a mournful one. And the part that sang the song of gladness reproached the other for not rejoicing with it; likewise the part singing the sad song reproached the other for not grieving with it. And these things were done to suggest the vanity of gladness, and the lack of compassion and friendship, in this world. Some by these children understand the preachers and disciples of Christ, of whom Christ testifies by Isaias: [[Is 8:18|Behold I and my children, whom the Lord hath given me|Ecce ego et pueri mei, quos dedit mihi Dominus]]. These preached to the Jews the song of spiritual joy, that they might delight in God, and the song of sorrow, that they might repent; but the Jews consented to neither song. But it does not seem that the scribes and Pharisees are compared to these good and holy children. Rather Christ, who sang the song of consolation and grace, and John too, singing the song of threatening and penance, are likened to them; and the scribes and Pharisees are likened to those who neither [[Rom 12:15|weep with them that weep|flent cum flentibus]], nor [[Rom 12:15|Rejoice with them that rejoice|gaudent cum gaudentibus]]. Such, alas! there are still many, who interpret all the deeds of others in the worse part, making poison for themselves out of honey, and who would rather blame by detraction and mockery the good things they cannot imitate than humbly reverence them.

paras.t: Et justificata, id est laudata et vera esse cognita, est sapientia, id est sapientialis Christi doctrina, vel ipsemet Christus, qui est increata sapientia Patris, a filiis suis, id est ab amatoribus et studiosis auditoribus ejus, puta Apostolis, ceterisque Judæi: fidelibus, qui ut allegatum est, auditis prædictis Christi sermonibus, justificaverunt Deum, et Christi eloquia approbaverunt. Stultus autem, ut Salomon dicit, non recipit verba prudentis. Nec animalis homo percipit ea quæ Dei sunt, teste Apostolo.
paras.en: [[11:19|And wisdom is justified|Et justificata est sapientia]], that is, praised and known to be true, that is, the wise teaching of Christ, or Christ Himself, who is the uncreated Wisdom of the Father, [[11:19|by her children|a filiis suis]], that is, by those who love Him and diligently hear Him, namely the Apostles and the other faithful Jews, who, as was alleged, having heard the aforesaid words of Christ, [[Luke 7:29|justified God|justificaverunt Deum]] and approved Christ's sayings. But the fool, as Solomon says, [[Prov 18:2|receiveth not the words of prudence|non recipit verba prudentis]]. [[1 Cor 2:14|the sensual man perceiveth not these things that are of the Spirit of God|Nec animalis homo percipit ea quæ Dei sunt]], as the Apostle witnesses.

paras.t: Tunc Jesus cœpit exprobrare, ex compassionis affectu vel zelo justitiæ, non ex inordinato motivo, civitatibus, id est urbium habitatoribus, in quibus facta sunt plurimæ virtutes ejus, id est multa miracula a Christo, et forte etiam ab Apostolis, quia non egissent pœnitentiam. stabilem visis tot signis. Væ, id est, æterna damnatio manet, tibi, Corozain, væ tibi, Bethsaida: quia si in Tyro et Sidone, urbibus idololatriæ deditis, factæ essent virtutes, id est miracula et efficacissimæ prædicationes, quæ factæ sunt in vobis; olim in cilicio, illud induendo, et cinere, illum capitibus suis superponendo, vel in cinerem se prosternendo, pœnitentiam egissent, quemadmodum Ninivitæ ad prædicationem Jonæ. Quam verum sit hoc, constat ex Actis Apostolorum, ubi fides atque devotio Tyriorum describitur, qui crediderunt Apostolis, maxime Paulo. Huic testimonio Christi omnino simile est quod ad Ezechielem Dominus ait: Fili hominis, non ad populum profundi sermonis et ignotæ linguæ tu mitteris: et si ad illos mittereris, ipsi audirent te; domus autem Israel, ad quam mitto te, nolunt audire te, quia nolunt audire me.
paras.en: [[11:20|Then began he to upbraid|Tunc Jesus cœpit exprobrare]], Jesus, from a feeling of compassion or zeal for justice, not from a disordered motive, [[11:20|the cities|civitatibus]], that is, the inhabitants of the towns, [[11:20|wherein were done the most of his miracles|in quibus factæ sunt plurimæ virtutes ejus]], that is, many miracles by Christ, and perhaps also by the Apostles, [[11:20|for that they had not done penance|quia non egissent pœnitentiam]], lasting penance, after seeing so many signs. [[11:21|Woe thee, Corozain, woe to thee, Bethsaida|Væ tibi, Corozain, væ tibi, Bethsaida]], that is, eternal damnation awaits you; [[11:21|for if in Tyre and Sidon|quia si in Tyro et Sidone]], cities given over to idolatry, [[11:21|had been wrought the miracles|factæ essent virtutes]], that is, the miracles and most effective preaching, [[11:21|that have been wrought in you|quæ factæ sunt in vobis]], [[11:21|they had long ago done penance in sackcloth and ashes|olim in cilicio … et cinere … pœnitentiam egissent]], putting on sackcloth and putting ashes on their heads, or lying down in ashes, as the Ninivites did at the preaching of Jonas[[Jon 3:5||]]. How true this is appears from the Acts of the Apostles, where the faith and devotion of the Tyrians is described, who believed the Apostles, above all Paul[[Acts 12:20||]][[Acts 21:4||]]. Wholly like this testimony of Christ is what the Lord says to Ezechiel: Son of man, [[Ezech 3:5|thou art not sent to a people of a profound speech, and of an unknown tongue|non ad populum profundi sermonis et ignotæ linguæ tu mitteris]]: [[Ezech 3:6|and if thou wert sent to them, they would hearken to thee|et si ad illos mittereris, ipsi audirent te]]; [[Ezech 3:7|But the house of Israel will not hearken to thee: because they will not hearken to me|domus autem Israel, ad quam mitto te, nolunt audire te, quia nolunt audire me]] [Denis inserts 'to which I send thee'].

paras.t: Verumtamen dico vobis: Tyro et Sidoni, id est populo urbium harum in gentilitate defuncto, remissius erit, id est minor damnatio, in die judicii, quoniam solam naturalem legem transgressi sunt, quam vobis, qui prævaricati estis legem naturalem ac scriptam, et insuper signa documentaque Christi parvi pendistis: propter quod tanto graviora sunt scelera vestra, quanto majora beneficia contempsistis, et ingratissimi exstitistis.
paras.en: [[11:22|But I say unto you, it shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon|Verumtamen dico vobis: Tyro et Sidoni remissius erit]], that is, for the people of these cities who died in heathenism, that is, a lesser damnation, [[11:22|in the day of judgment, than for you|in die judicii, quam vobis]], since they transgressed only the natural law, while you have broken the natural and the written law, and moreover have made little of the signs and teachings of Christ: for which reason your crimes are the graver as the benefits you have despised are the greater, and you have been most ungrateful.

paras.t: Et tu, Capharnaum, principalis urbs Galilææ, numquid usque in colum exaltaberis, sicut præsumis? id est, numquid ad tantam sublimitatem pertinges, sicut elatio tua conatur? Per talem enim modum loquendi designatur magnitudo superbiæ, ut est illud in Psalmo: Posuerunt in cœlum os suum. Usque in infernum descendes, propter pompam et ingratitudinem tuam: juxta illud, Si ascenderit usque ad cœlum superbia ejus, et caput ejus nubes tetigerit, quasi sterquilinium in fine perdetur. Simile est quod ait Abdias propheta: Si exaltatus fueris ut aquila, et si inter sidera posueris nidum tuum, inde detraham te, dicit Dominus. Porro, Capharnaum, Corozain et Bethsaida, urbes Galilææ, et sitæ in littore laci seu stagni vel maris Genesareth, primo receperunt doctrinam Christi, sed post redierunt ad vomitum: ideo non pœnituerunt veraciter ac stabiliter, sicut supra capitulo quarto plenius patuit. Quia si in Sodomis, id est in Pentapoli, propter peccatum contra naturam submersa: illorum enim quinque urbium principalis fuerat Sodoma; factæ fuissent virtutes quæ factæ sunt in te a me ipso, forte permansissent usque in hanc diem, id est, habitatores pœnituissent, nec essent urbes illæ submersæ, vel potius combustæ igne ac sulfure. Dicit autem, Forte, non quasi dubitans, sed ut servet sobrietatem sermonis, et libertatem voluntatis designet. Verumtamen dico vobis, quia terra, id est habitatoribus olim, Sodomorum, remissius erit in die judicii quam tibi. Et probabile est, quod absolute loquendo, minor erit damnatio Sodomorum quam istorum, et quod minus graviter peccaverunt quam isti, prout in præcedenti capitulo dictum est de non recipientibus ipsos Apostolos.
paras.en: [[11:23|And thou Capharnaum|Et tu, Capharnaum]], chief city of Galilee, [[11:23|shalt thou be exalted up to heaven?|numquid usque in cœlum exaltaberis]], as you presume? That is, will you reach such a height as your pride strives for? For by such a way of speaking the greatness of pride is signified, as in that of the Psalm: [[Ps 72:9|They have set their mouth against heaven|Posuerunt in cœlum os suum]]. [[11:23|thou shalt go down even unto hell|Usque in infernum descendes]], for your pomp and ingratitude: according to that saying: [[Job 20:6|If his pride mount up even to heaven, and his head touch the clouds|Si ascenderit usque ad cœlum superbia ejus, et caput ejus nubes tetigerit]]: [[Job 20:7|In the end he shall be destroyed like a dunghill|quasi sterquilinium in fine perdetur]]. Like this is what the prophet Abdias says: [[Abd 1:4|Though thou be exalted as an eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars: thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord|Si exaltatus fueris ut aquila, et si inter sidera posueris nidum tuum, inde detraham te, dicit Dominus]]. Moreover, Capharnaum, Corozain and Bethsaida, cities of Galilee situated on the shore of the lake, or pool, or sea of Genesareth, first received Christ's teaching, but afterwards returned to their vomit[[Prov 26:11||]]: so they did not repent truly and lastingly, as appeared more fully above in the fourth chapter[[Matt 4:13||]]. [[11:23|For if in Sodom|Quia si in Sodomis]], that is, in the Pentapolis, sunk for the sin against nature[[Gen 19:24||]] (for Sodom had been the chief of those five cities), [[11:23|had been wrought the miracles that have been wrought in thee|factæ fuissent virtutes quæ factæ sunt in te]] by Me Myself, [[11:23|perhaps it had remained unto this day|forte permansissent usque in hanc diem]], that is, the inhabitants would have repented, and those cities would not have been sunk, or rather burnt with fire and brimstone. He says 'perhaps', not as doubting, but to keep sobriety of speech and to signify the freedom of the will. [[11:24|But I say unto you, that it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment than for thee|Verumtamen dico vobis, quia terræ Sodomorum remissius erit in die judicii, quam tibi]], that is, for those who once lived there. And it is probable that, speaking absolutely, the damnation of the Sodomites will be less than that of these, and that they sinned less gravely than these, as was said in the preceding chapter of those who did not receive the Apostles themselves[[Matt 10:15||]].

paras.t: Merito ait Psalmista: Venite et videte opera Dei, terribilis in consiliis super filios hominum; et, Justitia tua sicut montes Dei, judicia tua abyssus multa. Quis enim investiget vel explicet, cur justus atque omnipotens Deus coram illis miracula fecit, et illis nuntios suos ac prædicatores misit, quos noverat non eredituros, et horum nullum fecit his quos noverat eredituros, si vidissent vel audissent quod isti? Unde cum Apostolo exclamare oportet; O altitudo divitiarum sapientiæ et scientiæ Dei! etc.
paras.en: Rightly does the Psalmist say: [[Ps 65:5|Come and see the works of God; who is terrible in his counsels over the sons of men|Venite et videte opera Dei, terribilis in consiliis super filios hominum]]; and: [[Ps 35:7|Thy justice is as the mountains of God, thy judgments are a great deep|Justitia tua sicut montes Dei, judicia tua abyssus multa]]. For who can search out or explain why the just and almighty God worked miracles before those, and sent His messengers and preachers to those whom He knew would not believe, and did none of these things for those whom He knew would have believed if they had seen or heard what these did? Hence we must cry out with the Apostle: [[Rom 11:33|O the depth of the riches of the wisdom and of the knowledge of God!|O altitudo divitiarum sapientiæ et scientiæ Dei!]] etc.

paras.t: Præterea ipsemet Christus, quum ista dixisset, in vocem confessionis, laudis ac gratiarum actionis prorupit, sicut subjungitur. In illo tempore, quum ista dixisset, respondens, id est, ad prædicta proportionate ac pertinenter adjiciens, Jesus dixit; Confiteor tibi confessione laudis et gratiarum actionis, hoc est, laudo te et gratias ago, et ad manifestandum justitiam tuam, dico ac fateor tibi, id est ad gloriam tuam, Pater mi naturalis, qui es aliorum pater per gratiam adoptionis: qui in Psalmo ais ad me, Ex utero ante luciferum genui te; et, Ego hodie genui te; Domine cœli et terræ, id est cœlestium atque terrestrium, visibilium et invisibilium dominator: de quo Esther ait, Domine rex omnipotens, in ditione tua cuncta sunt posita. Est ergo duplex confessio, scilicet propriæ culpæ, de qua David: Dixi, Confitebor adversum me injustitiam meam Domino; et laudis divine, de qua Sapiens: Confitebor tibi, Domine rex, et collaudabo te Deum salvatorem meum.
paras.en: Moreover, Christ Himself, when He had said these things, broke out into a voice of confession, praise and thanksgiving, as is added: [[11:25|At that time|In illo tempore]], when He had said these things, [[11:25|Jesus answered and said|respondens Jesus dixit]], that is, adding something proportioned and pertinent to what had been said: [[11:25|I confess to thee|Confiteor tibi]] with the confession of praise and thanksgiving, that is, I praise You and give You thanks, and to make Your justice manifest I say and acknowledge to You, that is, to Your glory, [[11:25|O Father|Pater]], My Father by nature, who are the Father of others by the grace of adoption; who in the Psalm say to Me: [[Ps 109:3|from the womb before the day star I begot thee|Ex utero ante luciferum genui te]]; and: [[Ps 2:7|this day have I begotten thee|Ego hodie genui te]]; [[11:25|Lord of Heaven and earth|Domine cœli et terræ]], that is, Ruler of things heavenly and earthly, visible and invisible: of whom Esther says: [[Esth 13:9|O Lord, Lord, almighty king, for all things are in thy power|Domine rex omnipotens, in ditione tua cuncta sunt posita]]. So there is a twofold confession, namely of one's own guilt, of which David says: [[Ps 31:5|I said I will confess against my self my injustice to the Lord|Dixi, Confitebor adversum me injustitiam meam Domino]]; and of the divine praise, of which the Wise Man says: [[Ecclus 51:1|I will give glory to thee, O Lord, O King, and I will praise thee, O God my Saviour|Confitebor tibi, Domine rex, et collaudabo te Deum salvatorem meum]].

paras.t: Quia abscondisti hæc mysteria fidei et sacramenta novæ legis et prædicationis meæ notitiam, a sapientibus et prudentibus in oculis suis: de qualibus asserit Isaias, Væ (inquiens) qui sapientes estis in oculis vestris, et coram vobismetipsis prudentes; itemque, Sapientia et scientia tua decepit te. Qui tamen veraciter stulti sunt quemadmodum Jeremias fatetur: Stultus factus est omnis homo a scientia sua. In malevolam enim animam non introibit sapientia. Quamvis autem per sapientes et prudentes intelligi possint omnes litterati hujus sæculi, philosophi et legisperiti, et quos mundus reputat sapientes, tamen hoc loco, per sapientes et prudentes præsertim signantur Scribæ ac Pharisæi, qui se eruditos putabant, sequentes litteram occidentem, non spiritum vivificantem. Dicuntur autem sapientes, quantum ad notitiam divinorum; prudentes, quoad humanarum rerum notitiam.
paras.en: [[11:25|because thou hast hid these things|Quia abscondisti hæc]], the mysteries of the faith and the sacraments of the new law and the knowledge of My preaching, [[11:25|from the wise and prudent|a sapientibus et prudentibus]] in their own eyes; of whom Isaias asserts: [[Is 5:21|Woe to you that are wise in your own eyes, and prudent in your own conceits|Væ … qui sapientes estis in oculis vestris … prudentes]]; and likewise: [[Is 47:10|Thy wisdom, and, thy knowledge, this hath deceived thee|Sapientia et scientia tua decepit te]]. Yet these are truly fools, as Jeremias declares: [[Jer 10:14|Every man is become a fool for knowledge|Stultus factus est omnis homo a scientia sua]]. For [[Wis 1:4|wisdom will not enter into a malicious soul|In malevolam enim animam non introibit sapientia]]. And although by the wise and prudent may be understood all the learned of this world, philosophers and lawyers, and those whom the world reckons wise, yet in this place the wise and prudent signify above all the scribes and Pharisees, who thought themselves learned, following [[2 Cor 3:6|the letter killeth|litteram occidentem]], not [[2 Cor 3:6|the spirit quickeneth|spiritum vivificantem]]. They are called wise as to the knowledge of divine things, prudent as to the knowledge of human affairs.

paras.t: Et revelasti ea, per illuminationem internam, parvulis, id est humilibus: de quibus ait Psalmista, Declaratio sermonum tuorum illuminat, et intellectum dat parvulis; et Sapientia in Proverbiis, Si quis est parvulus, veniat ad me. Ad hos enim, quasi ad valles profundas, descendunt a Patre luminum et fonte, rivi bonitatis, ac radii sapientiæ, quos corda pomposa nequeunt continere, juxta illud Psalmista: Qui emittis fontes in convallibus, inter medium montium pertransibunt aquæ. Hinc dicit Apostolus: Videte vocationem vestram, fratres, quia non multi sapientes secundum carnem sunt inter vos; et rursus, Nonne stultam fecit Deus sapientiam hujus mundi? Sapientes ergo et prudentes in oculis proprii cordis, propter suam superbiam divinæ veritatis illustratione privati sunt. Parvuli vero, per humilitatem meruerunt a Spiritu Sancto doceri, sicut Apostoli, aliique credentes, de quibus jam dicebatur: Justificata est sapientia a filiis suis. Propter quod Salomon loquitur: Ubi humilitas, ibi sapientia.
paras.en: [[11:25|and hast revealed them|Et revelasti ea]], by inward enlightenment, [[11:25|to little ones|parvulis]], that is, to the humble; of whom the Psalmist says: [[Ps 118:130|The declaration of thy words giveth light: and giveth understanding to little ones|Declaratio sermonum tuorum illuminat, et intellectum dat parvulis]]; and Wisdom in the Proverbs: [[Prov 9:4|Whosoever is a little one, let him come to me|Si quis est parvulus, veniat ad me]]. For to these, as to deep valleys, there come down from [[Jas 1:17|the Father of lights|Patre luminum]] and fountain the streams of goodness and the rays of wisdom, which proud hearts cannot hold; according to that of the Psalmist: [[Ps 103:10|Thou sendest forth springs in the vales: between the midst of the hills the waters shall pass|Qui emittis fontes in convallibus, inter medium montium pertransibunt aquæ]]. Hence the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 1:26|see your vocation, brethren, that there are not many wise according to the flesh|Videte vocationem vestram, fratres, quia non multi sapientes secundum carnem]] among you; and again: [[1 Cor 1:20|Hath not God made foolish the wisdom of this world?|Nonne stultam fecit Deus sapientiam hujus mundi?]] So the wise and prudent in the eyes of their own heart were deprived, because of their pride, of the enlightening of divine truth; but the little ones by humility deserved to be taught by the Holy Ghost, as were the Apostles and the other believers, of whom it was just said: [[11:19|wisdom is justified by her children|Justificata est sapientia a filiis suis]]. For which reason Solomon says: [[Prov 11:2|where humility is, there also is wisdom|Ubi humilitas, ibi sapientia]].

paras.t: Ita, Pater, id est, sic vere est, et ita contigit, o Pater æterne, quoniam sic placitum est ante te, hoc est in conspectu tuo, vel in corde ac luce sapientiæ tua. Tanquam dicat: Prima causa istius, quod quidam præ aliis illuminati sunt, non est nisi ipsum beneplacitum voluntatis divinæ. Quod enim unus præ alio humilitatem et cetera quæ ad divinam illuminationem disponunt, habet, originaliter procedit ex prædestinatione divina, quam nulla præcedunt merita. Præterea, quamvis in communi ratio assignetur, cur quidam electi, quidam præsciti sint, utpote quatenus misericordia Dei refulgeat in electis, qui sunt vasa pietatis in honorem et gloriam, et justitia Dei manifestetur in reprobis, qui sunt vasa iræ in interitum; in speciali tamen causa dari non valet, cur potius iste quam ille electus sit, nisi voluntas divina. Propter quod ait Augustinus: Quem trahat, et quem non trahat, cur istum trahat et illum non trahat, noli dijudicare, si non vis errare. Voluntas etenim Dei, quum sit prima omnium entium causa, causam non habet. Nec tamen irrationalis vel injusta esse potest, quum essentialiter sit ipsa sapientia atque justitia infinita. Quod igitur comprehendere non valemus, eum omni reverentia veneremur, quoniam scrutator majestatis opprimetur a gloria.
paras.en: [[11:26|Yea, Father|Ita, Pater]], that is, so it truly is, and so it has come about, O eternal Father, [[11:26|for so hath it seemed good in thy sight|quoniam sic placitum est ante te]], that is, in Your sight, or in the heart and light of Your wisdom. As if to say: The first cause of this, that some are enlightened before others, is nothing but the good pleasure of the divine will itself. For that one man rather than another has humility and the other things that dispose to divine enlightenment proceeds originally from the divine predestination, which no merits go before. Moreover, although in general a reason is given why some are elect and some foreknown [that is, foreseen as lost], namely that the mercy of God may shine forth in the elect, who are [[Rom 9:23|vessels of mercy|vasa pietatis]] unto honour and glory, and the justice of God be made manifest in the reprobate, who are [[Rom 9:22|vessels of wrath, fitted for destruction|vasa iræ in interitum]]; yet in particular no cause can be given why this one rather than that one is elect, except the divine will. For which reason Augustine says: Whom He draws and whom He does not draw, why He draws this one and does not draw that one, do not judge, if you do not wish to err. For the will of God, since it is the first cause of all beings, has no cause. Nor yet can it be irrational or unjust, since it is in essence wisdom itself and infinite justice. What, then, we cannot comprehend, let us venerate with all reverence, since [[Prov 25:27|he that is a searcher of majesty shall be overwhelmed by glory|scrutator majestatis opprimetur a gloria]].

paras.t: Prædictis Christi verbis consonat illud Psalmistæ: Brachium eorum non salvavit eos, sed dextera tua, et brachium tuum, et illuminatio vultus tui, quoniam complacuisti in eis; et quod in Exodo ait Deus sublimis et benedictus, Miserebor cui voluero, et clemens ero in quem mihi placuerit. Ideo dicit Apostolus: Cujus vult miseretur, et quem vult indurat.
paras.en: With these words of Christ agrees that of the Psalmist: [[Ps 43:4|neither did their own arm save them. But thy right hand and thy arm, and the light of thy countenance: because thou wast pleased with them|Brachium eorum non salvavit eos, sed dextera tua, et brachium tuum, et illuminatio vultus tui, quoniam complacuisti in eis]]; and what God, sublime and blessed, says in Exodus: [[Ex 33:19|I will have mercy on whom I will, and I will be merciful to whom it shall please me|Miserebor cui voluero, et clemens ero in quem mihi placuerit]]. Therefore the Apostle says: [[Rom 9:18|he hath mercy on whom he will. And whom he will, he hardeneth|Cujus vult miseretur, et quem vult indurat]].

paras.t: Omnia mihi tradita sunt a Patre meo. In Christo est duplex natura. Secundum ergo divinam naturam, omnia, id est tota divinitatis plenitudo et quidquid perfectionis in Patre est, tradita, hoc est, per modum naturalis emanationis data sunt Filio per generationem æternam, quemadmodum apud Joannem ipse protestatur: Omnia (inquiens) quæcumque habet Pater, mea sunt; et rursus ad Patrem, Omnia (inquit) mea tua sunt, et tua mea sunt. Ex quo innotescit, sic omnia hæc data Filio, ut in Patre permanserint, ita quod idem numero esse ac posse in utroque consistat. Et quamvis in Patre non sit diversitas, sed simplicissima unitas, Filius tamen pluraliter dicit, Omnia, quoniam divinitas Patris omnium perfectiones cum infinita plenitudine comprehendit. Unde et Paulus pluraliter dicit: Invisibilia Dei per ea quæ facta sunt intellecta, cognoscuntur. Insuper, secundum humanam Christi naturam, omnia creata, data et subjecta sunt ei, quantum ad auctoritatem, ab exordio incarnationis. Nam eo ipso quo ejus humanitas unita est Verbo hypostatica unione, prælata est omni creaturæ. Propter quod ait: Pater diligit Filium, et omnia dedit in manu ejus. In resurrectione vero omnia data sunt Christo homini, quantum ad manifestationem, quia ex tunc cœpit innotescere et publice prædicari excellentia Christi. Ideo infra: Data est (ait) mihi omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra. In die autem judicii, omnia ei subjicientur, quantum ad plenissimam exsecutionem. Loquendo autem de Christo secundum quod est mediator Dei ac hominum, sic omnia tradita sunt ei a Patre, id est omnia genera hominum salvandorum, seu omnes electi, qui per ipsum reducuntur ad Patrem. De quibus ait: Ego si exaltatus fuero a terra, omnia traham ad me ipsum; et, Nemo venit ad Patrem, nisi per me. Et item ad Patrem loquens: Dedisti (inquit) ei potestatem omnis carnis, ut omne quod dedisti ei, det eis vitam æternam.
paras.en: [[11:27|All things are delivered to me by my Father|Omnia mihi tradita sunt a Patre meo]]. In Christ there is a twofold nature. According to the divine nature, then, 'all things', that is, the whole fulness of the Godhead and whatever perfection is in the Father, 'are delivered', that is, are given to the Son by way of natural emanation, through eternal generation; as He Himself declares in John: [[John 16:15|All things whatsoever the Father hath are mine|Omnia (inquiens) quæcumque habet Pater, mea sunt]]; and again to the Father: [[John 17:10|all my things are thine, and thine are mine|Omnia (inquit) mea tua sunt, et tua mea sunt]]. From this it is known that all these things were so given to the Son that they remained in the Father, so that the same being and power in number is in both. And although in the Father there is no diversity but the most simple unity, the Son yet says in the plural, 'all things', since the Godhead of the Father comprehends the perfections of all things with infinite fulness. Hence Paul too says in the plural: [[Rom 1:20|the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made|Invisibilia Dei per ea quæ facta sunt intellecta, cognoscuntur]] [Denis's wording: 'are known, being understood']. Further, according to Christ's human nature, all created things were given and made subject to Him, as to authority, from the beginning of the incarnation[[Ps 8:8||]][[Heb 2:8||]]. For by the very fact that His humanity was united to the Word in the hypostatic union, it was set over every creature. For which reason it is said: [[John 3:35|The Father loveth the Son: and he hath given all things into his hand|Pater diligit Filium, et omnia dedit in manu ejus]]. But at the resurrection all things were given to Christ as man as to manifestation, because from then on the excellence of Christ began to be known and publicly preached. So below He says: [[Matt 28:18|All power is given to me in heaven and in earth|Data est (ait) mihi omnis potestas in cœlo et in terra]]. And on the day of judgement all things will be made subject to Him as to the fullest execution. But speaking of Christ as the mediator of God and men, all things were so delivered to Him by the Father, that is, all kinds of men to be saved, or all the elect, who are brought back to the Father through Him. Of whom He says: [[John 12:32|I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all things to myself|Ego si exaltatus fuero a terra, omnia traham ad me ipsum]]; and: [[John 14:6|No man cometh to the Father, but by me|Nemo venit ad Patrem, nisi per me]]. And again, speaking to the Father: [[John 17:2|thou hast given him power over all flesh, that he may give eternal life to all whom thou hast given him|Dedisti … ei potestatem omnis carnis … det eis vitam æternam]].

paras.t: Nemo, id est nullus seu nulla intelleciualis persona, novit Filium secundum ejus divinitatem, notitia comprehensionis j perfecta, nisi Pater æternus, qui æqualis est Filio in essendo et cognoscendo. Neque Patrem quis novit notitia plene comprehensionis, nisi Filius Patri æqualis, et cui voluerit Filius revelare per fidem in via, vel per speciem in patria, ut sunt homines electi, et angeli sancti. Non quod isti ex revelatione Christi agnoscant Patrem aut Filium modo prædicto, videlicet comprehensione plenaria: imo omnis intellectus creatus in infinitum distat, id est, occumbit et deficit, ab hujuscemodi notitia Dei immensi seu summæ Trinitatis atque cujuslibet divinæ Personæ. Quoniam sicut Deus est infinitæ actualitatis ac perfectionis, sic est infinitæ cognoscibilitatis: non ergo comprehenditur plene, nisi ab intellectu virtutis et capacitatis immensæ. Denique, per hoc quod dictum est, Nemo novit Filium nisi Pater, nec Patrem nisi Filius, non excluditur quin Filius cognoscat se ipsum, et Pater similiter, nec excluditur Spiritus Sanctus a notitia Patris et Filii: quia in his qui absolute dicuntur de Deo, quod de una Persona affirmatur, de qualibet trium vere accipitur. Unde Apostolus, dicens, Quæ Dei sunt, nullus novit nisi Spiritus ejus, non negat quin Pater et Filius cognoscant quæ Dei sunt. Patet quoque ex his, quod nulla divina Persona nec Trinitas cognita sit ex lumine naturali, sed ex revelatione supernaturali per fidem. Postremo, secundum principem theologorum in libro Mysticæ theologiæ, imo secundum theologos atque philosophos communiter et concorditer, perfectissima cognitio quæ haberi potest de Deo in via, est per meram ac puram ablationem seu negationem: ita ut uniamur Deo tanquam enti incomprehensibili et prorsus ignoto quantum ad quid est.
paras.en: [[11:27|And no one|Nemo]], that is, no intellectual person, [[11:27|knoweth the Son|novit Filium]] according to His Godhead with the perfect knowledge of comprehension, [[11:27|but the Father|nisi Pater]], the eternal Father, who is equal to the Son in being and knowing. [[11:27|neither doth any one know the Father|Neque Patrem quis novit]] with the knowledge of full comprehension, [[11:27|but the Son|nisi Filius]], who is equal to the Father, [[11:27|and he to whom it shall please the Son to reveal him|et cui voluerit Filius revelare]], by faith on the way, or by sight in the fatherland, such as are elect men and the holy angels. Not that these, by Christ's revelation, know the Father or the Son in the way just said, namely by full comprehension: nay, every created intellect is infinitely distant from, that is, falls short of and fails before, such knowledge of the immense God or of the supreme Trinity and of any divine Person. For as God is of infinite actuality and perfection, so He is of infinite knowability: so He is not comprehended fully except by an intellect of immense power and capacity. Further, by its being said, 'No one knoweth the Son but the Father, neither the Father but the Son', it is not excluded that the Son knows Himself, and the Father likewise, nor is the Holy Ghost excluded from the knowledge of the Father and the Son: because in what is said absolutely of God, what is affirmed of one Person is truly taken of each of the three. Hence the Apostle, saying, [[1 Cor 2:11|the things also that are of God, no man knoweth, but the Spirit of God|Quæ Dei sunt, nullus novit nisi Spiritus ejus]], does not deny that the Father and the Son know the things that are of God. It is clear also from this that no divine Person, nor the Trinity, is known by natural light, but by supernatural revelation through faith. Lastly, according to the prince of theologians in the book of Mystical Theology [Dionysius], nay according to theologians and philosophers commonly and with one accord, the most perfect knowledge of God that can be had on the way is by mere and pure removal, that is, negation: so that we are united to God as to a being incomprehensible and wholly unknown as to what He is.

paras.t: Et quia Salvator dixit sibi omnia tradita a Patre, et se Patrem perfecte cognoscere: ideo monet nos ut confidenter accedamus ad ipsum, quemadmodum Salvator ipse testatur: Eum, inquiens, qui venit ad me, non ejiciam foras. Venite ad me spirituali accessu seu mentis conversione: juxta illud Prophetæ, Venite, et revertamur ad Dominum; et rursus, Convertimini ad me in toto corde vestro. Unde et Jacobus dicit: Appropinquate Deo, et appropinquabit vobis. Hoc est: ab istis caducis, terrenis et vanis, avertite corda vestra, et ad summum bonum dirigite ea, totumque affectum vestrum et cogitatum in Christo stabilire satagite: sicut ait Psalmista, Deus cordis mei, et pars mea Deus in æternum. Omnes qui laboratis in via hujus exsilii. Homo enim ad laborem nascitur, et avis ad volatum. Quidam enim laborant in operibus pœnitentiæ, quidam in opere manuum, quidam in diversis languoribus, quidam in actibus vitiosis, prout apud Sapientem deplorant, dicentes: Lassati sumus in via iniquitatis. Quocumque ergo labore laboremus, accedamus ad Christum, malos labores dimittendo, et bonos continuando, vel in melius transferendo, eundo videlicet de labore actionis ad quietem contemplationis. Et onerati estis malis culpæ et pœna, seu onere observantiarum legalium, quod Petro teste, importabile fuit. Est autem onus quoddam grave, universis commune, ex originali peccato secutum, de quo in Ecclesiastico legitur: Occupatio magna creata est omnibus hominibus, et jugum grave super omnes filios Adam, a die exitus de ventre matris eorum, usque in diem sepulturæ in matrem omnium. Propter quod ait beatus Job: Homo natus de muliere, brevi vivens tempore, repletur multis miseriis.
paras.en: And since the Saviour said that all things were delivered to Him by the Father, and that He knows the Father perfectly, He therefore admonishes us to come to Him with confidence, as the Saviour Himself testifies, saying: [[John 6:37|him that cometh to me, I will not cast out|Eum, inquiens, qui venit ad me, non ejiciam foras]]. [[11:28|Come to me|Venite ad me]] by spiritual approach, that is, by turning of the mind; according to that of the Prophet: [[Osee 6:1|Come, and let us return to the Lord|Venite, et revertamur ad Dominum]]; and again: [[Joel 2:12|Be converted to me with all your heart|Convertimini ad me in toto corde vestro]]. Hence James too says: [[Jas 4:8|Draw nigh to God: and he will draw nigh to you|Appropinquate Deo, et appropinquabit vobis]]. That is: turn your hearts away from these perishable, earthly and vain things, and direct them to the highest good, and strive to settle all your affection and thought in Christ; as the Psalmist says: [[Ps 72:26|thou art the God of my heart, and the God that is my portion for ever|Deus cordis mei, et pars mea Deus in æternum]]. [[11:28|all you that labor|Omnes qui laboratis]] on the way of this exile. For [[Job 5:7|Man is born to labour, and the bird to fly|Homo enim ad laborem nascitur, et avis ad volatum]]. For some labour in works of penance, some in the work of their hands, some in various sicknesses, some in sinful acts, as in the Wise Man they lament, saying: [[Wis 5:7|We wearied ourselves in the way of iniquity|Lassati sumus in via iniquitatis]]. With whatever labour, then, we labour, let us come to Christ, leaving off bad labours and continuing good ones, or changing them for the better, namely by passing from the labour of action to the rest of contemplation. [[11:28|and are burdened|Et onerati estis]] with evils of guilt and punishment, or with the burden of the observances of the law, which, as Peter witnesses, was unbearable[[Acts 15:10||]]. And there is a certain heavy burden, common to all, that followed from original sin, of which we read in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 40:1|Great labour is created for all men, and a heavy yoke is upon the children of Adam from the day of their coming out of their mother's womb, until the day of their burial into the mother of all|Occupatio magna creata est omnibus hominibus, et jugum grave super omnes filios Adam, a die exitus de ventre matris eorum, usque in diem sepulturæ in matrem omnium]]. For which reason blessed Job says: [[Job 14:1|Man born of a woman, living for a short time, is filled with many miseries|Homo natus de muliere, brevi vivens tempore, repletur multis miseriis]].

paras.t: Et ego reficiam vos, id est, confortabo et consolabor vos, minuendo gravitatem laboris, ut opera bona quæ cum difficultate tædioque fecistis, cum fervore et gaudio facere inchoetis: sicut ait Propheta, Viam mandatorum tuorum cucurri quum dilatasti cor meum. Hinc Salvator inquit: Qui sitit, veniat ad me et bibat; et in Apocalypsi, Ego sitienti dabo de fonte aquæ vitæ gratis. Sic refecta fuit Sponsa, quæ ait in Canticis: Introduxit me rex in cellam vinariam. Hæc refectio inchoatur in via per gratiam, et consummatur in regno per gloriam.
paras.en: [[11:28|and I will refresh you|Et ego reficiam vos]], that is, I will strengthen and console you, lessening the weight of the labour, so that the good works you did with difficulty and weariness you may begin to do with fervour and joy; as the Prophet says: [[Ps 118:32|I have run the way of thy commandments, when thou didst enlarge my heart|Viam mandatorum tuorum cucurri quum dilatasti cor meum]]. Hence the Saviour says: [[John 7:37|If any man thirst, let him come to me and drink|Qui sitit, veniat ad me et bibat]]; and in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 21:6|To him that thirsteth, I will give of the fountain of the water of life, freely|Ego sitienti dabo de fonte aquæ vitæ gratis]]. So was the Bride refreshed, who says in the Canticles: [[Cant 2:4|He brought me into the cellar of wine|Introduxit me rex in cellam vinariam]] [Denis reads 'the king brought me']. This refreshment is begun on the way by grace, and completed in the kingdom by glory.

paras.t: Tollite jugum meum super vos, id est, præceptis meis subjicite vosmetipsos, et evangelicam legem servate. Unde inobedienti populo dicit Dominus per Jeremiam: A sæculo, inquiens, confregisti jugum, rupisti vincula mea, et dixisti, Non serviam. Et discite a me, non miracula facere, non mundum creare, sed quia mitis sum, inordinationem iræ et impatientiæ penitus non habendo. Mititas quippe seu mansuetudo, proprie dicitur virtus moralis iram refrenans. Mitis utique, imo mitissimus exstitit Christus, qui tanquam ovis ad occisionem ductus est, et quasi agnus coram tondente obmutuit. Et humilis corde: quia quidquid ago, ad gloriam Patris refero, et ei omne bonum adscribo, nullum contemno, claritatem ab hominibus non accipio; in medio discipulorum fui sicut qui ministrat, pedes eorum lavi, in omnibus me ipsum humilitatis exemplum præbui. Et invenietis requiem animabus vestris, id est, in me dulciter quiescetis, motibus iræ atque superbiæ mitigatis. Qui enim mitis et humilis est, ad contemplationem et stabilitatem mentis aptissimus est, et delectatur in multitudine pacis. Hinc Jeremias ait: Interrogate quæ sit via bona, et ambulate in ea, et invenietis requiem animabus vestris. Hæc requies perficietur et plena erit in patria. Non enim perfecte quietatur cor nostrum, nisi summo bono fuerit immediate seu fruitive conjunctum. Ideo dicit Psalmista: Convertere, anima mea, in requiem tuam.
paras.en: [[11:29|Take up my yoke upon you|Tollite jugum meum super vos]], that is, subject yourselves to My precepts and keep the Gospel law. Hence the Lord says to the disobedient people through Jeremias: [[Jer 2:20|Of old time thou hast broken my yoke, thou hast burst my bands, and thou saidst: I will not serve|A sæculo, inquiens, confregisti jugum, rupisti vincula mea, et dixisti, Non serviam]]. [[11:29|and learn of me|Et discite a me]], not to work miracles, not to create the world, but [[11:29|because I am meek|quia mitis sum]], having no disorder of anger or impatience at all. For mildness, or meekness, is properly called the moral virtue that bridles anger. Meek indeed, nay most meek, was Christ, who [[Is 53:7|shall be led as a sheep to the slaughter, and shall be dumb as a lamb before his shearer|tanquam ovis ad occisionem ductus est, et quasi agnus coram tondente obmutuit]]. [[11:29|and humble of heart|Et humilis corde]]: because whatever I do I refer to the glory of the Father, and ascribe every good to Him[[John 8:50||]]; I despise no one; [[John 5:41|I receive not glory from men|claritatem ab hominibus non accipio]]; in the midst of the disciples I was [[Luke 22:27|as he that serveth|sicut qui ministrat]]; I washed their feet[[John 13:5||]]; in all things I gave Myself as an example of humility. [[11:29|And you shall find rest to your souls|Et invenietis requiem animabus vestris]], that is, you will rest sweetly in Me, the motions of anger and pride being calmed. For he who is meek and humble is most fit for contemplation and stability of mind, and [[Ps 36:11|shall delight in abundance of peace|delectatur in multitudine pacis]]. Hence Jeremias says: [[Jer 6:16|ask for the old paths, which is the good way, and walk ye in it: and you shall find refreshment for your souls|Interrogate quæ sit via bona, et ambulate in ea, et invenietis requiem animabus vestris]]. This rest will be perfected and full in the fatherland. For our heart does not rest perfectly unless it is joined to the highest good immediately, that is, by enjoyment. Therefore the Psalmist says: [[Ps 114:7|Turn, O my soul, into thy rest|Convertere, anima mea, in requiem tuam]].

paras.t: Jugum enim meum, id est observatio præceptorum, suave est diligenti: quoniam nulla forma delectabilius vel facilius agit quam caritas. Ideo ait Scriptura: Judicia Domini (id est præcepta) vera, justificata in semetipsa; desiderabilia super aurum, et dulciora super mel et favum: etenim servus tuus custodit ea. Et onus meum leve est, scilicet observatio consiliorum, quæ sicut pigro et frigido exstat gravissima, sic fervido amatori levissima est atque dulcissima, ita ut dicat: Quam dulcia faucibus meis eloquia tua! et, Non sunt condigna passiones hujus temporis ad futuram gloriam.
paras.en: [[11:30|For my yoke|Jugum enim meum]], that is, the keeping of the precepts, [[11:30|is sweet|suave est]] to him who loves: since no form acts more delightfully or more easily than charity. Therefore Scripture says: [[Ps 18:10|the judgments of the Lord are true, justified in themselves|judicia Domini vera, justificata in semetipsa]] (judgements, that is, precepts); [[Ps 18:11|More to be desired than gold and many precious stones: and sweeter than honey and the honeycomb|desiderabilia super aurum, et dulciora super mel et favum]]. [[Ps 18:12|For thy servant keepeth them|etenim servus tuus custodit ea]]. [[11:30|and my burden light|Et onus meum leve est]], namely the keeping of the counsels, which, as it seems most heavy to the slothful and cold, so is most light and most sweet to the fervent lover, so that he says: [[Ps 118:103|How sweet are thy words to my palate!|Quam dulcia faucibus meis eloquia tua!]] and: [[Rom 8:18|the sufferings of this time are not worthy to be compared with the glory to come|Non sunt condignæ passiones hujus temporis ad futuram gloriam]].

paras.t: Quæritur, si jugum Christi suave est et onus ejus leve, quomodo ait, Intrate per angustam portam; et, Arcta est via quæ ducit ad vitam; itemque, Regnum cœlorum vim patitur, et violenti rapiunt illud? Et respondendum, quod unum et idem est angustum, laboriosum et grave, incipienti, imperfecto et spiritualem consolationem nondum experto; quod tamen lætum, jucundum et leve est, exercitato, proficienti, perfecto et habituato in bonis. Denique mandata atque consilia Christi ex sua natura dulcia exstant et levia, quamvis per comparationem ad nostram fragilitatem et pronitatem in malum, difficulter in principio impleantur.
paras.en: It is asked: if Christ's yoke is sweet and His burden light, how does He say, [[Matt 7:13|Enter ye in at the narrow gate|Intrate per angustam portam]]; and, [[Matt 7:14|strait is the way that leadeth to life|Arcta est via quæ ducit ad vitam]]; and likewise, [[11:12|the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent bear it away|Regnum cœlorum vim patitur, et violenti rapiunt illud]]? And it must be answered that one and the same thing is narrow, laborious and heavy to the beginner, the imperfect, and one who has not yet tasted spiritual consolation; which yet is glad, pleasant and light to the practised, the proficient, the perfect, and one settled in good habits. Lastly, the commandments and counsels of Christ are of their nature sweet and light, though in comparison with our frailty and proneness to evil they are hard to fulfil at the beginning.

paras.t: Quæritur etiam, an jugum Christi seu evangelica lex, gravior sit ad observandum, quam lex Mosaica. Et videtur quod imo: quia quo perfectio major, eo ad eam difficilius homo pertingit. Major est autem perfectio novæ legis quam veteris. Item superius patuit, quomodo præceptis legis Christus sua majora præcepta adjecit, prohibens irasci, et dicere, Raca, aut, Fatue: quod difficillimum est implere. Gregorius quoque aperte affirmat hoc ipsum. Sed, si ita est, non videtur quomodo jugum Christi sit suave, et onus ipsius leve. Et respondendum, quod in veteri lege erant præcepta triplicia, puta moralia, judicialia, ac cæremonialia. Si ergo loquamur de veteri lege quoad præcepta ejus cæremonialia, constat quod difficilius fuit eam servare, quam novam legem. Unde in Actibus Petrus dicit: Quid tentatis imponere jugum super cervicem discipulorum, quod neque nos neque patres nostri portare potuimus? Quod intelligitur de cæremonialibus legis. Præcepta vero moralia utriusque legis sunt eadem: qua tamen nunc facilius implentur quam tunc, propter magnitudinem gratiæ quæ confertur in nova lege per sacramenta Ecclesiæ. Consilia vero Christi difficiliora sunt quam przcepta moralia legis, per comparationem ad nostram infirmitatem; sed per comparationem ad gratiam, quæ adjuvat nostram imbecillitatem, etiam ipsa consilia facillime adimplentur. Hanc quæstionem non intendo hoc loco plenius prosequi, sed sic eam tetigisse sufficiat.
paras.en: It is asked also whether the yoke of Christ, that is, the Gospel law, is heavier to keep than the law of Moses. And it seems that it is: because the greater the perfection, the harder it is for a man to reach it; and the perfection of the new law is greater than that of the old. Again, it appeared above how Christ added His greater precepts to the precepts of the law, forbidding anger and saying 'Raca' or 'Thou fool'[[Matt 5:22||]], which is most difficult to fulfil. Gregory too plainly affirms this very thing. But if it is so, it is not clear how Christ's yoke is sweet and His burden light. And it must be answered that in the old law there were three kinds of precepts, namely moral, judicial and ceremonial. If then we speak of the old law as to its ceremonial precepts, it is certain that it was harder to keep than the new law. Hence in the Acts Peter says: [[Acts 15:10|why tempt you God to put a yoke upon the necks of the disciples which neither our fathers nor we have been able to bear?|Quid tentatis imponere jugum super cervicem discipulorum, quod neque nos neque patres nostri portare potuimus?]] Which is understood of the ceremonies of the law. But the moral precepts of both laws are the same: yet they are fulfilled more easily now than then, because of the greatness of the grace conferred in the new law through the sacraments of the Church. And the counsels of Christ are harder than the moral precepts of the law in comparison with our weakness; but in comparison with the grace that [[Rom 8:26|helpeth our infirmity|adjuvat nostram imbecillitatem]], even the counsels themselves are fulfilled most easily. I do not mean to pursue this question more fully in this place; let it suffice to have touched on it thus.

paras.t: Hoc vero summe requiritur, et maxime admonendum est, ut discamus a Magistro nostro (in quo sunt omnes thesauri sapientiæ et scienti? absconditi, imo qui est sapientia Patris) veram mansuetudinem, et humilitatem sinceram, quoniam hæ duæ virtutes præcipue faciunt hominem tam Deo quam proximis suis amabilem, fratribus exemplarem, laudabilem, dulcem, solatiosumque omnibus. Scriptum est enim: Deus superbis resistit, humilibus autem dat gratiam; et iterum, Odibilis coram Deo et hominibus est superbia; et rursus, In mansuetudine opera tua fac, et super omnem hominum gloriam diligeris. Unde Leo Papa optime dicit: Tota christianæ sapientiæ disciplina, non in abundantia verbi, non in astutia disputandi, non in appetitu laudis et gloriæ, sed in vera et voluntaria humilitate consistit, quam Dominus Jesus ab utero matris usque ad supplicium erueis, pro omni fortitudine elegit et docuit. Et denuo: Tota, inquit, victoria Salvatoris, qua et diabolum stravit et mundum, humilitate est concepta, humilitate confecta.
paras.en: But this is required above all, and must most of all be urged: that we learn from our Master ([[Col 2:3|In whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge|in quo sunt omnes thesauri sapientiæ et scientiæ absconditi]], nay who is the Wisdom of the Father[[1 Cor 1:24||]]) true meekness and sincere humility, since these two virtues above all make a man lovable to God and to his neighbours, an example to his brethren, praiseworthy, sweet and a comfort to all. For it is written: [[Jas 4:6|God resisteth the proud and giveth grace to the humble|Deus superbis resistit, humilibus autem dat gratiam]]; and again: [[Ecclus 10:7|Pride is hateful before God and men|Odibilis coram Deo et hominibus est superbia]]; and further: [[Ecclus 3:19|do thy works in meekness, and thou shalt be beloved above the glory of men|In mansuetudine opera tua fac, et super omnem hominum gloriam diligeris]]. Hence Pope Leo says excellently: The whole discipline of Christian wisdom consists not in abundance of words, not in cleverness of disputing, not in the desire of praise and glory, but in true and willing humility, which the Lord Jesus, from His mother's womb to the punishment of the cross, chose and taught in place of all strength. And again: The whole victory of the Saviour, by which He overthrew both the devil and the world, was conceived in humility and accomplished in humility.

12.title: Explanatio capituli duodecimi: In illo tempore, abiit Jesus sabbato per sata
12.title_en: Explanation of the twelfth chapter: “At that time Jesus went through the corn on the sabbath”

paras.t: In illo tempore, quum dicta et facta sunt præinducta, abiit Jesus sabbato, id est septima die hebdomadis, qui celebris fuit apud Judæos, per sata, id est per fruges seu segetes agri. Discipuli autem ejus euntes secum per sata, esurientes. Sæpius enim, ut Marcus testatur, non habebant manducandi spatium, propter turbam concurrentem. Interdum etiam voluit Christus ut aliquam paterentur inopiam. Cœperunt vellere, id est extrahere, spicas, et manducare grana inclusa, spicis manibus confricatis. Pharisæi autem videntes hoc, dixerunt ei, videlicet Christo. Lucas refert, quod Pharisæi dixerunt discipulis; sed non est contrarietas. Poterant enim tam Christo quam ejus discipulis, dicere quæ sequuntur. Vel quidam eorum dixerunt hæc Christo, alii ejus discipulis. Unde in Luca notanter scriptum est, quod quidam Pharisæorum dicebant discipulis ejus. Dixerunt ergo Magistro, in quem culpam discipulorum retorquere conati sunt. Dixerunt autem, non zelo justitiæ, sed rancoris affectu: Ecce discipuli tui faciunt quod non licet eis facere sabbatis, scilicet spicas vellere et confricare. Moyses enim præcepit in Exodo, ut filii Israel præpararent cibaria, non in sabbato, sed in die præcedenti.
paras.en: [[12:1|At that time|In illo tempore]], when the things already brought forward had been said and done, [[12:1|Jesus went|abiit Jesus]] [[12:1|on the sabbath|sabbato]], that is, the seventh day of the week, which was a feast among the Jews, [[12:1|through the corn|per sata]], that is, through the crops or standing corn of the field. [[12:1|and his disciples|Discipuli autem ejus]], going with Him through the corn, [[12:1|being hungry|esurientes]]. For often, as Mark testifies, [[Mark 6:31|they had not so much as time to eat|non habebant manducandi spatium]], because of the crowd flocking together. And sometimes Christ also willed that they should suffer some want. [[12:1|began to pluck the ears|cœperunt vellere spicas]], that is, to pull them out, [[12:1|and to eat|et manducare]] the grain enclosed in them, rubbing the ears in their hands. [[12:2|And the Pharisees seeing them, said to him|Pharisæi autem videntes hoc, dixerunt ei]], that is, to Christ. Luke relates that the Pharisees spoke to the disciples[[Luke 6:2||]]; but there is no contradiction. For they could say what follows both to Christ and to His disciples. Or some of them said this to Christ, others to His disciples. Hence in Luke it is pointedly written that [[Luke 6:2|some of the Pharisees said to them|quidam Pharisæorum dicebant]]. So they spoke to the Master, on whom they tried to turn back the fault of the disciples. And they spoke not from zeal for justice but from a feeling of rancour: [[12:2|Behold thy disciples do that which is not lawful to do on the sabbath days|Ecce discipuli tui faciunt quod non licet eis facere sabbatis]], namely to pluck and rub ears of corn. For Moses commanded in Exodus that the children of Israel should prepare their food, not on the sabbath, but on the day before[[Ex 16:23||]].

paras.t: At ille, videlicet Christus, dixit eis, excusando discipulos suos, et quodammodo exponendo præceptum: Non legistis (primo Regum): quod utique legistis, vel legere aut scire debuistis; quid fecerit David, quando esuriit, fugiens a facie Saul, et qui cum eo erant, hoc est, quid fecerint viri, seu servi vel pueri ejus? Quomodo intravit in domum Dei, id est tabernaculum Domini, in Nobe urbe sacerdotum, et panes propositionis, id est panes qui die sabbati ponebantur calidi super mensam in tabernaculo, pro usu sacerdotum, comedit, tam ipse quam socii ejus necessitate famis compulsi: quos dedit ei Achimelech pontifex, quoniam panes laicos non habebat ad manum; quos panes non licebat ei, id est ipsi David, edere, extra necessitatis articulum, seu aliis horis, neque his qui cum eo erant, nisi solis sacerdotibus. Si ergo David et sui ac pontifex excusantur a transgressione legis propter famis necessitatem, cur non simili ratione excusantur discipuli mei? Præcepta enim illa intelligenda non erant in articulo necessitatis, sed dispensationem et expositionem admittebant. Necessitas vero est mater dispensationis, secundum quod ait ad Eugenium Papam S. Bernardus: Non sum tam rudis, ut ignorem vos dispensatores esse positos, sed in ædificationem, non in destructionem. Ubi ergo urget necessitas, excusabilis est dispensatio. Ubi utilitas provocat, laudabilis est dispensatio: utilitas, inquam, communis, non propria.
paras.en: [[12:3|But he said to them|At ille, videlicet Christus, dixit eis]], namely Christ, excusing His disciples and in a manner expounding the precept: [[12:3|Have you not read|Non legistis]] (in the first book of Kings[[1 Kings 21:6||]]), which surely you have read, or ought to have read or known, [[12:3|what David did when he was hungry|quid fecerit David, quando esuriit]], fleeing from the face of Saul, [[12:3|and they that were with him|et qui cum eo erant]], that is, what his men, or servants or young men, did? [[12:4|How he entered into the house of God|Quomodo intravit in domum Dei]], that is, the tabernacle of the Lord, in Nobe, the city of the priests, [[12:4|and did eat the loaves of proposition|et panes propositionis comedit]], that is, the loaves that were set hot on the table in the tabernacle on the sabbath day for the use of the priests[[Lev 24:9||]], both he and his companions, driven by the need of hunger: which Achimelech the high priest gave him, since he had no common bread at hand; [[12:4|which it was not lawful for him to eat|quos panes non licebat ei, id est ipsi David, edere]], that is, for David himself, outside the extremity of need, or at other times, [[12:4|nor for them that were with him, but for the priests only|neque his qui cum eo erant, nisi solis sacerdotibus]]. If then David and his men and the high priest are excused from transgressing the law because of the need of hunger, why are not My disciples excused for a like reason? For those precepts were not to be understood as binding in the extremity of need, but admitted dispensation and interpretation. And necessity is the mother of dispensation, according to what St Bernard says to Pope Eugene: I am not so untaught as not to know that you have been set as dispensers, but for edification, not for destruction. Where, then, necessity presses, dispensation is excusable; where utility calls for it, dispensation is praiseworthy: utility, I mean, that is common, not private.

paras.t: Denique Pharisæi non reprehendebant discipulos Christi, de hoc quod spicas vellebant et manducabant (quia hoc licuit eis, juxta illud quod in Deuteronomio scriptum est: Si intraveris segetem amici tui, franges spicas, et manu conteres; falce autem non metes); sed quod fecerunt hoc sabbato.
paras.en: Moreover, the Pharisees did not blame Christ's disciples for plucking and eating the ears (for this was lawful for them, according to what is written in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 23:25|If thou go into thy friend's corn, thou mayst break the ears, and rub them in thy hand: but not reap them with a sickle|Si intraveris segetem amici tui, franges spicas, et manu conteres; falce autem non metes]]); but because they did this on the sabbath.

paras.t: Consequenter excusat Christus suos discipulos alia ratione, videlicet, quia de ejus licentia ista fecerunt: ipse autem vim dispensandi se habere testatur. An non legistis in lege, videlicet in libris Moysis, quia sabbatis, hoc est diebus sabbatorum sacerdotes legales in templo sabbatum violant, id est, sabbati celebrationem non servant, quantum ad verba præcepti, sed manualiter operantur, animalia Deo immolando et ea excoriando, hostiasque lavando, et sine crimine sunt, hoc est sine transgressione præcepti? quia non agunt contra intentionem præcepti, quoniam opera illa directe ordinabantur ad cultum divinum et Deo jubente fiebant in sabbato. Dico autem vobis, quia templo major est hic, locus in quo ego sum (sic exponit Hieronymus): quoniam locus continens Christum dignior fuit templo. Vel, Hic, id est ego Christus, major seu dignior sum templo, quum sim Dominus templi. Ideo mea auctoritate potest hic fieri a discipulis meis, quod fit in templo a sacerdotibus.
paras.en: Next Christ excuses His disciples for another reason, namely because they did these things by His leave; and He testifies that He has the power of dispensing. [[12:5|Or have ye not read in the law|An non legistis in lege]], namely in the books of Moses, [[12:5|that on the sabbath days|quia sabbatis]], that is, on the days of the sabbaths, [[12:5|the priests in the temple break the sabbath|sacerdotes legales in templo sabbatum violant]], the priests of the law, that is, do not keep the observance of the sabbath as to the words of the precept, but work with their hands, sacrificing animals to God and flaying them and washing the victims, [[12:5|and are without blame|et sine crimine sunt]], that is, without transgression of the precept? Because they do not act against the intention of the precept, since those works were ordered directly to the worship of God and were done on the sabbath at God's command. [[12:6|But I tell you that there is here a greater than the temple|Dico autem vobis, quia templo major est hic]]: the place in which I am (so Jerome expounds), since the place containing Christ was worthier than the temple. Or, 'here', that is, I, Christ, am greater or worthier than the temple, since I am the Lord of the temple. Therefore by My authority My disciples may do here what is done in the temple by the priests.

paras.t: Si autem sciretis, hoc est, perfecte intelligeretis, quid est, id est, quid significet illud Oseæ prophetæ: Misericordiam, id est opera pietatis, et affectum compassionis, volo ego Dominus, et non sacrificium, hoc est plus quam legalem hostiam: nunquam condemnassetis, id est, præcepti prævaricatores judicassetis, innocentes discipulos meos; sed opera misericordiæ sacrificiis templi præponendo, condoluissetis discipulis meis necessitate famis spicas vellentibus, et excusassetis eosdem. Quod autem Christus potestatem habuerit dispensandi de observatione sabbati, declaratur subdendo: Dominus est enim Filius hominis, scilicet Christus, qui propter humilitatem frequenter se nominat Filium hominis, raro Filium Dei, etiam sabbati, id est septimi diei, et per consequens aliorum dierum, totiusque temporis. Ex quo ostenditur, quod Christus sit verus Deus, cui proprium est temporibus præesse ac dominari. Unde in nova lege, Christi auctoritate celebritas sabbati cessavit, et prima feria facta est celebris. Eadem auctoritate discipuli spicas sabbato vellere poterant, eundo per sata seu blada.
paras.en: [[12:7|And if you knew|Si autem sciretis]], that is, understood perfectly, [[12:7|what this meaneth|quid est]], that is, what that saying of the prophet Osee signifies[[Osee 6:6||]]: [[12:7|I will have mercy|Misericordiam volo]], that is, works of piety and the feeling of compassion I, the Lord, will, [[12:7|and not sacrifice|et non sacrificium]], that is, more than the victim of the law: [[12:7|you would never have condemned|nunquam condemnassetis]], that is, judged as transgressors of the precept, [[12:7|the innocent|innocentes]], My innocent disciples; but setting works of mercy before the sacrifices of the temple, you would have had compassion on My disciples plucking the ears from the need of hunger, and would have excused them. And that Christ had the power of dispensing from the observance of the sabbath is declared by what is added: [[12:8|For the Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath|Dominus est enim Filius hominis, scilicet Christus, qui propter humilitatem frequenter se nominat Filium hominis, raro Filium Dei, etiam sabbati]], namely Christ, who out of humility often calls Himself the Son of man, rarely the Son of God; that is, of the seventh day, and consequently of the other days and of all time. From which it is shown that Christ is true God, to whom it belongs to be over the times and to rule them. Hence in the new law, by Christ's authority, the feast of the sabbath ceased and the first day of the week was made a feast. By the same authority the disciples could pluck ears on the sabbath, going through the corn or crops.

paras.t: Et quum inde, id est a campo seu agro, ubi hæc contigerunt, transisset Jesus, venit in synagogam eorum, videlicet Pharisæorum a quibus fuerat redargutus, vel aliorum Judæorum. Et ecce homo manum habens aridam, id est contractam, erat ibi in synagoga; et interrogabant Pharisæi eum, dicentes: Si, id est an, licet sabbatis curare, id est infirmum sanare? ut accusarent eum, quomodocumque responderet aut faceret. Quoniam enim Christus discipulos suos excusavit, et misericordiam sacrificio prætulit, Pharisæi insidiari cœperunt Magistro, inquirentes an liceret sabbato sanare: ut si Christus diceret, Imo, arguerent eum de sabbati transgressione; si diceret, Non, arguerent eum de immisericordia seu crudelitate, vel etiam de impotentia, si non curaret. Scriptum est in Luca et Marco, quod Jesus interrogavit Pharisæos, An licet sabbato curare? Hic dicitur, quod illi interrogaverunt eum: et utrumque verum est. Ipsi namque primo interrogaverunt Jesum de hoc, dolose ac insidiose; deinde Christus jussit hominem illum in medio stare: quo stante, Christus quæstionem illorum repetiit, ut eis convenientius responderet.
paras.en: [[12:9|And when he had passed from thence|Et quum inde, id est a campo seu agro, ubi hæc contigerunt, transisset Jesus]], that is, from the field or land where these things happened, [[12:9|he came into their synagogues|venit in synagogam eorum]], namely of the Pharisees by whom He had been reproved, or of other Jews. [[12:10|And behold there was a man who had a withered hand|Et ecce homo manum habens aridam, id est contractam, erat]], that is, shrunken, there in the synagogue; [[12:10|and they asked him, saying|et interrogabant eum, dicentes]], the Pharisees: [[12:10|Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath days?|Si licet sabbatis curare?]] 'If', that is, whether; 'to heal', that is, to make the sick whole; [[12:10|that they might accuse him|ut accusarent eum]], however He might answer or act. For since Christ had excused His disciples and set mercy before sacrifice, the Pharisees began to lay snares for the Master, asking whether it was lawful to heal on the sabbath: so that if Christ said Yes, they might accuse Him of transgressing the sabbath; if He said No, they might accuse Him of mercilessness or cruelty, or even of powerlessness, if He did not cure. It is written in Luke and Mark that Jesus asked the Pharisees, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath[[Luke 6:9||]][[Mark 3:4||]]? Here it is said that they asked Him: and both are true. For they first asked Jesus about this, craftily and with intent to ensnare; then Christ ordered that man to stand in the midst; and when he stood there, Christ repeated their question, so as to answer them more fittingly.

paras.t: Ipse autem dicit illis, proprie quæstioni respondendo, quoniam ipsi respondere non poterant, vel nolebant. Seeundum Marcum, Jesus circumspexit eos cum ira, contristatus super cæcitate cordis eorum. Probat itaque Christus quod liceat sabbato hominem reparare et confortare, per locum a minori vel majori, eo quod liceat in die sabbati, bruto succurrere. Quis erit ex vobis homo rationabiliter judicans, rationemque sequens, qui habeat ovem unam, et si ceciderit hæc sabbatis in foveam, nonne tenebit et levabit eam de fovea sabbato? Quanto magis melior est homo summæ Trinitatis imagine insignitus, ove, et a qualibet irrationali creatura? id est, quanto homo per naturam et gratiam, dignior est ove, tanto convenientius est hominem sabbato curare, quam ovem de lacu levare. Itaque licet sabbatis benefacere, id est opera pietatis et actus virtutum exercere. Judæi vero male intelligebant præceptum de sabbati celebratione, putantes quemlibet actum exteriorem illicitum sabbato, quum tamen Moyses notanter præceperit: Omne opus servile non facietis in eo. Et potest per opus servile intelligi quælibet operatio non habens bonitatem ex sua ratione in genere moris, ut arare, ædificare: tales actus illiciti erant in sabbato. Actus vero ex se boni in genere moris, liciti erant, ut sanare infirmum ex caritate et misericordia, et præsertim quando hoc fit miraculose. Hinc etiam licuit sabbato se defendere, et vim vi repellere. Quod ignorantes quidam Judæi, permiserunt se occidi a gentibus, ut legitur in libris Machabæorum.
paras.en: [[12:11|But he said to them|Ipse autem dicit illis]], answering their question Himself, since they could not or would not answer. According to Mark, Jesus [[Mark 3:5|looking round about on them with anger, being grieved for the blindness of their hearts|circumspexit eos cum ira, contristatus super cæcitate cordis eorum]]. So Christ proves that it is lawful to restore and strengthen a man on the sabbath by an argument from the less or the greater, in that it is lawful to help a beast on the sabbath day. [[12:11|What man shall there be among you|Quis erit ex vobis homo]], judging reasonably and following reason, [[12:11|that hath one sheep: and if the same fall into a pit on the sabbath day, will he not take hold on it and lift it up?|qui habeat ovem unam, et si ceciderit hæc sabbatis in foveam, nonne tenebit et levabit eam]] from the pit on the sabbath? [[12:12|How much better is a man than a sheep?|Quanto magis melior est homo ove?]] a man marked with the image of the supreme Trinity, than a sheep or any irrational creature? That is, as much as a man by nature and grace is worthier than a sheep, so much more fitting is it to cure a man on the sabbath than to lift a sheep out of a pit. [[12:12|Therefore it is lawful to do a good deed on the sabbath days|Itaque licet sabbatis benefacere]], that is, to do works of piety and acts of virtue. But the Jews misunderstood the precept about keeping the sabbath, thinking any outward act unlawful on the sabbath, though Moses pointedly commanded: [[Lev 23:36|You shall do no servile work therein|Omne opus servile non facietis in eo]][[Num 29:35||]]. And by servile work may be understood any work that has no goodness of its own nature in the moral order, such as ploughing or building: such acts were unlawful on the sabbath. But acts good in themselves in the moral order were lawful, such as healing the sick out of charity and mercy, and especially when this is done miraculously. Hence too it was lawful to defend oneself on the sabbath and to repel force by force. Not knowing this, certain Jews let themselves be killed by the Gentiles, as we read in the books of Machabees[[1 Mach 2:38||]].

paras.t: Tunc Jesus ait homini contractam manum habenti: Extende manum tuam arefactam. Et extendit eam, non naturali, sed divina virtute, quia vis motiva impedita erat per defectionem spirituum; et restituta est sanitati manus contracta, in illo momento quo dixerat Jesus, Extende manum tuam. In quo patet efficacia potestatis divinæ, in instanti agentis. Quamvis enim sæpe per naturam et artis operationem, contractus curetur, non tamen in instanti, vel solo imperio. Natura enim et ars operantur successive, non subito. Non autem potuit manus arida extendi, nisi prius sanaretur. Restituta est ergo sanitati, sicut altera, id est sinistra (quia secundum Lucam, dextera fuit contracta): non quod sinistra restituta sit sanitati; sed dextera restituta est sanitati, id est, sana effecta est, sicut sinistra sana fuit. Porro moraliter, per hominem habentem manum aridam, et hanc dexteram, intelligitur quilibet piger, acediosus, sive peccator, qui negligit operari quæ Dei sunt. Unde de negligente pastore scriptum est: Brachium ejus ariditate siccabitur. Huic præcipit Christus, ut surgat a culpa, per pœnitentiam; stet in medio, per exemplarem conversationem; manum quoque extendat, per operum misericordiæ exhibitionem.
paras.en: [[12:13|Then he saith to the man|Tunc Jesus ait homini]] with the shrunken hand: [[12:13|Stretch forth thy hand|Extende manum tuam]], your withered hand. [[12:13|and he stretched it forth|Et extendit]], not by natural but by divine power, since the power of movement was hindered by the failure of the spirits; [[12:13|and it was restored to health|et restituta est sanitati]], the shrunken hand, in that moment in which Jesus said, Stretch forth thy hand. In which the efficacy of the divine power, acting in an instant, is plain. For although a contracted limb is often cured by nature and the working of art, it is not done in an instant, nor by command alone. For nature and art work successively, not suddenly. And the withered hand could not be stretched out unless it were first healed. So it was restored to health, [[12:13|even as the other|sicut altera]], that is, the left (since according to Luke it was the right hand that was shrunken[[Luke 6:6||]]): not that the left was restored to health, but the right was restored to health, that is, was made sound, as the left was sound. Moreover, morally, by the man with the withered hand, and that his right, is understood every slothful, listless man, or sinner, who neglects to do the things of God. Hence of the negligent shepherd it is written: [[Zach 11:17|his arm shall quite wither away|Brachium ejus ariditate siccabitur]]. Christ commands such a man to rise from guilt by penance, to stand in the midst by an exemplary life, and to stretch out his hand by showing works of mercy.

paras.t: Exeuntes autem Pharisæi de synagoga, consilium faciebant adversus eum, videlicet Jesum, quomodo eum perderent, id est, accusarent atque occiderent. Secundum Marcum, consilium fecerunt cum Herodianis. In quo patet intolerabilis Pharisæorum perversitas, qui inde deteriorati sunt, unde emendari debebant. Firmaverunt enim sibi sermonem nequam, et ex deliberatione, ex certa malitia, ex habitu malo, inique egerunt: propter quod insanabiles incorrigibilesque fuerunt, præcipue propter odium contra Christum, quod pervertit omne judicium. Unde de eis dici potest illud Jeremiæ prophetæ: Induraverunt facies suas supra petram, et noluerunt reverti.
paras.en: [[12:14|And the Pharisees going out|Exeuntes autem Pharisæi]] of the synagogue, [[12:14|made a consultation against him|consilium faciebant adversus eum]], namely Jesus, [[12:14|how they might destroy him|quomodo eum perderent]], that is, accuse and kill Him. According to Mark, they took counsel with the Herodians[[Mark 3:6||]]. In which the intolerable perversity of the Pharisees is plain, who were made worse by what should have amended them.
