For [[Ps 63:6|they are resolute in wickedness|Firmaverunt enim sibi sermonem nequam]], and acted wickedly with deliberation, from certain malice, from evil habit: for which reason they were incurable and incorrigible, above all because of their hatred against Christ, which perverts all judgement. Hence of them may be said that of the prophet Jeremias: [[Jer 5:3|they have made their faces harder than the rock, and they have refused to return|Induraverunt facies suas supra petram, et noluerunt reverti]].

paras.t: Jesus autem sciens machinationes eorum, recessit inde, id est a synagoga ad mare, ut Marcus habet: non ex timore mortis, sed cedens furori, et condolens cæcitati eorum, et quoniam nondum venit hora ejus, et quia non capiebat perire Prophetam extra Jerusalem; et item, ut daret exemplum fugiendi, pro loco, causa et tempore, sicut superius dixit: Quum persecuti vos fuerint in una civitate, fugite in aliam. Et secuti sunt eum, cordis affectu, corporis gressu, multi, qui omiserant Jesum sequi propter timorem Pharisæorum; et curavit eos omnes qui cura indigebant, et eam requirebant. Alios curavit spiritualiter, vel realiter, vel quantum in se fuit. Et præcepit eis ne manifestum eum facerent, miracula ejus aliis insinuando: in quo docuit nos humilitatem amplecti, et vanam gloriam abominari. Vel, Ne manifestum eum facerent, id est, ne adversariis suis ac Pharisæis manifestarent quo isset, ac ubi esset. Propter easdem enim causas voluit Christus latere, propter quas abiit.
paras.en: [[12:15|But Jesus knowing it|Jesus autem sciens]], knowing their plots, [[12:15|retired from thence|recessit inde]], that is, from the synagogue to the sea, as Mark has it[[Mark 3:7||]]: not from fear of death, but giving way to their fury and pitying their blindness, and because His hour had not yet come[[John 7:30||]], and because [[Luke 13:33|it cannot be that a prophet perish, out of Jerusalem|non capiebat perire Prophetam extra Jerusalem]]; and also to give an example of flight, as place, cause and time require, as He said above: [[Matt 10:23|when they shall persecute you in this city, flee into another|Quum persecuti vos fuerint in una civitate, fugite in aliam]] [Denis reads 'in one city']. [[12:15|and many followed him|et secuti sunt eum multi]], with the affection of the heart and the steps of the body, who had left off following Jesus for fear of the Pharisees; [[12:15|and he healed them all|et curavit eos omnes]], who needed a cure and sought it. Some He cured spiritually, or in fact, or as far as lay in Him. [[12:16|And he charged them that they should not make him known|Et præcepit eis ne manifestum eum facerent]], by telling others of His miracles: in which He taught us to embrace humility and to abhor vainglory. Or, 'that they should not make him known', that is, that they should not make known to His adversaries, the Pharisees, where He had gone and where He was. For Christ wished to stay hidden for the same reasons for which He went away.

paras.t: Ut adimpleretur quod dictum est per Isaiam prophetam, dicentem in persona Dei Patris: Ecce puer meus, id est Christus: de quo in Actibus asseritur, Convenerunt adversum sanctum puerum tuum Jesum, Pontius Pilatus et Herodes; et Isaias, Puer, inquit, natus est nobis. In veteri Testamento, puer pro servo frequenter accipitur. Unde nostra translatio habet: Ecce servus meus. Quod convenit Christo, ratione naturæ assumptæ, secundum quam Pater major est Filio, qui exinanivit semetipsum, formam servi accipiens. Si autem puer pro filio accipiatur, sic Christus secundum divinam naturam est puer naturalis. Quem elegi, non secundum divinam naturam, sed secundum humanitatem assumptam. Electio enim ex libertate procedit, et tendit ad bona gratis, donaque gloriæ. Christus vero, ut Verbum ac Filius Dei, procedit a Patre per modum naturalis emanationis, et æternaliter essentialiterque beatus est, imo eamdem numero cum Patre ac Spiritu Sancto beatitudinem habens. Electus ergo dicitur Christus, ut homo. De quo Sponsa dicit in Canticis: Dilectus meus candidus et rubicundus, electus ex millibus; et Apostolus, Qui prædestinatus est, ait, Filius Dei in virtute, secundum spiritum sanctificationis.
paras.en: [[12:17|That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Isaias the prophet, saying|Ut adimpleretur quod dictum est per Isaiam prophetam, dicentem]], in the person of God the Father: [[12:18|Behold my servant|Ecce puer meus]], that is, Christ: of whom it is asserted in the Acts: [[Acts 4:27|there assembled together in this city against thy holy child Jesus, whom thou hast anointed, Herod, and Pontius Pilate|Convenerunt adversum sanctum puerum tuum Jesum, Pontius Pilatus et Herodes]]; and Isaias: [[Is 9:6|a CHILD IS BORN to us|Puer, inquit, natus est nobis]]. In the Old Testament 'child' [puer] is often taken for 'servant'. Hence our translation has: [[Is 42:1|Behold my servant|Ecce servus meus]]. Which befits Christ by reason of the nature He took, according to which the Father is greater than the Son, who [[Phil 2:7|emptied himself, taking the form of a servant|exinanivit semetipsum, formam servi accipiens]]. But if 'child' is taken for 'son', then Christ according to His divine nature is the natural Child. [[12:18|whom I have chosen|Quem elegi]], not according to the divine nature, but according to the humanity He took. For choice proceeds from freedom, and tends to the goods of grace and the gifts of glory. But Christ, as the Word and Son of God, proceeds from the Father by way of natural emanation, and is eternally and essentially blessed, nay has the same beatitude in number with the Father and the Holy Ghost. So Christ is called chosen as man. Of whom the Bride says in the Canticles: [[Cant 5:10|My beloved is white and ruddy, chosen out of thousands|Dilectus meus candidus et rubicundus, electus ex millibus]]; and the Apostle: [[Rom 1:4|Who was predestinated the Son of God in power, according to the spirit of sanctification|Qui prædestinatus est, ait, Filius Dei in virtute, secundum spiritum sanctificationis]].

paras.t: Dilectus meus, quem secundum divinitatem ipsius diligo amore simpliciter infinito, tanquam æqualem mihi in bonitate. Secundum humanitatem vero ejus Verbo unitam, diligo eum magis quam totum universum. Vere enim Pater diligit Filium amore superdulcissimo, omni creaturæ ignoto ac inexperto quantum ad plenitudinem suam. Sancti tamen in patria gustant eum pleno ore. In quo bene complacuit animæ meæ, hoc est cordi meo. Tantam enim complacentiam habet Pater in Filio, quantam et dilectionem. Nec aliquid inest Filio, quod oculos Patris offendat. Propter quod ait: Ego quæ placita sunt ei, facio semper. Et Christo baptizato ac transfigurato, audita est vox Patris, dicens: Hic est Filius meus dilectus, in quo mihi complacuit. Loquitur autem Deus Pater affectu et more humano, quum ait, In quo bene complacuit animæ meæ. Non quod habeat animam, quum sit simplicissima unitas, purissimaque natura; sed ad denotandum quod intime diligat Filium. Secundum quod Sponsa ait in Canticis: Indica mihi, quem diligit anima mea; et, Inveni quem diligit anima mea. In veteri tamen Testamento, frequenter dicitur Deus animam habere, vel per animam suam jurare, ut patet in Amos, quo legitur: Juravit Dominus in anima sua, Detestor ego superbiam. Et Jeremias ait: In gente iniqua ulciscetur anima mea.
paras.en: [[12:18|my beloved|Dilectus meus]], whom according to His Godhead I love with a love simply infinite, as equal to Me in goodness; and according to His humanity united to the Word I love Him more than the whole universe. For truly the Father loves the Son[[John 3:35||]][[John 5:20||]] with a love most surpassingly sweet, unknown and untasted by every creature as to its fulness; yet the Saints in the fatherland taste it with full mouth. [[12:18|in whom my soul hath been well pleased|In quo bene complacuit animæ meæ]], that is, My heart. For the Father has as much good pleasure in the Son as He has love. Nor is there anything in the Son to offend the Father's eyes. For which reason He says: [[John 8:29|I do always the things that please him|Ego quæ placita sunt ei, facio semper]]. And when Christ was baptized and transfigured, the voice of the Father was heard saying: [[Matt 3:17|This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased|Hic est Filius meus dilectus, in quo mihi complacuit]][[Luke 3:22||]][[Matt 17:5||]]. And God the Father speaks with human feeling and in human fashion when He says, 'in whom my soul hath been well pleased'; not that He has a soul, since He is the most simple unity and the purest nature, but to signify that He loves the Son inwardly. As the Bride says in the Canticles: [[Cant 1:6|Shew me, O thou whom my soul loveth|Indica mihi, quem diligit anima mea]]; and: [[Cant 3:4|I found him whom my soul loveth|Inveni quem diligit anima mea]]. Yet in the Old Testament God is often said to have a soul, or to swear by His soul, as is clear in Amos, where we read: [[Amos 6:8|The Lord God hath sworn by his own soul, saith the Lord the God of hosts: I detest the pride|Juravit Dominus in anima sua, Detestor ego superbiam]]. And Jeremias says: [[Jer 5:9|shall not my soul take revenge on such a nation?|In gente iniqua ulciscetur anima mea]][[Jer 9:9||]] [Denis's wording: 'on a wicked nation my soul shall take revenge'].

paras.t: Ponam spiritum meum super eum, id est, Spiritum Sanctum anima ejus supercopiose infundam: quia non ad mensuram dat Deus Spiritum homini Christo, ut Joannes habet; et in Luca scriptum est, Jesus plenus Spiritu Sancto, regressus est a Jordane. Denique conceptus est de Spiritu Sancto; et a primo illius conceptionis instanti tam plenus fuit Spiritu Sancto, quod nunquam in gratia, caritate, vel contemplatione profecit. Propter quod Isaias: Requiescet, inquit, super eum spiritus Domini, spiritus sapientiæ. Et judicium discretionis, id est distantiam inter bonum et malum, futurum quoque judicium remunerationis; vel, Judicium, id est divinum præceptum, quod Deus judicat esse justum; gentibus nuntiabit, per prædicationem Apostolorum, quibus locutus est: Euntes docete omnes gentes. Unde in Genesi dicitur: Ipse erit exspectatio gentium; et in Aggeo, Veniet Desideratus cunctis gentibus. Unde per Isaiam loquitur Pater de Christo: Ecce testem populis dedi eum, ducem et præceptorem gentibus. Christus autem in propria persona, non prædicavit nisi Judæis. In die quoque novissimo Christus proprio ore pronuntiabit judicium, id est judicialem sententiam: dicens iniquis, Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum; et justis, Venite, benedicti Patris mei.
paras.en: [[12:18|I will put my spirit upon him|Ponam spiritum meum super eum]], that is, I will pour the Holy Ghost most abundantly into His soul: since [[John 3:34|God doth not give the Spirit by measure|non ad mensuram dat Deus Spiritum]] to the man Christ, as John has it; and in Luke it is written: [[Luke 4:1|Jesus being full of the Holy Ghost, returned from the Jordan|Jesus plenus Spiritu Sancto, regressus est a Jordane]]. Moreover, He was conceived of the Holy Ghost[[Matt 1:20||]]; and from the first instant of that conception He was so full of the Holy Ghost that He never advanced in grace, charity or contemplation. For which reason Isaias says: [[Is 11:2|the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him: the spirit of wisdom|Requiescet, inquit, super eum spiritus Domini, spiritus sapientiæ]]. [[12:18|and he shall shew judgment|Et judicium]], the judgement of discernment, that is, the distance between good and evil, and also the judgement of reward to come; or, 'judgment', that is, the divine precept, which God judges to be just; [[12:18|to the Gentiles|gentibus nuntiabit]] by the preaching of the Apostles, to whom He said: [[Matt 28:19|Going therefore, teach ye all nations|Euntes docete omnes gentes]]. Hence in Genesis it is said: [[Gen 49:10|he shall be the expectation of nations|Ipse erit exspectatio gentium]]; and in Aggeus: [[Agg 2:8|THE DESIRED OF ALL NATIONS SHALL COME|Veniet Desideratus cunctis gentibus]]. Hence by Isaias the Father says of Christ: [[Is 55:4|Behold I have given him for a witness to the people, for a leader and a master to the Gentiles|Ecce testem populis dedi eum, ducem et præceptorem gentibus]]. But Christ in His own person preached only to the Jews. And on the last day Christ with His own mouth will pronounce judgement, that is, the judicial sentence, saying to the wicked: [[Matt 25:41|Depart from me, you cursed, into everlasting fire|Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum]]; and to the just: [[Matt 25:34|Come, ye blessed of my Father|Venite, benedicti Patris mei]].

paras.t: Non contendet, contra adversarios suos ex passione rixando, neque clamabit, alte loquendo, propter desiderium laudis humanæ, vel affectu vindictæ, seu inordinate et impatienter loquendo. De quo clamore dicit Apostolus: Omnis amaritudo, et ira, et clamor tollatur a vobis. Unde in passione obmutuit in tantum, ut ab Herode illuderetur, atque Pilatus vehementer miraretur. Nihilo minus Christus in sua prædicatione frequenter clamavit ex caritatis fervore, juxta illud: Jesus hæc dicens, clamavit, Qui habet aures, etc.; et rursus Clamabat Jesus, Si quis sitit, veniat ad me. Apostolus quoque ad Hebræos dicit, quod cum clamore valido et lacrimis preces fudit. Neque audiet aliquis in plateis vocem ejus. Videtur contrarium, quod alibi Christus ait: Ego palam locutus sum mundo, et in occulto locutus sum nihil. Insuper certum est, quod Christus eundo per vias et plateas, sæpe prædicavit discipulis suis et etiam aliis, sicut in die Palmarum, quum venit a Bethania in Jerusalem. Et respondendum, quod Christus dicitur non esse locutus in plateis, quoniam propter vanam ostentationem et gloriam nihil locutus est. Alii plateas spiritualiter sumunt pro lata via quæ ducit ad mortem: in qua certum est Christum nunquam fuisse aut prædicasse.
paras.en: [[12:19|He shall not contend|Non contendet]] against His adversaries, quarrelling from passion, [[12:19|nor cry out|neque clamabit]], speaking loudly from desire of human praise, or from a feeling of vengeance, or speaking disorderly and impatiently. Of which crying the Apostle says: [[Eph 4:31|Let all bitterness and anger and indignation and clamour and blasphemy be put away from you|Omnis amaritudo, et ira, et clamor tollatur a vobis]]. Hence in the passion He was silent, so much so that He was mocked by Herod[[Luke 23:11||]] and Pilate [[Matt 27:14|wondered exceedingly|vehementer miraretur]]. Nevertheless in His preaching Christ often cried out from the fervour of charity, according to that saying: [[Luke 8:8|Saying these things, he cried out: He that hath ears to hear|Jesus hæc dicens, clamavit, Qui habet aures]], etc.; and again: [[John 7:37|Jesus stood and cried, saying: If any man thirst, let him come to me|Clamabat Jesus, Si quis sitit, veniat ad me]]. The Apostle too, to the Hebrews, says that [[Heb 5:7|with a strong cry and tears, offering up prayers|cum clamore valido et lacrimis]] [Denis: 'He poured out prayers']. [[12:19|neither shall any man hear his voice in the streets|Neque audiet aliquis in plateis vocem ejus]]. What Christ says elsewhere seems contrary: [[John 18:20|I have spoken openly to the world. I have always taught in the synagogue and in the temple, whither all the Jews resort: and in secret I have spoken nothing|Ego palam locutus sum mundo: ego semper docui in synagoga, et in templo, quo omnes Judæi conveniunt, et in occulto locutus sum nihil]]. Besides, it is certain that Christ, going through the ways and streets, often preached to His disciples and to others too, as on Palm Sunday, when He came from Bethania into Jerusalem[[Matt 21:1||]]. And it must be answered that Christ is said not to have spoken in the streets because He spoke nothing for vain show and glory. Others take the streets spiritually for [[Matt 7:13|broad is the way that leadeth to destruction|lata via quæ ducit ad mortem]] [Denis: 'to death']: on which it is certain that Christ never was nor preached.

paras.t: Arundinem quassatam, hoc est calamum læsum, et pene destructum, non confringet, id est, non penitus relinquet, aut perdet. Per arundinem istam, signatur populus gentilis, diversis erroribus et peccatis attritus et laceratus. Quem Christus misericorditer reparavit, convertendo eum ad fidem et gratiam, prout apud Joannem protestatur: Alias, inquiens, oves habeo, quæ non sunt ex hoc ovili, et illas oportet me adducere. Et linum fumigans, id est populum Judaorum, qui propter aliqualem legis et Christi notitiam, licet valde obscuram, lino fumiganti comparantur. Quibus ait: Adhuc modicum lumen in vobis est. Non exstinguet, id est, penitus excæcari non desinet, sed quosdam illorum misericorditer illuminabit: quibus et dixit, Quum exaltaveritis Filium hominis, tunc cognoscetis quia ego sum. Reliquiæ equidem per electionem gratiæ salvæ factæ sunt. Possumus autem per arundinem quassatam et linum fumigans, eamdem plebem, imo eamdem personam accipere: quæ dicitur arundo quassata, propter vitiorum corruptionem, et linum fumigans, propter intellectualis luminis parvitatem, cæcitati interne propinquum. Sic omnis bonus prælatus, prædicator ac frater, non debet arundinem quassatam confringere, nec linum fumigans exstinguere, sed subdito seu confratri vitiis irretito, tentato, et pene excæcato, infatigabili caritate succurrere, sicut hortatur Apostolus: Fratres, inquiens, si præoccupatus fuerit homo in aliquo delicto, vos, qui spirituales estis, hujusmodi instruite in spiritu lenitatis; et rursus, Corripite inquietos, consolamini pusillanimes, suscipite infirmos, patientes estote ad omnes. Unde Hieronymus ait: Qui peccatori non porrigit manum, et non portat onus fratris sui, iste calamum quassatum confringit; et qui modicam scintillam fidei contemnit in parvulis, iste linum exstinguit fumigans. Sequamur ergo vestigia Christi, qui venit quærere et salvum facere quod perierat.
paras.en: [[12:20|The bruised reed|Arundinem quassatam]], that is, the injured and almost destroyed cane, [[12:20|he shall not break|non confringet]], that is, will not wholly abandon or destroy it. By this reed is signified the Gentile people, crushed and torn by various errors and sins. Christ mercifully restored it, converting it to faith and grace, as He declares in John: [[John 10:16|other sheep I have that are not of this fold: them also I must bring|Alias, inquiens, oves habeo, quæ non sunt ex hoc ovili, et illas oportet me adducere]]. [[12:20|and smoking flax|Et linum fumigans]], that is, the people of the Jews, who, because of some knowledge of the law and of Christ, though very obscure, are compared to smoking flax. To whom He says: [[John 12:35|Yet a little while, the light is among you|Adhuc modicum lumen in vobis est]]. [[12:20|he shall not extinguish|Non exstinguet]], that is, He will not cease altogether to blind them, but will mercifully enlighten some of them: to whom He also said: [[John 8:28|When you shall have lifted up, the Son of man, then shall you know that I am he|Quum exaltaveritis Filium hominis, tunc cognoscetis quia ego sum]]. For [[Rom 11:5|a remnant saved according to the election of grace|Reliquiæ equidem per electionem gratiæ salvæ factæ sunt]]. And by the bruised reed and the smoking flax we may take the same people, nay the same person: who is called a bruised reed because of the corruption of vices, and smoking flax because of the smallness of the light of understanding, near to inward blindness. So every good prelate, preacher and brother must not break the bruised reed nor quench the smoking flax, but must help with untiring charity a subject or fellow-brother entangled in vices, tempted and almost blinded; as the Apostle exhorts, saying: [[Gal 6:1|Brethren, and if a man be overtaken in any fault, you, who are spiritual, instruct such a one in the spirit of meekness|Fratres, inquiens, si præoccupatus fuerit homo in aliquo delicto, vos, qui spirituales estis, hujusmodi instruite in spiritu lenitatis]]; and again: [[1 Thess 5:14|rebuke the unquiet, comfort the feeble-minded, support the weak, be patient towards all men|Corripite inquietos, consolamini pusillanimes, suscipite infirmos, patientes estote ad omnes]]. Hence Jerome says: He who does not hold out his hand to a sinner, and does not carry his brother's burden, breaks the bruised reed; and he who despises a little spark of faith in the little ones quenches the smoking flax. Let us, then, follow the footsteps of Christ, who [[Luke 19:10|is come to seek and to save that which was lost|venit quærere et salvum facere quod perierat]].

paras.t: Donec ejiciat ad victoriam judicium. Hoc intelligi potest, tam de judicio discretionis, quam extrema remunerationis. Primo sic: Prædicta Christus non faciet, sed eorum opposita, donec ejiciat, id est, prosequatur, sive effundat ac perducat, judicium discretionis, id est separationem electorum a reprobis in præsenti per fidem et gratiam, ad victoriam, id est dejectionem diaboli, illum ab electorum cordibus excludendo. De hoc judicio dicit Salvator: Nunc judicium est mundi, nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras. Cœpit quippe istud judicium maxime a prædicatione Christi et Apostolorum, quia ex tunc in toto mundo cœperunt quidam ad fidem et caritatem vocari, aliis derelictis, et ita tunc separabantur ab invicem, fide, voto, ac merito: quod ad discretionis judicium pertinet, per quod Christus diabolum vicit, ejiciendo eum foras, et tribuendo fidelibus potestatem prævalendi contra eum. Secundo sic: Donec ejiciat ad victoriam judicium, id est, judicium ultima discussionis, seu extremæ remunerationis, exerceat et perducat ad victoriam, id est ad plenum sui ipsius triumphum, quia tunc perfecte dejiciet omnes adversarios suos, secundum illud Isaiæ prophetæ: Ad eum venient, et confundentur omnes qui repugnant ei. Illo autem judicio consummato, Christus non amplius reparabit quassatam arundinem, nec illuminabit fumigans linum. Et in nomine ejus gentes sperabunt.
paras.en: [[12:20|till he send forth judgment unto victory|Donec ejiciat ad victoriam judicium]]. This can be understood both of the judgement of discernment and of the final judgement of reward. First thus: Christ will not do the things just said, but their opposites, until He send forth, that is, pursue, or pour out and bring to completion, the judgement of discernment, that is, the separation of the elect from the reprobate in the present by faith and grace, unto victory, that is, the overthrow of the devil, shutting him out of the hearts of the elect. Of this judgement the Saviour says: [[John 12:31|Now is the judgment of the world: now shall the prince of this world be cast out|Nunc judicium est mundi, nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras]]. For this judgement began above all with the preaching of Christ and the Apostles, since from then on, throughout the world, some began to be called to faith and charity while others were left; and so they were then separated from one another in faith, will and merit: which belongs to the judgement of discernment, by which Christ overcame the devil, casting him out and giving the faithful power to prevail against him. Secondly thus: till He send forth judgement unto victory, that is, exercise the judgement of the last trial, or of the final reward, and bring it unto victory, that is, to His own full triumph, since then He will perfectly cast down all His adversaries, according to that of the prophet Isaias: [[Is 45:25|they shall come to him, and all that resist him shall be confounded|Ad eum venient, et confundentur omnes qui repugnant ei]]. And when that judgement is completed, Christ will no longer restore the bruised reed nor enlighten the smoking flax. [[12:21|And in his name the Gentiles shall hope|Et in nomine ejus gentes sperabunt]].

12.title: Prosecutio expositionis præsentis capituli
12.title_en: Continuation of the exposition of this chapter

paras.t: Tunc oblatus est ei, videlicet Christo ad sanandum, dæmonium habens, id est homo obsessus a dæmone, cæcus et mutus, non a natura vel ægritudine naturali, sed a dæmonis operatione. Unde in Luca scriptum est, Erat ejiciens dæmonium, et illud erat mutum: non utique formaliter, sed efficienter, id est mutificans hominem. Et curavit eum Jesus, dæmonem expellendo, ita ut loqueretur et videret, qui paulo ante mutus fuit ac cæcus. Sicque secundum Hieronymum, tria signa in eodem peracta sunt. Nam obsessus curatur, mutus loquelam, et cæcus visum recipit. Tamen duo ista consecuta sunt naturali ordine primum signum, videlicet dæmonis ejectionem: quoniam enim dæmon hominem cæcum ac mutum effecit sua præsentia, ideo eo ejecto, homo recepit facultatem linguæ ac oculorum. Et stupebant, id est, vehementer mirabantur, omnes turbæ quæ aderant; et dicebant, quærendo ad invicem: Nonne hic est filius David, hoc est Christus in lege promissus, et prænuntiatus nasci de semine David? tanquam dicant: Quum hic sit Christus, vel si est Christus, prout verba et opera ejus testantur, non debemus in tantum mirari quod signa hæc operetur, quum hoc sit prophetatum de eo. Pharisæi autem audientes turbam tam reverenter de Jesu loquentem, dixerunt, ex gravi invidia, quæ omnia etiam bona interpretatur sinistre, et occasionem calumniandi confingit: Hic non ejicit dæmones, nisi in Beelzebub principe dæmoniorum, hoc est virtute summi ac pessimi damonis, cum Jesu pactum et familiaritatem habentis: cui dæmonum principi alii inferiores obediunt, egrediendo ab obsessis ad verba Jesu, quatenus homines decipiantur, putando quod Jesus divina virtute hæc agat, et Christus exsistat. Jesus autem sciens certitudinaliter cogitationes eorum: quod Deo est proprium, ut propria potestate cogitationes cordium intueatur, nec homo potest eas cognoscere, nisi Deo revelante; dixit eis.
paras.en: [[12:22|Then was offered to him|Tunc oblatus est ei]], that is, to Christ, to be healed, [[12:22|one possessed with a devil|dæmonium habens]], that is, a man possessed by a demon, [[12:22|blind and dumb|cæcus et mutus]], not by nature or natural sickness, but by the working of the demon. Hence it is written in Luke: [[Luke 11:14|he was casting out a devil, and the same was dumb|Erat ejiciens dæmonium, et illud erat mutum]]: not formally, but effectively, that is, making the man dumb. [[12:22|and he healed him|Et curavit eum]], Jesus, by driving out the demon, [[12:22|so that he spoke and saw|ita ut loqueretur et videret]], who a little before was dumb and blind. And so, according to Jerome, three signs were done in the same man: for the possessed is cured, the dumb receives speech, and the blind sight. Yet these two followed in natural order upon the first sign, namely the casting out of the demon: for since the demon had made the man blind and dumb by his presence, when he was cast out the man received the use of tongue and eyes. [[12:23|And all the multitudes were amazed|Et stupebant omnes turbæ]], that is, wondered greatly, that were present; [[12:23|and said|et dicebant]], asking one another: [[12:23|Is not this the son of David?|Nonne hic est filius David]], that is, the Christ promised in the law and foretold to be born of the seed of David? As if to say: Since this is the Christ, or if He is the Christ, as His words and works testify, we ought not so much to wonder that He works these signs, since this was prophesied of Him. [[12:24|But the Pharisees hearing it|Pharisæi autem audientes]], hearing the crowd speak so reverently of Jesus, [[12:24|said|dixerunt]], out of grievous envy, which interprets all things, even good ones, in the worse sense, and makes up occasions for slander: [[12:24|This man casteth not out devils but by Beelzebub the prince of the devils|Hic non ejicit dæmones, nisi in Beelzebub principe dæmoniorum]], that is, by the power of the highest and worst demon, who has a pact and familiarity with Jesus; whom, as prince of the demons, the other lower ones obey, going out of the possessed at the words of Jesus, so that men may be deceived, thinking that Jesus does these things by divine power and is the Christ. [[12:25|And Jesus knowing their thoughts|Jesus autem sciens certitudinaliter cogitationes eorum]] with certainty (which is proper to God, to behold the thoughts of hearts by His own power, nor can a man know them unless God reveals them), [[12:25|said to them|dixit eis]].

paras.t: Antequam Christi responsionem elucidem, commemorare oportet quid moraliter per dæmoniacum istum surdum ac mutum signetur. Significatur autem per eum quicumque habituatus in vitiis: quem dæmon ducit quo vult, habens eum captivum ad suam voluntatem; qui verba Dei aure cordis non percipit, nec gratias agit Deo. Hunc curat Christus, dæmonem per gratiæ infusionem ejiciendo, ita ut homo talis audiat quid loquatur Spiritus, et Domino confiteatur, sitque spiritualia loquens, et audiens sic loquentes.
paras.en: Before I explain Christ's answer, it should be recalled what is signified morally by this deaf and dumb demoniac. By him is signified anyone hardened in vices, whom the demon leads where he will, holding him [[2 Tim 2:26|captive at his will|captivum ad suam voluntatem]]; who does not hear the words of God with the ear of the heart, nor give thanks to God. Christ cures him by casting out the demon through the infusion of grace, so that such a man [[Ps 84:9|will hear what the Lord God will speak|audiat quid loquatur]] in him [Denis: 'what the Spirit speaks'], and confess to the Lord, and speak spiritual things, and hear those who speak so.

paras.t: Audiens itaque Jesus, pravitatem Pharisæorum redarguens, non ad verba, sed ad cogitata eorum respondet, ut vel sic fateantur ejus majestatem, quem experiuntur cordium secreta rimari. Omne regnum, divisum contra se, hoc est intestinam discordiam habens et pugnam, ita quod una pars contra aliam præliatur, desolabitur, hoc est, cito destruetur, et omnis civitas vel domus divisa contra se, non stabit, hoc est, urbs et habitatio quarum habitatores contra se dimicant, destruentur. Et si Satanas Satanam ejicit, hoc est, si adjutorio superioris dæmonis, alii ab hominibus expelluntur, adversus se divisus est, id est, contra se pugnat, et proprium regnum corrumpit, quum regnum ejus sit hominibus prævalere. Quomodo ergo stabit regnum ejus? hoc est, qualiter potestas et dominatio principis dæmonum perseverabit, quam ad probationem electorum stare oportet usque ad diem judicii? Sed ad hoc poterant dicere Pharisæi, quod Satanas Satanam ejiciebat, ita quod ejectio dæmonum fuit obedientia in principem suum in Christo, quatenus homines majoribus involverentur erroribus, æstimando Jesum esse Filium Dei. Ad quod facile est respondere. Nam Christus in omnibus ore et opere docuit ea quæ maxime contrariantur diabolo, scilicet caritatem, obedientiam, patientiam, pacem, humilitatem, paupertatem, mundi contemptum, idololatriæ destructionem, perfectam mentis adhæsionem seu unionem cum Deo, plenam abrenuntiationem diaboli: per quæ potestas et regnum diaboli dejiciuntur. Si ergo diabolus sibi cooperabatur, directe divisus erat contra se ipsum, nec erat vera ejectio dæmonum, quam fecerat Christus, sed fraudulenta a vexatione cessatio.
paras.en: So Jesus, rebuking the wickedness of the Pharisees, answers not their words but their thoughts, so that even so they may confess His majesty, whom they find searching the secrets of hearts. [[12:25|Every kingdom divided against itself|Omne regnum divisum contra se]], that is, having civil discord and fighting, so that one part fights against another, [[12:25|shall be made desolate|desolabitur]], that is, will soon be destroyed; [[12:25|and every city or house divided against itself shall not stand|et omnis civitas vel domus divisa contra se, non stabit]], that is, the city and the dwelling whose inhabitants fight against themselves will be destroyed. [[12:26|And if Satan cast out Satan|Et si Satanas Satanam ejicit]], that is, if by the help of a higher demon others are driven out of men, [[12:26|he is divided against himself|adversus se divisus est]], that is, fights against himself and ruins his own kingdom, since his kingdom is to prevail over men. [[12:26|how then shall his kingdom stand?|Quomodo ergo stabit regnum ejus?]] That is, how will the power and dominion of the prince of demons last, which must stand until the day of judgement for the testing of the elect? But to this the Pharisees could say that Satan cast out Satan, so that the casting out of demons was obedience to their prince in Christ, so that men might be entangled in greater errors, thinking Jesus to be the Son of God. To which it is easy to answer. For Christ in all things, by mouth and deed, taught what is most contrary to the devil, namely charity, obedience, patience, peace, humility, poverty, contempt of the world, the destruction of idolatry, perfect cleaving or union of the mind with God, full renunciation of the devil: by which the power and kingdom of the devil are cast down. If, then, the devil were working with Him, he was directly divided against himself; nor was the casting out of demons that Christ did a true one, but a fraudulent ceasing from torment.

paras.t: Interea ponit Salvator aliam rationem ad idem. Et si ego in Beelzebub ejicio dæmones, filii vestri, hoc est exorcistæ, qui proferendo exorcismos seu adjurationes a Salomone editos, expellebant dæmonia: vel, Filii vestri, id est Apostoli et alii discipuli mei, de vestra stirpe exorti; in quo, hoc est cujus virtute, ejiciunt dæmones? Ideo ipsi judices vestri erunt: id est, quum de illis dici non possit, quod magica arte, seu dæmonis ope ejiciant dæmones, sed virtute divina, ideo ipsi in die judicii judicabunt vos, hoc est, damnatione dignos ostendent vos, qui eumdem effectum, scilicet dæmonum ejectionem, in me adscribitis principi dæmonum, quam in eis adscribitis Deo. Itaque judices vestri erunt, quoniam vobis non credentibus, ipsi crediderunt. Si autem per filios Judæorum intelligantur exorcistæ, illi judices erunt infidelium Judæorum, comparatione, vel sententiæ approbatione, quemadmodum regina Saba dicitur in die judicii condemnatura Judæos incredulos. Si autem per filios intelligantur Apostoli aliique discipuli viri perfecti, illi judices Judæorum erunt per assessionem cum Christo, juxta illud: Vos qui secuti estis me, sedebitis super sedes, judicantes duodecim tribus Israel.
paras.en: Meanwhile the Saviour gives another reason to the same end. [[12:27|And if I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your children cast them out?|Et si ego in Beelzebub ejicio dæmones, filii vestri in quo ejiciunt?]] 'Your children', that is, the exorcists, who by pronouncing exorcisms or adjurations made by Solomon drove out demons; or, 'your children', that is, the Apostles and My other disciples, sprung from your stock: 'by whom', that is, by whose power, do they cast out demons? [[12:27|Therefore they shall be your judges|Ideo ipsi judices vestri erunt]]: that is, since it cannot be said of them that they cast out demons by magic art or the help of a demon, but by divine power, therefore they will judge you on the day of judgement, that is, show you worthy of damnation, who ascribe the same effect, namely the casting out of demons, to the prince of demons in Me, and to God in them. So they will be your judges, since they believed while you did not believe. If by the children of the Jews are understood the exorcists, they will be judges of the unbelieving Jews by comparison, or by approving the sentence, as the queen of Saba is said to be going to condemn the unbelieving Jews on the day of judgement[[12:42||]]. But if by the children are understood the Apostles and other disciples, perfect men, they will be judges of the Jews by sitting with Christ, according to that saying: [[Matt 19:28|you who have followed me, in the regeneration, when the Son of man shall sit on the seat of his majesty, you also shall sit on twelve seats judging the twelve tribes of Israel|vos, qui secuti estis me, in regeneratione cum sederit Filius hominis in sede majestatis suæ, sedebitis et vos super sedes duodecim, judicantes duodecim tribus Israël]].

paras.t: Si autem ego in spiritu Dei, hoc est virtute et operatione Spiritus Sancti, ejicio dæmones, igitur, id est, ex hoc sequitur, quod pervenit in vos regnum Dei, hoc est virtus et dominatio, regimen seu gubernatio Creatoris, qui per me operatur inter vos dæmonum expulsionem, ita quod ego sum Christus vobis promissus, et inter vos regnaturus: sicut Isaias prædixit, Super solium David sedebit, et multiplicabitur ejus imperium; et Jeremias, Regnabit (ait) rex, et sapiens erit. Quod angelus quoque locutus est Virgini benediete: Regnabit, inquiens, in domo Jacob in æternum, et regni ejus non erit finis. Vel, Regnum Dei, id est vita æterna, quam ego prædico et præparo vobis, dicendo, Pœnitentiam agite, appropinquabit enim regnum cœlorum, et moriendo pro salute vestra. Pervenit ergo in vos regnum Dei, id est, per me patefit vobis ingressus regni cœlestis, qui a dæmonibus eripio vos, et potestatem do vobis filios Dei fieri.
paras.en: [[12:28|But if I by the Spirit of God|Si autem ego in spiritu Dei]], that is, by the power and working of the Holy Ghost, [[12:28|cast out devils|ejicio dæmones]], [[12:28|then|igitur]], that is, it follows from this, [[12:28|is the kingdom of God come upon you|pervenit in vos regnum Dei]], that is, the power and dominion, the rule or government of the Creator, who works through Me the driving out of demons among you; so that I am the Christ promised to you, and to reign among you; as Isaias foretold: [[Is 9:7|he shall sit upon the throne of David|Super solium David sedebit]]; [[Is 9:7|His empire shall be multiplied|multiplicabitur ejus imperium]]; and Jeremias: [[Jer 23:5|a king shall reign, and shall be wise|Regnabit (ait) rex, et sapiens erit]]. Which the angel also said to the blessed Virgin: [[Luke 1:32|he shall reign in the house of Jacob for ever|Regnabit, inquiens, in domo Jacob in æternum]]. [[Luke 1:33|And of his kingdom there shall be no end|et regni ejus non erit finis]]. Or, 'the kingdom of God', that is, eternal life, which I preach and prepare for you, saying: [[Matt 4:17|Do penance, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand|Pœnitentiam agite, appropinquabit enim regnum cœlorum]], and by dying for your salvation. So the kingdom of God is come upon you, that is, through Me the entrance to the heavenly kingdom is opened to you, since I snatch you from the demons and give you [[John 1:12|power to be made the sons of God|potestatem do vobis filios Dei fieri]].

paras.t: Subditur tertia ratio ad idem. Aut quomodo potest quisquam intrare in domum fortis, id est potentis habitatoris, et vasa ejus diripere, id est bona ejus auferre, nisi prius alligaverit fortem, ne possit resistere? Hoc generaliter sic est, quod nemo potest potentis domum manifeste intrare, ac deprædari, nisi prævaluerit contra potentem qui in domo presens exsistit, et vinxerit eum, sive tenuerit. Et tunc domum illius diripiet, id est, spolia tollet, et domum vacuabit invito domino. Per hunc fortem Christus intelligit dæmonem: in quo naturalia integra permanserunt, secundum Dionysium, propter quod potens est valde, quum naturaliter sit nobilis immaterialisque spiritus. De quo inquit Job: Non est potestas super terram, quæ comparetur ei, qui factus est ut nullum timeret. Domus istius fortis, est mundus, qui totus in maligno positus est, id est ecclesia malignantium, seu corda malorum. Unde ait Salvator: Venit ad me princeps mundi hujus. Vasa ejus, sunt omnes perversi vel obsessi, in quibus regnat ac demoratur. Christus ergo non potuisset domum diaboli introisse peccatoribus prædicando, et vasa ejus diripuisse obsessos a dæmone liberando, vel impios ad pœnitentiam convertendo et suo dominio subjiciendo, qui ante subdebantur diabolo et serviebant peccato, nisi alligasset diabolum, ei prevalendo tanquam adversario. Non ergo societatem habebat cum ipso, nec operabatur subsidio ejus. Quoniam ergo adversarius noster diabolus, Christi victoris ore fortis asseritur, non debemus esse securi, sed timorati atque solliciti, prout Petrus nos hortatur, dicens: Vigilate, quia adversarius vester diabolus tanquam leo rugiens circuit.
paras.en: A third reason to the same end is added. [[12:29|Or how can any one enter into the house of the strong|Aut quomodo potest quisquam intrare in domum fortis]], that is, of a powerful dweller, [[12:29|and rifle his goods|et vasa ejus diripere]], that is, take away his goods, [[12:29|unless he first bind the strong?|nisi prius alligaverit fortem]], so that he cannot resist? This is generally so, that no one can openly enter the house of a powerful man and plunder it unless he has prevailed against the powerful man who is present in the house, and has bound or held him. [[12:29|and then he will rifle his house|Et tunc domum illius diripiet]], that is, will carry off the spoils and empty the house against the owner's will. By this strong man Christ means the demon, in whom the natural gifts remained whole, according to Dionysius, for which reason he is very powerful, since by nature he is a noble and immaterial spirit. Of whom Job says: [[Job 41:24|There is no power upon earth that can be compared with him who was made to fear no one|Non est potestas super terram, quæ comparetur ei, qui factus est ut nullum timeret]]. The house of this strong man is the world, which [[1 John 5:19|is seated in wickedness|totus in maligno positus est]], that is, the church of the malignant[[Ps 25:5||]], or the hearts of the wicked. Hence the Saviour says: [[John 14:30|the prince of this world cometh|Venit ad me princeps mundi hujus]]. His goods [vasa, 'vessels'] are all the perverse or possessed, in whom he reigns and dwells. So Christ could not have entered the devil's house by preaching to sinners, and rifled his goods by freeing the possessed from the demon, or by converting the wicked to repentance and subjecting to His dominion those who before were subject to the devil and served sin, unless He had bound the devil, prevailing over him as an adversary. So He had no fellowship with him, nor did He work with his help. Since, then, our adversary the devil is declared strong by the mouth of Christ the victor, we ought not to be secure, but fearful and watchful, as Peter exhorts us, saying: [[1 Pet 5:8|watch: because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, goeth about|Vigilate, quia adversarius vester diabolus tanquam leo rugiens circuit]].

paras.t: Sequitur ratio quarta ad idem. Qui non est mecum, contra me est, hoc est, qui mihi concors non est, adversatur voluntati meæ; et qui non congregat mecum, id est, homines non reducit a diversis erroribus, vitiis et dissentionibus, ad fidei unitatem, ad pacem et veri Dei unanimem cultum, quantum in se est, orando, exemplariter conversando sive docendo, spargit, id est, a Deo separat, et diversis erroribus implicat alios, quantum in se est. Quum ergo ego hoc prædicem, ut reducam homines ad unitatem, pacem et cultum divinum, diabolus vero laboret ad oppositum; constat quod non sit mecum, sed contra me: ideo in nomine ejus non ago, nec dæmones ejicio.
paras.en: A fourth reason to the same end follows. [[12:30|He that is not with me, is against me|Qui non est mecum, contra me est]], that is, he who is not in agreement with Me opposes My will; [[12:30|and he that gathereth not with me|et qui non congregat mecum]], that is, does not bring men back from various errors, vices and dissensions to the unity of faith, to peace and the united worship of the true God, as far as in him lies, by praying, by exemplary living or by teaching, [[12:30|scattereth|spargit]], that is, separates others from God and entangles them in various errors, as far as in him lies. Since, then, I preach this, to bring men back to unity, peace and the worship of God, while the devil labours for the opposite, it is clear that he is not with Me but against Me: therefore I do not act in his name, nor cast out demons by him.

paras.t: Ideo dico vobis: Omne peccatum et blasphemia remittetur hominibus. Secundum Augustinum, locus iste ita difficilis est, ut vix in tota Scriptura canonica aliquid ita difficile inveniatur. Verumtamen nunc tam evidenter a sanctis catholicisque doctoribus explanatus est, ut non oporteat diutius immorari. Est igitur sensus: Omne peccatum et blasphemia, preter illam blasphemiam de qua statim subjungitur, hoc est omne peccatum in proximum, et blasphemia contra Deum vel Sanctos procedens ex ignorantia (quæ dicitur blasphemia contra Filium, cui appropriatur sapientia), vel ex infirmitate seu fragilitate (quæ dicitur blasphemia contra Patrem, cui appropriatur potentia), remittetur hominibus, id est, remissibile peccatum est: quoniam licet in se grande peccatum sit, tamen ex aliqua parte et circumstantia excusabile est, sicque faciliter dimittitur pœnitenti. Spiritus autem blasphemia, hoc est blasphemia procedens ex certa malitia, ex impugnatione agnita veritatis, ex invidentia fraternze gratiæ: quæ vocatur blasphemia contra Spiritum Sanctum, cui appropriatur bonitas, amor et liberalitas; non remittetur, id est, ex se irremissibile erimen est, quoniam nullam habet excusationem, et obviat principio quo fit peccati remissio, scilicet bonitati, caritati seu pietati. Ideo dicitur irremissibile, non quasi nequaquam remissibile, sed quoniam difficulter et raro dimittitur, non ex immisericordia Dei, sed quoniam homines de tali peccato raro et difficillime pœnitent. Itaque, quum dicitur, Spiritus autem blasphemia, sensus est, Ipsius Spiritus Sancti blasphemia, seu blasphemia contra eum. Porro, quum dicitur blasphemia contra Patrem et Filium remissibilis, blasphemia vero contra Spiritum Sanctum irremissibilis, non est sic intelligendum, quasi minus peccatum sit blasphemare Patrem vel Filium, quam Spiritum Sanctum; sed quod blasphemia dicitur contra Patrem et Filium et Spiritum Sanctum, ex parte originis, quia procedit ex infirmitate, ignorantia, vel certa malitia, quæ pejor est et inexcusabilior quam infirmitas vel ignorantia, nisi sit ignorantia penitus volita, quæ ad malitiam pertinet.
paras.en: [[12:31|Therefore I say to you: Every sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven men|Ideo dico vobis: Omne peccatum et blasphemia remittetur hominibus]]. According to Augustine, this place is so difficult that hardly anything so difficult is found in the whole canonical Scripture. Yet it has now been so clearly explained by the holy and Catholic doctors that there is no need to dwell on it longer. The sense, then, is this: Every sin and blasphemy, except that blasphemy which is added at once, that is, every sin against one's neighbour, and blasphemy against God or the Saints proceeding from ignorance (which is called blasphemy against the Son, to whom wisdom is appropriated), or from weakness or frailty (which is called blasphemy against the Father, to whom power is appropriated), shall be forgiven men, that is, is a forgivable sin: since, though it be a great sin in itself, yet on some side and in some circumstance it is excusable, and so is easily forgiven to the penitent. [[12:31|but the blasphemy of the Spirit|Spiritus autem blasphemia]], that is, blasphemy proceeding from certain malice, from attacking acknowledged truth, from envy of a brother's grace, which is called blasphemy against the Holy Ghost, to whom goodness, love and liberality are appropriated, [[12:31|shall not be forgiven|non remittetur]], that is, is of itself an unforgivable crime, since it has no excuse, and opposes the very principle by which the forgiveness of sin is brought about, namely goodness, charity or kindness. So it is called unforgivable, not as though in no way forgivable, but because it is forgiven with difficulty and rarely: not from any lack of mercy in God, but because men rarely and with the greatest difficulty repent of such a sin. So when it is said, 'the blasphemy of the Spirit', the sense is: the blasphemy of the Holy Ghost Himself, that is, blasphemy against Him. Moreover, when blasphemy against the Father and the Son is called forgivable, and blasphemy against the Holy Ghost unforgivable, it is not to be understood as though it were a lesser sin to blaspheme the Father or the Son than the Holy Ghost; but that blasphemy is said to be against the Father, the Son and the Holy Ghost by reason of its origin, according as it proceeds from weakness, ignorance, or certain malice, which is worse and less excusable than weakness or ignorance, unless the ignorance be wholly willed, which belongs to malice.

paras.t: Hæc dicit Salvator ad dæmonstrandum gravitatem criminis Pharisæorum, qui opera sua divinitus facta, dæmoni adscripserunt: peccabant enim ex certa malitia. Ideo subditur: Et quicumque dixerit verbum contra Filium hominis, hoc est, blasphemaverit Christum quantum ad ejus humanitatem, dicendo mala de ipso ex consideratione naturalis fragilitatis et defectuositatis suæ carnis, ut quod esset filius fabri, potator vini, homo vorax; remittetur ei, id est, tale peccatum aliquo modo excusabile et remissibile est, propter conditionem humanæ naturæ, et pœnitenti faciliter dimittitur, quamvis sit magnum peccatum. Qui autem dixerit contra Spiritum Sanctum, id est, Christum blasphemaverit quantum ad ejus divinitatem, ex pura malitia, dicendo quod in Beelzebub ejiciat dæmones, et dæmoniacus sit, ceteraque opera deitatis adseribendo diabolo; non remittetur ei, neque in hoc sæculo neque in futuro, id est nunquam, quia nec in præsenti, nec postea. In inferno namque non est remissio, et talis in infernum demergitur, non in purgatorio collocatur. Unde in Marco scriptum est, quod erit reus æterni delicti. Cujus causam Marcus subjungit: quia (inquit) dicebant, Spiritum immundum habet: hoc est, ex consideratione miraculorum Christi, stimulante invidia, moti sunt ad dicendum quod spiritum diabolicum haberet, per quem operaretur: quod fuit peccatum in Spiritum Sanctum, videlicet impugnatio apertissimæ veritatis. Nam inle exezeati ad blasphemiamque inducti sunt, unde illuminari et Christi divinitatem agnoscere debuerunt.
paras.en: The Saviour says these things to show the gravity of the crime of the Pharisees, who ascribed to the demon His works done by divine power: for they sinned from certain malice. So it is added: [[12:32|And whosoever shall speak a word against the Son of man|Et quicumque dixerit verbum contra Filium hominis]], that is, shall blaspheme Christ as to His humanity, speaking evil of Him from consideration of the natural frailty and weakness of His flesh, as that He was the carpenter's son, a wine drinker, a glutton[[Matt 11:19||]], [[12:32|it shall be forgiven him|remittetur ei]], that is, such a sin is in some way excusable and forgivable, because of the condition of human nature, and is easily forgiven to the penitent, though it is a great sin. [[12:32|but he that shall speak against the Holy Ghost|Qui autem dixerit contra Spiritum Sanctum]], that is, shall blaspheme Christ as to His Godhead, from pure malice, saying that He casts out demons by Beelzebub and is possessed, and ascribing the other works of the Godhead to the devil, [[12:32|it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, nor in the world to come|non remittetur ei, neque in hoc sæculo neque in futuro]], that is, never, since neither now nor afterwards. For in hell there is no forgiveness, and such a man is plunged into hell, not placed in purgatory. Hence in Mark it is written that he [[Mark 3:29|shall be guilty of an everlasting sin|erit reus æterni delicti]]. The cause of which Mark adds: [[Mark 3:30|Because they said: He hath an unclean spirit|quia (inquit) dicebant, Spiritum immundum habet]]: that is, from considering Christ's miracles, goaded by envy, they were moved to say that He had a diabolical spirit by which He worked: which was a sin against the Holy Ghost, namely the attacking of most evident truth. For they were blinded and led to blasphemy by what should have enlightened them and made them acknowledge Christ's Godhead.

paras.t: Consequenter Salvator cogit adversarios rationabili argumento, ut fateantur ipsum operari in Deo, non in Beelzebub. Aut facite, id est, judicando affirmate, arborem bonam, hoc est me operantem, seu meam voluntatem, quæ est operationis principium et arbori comparatur, esse rectam et justam, et fructum, id est opus ejus, dicite esse bonum; aut facite arborem malam, id est, me operantem dicite malum, et fructum ejus, id est opus, judicate malum. Alterum enim istorum oportet vos confiteri, siquidem ex fructu arbor cognoscitur, id est, ex operatione hominis patet qualis exsistat. Operatio quippe arguit formam. Per hæc verba, Christus innuit talem argumentationem: Quum hominem dæmoniacum, cæcum ac mutum, liberare a dæmone, et cæcitate et impedimento loquelæ, sit opus caritativum ac pium, ego qui hæc feci, non debeo judicari in principe dæmonum operari, sed potius bonus atque deifice agens judicari. Per arborem ergo intelligit voluntatem, seu hominem operantem. Unde superius dicitur: Omnis arbor quæ non facit fructum bonum, excidetur. Facere quoque, accipitur hoc loco communiter, pro actu quocumque: sicque accipitur, ut legitur in Jacobo: Tu credis quoniam unus est Deus, bene facis; et dæmones credunt.
paras.en: Next the Saviour forces His adversaries by a reasonable argument to confess that He works in God, not in Beelzebub. [[12:33|Either make the tree good|Aut facite arborem bonam]], that is, by judging, affirm that the tree, that is, Me who work, or My will, which is the principle of working and is compared to a tree, is upright and just, [[12:33|and its fruit good|et fructum ejus bonum]], that is, say that its work is good; [[12:33|or make the tree evil|aut facite arborem malam]], that is, call Me who work evil, [[12:33|and its fruit evil|et fructum ejus malum]], that is, judge the work evil. For you must confess one of the two, [[12:33|for by the fruit the tree is known|siquidem ex fructu arbor cognoscitur]], that is, from a man's working it is clear what he is. For the working shows the form. By these words Christ hints at this argument: Since to free a man possessed, blind and dumb, from the demon, and from blindness and the hindrance of speech, is a charitable and holy work, I who did these things ought not to be judged to work by the prince of demons, but rather to be judged good and acting in a godly way. So by the tree He means the will, or the man who works. Hence it is said above: [[Matt 3:10|Every tree therefore that doth not yield good fruit, shall be cut down|Omnis arbor quæ non facit fructum bonum, excidetur]]. And 'make' is taken here broadly for any act; and so it is taken as we read in James: [[Jas 2:19|Thou believest that there is one God. Thou dost well: the devils also believe|Tu credis quoniam unus est Deus, bene facis; et dæmones credunt]].

paras.t: Progenies viperarum, id est, generatio serpentina, dolosa ac invidiosa, quomodo potestis bona loqui, hoc est veritatem de me profiteri, et verba virtuosa bona intentione proferre, quam sitis mali, id est vitiosi, invidi et in vitiis habituati? Quamdiu enim homo in malitia permanet, non potest bona loqui bene, seu recta intentione, quemadmodum dictum est: Non potest arbor bona fructus malos facere, nec arbor mala fructus bonos facere. Impius tamen potest in animo pœnitere, et sic bona proferre. Per hoc tamen quod dicit, Quomodo potestis? potius designatur difficultas quam impossibilitas. Juxta quem sensum scriptum est: Si mutare potest Æthiops pellem suam, aut pardus varietates suas, et vos poteritis benefacere, quum didiceritis malum. Ex abundantia enim cordis, id est cogitatione seu affectione quæ magis abundat in mente, os loquitur; prout Eliphaz in Job inquit, Conceptum sermonem tenere quis poterit? Propter quod Eliu ait: Plenus sum sermonibus, et coarctat me spiritus uteri mei. Bonus homo de bono thesauro cordis sui, hoc est ex sapientia, caritate, bona meditatione seu affectione, profert bona verba ac opera, et malus homo de malo thesauro, id est interiori pravitate, profert mala. Unde secundum Philosophum, Ea quæ sunt in voce, sunt earum quæ sunt in anima passionum nota, et verba oris, signa sunt interioris conceptus.
paras.en: [[12:34|O generation of vipers|Progenies viperarum]], that is, serpent-like, deceitful and envious race, [[12:34|how can you speak good things, whereas you are evil?|quomodo potestis bona loqui, quum sitis mali?]] That is, profess the truth about Me, and utter virtuous words with good intention, since you are vicious, envious and hardened in vices? For as long as a man remains in malice he cannot speak good things well, that is, with right intention; as was said: [[Matt 7:18|A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can an evil tree bring forth good fruit|Non potest arbor bona fructus malos facere, nec arbor mala fructus bonos facere]]. Yet the wicked man can repent in his mind and so speak good things. And by His saying 'How can you?' difficulty rather than impossibility is signified. In which sense it is written: [[Jer 13:23|If the Ethiopian can change his skin, or the leopard his spots: you also may do well, when you have learned evil|Si mutare potest Æthiops pellem suam, aut pardus varietates suas, et vos poteritis benefacere, quum didiceritis malum]]. [[12:34|For out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh|ex abundantia enim cordis os loquitur]], that is, out of the thought or affection that most abounds in the mind; as Eliphaz says in Job: [[Job 4:2|who can withhold the words he hath conceived?|Conceptum sermonem tenere quis poterit?]] For which reason Eliu says: [[Job 32:18|I am full of matter to speak of, and the spirit of my bowels straiteneth me|Plenus sum sermonibus, et coarctat me spiritus uteri mei]]. [[12:35|A good man out of a good treasure bringeth forth good things|Bonus homo de bono thesauro profert bona]], out of the good treasure of his heart, that is, out of wisdom, charity, good meditation or affection, good words and works; [[12:35|and an evil man out of an evil treasure bringeth forth evil things|et malus homo de malo thesauro profert mala]], that is, out of inward wickedness. Hence according to the Philosopher, the things in the voice are signs of the passions in the soul, and the words of the mouth are signs of the inward concept.

paras.t: Quam periculosum autem sit mala verba proferre, maxime verba blasphemiæ, declaratur quum subinfertur: Dico autem vobis, quoniam omne verbum otiosum, hoc est, quod justa necessitate seu pia utilitate caret, quod locuti fuerint homines, reddent, id est, dare exigentur, rationem de eo in die judicii (nisi interim pœniteant). Quod tamen non poterunt facere, quoniam tale verbum non habet rationem, sed irrationabiliter dicitur. Si enim rationem haberet, otiosum non esset. Simili modo dicit Apostolus, Unusquisque rationem pro se reddet: et tamen multi non poterunt rationem reddere Deo, ut patet de illo qui non habuit vestem nuptialem, et interrogatus obmutuit. Sed, Unusquisque rationem pro se reddet, id est, reddere exigetur: quod si non poterit, damnabitur. Ex quibus patet horrenda nimis districtio futuri judicii. Si namque de omni ac minimo verbo otioso ratio requiretur a Christo quid erit de verbis nocivis, mendosis, contumeliosis, magnisque peccatis? Ideo monet Apostolus: Omnis sermo (inquiens) malus, ex ore vestro non procedat, sed qui bonus est ad ædificationem. Et Ecclesiastes ait: Cuncta quæ fiunt, adducet Deus in judicium pro omni errato, sive bonum sit, sive malum.
paras.en: And how dangerous it is to utter evil words, above all words of blasphemy, is declared by what follows: [[12:36|But I say unto you, that every idle word|Dico autem vobis, quoniam omne verbum otiosum]], that is, one lacking just necessity or holy usefulness, [[12:36|that men shall speak, they shall render an account for it in the day of judgment|quod locuti fuerint homines, reddent rationem de eo in die judicii]], that is, they will be required to give it (unless they repent meanwhile). Which yet they will not be able to do, since such a word has no reason, but is said unreasonably. For if it had a reason it would not be idle. In like manner the Apostle says: [[Rom 14:12|every one of us shall render account to God for himself|Unusquisque rationem pro se reddet]]; and yet many will not be able to render an account to God, as is clear of him who had not a wedding garment, and when asked was silent[[Matt 22:12||]]. But 'every one shall render account for himself', that is, will be required to render it; and if he cannot, he will be damned. From which appears the exceedingly dreadful strictness of the judgement to come. For if an account is to be required by Christ of every least idle word, what will it be of harmful, lying, insulting words, and of great sins? Therefore the Apostle warns, saying: [[Eph 4:29|Let no evil speech proceed from your mouth; but that which is good, to the edification|Omnis sermo (inquiens) malus, ex ore vestro non procedat, sed qui bonus est ad ædificationem]]. And Ecclesiastes says: [[Eccles 12:14|all things that are done, God will bring into judgment for every error, whether it be good or evil|Cuncta quæ fiunt, adducet Deus in judicium pro omni errato, sive bonum sit, sive malum]].

paras.t: Ex verbis enim tuis, hoc est merito tui sermonis, justificaberis nunc formaliter, et in futuro judicialiter, id est, a Christo justus diceris, si fuerint verba tua justa: quemadmodum in Proverbiis Salomonis legitur, De fructu oris sui unusquisque replebitur bonis; et in Ecclesiastico, Beatus vir qui non est lapsus verbo. Propterea ait Psalmista: Dixi, Custodiam vias meas, ut non delinquam in lingua mea. Et ex verbis tuis condemnaberis, si fuerint prava. Propter quod per Ecclesiasticum asseritur: Multi ceciderunt in ore gladii; sed non sic sicut qui interierunt per linguam suam. Et rursus: Qui custodit os suum, custodit animam suam; qui autem inconsideratus est ad loquendum, sentiet mala. Denique, Jacobo contestante, Universitas iniquitatis lingua constituitur in membris nostris. Secundum Hieronymum, Qui scurrilia replicat, et cachinnis ora dissolvit, et aliquid profert turpitudinis, hic non otiosi verbi, sed criminosi tenebitur reus.
paras.en: [[12:37|For by thy words thou shalt be justified|Ex verbis enim tuis justificaberis]], that is, by the merit of your speech, now formally and in the future judicially, that is, you will be pronounced just by Christ if your words are just; as we read in the Proverbs of Solomon: [[Prov 12:14|By the fruit of his own mouth shall a man be filled with good things|De fructu oris sui unusquisque replebitur bonis]]; and in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 14:1|Blessed is the man that hath not slipped by a word|Beatus vir qui non est lapsus verbo]]. Therefore the Psalmist says: [[Ps 38:2|I said: I will take heed to my ways: that I sin not with my tongue|Dixi, Custodiam vias meas, ut non delinquam in lingua mea]]. [[12:37|and by thy words thou shalt be condemned|Et ex verbis tuis condemnaberis]], if they are wicked. For which reason it is asserted in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 28:22|Many have fallen by the edge of the sword, but not so many as have perished by their own tongue|Multi ceciderunt in ore gladii; sed non sic sicut qui interierunt per linguam suam]]. And again: [[Prov 13:3|He that keepeth his mouth, keepeth his soul: but he that hath no guard on his speech shall meet with evils|Qui custodit os suum, custodit animam suam; qui autem inconsideratus est ad loquendum, sentiet mala]] [Denis cites this too as Ecclesiasticus]. Lastly, as James testifies, the tongue, [[Jas 3:6|a world of iniquity|Universitas iniquitatis lingua]], is set among our members. According to Jerome, he who repeats scurrilous things, and loosens his mouth with guffaws, and utters anything shameful, will be held guilty not of an idle but of a criminal word.

paras.t: Tunc responderunt ei quidam de Scribis et Pharisæis, dicentes: Magister, volumus a te signum videre. Quod dicunt, Magister, ad humilitatem pertinere videtur; quod vero adjiciunt, Volumus, superbiam sonat; sed quod subdunt, Signum videre, ex infidelitate et curiositate procedit. Unde Lucas habet, quod dixerunt hoc tentantes eum. Et jam multa signa viderunt: quid ergo quærunt adhuc signum, id est miraculum per quod certitudinaliter innotescat, quod ipse sit Christus, vel in Deo operans? Dicendum, quod priora signa quæ viderant, parvi penderunt, tanquam quæ fieri possent magica arte, seu opere diaboli: ideo quærunt magnum et penitus supernaturale prodigium. Scribitur enim in Luca, quod quærebant signum de cœlo, videlicet insolitam immutationem in corporibus cœlestibus, sicut factum est tempore Josue, stantibus sole et luna in medio cœli, et tempore Ezechiæ, redeunte sole retrorsum; vel signum in cœlo aerio, scilicet descensum ignis, ut in diebus Eliæ, vel aliud simile. Sed quoniam non humiliter neque fideliter petierunt, eumque magistrum appellaverunt magis timore turbæ, quam ex sinceritate, ideo exauditi non sunt. Propter quod subditur:
paras.en: [[12:38|Then some of the scribes and Pharisees answered him, saying: Master, we would see a sign from thee|Tunc responderunt ei quidam de Scribis et Pharisæis, dicentes: Magister, volumus a te signum videre]]. Their saying 'Master' seems to belong to humility; but what they add, 'we would', sounds of pride; and what follows, 'to see a sign', proceeds from unbelief and curiosity. Hence Luke has it that they said this tempting Him[[Luke 11:16||]]. And they had already seen many signs: why then do they still seek a sign, that is, a miracle by which it might be known with certainty that He is the Christ, or works in God? It must be said that they made little of the earlier signs they had seen, as things that could be done by magic art or the work of the devil: so they seek a great and wholly supernatural wonder. For it is written in Luke that they sought [[Luke 11:16|a sign from heaven|signum de cœlo]], namely an unaccustomed change in the heavenly bodies, as happened in the time of Josue, when the sun and moon stood still in the midst of heaven[[Jos 10:13||]], and in the time of Ezechias, when the sun went back[[4 Kings 20:11||]]; or a sign in the heaven of the air, namely fire coming down, as in the days of Elias[[4 Kings 1:10||]], or something like it. But since they did not ask humbly or faithfully, and called Him master more from fear of the crowd than from sincerity, they were not heard. For which reason it is added:

paras.t: Qui respondens, ait illis: Generatio mala, id est vitiosa, et adultera spirituali adulterio, scilicet recedendo a Deo, de quo ait Psalmista, Perdidisti omnes qui fornicantur abs te; et in Osee, Fornicati sunt a Deo suo. Quemadmodum enim corporale adulterium est, quum alter conjugum alienæ corporaliter commiscetur; sic spirituale adulterium est, quum homo seu anima, Deo relicto, creaturis finaliter adhæret, sicut in Deuteronomio Dominus dixit ad Moysen: Populus iste fornicabitur post deos alienos. Hæc ergo generatio seu populus iste, signum quærit; et signum non dabitur ei, hoc est, ego pro præsenti non dabo ei signum, quo sciat me esse Christum, nisi signum Jonæ prophetæ, id est, quod significatum est per signum seu miraculum quod contigit in Jona. Sicut enim fuit Jonas in ventre ceti tribus diebus et tribus noctibus: juxta illud Jonæ: Miserunt Jonam in mare; et præparavit Dominus piscem grandem ut deglutiret Jonam, et erat in ventre piscis tribus diebus et tribus noctibus; et dixit Dominus pisci, et evomuit Jonam in aridam; sic erit Filius hominis in corde terræ, hoc est sub terra, videlicet in monumento, tribus diebus et tribus noctibus. Quemadmodum Christus dicitur fuisse in monumento vel in limbo, per synecdochen, scilicet ratione suæ partis: nam fuit in tumulo per corpus, in limbo per animam; sic fuit ibi tribus diebus et totidem noctibus, per synecdochen, utpote per unum integrum diem et duorum dierum partes. Conclusio ergo Jonæ in pisce, fuit signum figurativum collocationis Christi in monumento: unde Christus dat Judæis signum resurrectionis. Et loquebatur tunc de signo rememorativo præteriti, non de signo prognostico futuri.
paras.en: [[12:39|Who answering said to them: An evil|Qui respondens, ait illis: Generatio mala]], that is, vicious, [[12:39|and adulterous generation|et adultera]] by spiritual adultery, namely by departing from God, of which the Psalmist says: [[Ps 72:27|thou hast destroyed all them that are disloyal to thee|Perdidisti omnes qui fornicantur abs te]]; and in Osee: [[Osee 4:12|they have committed fornication against their God|Fornicati sunt a Deo suo]]. For as bodily adultery is when one of the spouses joins bodily with another, so spiritual adultery is when a man or a soul, forsaking God, cleaves to creatures as its end; as the Lord said in Deuteronomy to Moses: [[Deut 31:16|this people rising up will go a fornicating after strange gods|Populus iste fornicabitur post deos alienos]]. So this generation, or this people, [[12:39|seeketh a sign: and a sign shall not be given it|signum quærit; et signum non dabitur ei]], that is, I will not for the present give it a sign by which it may know that I am the Christ, [[12:39|but the sign of Jonas the prophet|nisi signum Jonæ prophetæ]], that is, what was signified by the sign or miracle that happened in Jonas. [[12:40|For as Jonas was in the whale's belly three days and three nights|Sicut enim fuit Jonas in ventre ceti tribus diebus et tribus noctibus]]: according to that in Jonas: [[Jon 1:15|cast him into the sea|Miserunt Jonam in mare]]; [[Jon 2:1|Now the Lord prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah|præparavit Dominus piscem grandem ut deglutiret Jonam]], [[Jon 2:1|and Jonah was in the belly of a fish for three days and three nights|et erat in ventre piscis tribus diebus et tribus noctibus]]; [[Jon 2:11|And the Lord spoke to the fish|et dixit Dominus pisci]], [[Jon 2:11|and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land|et evomuit Jonam in aridam]]; [[12:40|so shall the Son of man be in the heart of the earth|sic erit Filius hominis in corde terræ]], that is, under the earth, namely in the tomb, [[12:40|three days and three nights|tribus diebus et tribus noctibus]]. As Christ is said to have been in the tomb or in limbo by synecdoche, that is, by reason of a part of Him (for He was in the tomb in His body, in limbo in His soul), so He was there three days and as many nights by synecdoche, namely one whole day and parts of two days. So the shutting up of Jonas in the fish was a figurative sign of Christ's being laid in the tomb: so Christ gives the Jews the sign of His resurrection. And He was speaking then of a sign that recalls a thing past, not of a sign that foretells a thing to come.

paras.t: De hujusmodi signo rememorativo loquitur Isaias Judæis sui temporis: Ecce, inquiens, virgo concipiet et pariet filium. Tale namque signum non præcedit signatum, sed sequitur.
paras.en: Of a recalling sign of this kind Isaias speaks to the Jews of his time: [[Is 7:14|Behold a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son|Ecce, inquiens, virgo concipiet et pariet filium]]. For such a sign does not go before the thing signified, but follows it.

paras.t: Viri Ninivitæ, qui habitaverunt in Ninive civitate magna, tempore Jonæ, surgent in judicio, hoc est, in die judicii resuscitabuntur, cum generatione ista, id est, sicut et generatio hæc Scribarum et Pharisæorum incredula surrectura est; vel, Surgent, id est apparebunt, in judicio cum generatione ista in conspectu meo. Et condemnabunt eam, id est, suo facto præterito ostendent eam damnatione dignissimam; quia pœnitentiam egerunt in prædicatione Jonc, dicentis: Adhuc quadraginta dies, et Ninive subvertetur. Quo audito rex Ninive surrexit de solio, indutoque sacco, sedit in cinere; similiter principes ejus et vulgus. Timendum est tamen, quod non diu permanserunt in opere pœnitentiali. Et ecce plus quam Jonas hic: id est, ego qui in præsentia vestra sum, et a vobis contemnor, major sum Jona, qui nec miracula fecit in Ninive: ideo Ninivitis estis pejores, duriores, et infideliores.
paras.en: [[12:41|The men of Ninive|Viri Ninivitæ]], who dwelt in Ninive, the great city, in the time of Jonas, [[12:41|shall rise in judgment|surgent in judicio]], that is, will be raised on the day of judgement, [[12:41|with this generation|cum generatione ista]], that is, as this unbelieving generation of scribes and Pharisees will also rise; or, 'shall rise', that is, will appear, in judgement with this generation in My sight. [[12:41|and shall condemn it|Et condemnabunt eam]], that is, by their past deed will show it most worthy of damnation; [[12:41|because they did penance at the preaching of Jonas|quia pœnitentiam egerunt in prædicatione Jonæ]], who said: [[Jon 3:4|Yet forty days, and Ninive shall be destroyed|Adhuc quadraginta dies, et Ninive subvertetur]]. Hearing which, the king of Ninive rose up from his throne and, putting on sackcloth, sat in ashes; likewise his princes and the common people[[Jon 3:6||]]. Yet it is to be feared that they did not long persevere in works of penance. [[12:41|And behold a greater than Jonas here|Et ecce plus quam Jonas hic]]: that is, I, who am present with you and despised by you, am greater than Jonas, who did no miracles in Ninive: so you are worse, harder and more unbelieving than the Ninivites.

paras.t: Regina austri, id est regina Saba: quæ nuncupatur regina austri, quoniam regio ejus fuit in plaga australi, respectu Jerusalem; surget in judicio cum generatione ista, et condemnabit eam: secundum eumdem intellectum quo dictum est hoc de Ninivitis; quia venit cum grandi comitatu et aromatibus pretiosissimis, a finibus terræ, id est a remotis valde locis, in Jerusalem, audire sapientiam Salomonis: ut legitur in libris Regum. Et ecce plus quam Salomon hic, id est Salomone major et sapientior ego. Ille enim potens et sapiens, ego virtus et sapientia Patris; qui etiam quantum ad sapientiam creatam mihi infusam, incomparabiliter Salomonem excedo: et tamen a vobis derideor, dijudicor et contemnor. Ex his constat, quod viri perfecti interdum possunt proprias virtutes commemorare humiliter ad gloriam Dei, ædificationemque proximi. Unus tamen alteri se præferre non debet, sed hoc soli Christo præcipue licuit, tanquam infallibili judici.
paras.en: [[12:42|The queen of the south|Regina austri]], that is, the queen of Saba, who is called queen of the south because her country was in the southern region with respect to Jerusalem; [[12:42|shall rise in judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it|surget in judicio cum generatione ista, et condemnabit eam]]: in the same sense in which this was said of the Ninivites; [[12:42|because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon|quia venit … a finibus terræ … audire sapientiam Salomonis]], with a great train and most precious spices, from the ends of the earth, that is, from very distant places, to Jerusalem, as we read in the books of Kings[[3 Kings 10:1||]]. [[12:42|and behold a greater than Solomon here|Et ecce plus quam Salomon hic]], that is, I, greater and wiser than Solomon. For he was mighty and wise, I am the power and wisdom of the Father[[1 Cor 1:24||]]; who even as to the created wisdom poured into Me surpass Solomon beyond compare: and yet I am mocked, judged and despised by you. From this it is clear that perfect men may sometimes humbly recall their own virtues to the glory of God and the edification of their neighbour. Yet one ought not to prefer himself to another; but this was allowed above all to Christ alone, as an infallible judge.

paras.t: Quum autem immundus spiritus exierit ab homine. Quod istud ad litteram dicatur de populo Judæorum, hine constat, quoó Christus finito hoc exemplo, mox addidit: Sic erit generationi huic pessimæ. Est igitur sensus: Quum autem immundus spiritus exierit ab homine, id est, quando diabolus ejectus est a populo Judæorum, tempore quo suscepit legem Dei per Moysen, et Deum colere cœpit secundum legis tenorem, ambulat per loca arida, id est, tunc circuivit congregationes seu corda gentilium, non habentium rorem gratiæ, vel aquam sapientiæ. Quando enim ab una populo ejicitur dæmon, fortius nititur decipere alium. Quærens requiem, id est stabilem atque perpetuam habitationem in ipsis gentilibus, ut suo semper subdantur obsequio; et non invenit in eis requiem talem. Nam licet ad tempus in idololatria fuerint, tamen ad prædicationem Apostolorum conversi sunt.
paras.en: [[12:43|And when an unclean spirit is gone out of a man|Quum autem immundus spiritus exierit ab homine]]. That this is said literally of the people of the Jews is clear from this, that Christ, having finished this example, at once added: [[12:45|So shall it be also to this wicked generation|Sic erit generationi huic pessimæ]]. The sense, then, is: When the unclean spirit is gone out of a man, that is, when the devil was cast out of the people of the Jews, at the time when it received the law of God through Moses and began to worship God according to the tenor of the law, [[12:43|he walketh through dry places|ambulat per loca arida]], that is, he then went round the gatherings or hearts of the Gentiles, who had not the dew of grace or the water of wisdom. For when the demon is cast out of one people, he strives the harder to deceive another. [[12:43|seeking rest|Quærens requiem]], that is, a stable and lasting dwelling in the Gentiles themselves, so that they might always be subject to his service; [[12:43|and findeth none|et non invenit]] such rest in them. For though they were in idolatry for a time, yet they were converted at the preaching of the Apostles.

paras.t: Tunc dicit, id est dæmon videns gentium conversionem, seque ab eis expelli, quemadmodum Christus alibi dixit: Nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras. Revertar in domum meam, id est Synagogam incredulam, quæ nec Christo neque Apostolis credidit: de qua in Apocalypsi inducitur, Dicunt se Judæos esse, et non sunt, sed sunt synagoga Satanæ; unde exivi, eo tempore quo Deo servivit. In isto sermone seu exemplo, non loquitur Christus de eisdem numero gentilibus et Judæis, sed specie, sicut et Isaias frequenter loquitur de populo Synagogæ. Et veniens invenit eam vacantem, id est a fide atque virtutibus vacuam, otiosam, et suæ inhabitationi patentem, quoniam Deum habitatorem non habuit, prout Salvator prædixit: Relinquetur vobis domus vestra deserta. Et Jeremias: Reliqui, inquit, domum meam, dimisi hæreditatem meam Scopis mundatam, id est exterioribus observantiis legis seu traditionum Pharisaorum purgatam, non intus purificatam, et ornatam, quoad sanctitatis apparentiam, et corporalem compositionem, seu sanctum seculare. Propter quod similes asseruntur sepulcris dealbatis, atque hypocritis.
paras.en: [[12:44|Then he saith|Tunc dicit]], that is, the demon, seeing the conversion of the Gentiles and himself driven out of them, as Christ said elsewhere: [[John 12:31|now shall the prince of this world be cast out|Nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras]]. [[12:44|I will return into my house|Revertar in domum meam]], that is, the unbelieving Synagogue, which believed neither Christ nor the Apostles: of which it is said in the Apocalypse: there are those [[Apoc 2:9|that say they are Jews and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan|Dicunt se Judæos esse, et non sunt, sed sunt synagoga Satanæ]]; [[12:44|whence I came out|unde exivi]], at the time when it served God. In this saying or example Christ does not speak of the same Gentiles and Jews in number, but in kind, as Isaias too often speaks of the people of the Synagogue. [[12:44|And coming he findeth it empty|Et veniens invenit eam vacantem]], that is, void of faith and virtues, idle, and open to his dwelling, since it had not God as its indweller, as the Saviour foretold: [[Matt 23:38|your house shall be left to you, desolate|Relinquetur vobis domus vestra deserta]]. And Jeremias: [[Jer 12:7|I have forsaken my house, I have left my inheritance|Reliqui, inquit, domum meam, dimisi hæreditatem meam]].
