[[12:44|swept|Scopis mundatam]], that is, cleansed by the outward observances of the law or of the traditions of the Pharisees, not purified within, [[12:44|and garnished|et ornatam]], as to the appearance of holiness and outward composure, that is, worldly holiness. For which reason they are declared like whited sepulchres, and hypocrites[[Matt 23:27||]].

paras.t: Tunc vadit diabolus, et assumit septem alios spiritus immundos nequiores se, id est copiam sociorum seu multitudinem tentatorum. Septenario namque universitas designatur. Unde Raphael dixit se esse unum de septem spiritibus stantibus ante Deum. Et intrantes habitant ibi, id est, dæmones corda Judzeorum jam usque ad finem sæculi possident multo copiosius quam antea unquam. Dicuntur autem hi alii septem spiritus nequiores primo, quoniam homo recidivans meretur pejoribus dæmonibus subjici ac impleri, quam ante, dum nondum recidivavit. Nam melius est viam veritatis nescire, quam post agnitionem reverti ad vomitum. Ideo subditur: et fiunt novissima hominis illius pejora prioribus: id est, gravius nunc peccant Judæi non credendo, sed blasphemando Christum C (quem teste Hieronymo, quotidie in suis synagogis tribus vicibus blasphemant, et pro exstirpatione discipulorum Jesu Nazareni ac destructione Romani imperii jugiter orant), quam peccaverunt ante legis receptionem in Ægypto.
paras.en: [[12:45|Then he goeth, and taketh with him seven other spirits more wicked than himself|Tunc vadit … et assumit septem alios spiritus … nequiores se]], the devil, that is, a host of companions, or a multitude of tempters. For the number seven signifies totality. Hence Raphael said that he was [[Tob 12:15|one of the seven, who stand before the Lord|unum de septem spiritibus stantibus ante Deum]]. [[12:45|and they enter in and dwell there|Et intrantes habitant ibi]], that is, the demons possess the hearts of the Jews now until the end of the world far more abundantly than ever before. And these seven other spirits are called more wicked than the first, because a man who falls back deserves to be subjected to and filled with worse demons than before, while he had not yet fallen back. For it is better not to know the way of truth than after knowing it to return to the vomit[[2 Pet 2:21||]]. So it is added: [[12:45|and the last state of that man is made worse than the first|et fiunt novissima hominis illius pejora prioribus]]: that is, the Jews sin more gravely now, not believing but blaspheming Christ (whom, as Jerome testifies, they blaspheme in their synagogues three times daily, and they pray continually for the rooting out of the disciples of Jesus of Nazareth and the destruction of the Roman empire), than they sinned before receiving the law, in Egypt.

paras.t: Sic erit et generationi huic pessimæ, id est, tantum malum eveniet istis incredulis. Ex quo elicitur, quod presens exemplum de uno homine traditum, referatur ad infidelem populum Judæorum: quod tamen moraliter exponi potest de quolibet homine, de cujus corde dæmon expellitur in sacramento Pœnitentiæ vel Baptismi. Et tunc vadit per loca arida, id est, corda bonorum, vitantium fluxum luxuriæ, et corpora propria per abstinentiam macerantium, circuit, querens quem devoret: in quibus non invenit requiem, quoniam viriliter tentationibus reluctantur. Tunc redit ad eum unde exivit, et si invenerit eum vacantem, id est negligentem, scopis mundatum et ornatum, id est solum exterius cultum, non interius reformatum, tunc vadit, et assumit septem alios spiritus, secundum sensum jam præinductum, et ingressi habitant in homine tali: quia a tot dæmonibus homo habitatur, quot mortalibus vitiis implicatur. Unde de Maria Magdalene ejecta dicuntur septem dæmonia. Patet quoque ex his, quod septem sunt vitia principalia et mortalia, et unum simpliciter capitale, puta superbia, omnium vitiorum regina.
paras.en: [[12:45|So shall it be also to this wicked generation|Sic erit et generationi huic pessimæ]], that is, so great an evil will befall these unbelievers. From which it is gathered that the present example, given of one man, refers to the unbelieving people of the Jews: yet it can be expounded morally of any man from whose heart the demon is driven out in the sacrament of Penance or of Baptism. And then he walks through dry places, that is, goes round the hearts of the good, who avoid the flow of lust and wear down their bodies by abstinence, [[1 Pet 5:8|seeking whom he may devour|quærens quem devoret]]: in whom he finds no rest, since they struggle manfully against temptations. Then he returns to him from whom he went out, and if he finds him empty, that is, negligent, swept and garnished, that is, only outwardly adorned, not inwardly reformed, then he goes and takes seven other spirits, in the sense already brought forward, and they go in and dwell in such a man: since a man is inhabited by as many demons as the deadly vices in which he is entangled. Hence of Mary Magdalen[[Mark 16:9||]] [[Luke 8:2|seven devils were gone forth|ejecta dicuntur septem dæmonia]]. It is clear too from this that there are seven chief and deadly vices, and one simply capital, namely pride, the queen of all vices.

paras.t: Adhuc eo loquente ad turbas, videlicet præinducto sermone nondum finito, ecce mater ejus virginea, gloriosa et superdignissima, altissimorum angelorum puritatem transcendens, et fratres, id est cognati vel consobrini Christi, non filii Joseph de alia conjuge, secundum Hieronymum. Est autem consuetudo Scripturæ, idiomatisque Hebræi, ut consobrini et consanguinei, fratres vocentur. Unde Abraham dixit ad Lot: Fratres sumus. Stabant foris, non valentes intrare præ turba: cujus tantus fuit concursus, quod non poterant manducare, ut Marcus habet; querentes loqui ei. Secundum Chrysostomum, diabolus videns quod Jesus ostendebat se Filium Dei, introduxit parentes ejus carnales, ut per illorum præsentiam divinitatem Christi obscuraret. Sed non videtur bene sonare, ut Virgo sanctissima dicatur intrasse aut aliquid peregisse suggestione diaboli. Dicit autem ei quidam. Secundum Hieronymum, iste fuit insidiator, et dixit Christo de præsentia matris suæ, ac fratrum, volens experiri an propter eos omitteret opus Dei seu prædicationem: quod si faceret, argueret eum de carnali affectu. Verumtamen Marcus manifeste habet, quod mater et fratres ejus miserunt quemdam ad eum. Ecce mater tua et fratres tui foris stant, quærentes te alloqui.
paras.en: [[12:46|As he was yet speaking to the multitudes|Adhuc eo loquente ad turbas]], that is, the discourse already given not yet being finished, [[12:46|behold his mother|ecce mater ejus]], virginal, glorious and most supremely worthy, surpassing the purity of the highest angels, [[12:46|and his brethren|et fratres]], that is, the kinsmen or cousins of Christ, not sons of Joseph by another wife, according to Jerome. For it is the custom of Scripture and of the Hebrew idiom that cousins and kinsmen are called brothers. Hence Abraham said to Lot: [[Gen 13:8|we are brethren|Fratres sumus]]. [[12:46|stood without|stabant foris]], unable to get in for the crowd, whose thronging was so great that they could not eat, as Mark has it[[Mark 3:20||]]; [[12:46|seeking to speak to him|quærentes loqui ei]]. According to Chrysostom, the devil, seeing that Jesus was showing Himself to be the Son of God, brought in His kinsfolk according to the flesh, so as to obscure Christ's Godhead by their presence. But it does not seem to sound well that the most holy Virgin should be said to have come in, or done anything, at the suggestion of the devil. [[12:47|And one said unto him|Dixit autem ei quidam]]. According to Jerome, this was a spy, and spoke to Christ of the presence of His mother and brethren, wanting to test whether He would leave the work of God, that is, His preaching, for their sake: and if He did, he would accuse Him of carnal affection. Yet Mark plainly has it that His mother and brethren sent someone to Him[[Mark 3:31||]]. [[12:47|Behold thy mother and thy brethren stand without, seeking thee|Ecce mater tua et fratres tui foris stant, quærentes te]].

paras.t: At ipse respondens dicenti sibi, ait: Quæ est mater mea, et qui sunt fratre. nei? Hoc dicit, non aspernando vel negando matrem carnalem atque cognatos, quasi phantasticum corpus habens, ut Marcion et Manicheius mentiti sunt; sed ad ostendendum quod non solum habeat matrem et fratres carnales, sed etiam spirituales; itemque, ut doceat nos carnalem affectum abjicere, et operi Dei nihil præferre. Ideo subditur: Et extendens manum in discipulos suos, dicit: Ecce mater mea et fratres mei sunt hi. Quod tribus modis intelligi potest. Primo sic: Mater mea et fratres mei sunt, id est tam dilecti ut mater et fratres diliguntur. Secundo sic: Tanto propinquiores sunt mihi, quanto amplius intenti sunt rebus divinis. Tertio sic: Mater mea sunt, id est, per contemplationem internam spiritualiter me concipiunt, et per prædicationem ac vitam exemplarem generant me in cordibus aliorum: sicut Apostolus loquitur, Filioli mei, quos iterum parturio, donec formetur Christus in vobis. Sic ergo generant me, id est, esse et habitare me faciunt in aliorum præcordiis: juxta illud Apostoli, Habitare Christum per fidem in cordibus vestris. Et fratres mei sunt, non solum quia ejusdem naturæ mecum, sed quia opera Patris mei faciunt, mihique affectu et opere similes sunt. Quicumque enim fecerit perseveranter voluntatem Patris mei qui in cœlis est, divinis præceptis seu consiliis obediendo, ipse meus frater et soror et mater est, secundum eumdem sensum quo discipulos meos dixi matrem meam et fratres. Imo felicior est conceptio spiritualis quam carnalis, secundum quod libro de Virginitate asserit Augustinus: Beatior fuit Maria profitendo fidem Christi, quam concipiendo carnem Christi, quia nil ei materna profuisset propinquitas, nisi Christum felicius gestasset corde quam ventre.
paras.en: [[12:48|But he answering him that told him, said: Who is my mother, and who are my brethren?|At ipse respondens dicenti sibi, ait: Quæ est mater mea, et qui sunt fratres mei?]] He says this not scorning or denying His mother according to the flesh and His kinsfolk, as though He had a phantom body, as Marcion and Manichæus lyingly said; but to show that He has not only a mother and brethren according to the flesh, but also spiritual ones; and also to teach us to cast off carnal affection and to prefer nothing to the work of God. So it is added: [[12:49|And stretching forth his hand towards his disciples, he said: Behold my mother and my brethren|Et extendens manum in discipulos suos, dixit: Ecce mater mea et fratres mei]]. Which can be understood in three ways. First thus: they are My mother and My brethren, that is, as dearly loved as a mother and brethren are loved. Secondly thus: they are the nearer to Me the more intent they are on divine things. Thirdly thus: they are My mother, that is, by inward contemplation they conceive Me spiritually, and by preaching and exemplary life they bring Me forth in the hearts of others; as the Apostle says: [[Gal 4:19|My little children, of whom I am in labour again, until Christ be formed in you|Filioli mei, quos iterum parturio, donec formetur Christus in vobis]]. So they bring Me forth, that is, make Me to be and to dwell in the hearts of others; according to that saying of the Apostle: [[Eph 3:17|That Christ may dwell by faith in your hearts|Habitare Christum per fidem in cordibus vestris]]. And they are My brethren, not only because they are of the same nature with Me, but because they do the works of My Father, and are like Me in affection and deed. [[12:50|For whosoever shall do the will of my Father, that is in heaven, he is my brother, and sister, and mother|Quicumque enim fecerit … voluntatem Patris mei qui in cœlis est … ipse meus frater et soror et mater est]], perseveringly, by obeying the divine precepts or counsels, in the same sense in which I called My disciples My mother and brethren. Indeed spiritual conception is happier than carnal, according to what Augustine asserts in the book On Virginity: Mary was more blessed in professing the faith of Christ than in conceiving the flesh of Christ, since her nearness as mother would have profited her nothing had she not borne Christ more happily in her heart than in her womb.

13.title: Expositio capituli tertiidecimi: In illo die exiens Jesus de domo, sedebat secus mare
13.title_en: Exposition of the thirteenth chapter: The same day Jesus going out of the house, sat by the sea side

paras.t: In illo die exiens Jesus de domo. Si prudenter pensemus verba evangelistarum Lucæ et Marci, compellimur hoc loco accipere diem, non pro determinato die naturali aut artificiali, sed pro tempore, sicut et Prophetæ communiter diem accipiunt; Apostolus quoque, quum ait: Nox præcessit, dies autem appropinquavit. In illo itaque die, id est tempore quo dicta et facta sunt in præcedenti capitulo recitata, exiens Jesus de domo in qua prædicavit, nec ab omnibus propter eorum multitudinem audiri valebat, sedebat secus mare, videlicet in littore maris, forsitan Galilææ. Et congregatæ sunt ad eum turbæ multæ propter diversas causas, ut dictum est, ita ut naviculam ascendens, sederet in navi, quatenus melius audiretur ab omnibus in littore stantibus. Et omnis turba stabat in littore.
paras.en: [[13:1|The same day Jesus going out of the house|In illo die exiens Jesus de domo]]. If we weigh carefully the words of the evangelists Luke and Mark, we are compelled here to take "day" not for a fixed day, natural or artificial [that is, a full day of twenty-four hours, or the daylight hours only], but for a time, as the Prophets commonly take "day"; and the Apostle too, when he says: [[Rom 13:12|The night is passed And the day is at hand|Nox præcessit, dies autem appropinquavit]]. [[13:1|The same day|In illo die]], then, that is, at the time when the things said and done that are recorded in the preceding chapter took place, [[13:1|Jesus going out of the house|exiens Jesus de domo]] in which He had preached, and where He could not be heard by all because of their number, [[13:1|sat by the sea side|sedebat secus mare]], that is, on the shore of the sea, perhaps of Galilee. [[13:2|And great multitudes were gathered together unto him|Et congregatæ sunt ad eum turbæ multæ]] for various reasons, as has been said, [[13:2|so that he went up into a boat and sat|ita ut naviculam ascendens, sederet]] in the boat, so as to be better heard by all those standing on the shore. [[13:2|and all the multitude stood on the shore|Et omnis turba stabat in littore]].

paras.t: Et locutus est eis multa in parabolis, dicens. Multas ob causas loquitur Christus in parabolis. Primo, ut veritas abscondatur indignis, juxta illud: Nolite sanctum dare canibus. Secundo, ut studiosis detur occasio bonæ exercitationis seu diligentis inquisitionis. Tertio, ut discamus ex corporalibus ac sensibilibus spiritualia atque divina intelligere.
paras.en: [[13:3|And he spoke to them many things in parables, saying|Et locutus est eis multa in parabolis, dicens]]. Christ speaks in parables for many reasons. First, that the truth may be hidden from the unworthy, according to that saying: [[Matt 7:6|Give not that which is holy to dogs|Nolite sanctum dare canibus]]. Second, that the studious may be given occasion for good exercise, or diligent searching. Third, that we may learn to understand spiritual and divine things from bodily and sensible ones.

paras.t: Exiit qui seminat, seminare. In expositione hujus parabolæ, non præstatur nobis libertas qualitercumque exponendi, vel propriam rationem sequendi, sed Christi summi magistri expositionem sequi debemus. Exiit qui seminat, id est, Christus seminans in mundo verbum evangelicæ legis, exiit de cœlo in terram, juxta illud Joannis, Exivi a Patre, et veni in mundum; et in Psalmo, A summo cœlo egressio ejus. Vel, exiit de utero Virginis, apparendo in mundo, secundum illud: Ipse tanquam sponsus procedens de thalamo suo. Exitus autem convenit Christo ratione humanitatis assumptæ, imo et ex parte divinæ naturæ, quia secundum Augustinum et Hilarium, eo ipso dicitur Filius a Patre exire, quo generatur ab ipso. Propter quod Michæas inquit: Egressus ejus ab initio, a diebus æternitatis. Quantum ad operationem quoque convenit Christo ex parte divinæ naturæ, ut secundum quod Deus dicatur exire, id est in actum procedere, non locum mutare. Exiit ergo seminare, id est ad seminandum seu spargendum in cordibus hominum verbum salutis et gratiæ, prout apud Joannem testatur: Ego in hoc natus sum, et ad hoc veni in mundum, ut testimonium perhibeam veritati.
paras.en: [[13:3|the sower went forth to sow|exiit qui seminat, seminare]]. In expounding this parable we are not given freedom to explain it however we please, or to follow our own reasoning; we must follow the explanation of Christ, the supreme Master. [[13:3|the sower went forth|Exiit qui seminat]], that is, Christ, sowing in the world the word of the Gospel law, went forth from heaven to earth, according to that saying of John: [[John 16:28|I came forth from the Father and am come into the world|Exivi a Patre, et veni in mundum]]; and in the Psalm: [[Ps 18:7|His going out is from the end of heaven|A summo cœlo egressio ejus]]. Or: He went forth from the womb of the Virgin, appearing in the world, according to that saying: [[Ps 18:6|he as a bridegroom coming out of his bridechamber|Ipse tanquam sponsus procedens de thalamo suo]]. Going forth belongs to Christ by reason of the humanity He assumed, and indeed on the side of the divine nature as well; for according to Augustine and Hilary, the Son is said to go forth from the Father by the very fact that He is begotten of Him. Hence Micheas says: [[Mich 5:2|his going forth is from the beginning, from the days of eternity|Egressus ejus ab initio, a diebus æternitatis]]. As regards activity also, going forth befits Christ on the side of the divine nature, in the sense in which God is said to go forth, that is, to proceed into act, not to change place. He [[13:3|went forth to sow|Exiit ergo seminare]], then, that is, to sow or scatter in the hearts of men the word of salvation and grace, as He testifies in John: [[John 18:37|For this was I born, and for this came I into the world; that I should give testimony to the truth|Ego in hoc natus sum, et ad hoc veni in mundum, ut testimonium perhibeam veritati]].

paras.t: Et dum seminat, id est, doctrinam evangelicam prædicavit Judæis, alia, id est quædam semina seu verba prædicationis: semen enim est verbum Dei, ut Lucas habet; ceciderunt secus viam, id est in corda carnalium hominum, qui in terrenis versantur, et vias sæculi latas perambulant, vanitatibusque intendunt. De qualibus scriptum est: Domine, recedentes a te in terra scribentur. Et venerunt volucres cœli, id est aereæ potestates, de quibus Paulus: Non est nobis colluctatio adversus carnem et sanguinem, sed adversus principes et potestates, contra spiritualia nequitiæ in cœlestibus. Dicuntur autem diaboli volucres cœli: primo, propter subtilitatem naturæ; secundo, propter habitationem eorum in aere caliginoso; tertio, ratione inordinati ascensus eorum ad alta ex tumore superbiæ. Interdum tamen per volucrem intelligitur Christus, ratione suæ altissimæ contemplationis: ut quum Isaias ait, loquens de Deo, Vocans ab oriente avem: quod Hieronymus ad litteram exponit de Christo. Et in Job, Semitam ignoravit avis: ubi Gregorius per avem intelligit Christum. In parabolica quippe locutione, interdum per eamdem rem significantur diversa, secundum diversam proprietatem rei: quemadmodum per leonem, ratione fortitudinis, intelligitur Christus, ut in Apocalypsi patet, Ecce vicit leo de tribu Juda; per leonem quoque, ratione crudelitatis, signatur diabolus, ut Petrus inquit: Adversarius vester diabolus tanquam leo rugiens circuit. Hi itaque volucres comederunt ea, id est, suarum tentationum suggestionibus abstulerunt verba Dei de cordibus prædictorum.
paras.en: [[13:4|And whilst he soweth|Et dum seminat]], that is, preached the teaching of the Gospel to the Jews, [[13:4|some|quædam]], that is, certain seeds or words of preaching (for [[Luke 8:11|The seed is the word of God|semen enim est verbum Dei]], as Luke has it), [[13:4|fell by the way side|ceciderunt secus viam]], that is, into the hearts of carnal men, who busy themselves with earthly things, walk the broad ways of the world, and give their minds to vanities. Of such it is written: O Lord, [[Jer 17:13|they that depart from thee, shall be written in the earth|recedentes a te in terra scribentur]]. [[13:4|and the birds of the air came|Et venerunt volucres cœli]], that is, the powers of the air, of whom Paul says: [[Eph 6:12|our wrestling is not against flesh and blood|Non est nobis colluctatio adversus carnem et sanguinem]], but [[Eph 6:12|against principalities and powers|adversus principes et potestates]], [[Eph 6:12|against the spirits of wickedness in the high places|contra spiritualia nequitiæ in cœlestibus]]. The devils are called birds of the air: first, because of the subtlety of their nature; second, because they dwell in the misty air; third, by reason of their disordered climbing to the heights out of the swelling of pride. Sometimes, however, Christ is understood by a bird, by reason of His most high contemplation: as when Isaias says, speaking of God, [[Is 46:11|Who call a bird from the east|Vocans ab oriente avem]], which Jerome expounds literally of Christ. And in Job: [[Job 28:7|The bird hath not known the path|Semitam ignoravit avis]], where Gregory understands Christ by the bird. For in parabolic speech the same thing sometimes signifies different things, according to the different properties of the thing: as by the lion, by reason of its strength, Christ is understood, as is plain in the Apocalypse: "[[Apoc 5:5|behold the lion of the tribe of Juda|Ecce vicit leo de tribu Juda]] has prevailed"; and by the lion, by reason of its cruelty, the devil is also signified, as Peter says: [[1 Pet 5:8|your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, goeth about|Adversarius vester diabolus tanquam leo rugiens circuit]]. These birds, then, [[13:4|ate them up|comederunt ea]], that is, by the suggestions of their temptations took away the words of God from the hearts of the men just described.

paras.t: Alia autem semina, id est verba a Christo prolata, ceciderunt in petrosa, id est in corda lapidea, dura, rebellia, rore gratiæ destituta, ubi non habebant terram multam, id est mentes capaces, fructiferas, quæ instar profundæ terræ possint fructificare in bono; et continuo exorta sunt, id est, semina ista repente creverunt in fructum compunctionis instabilem, non firmum aut fixum, quia non habebant altitudinem terræ, id est fundamentum profundum, ita quod verba Dei non introierunt intima cordis eorum, nec radicem fecundam habuerunt in corde. Videmus quippe, quod corda dura et saxea sæpenumero audito verbo Dei de horrore futuri judicii ac tormentis inferni, compunctionem quamdam concipiunt, et aliquid boni agere ordiuntur; sed non perseverant in compunctione et opere bono. Ideo dicit Scriptura: Cor durum male habebit in novissimo, et cor nequam gravabitur in doloribus. Sole autem orto, id est igne tribulationis ac tentationis exsurgente, æstuaverunt, id est, semina ista infructuosa effecta sunt, et tribulationis calore consumpta. Et quia non habebant radicem, id est firmum atque fecundum fundamentum in corde, videlicet gratiam habitualem et stabilem devotionem, aruerunt, id est, a compunctione et opere bono defecerunt. Unde Lucas ait, quod semen aruit, quia non habebat humorem, videlicet gratiæ alimentum, quod mentem fecundat sicut arborem humor aquarum.
paras.en: [[13:5|And other some fell upon stony ground|Alia autem ceciderunt in petrosa]]: other seeds, that is, words spoken by Christ, fell upon stony ground, that is, into hearts of stone, hard, rebellious, without the dew of grace, [[13:5|where they had not much earth|ubi non habebant terram multam]], that is, minds with room in them and fruitful, which like deep soil could bear fruit in good; [[13:5|and they sprung up immediately|et continuo exorta sunt]], that is, these seeds suddenly grew into a fruit of compunction that was unstable, not firm or fixed, [[13:5|because they had no deepness of earth|quia non habebant altitudinem terræ]], that is, no deep foundation, so that the words of God did not enter the depths of their heart, nor have a fruitful root in the heart. For we see that hard and stony hearts, on hearing the word of God about the horror of the judgment to come and the torments of hell, often conceive a certain compunction and begin to do some good; but they do not persevere in compunction and good works. Therefore Scripture says: [[Ecclus 3:27|A hard heart shall fear evil at the last|Cor durum male habebit in novissimo]], and [[Ecclus 3:29|A wicked heart shall be laden with sorrows|cor nequam gravabitur in doloribus]]. [[13:6|And when the sun was up|Sole autem orto]], that is, when the fire of tribulation and temptation arose, [[13:6|they were scorched|æstuaverunt]], that is, these seeds became fruitless, consumed by the heat of tribulation. [[13:6|and because they had not root|Et quia non habebant radicem]], that is, a firm and fruitful foundation in the heart, namely habitual grace [that is, grace abiding in the soul as a settled quality] and steady devotion, [[13:6|they withered away|aruerunt]], that is, they fell away from compunction and good works. Hence Luke says that the seed [[Luke 8:6|withered away, because it had no moisture|aruit, quia non habebat humorem]], namely the nourishment of grace, which makes the mind fruitful as the moisture of the waters does a tree.

paras.t: Alia autem ceciderunt in spinas, id est, in corda sollicitudinibus vitæ præsentis amara, curis sæculi puncta, et divitiarum angustiis lacerata. Istæ expositiones postea tanguntur a Christo. Et creverunt spinæ, id est, curæ superfluæ in anima ortæ sunt, et suffocaverunt ea, id est, verba Dei amoverunt ab anima: quia dum tales de spiritualibus meditari incipiunt, statim cogitationes terrenæ et anxiæ se commiscent, et bonas meditationes impediunt.
paras.en: [[13:7|And others fell among thorns|Alia autem ceciderunt in spinas]], that is, into hearts made bitter by the anxieties of the present life, pricked by the cares of the world, and torn by the straits of riches. These explanations are touched on afterwards by Christ. [[13:7|and the thorns grew up|Et creverunt spinæ]], that is, superfluous cares sprang up in the soul, [[13:7|and choked them|et suffocaverunt ea]], that is, removed the words of God from the soul: for when such people begin to meditate on spiritual things, at once earthly and anxious thoughts mingle with them and hinder good meditations.

paras.t: Alia vero semina cœlestis verbi, ceciderunt in terram bonam, id est in cor fidele, docile atque tractabile; et dabant fructum, id est, in opus bonum creverunt, sed diversimode secundum diversam dispositionem cordium recipientium ea: ideo subditur, aliud semen, id est quoddam verbum Dei, dedit fructum centesimum, id est, habuit opus perfectum: sicut in spiritualibus, divinis atque heroicis viris. Talis est fructus castitatis in virginibus. Aliud semen protulit fructum sexagesimum, id est, opus proficiens habuit: sicut in his qui conantur quotidie tendere de virtute in virtutem, et de statu proficientium ad statum perfectorum pertingere. Aliud semen attulit fructum tricesimum, id est, opus bonum habuit, sed imperfectum, inchoativum, ac animale, ut in incipientibus.
paras.en: [[13:8|And others fell upon good ground|Alia vero semina cœlestis verbi, ceciderunt in terram bonam]]: other seeds of the heavenly word, that is, fell into a heart that is faithful, teachable and docile; [[13:8|and they brought forth fruit|et dabant fructum]], that is, grew into good works, but in different ways according to the different dispositions of the hearts that received them. So it is added: [[13:8|some|aliud]] seed, that is, a certain word of God, gave [[13:8|an hundred fold|centesimum]], that is, had perfect works, as in spiritual, godly and heroic men. Such is the fruit of chastity in virgins. Some seed brought forth [[13:8|sixty fold|sexagesimum]], that is, had works that were making progress, as in those who strive daily to go [[Ps 83:8|from virtue to virtue|de virtute in virtutem]] and to rise from the state of the proficient to the state of the perfect. Some seed bore [[13:8|thirty fold|tricesimum]], that is, had good works, but imperfect, only begun, and still of the senses [Latin animale, "animal" as opposed to "spiritual"], as in beginners.

paras.t: Porro, quod dicitur de fructu centesimo, specialiter solet referri ad statum virginalem; et quod dicitur de fructu sexagesimo, ad statum vidualem; quod vero de fructu tricesimo dicitur, ad statum conjugalem. Non tamen simpliciter et universaliter referri potest ad personas statuum prædictorum, quum sæpe in statu inferiori inveniantur perfectiores homines, quam in statu superiori. Tamen, comparando statum ad statum, sic se habet castitas virginalis ad vidualem, eam excedendo in merito, sicut centum ad sexaginta; et ita se habet castitas vidualis ad conjugalem, sicut sexaginta ad triginta. Nam finis ad quem ordinatur seminatio seminis hujus, id est prædicatio verbi divini, est homines a carnalibus ad spiritualia ducere: quod multo perfectius fit in continentia virginali, quam viduali, et in viduali, quam in conjugali. Unde dicit Apostolus: Virgo cogitat quæ Domini sunt, ut sit sancta corpore et spiritu; quæ autem nupta est, cogitat quæ sunt mundi, quomodo placeat viro; et divisa est.
paras.en: Further, what is said of the hundredfold fruit is usually referred especially to the state of virginity; what is said of the sixtyfold, to the state of widowhood; and what is said of the thirtyfold, to the married state. Yet it cannot be referred simply and universally to the persons in these states, since more perfect people are often found in a lower state than in a higher. Still, comparing state with state, virginal chastity stands to that of widows, surpassing it in merit, as a hundred to sixty; and the chastity of widows stands to married chastity as sixty to thirty. For the end to which the sowing of this seed, that is, the preaching of the divine word, is ordered is to lead men from carnal things to spiritual: and this is done far more perfectly in virginal continence than in that of widows, and in that of widows than in the married. Hence the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 7:34|the virgin thinketh on the things of the Lord: that she may be holy both in body and in spirit. But she that is married thinketh on the things of the world: how she may please her husband|Virgo cogitat quæ Domini sunt, ut sit sancta corpore et spiritu; quæ autem nupta est, cogitat quæ sunt mundi, quomodo placeat viro]]; and she is divided[[1 Cor 7:33||]].

paras.t: Consequenter Christus admonet auditores ad diligentem ac mysticam intelligentiam prædictorum. Qui habet aures audiendi, id est aures mentales, quibus verbum Dei salubriter percipitur, atque audiendo servatur et adimpletur, sicut alio in loco ait: Qui ex Deo est, verba Dei audit: audiat.
paras.en: Next, Christ urges His hearers to a careful and mystical understanding of what has been said. [[13:9|He that hath ears to hear|Qui habet aures audiendi]], that is, the ears of the mind, by which the word of God is received to salvation and, by being heard, is kept and fulfilled, as He says in another place: [[John 8:47|He that is of God heareth the words of God|Qui ex Deo est, verba Dei audit]]; [[13:9|let him hear|audiat]].

paras.t: Et accedentes discipuli, id est duodecim Apostoli, ut Marcus refert. Accesserunt autem ad Jesum, non in naviculam, vel actu prædicationis durante, sed quum esset separatus et vacans a populo. Unde Marcus: Quum esset (inquit) singularis, accesserunt ad eum. Dixerunt ei: Quare in parabolis, id est obscuris et metaphoricis sermonibus, loqueris eis, videlicet turbæ? Denique parabola est dissimilium rerum sub quadam similitudine facta comparatio.
paras.en: [[13:10|And his disciples came|Et accedentes discipuli]], that is, the twelve Apostles, as Mark relates[[Mark 4:10||]]. They came to Jesus, not in the boat or while the preaching was going on, but when He was apart and free of the people. Hence Mark says: [[Mark 4:10|when he was alone|Quum esset singularis]], they came to Him. [[13:10|and said to him: Why speakest thou to them in parables|dixerunt ei: Quare in parabolis loqueris eis?]]: why in parables, that is, in obscure and metaphorical speech, do You speak to them, namely the crowd? A parable, to be precise, is a comparison of unlike things made under a certain likeness.

paras.t: Qui respondens, ait illis: Quia vobis Apostolis datum est, per gratiam specialem, nosse, id est, ut noscatis, et me docente intelligatis, mysteria, id est sacra secreta seu spirituales ac mysticos intellectus, regni cœlorum, id est Ecclesiæ militantis, vel divinæ Scripturæ, in qua cœleste regnum nuntiatur, et spiritualium deliciarum epulæ continentur quasi in paradiso Dei, secundum Damascenum. Illis autem, id est turbis, non est datum, propter incapacitatem et culpam eorum, vel quia ad gratiam tantam prædestinati non sunt. Apostolis namque tanquam post Christum primis ac summis doctoribus, et quasi fundamentis Ecclesiæ, pandenda erant divina secreta, ut de sua plenitudine influerent aliis. De eis siquidem in Apocalypsi legitur: Murus civitatis habens fundamenta duodecim, et in ipsis duodecim nomina Apostolorum. Qui enim habet fidem sinceram, bonam intentionem, vel humilitatem; vel, Qui habet, id est, qui Deo gratus est, recognoscendo omne bonum suum esse a Deo; dabitur ei gratia major, sapientia plenior, vita perfectior, et abundabit spiritualibus bonis, juxta illud in Psalmo: Gloria et divitiæ in domo ejus. Ideo vobis discipulis meis fidelibus datur cognitio mysteriorum cœlestium. Qui autem non habet, id est, qui modicum habet, quod comparatione magnorum donorum pro nihilo reputatur. Vel, Qui non habet, id est, Deo datori ingratus est, non attendens unde acceperit, sed sic glorians quasi non acceperit. Vel, Qui non habet fidem et humilitatem. Et quod habet auferetur ab eo, id est, cetera dona sibi divinitus præstita meretur amittere. Ideo increduli et perversi Judæi non meruerunt incrementum, sed detrimentum spiritualis intelligentiæ cœlestiumque bonorum.
paras.en: [[13:11|Who answered and said to them: Because to you|Qui respondens, ait illis: Quia vobis]] Apostles [[13:11|it is given|datum est]], by special grace, [[13:11|to know|nosse]], that is, that you may know and, with Me teaching you, understand, [[13:11|the mysteries|mysteria]], that is, the sacred secrets, or the spiritual and mystical senses, [[13:11|of the kingdom of heaven|regni cœlorum]], that is, of the Church militant, or of divine Scripture, in which the heavenly kingdom is proclaimed and the feasts of spiritual delights are contained as in the paradise of God, according to Damascene. [[13:11|but to them it is not given|illis autem non est datum]], that is, to the crowds, because of their incapacity and fault, or because they are not predestined to so great a grace. For the divine secrets had to be laid open to the Apostles, as the first and highest teachers after Christ and as the foundations of the Church, so that from their fullness they might flow into others. Of them indeed we read in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 21:14|the wall of the city had twelve foundations: And in them, the twelve names|Murus civitatis habens fundamenta duodecim, et in ipsis duodecim nomina]] of the Apostles. [[13:12|For he that hath|Qui enim habet]] sincere faith, good intention, or humility; or, he that hath, that is, he who is grateful to God, acknowledging that all his good is from God, [[13:12|to him shall be given|dabitur ei]] greater grace, fuller wisdom, a more perfect life, [[13:12|and he shall abound|et abundabit]] in spiritual goods, according to that saying in the Psalm: [[Ps 111:3|Glory and wealth shall be in his house|Gloria et divitiæ in domo ejus]]. That is why to you, My faithful disciples, the knowledge of the heavenly mysteries is given. [[13:12|but he that hath not|Qui autem non habet]], that is, he who has little, which in comparison with great gifts is counted as nothing. Or, he that hath not, that is, he who is ungrateful to God the giver, not considering whence he received, but glorying as if he had not received[[1 Cor 4:7||]]. Or, he that hath not faith and humility. [[13:12|from him shall be taken away that also which he hath|et quod habet auferetur ab eo]], that is, he deserves to lose the other gifts granted him by God. Therefore the unbelieving and perverse Jews did not merit an increase, but a loss, of spiritual understanding and of heavenly goods.

paras.t: Ideo in parabolis loquor eis, quia videntes oculo corporali, non vident sincere, oculo intellectuali, quoniam excæcavit eos malitia eorum. Vel: Videntes facta et conversationem atque miracula Christi, non vident, id est, non considerant ea esse a Deo, sed principi dæmonum deputant ea. Vel: Videntes, id est, Scripturas veteris Testamenti litteraliter et superficialiter intelligentes, non vident spiritualem et verum intellectum earum: propter quod occiduntur a littera. Et audientes prædicationem meam, vel verba legis ac Prophetarum, auribus corporis, non audiunt ea auribus cordis, debite auscultando, neque intelligunt ea salubriter.
paras.en: [[13:13|Therefore do I speak to them in parables: because seeing|Ideo in parabolis loquor eis, quia videntes]] with the bodily eye, [[13:13|they see not|non vident]] truly with the eye of the understanding, because [[Wis 2:21|their own malice blinded them|excæcavit eos malitia eorum]]. Or: seeing the deeds, the manner of life and the miracles of Christ, they see not, that is, they do not consider that these are from God, but ascribe them to the prince of devils. Or: seeing, that is, understanding the Scriptures of the Old Testament literally and on the surface, they do not see their spiritual and true sense; and so they are slain by the letter[[2 Cor 3:6||]]. [[13:13|and hearing|Et audientes]] My preaching, or the words of the Law and the Prophets, with the ears of the body, [[13:13|they hear not|non audiunt]] them with the ears of the heart, by listening as they ought, [[13:13|neither do they understand|neque intelligunt]] them to their salvation.

paras.t: Ut adimpleatur in eis prophetia Isaiæ, dicentis: Auditu corporali audietis, o infideles Judæi, eloquia Christi parabolicosque sermones, et non intelligetis ea veraciter, scilicet parabolarum mysteria; et videntes videbitis opera humanitatemque Christi, et non videbitis oculo interiori operum qualitatem, et ejus divinitatem. Incrassatum est enim, id est, obtusum et carnale factum est, cor populi hujus, terrenis ac sensibilibus inhærendo, prout in Deuteronomio scribitur: Incrassatus est dilectus, et recalcitravit; et auribus graviter audierunt, id est, ad audiendum verbum Dei aure mentali tardi fuerunt, et oculos suos interiores, videlicet intellectum, clauserunt, id est, influentiæ seu irradiationi lucis divinæ instructionisque Christi incapacem fecerunt, ponendo obicem gratiæ Dei, videlicet contemptum et infidelitatem. Peccata enim separant mentem a Deo, et sunt velut murus seu januæ intermediæ inter mentem ac Deum. Propter quod Jeremias fatetur: Peccata vestra prohibuerunt bonum a vobis. De talibus scriptum est: Dicunt Deo, Recede a nobis, scientiam viarum tuarum nolumus. Nequando oculis cordis videant veritatem, et auribus interioribus audiant salutarem doctrinam, et corde intelligant, id est, intus legant, atque subtiliter penetrent spiritualem sensum divinorum verborum; et convertantur ab errore ad veritatem, et a caducis rebus ad summum ac incommutabile bonum, et sanem eos, liberando intellectum a falsitate, voluntatem a pravitate, animam ab omni læsione peccati. De qua sanitate Jeremias precatur: Sana me, Domine, et sanabor; et Psalmista, Sana animam meam, quia peccavi tibi.
paras.en: [[13:14|And the prophecy of Isaias is fulfilled in them, who saith|Ut adimpleatur in eis prophetia Isaiæ, dicentis]][[Is 6:9||]]: [[13:14|By hearing you shall hear|Auditu corporali audietis]] with bodily hearing, O unbelieving Jews, the words of Christ and His parabolic sayings, [[13:14|and shall not understand|et non intelligetis]] them truly, namely the mysteries of the parables; [[13:14|and seeing you shall see|et videntes videbitis]] the works and the humanity of Christ, [[13:14|and shall not perceive|et non videbitis]] with the inward eye the character of the works, and His divinity. [[13:15|For the heart of this people is grown gross|Incrassatum est enim cor populi hujus]]: grown gross, that is, become dull and carnal, by clinging to earthly and sensible things, as it is written in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 32:15|The beloved grew fat, and kicked|Incrassatus est dilectus, et recalcitravit]]; [[13:15|and with their ears they have been dull of hearing|et auribus graviter audierunt]], that is, they were slow to hear the word of God with the ear of the mind, [[13:15|and their eyes they have shut|et oculos suos clauserunt]]: their inner eyes, namely the understanding, that is, they made them incapable of the inflowing or shining of the divine light and of Christ's teaching, by putting an obstacle to the grace of God, namely contempt and unbelief. For sins separate the mind from God[[Is 59:2||]], and are like a wall or doors set between the mind and God. Hence Jeremias declares: [[Jer 5:25|your sins have withholden good things from you|Peccata vestra prohibuerunt bonum a vobis]]. Of such it is written: They say [[Job 21:14|to God: Depart from us, we desire not the knowledge of thy ways|Deo, Recede a nobis, scientiam viarum tuarum nolumus]]. [[13:15|lest at any time they should see|Nequando oculis cordis videant]] the truth with the eyes of the heart, [[13:15|and hear|et auribus interioribus audiant]] saving doctrine with the inner ears, [[13:15|and understand with their heart|et corde intelligant]], that is, read within [Denis derives intelligere from *intus legere*, "to read within"], and penetrate keenly the spiritual sense of the divine words, [[13:15|and be converted|et convertantur]] from error to truth, and from perishable things to the highest and unchangeable good, [[13:15|and I should heal them|et sanem eos]], freeing the understanding from falsehood, the will from perversity, and the soul from every wound of sin. For this health Jeremias prays: [[Jer 17:14|Heal me, O Lord, and I shall be healed|Sana me, Domine, et sanabor]]; and the Psalmist: [[Ps 40:5|heal my soul, for I have sinned against thee|Sana animam meam, quia peccavi tibi]].

paras.t: Vestri autem, o discipuli mei, beati sunt jam in spe, oculi interiores, beatificandi in re per claram divinæ essentiæ visionem, quia vident, id est, recte intelligunt, et fidei lumine illustrantur; et aures vestræ, de quibus jam dixi: Qui habet aures audiendi, audiat. Unde et Isaias inquit: Dominus Deus meus aperuit mihi aurem, ego autem non contradico. Hæ itaque aures vestræ beatæ sunt, quoniam audiunt verba mea fideliter. Beati enim qui audiunt verbum Dei et custodiunt illud.
paras.en: [[13:16|But blessed are your|Vestri autem beati]], O My disciples, already in hope, [[13:16|eyes|oculi]], your inner eyes, which are to be made blessed in reality by the clear vision of the divine essence, [[13:16|because they see|quia vident]], that is, understand rightly and are enlightened by the light of faith; [[13:16|and your ears|et aures vestræ]], of which I have already said: [[13:9|He that hath ears to hear, let him hear|Qui habet aures audiendi, audiat]]. Hence Isaias too says: [[Is 50:5|The Lord God hath opened my ear, and I do not resist|Dominus Deus meus aperuit mihi aurem, ego autem non contradico]]. These ears of yours, then, are blessed, [[13:16|because they hear|quoniam audiunt]] My words faithfully. For [[Luke 11:28|blessed are they who hear the word of God and keep it|Beati enim qui audiunt verbum Dei et custodiunt illud]].

paras.t: Amen quippe dico vobis, quia multi Prophetæ et justi, qui futuram Dei incarnationem spiritu prophetali, seu fide agnoverunt, cupierunt videre, id est, optaverunt, si fuisset possibile, videre, quæ vos videtis, videlicet Christum in carne, et conversationem ac signa ipsius; et non viderunt ea præsentialiter, corporali intuitu, sicut vos. Unde et Simeon justus pro suo desiderio quo Christum videre optavit, responsum accepit a Spiritu Sancto non visurum se mortem, donec videret Christum Domini.
paras.en: [[13:17|For, amen, I say to you, many prophets and just men|Amen quippe dico vobis, quia multi Prophetæ et justi]], who knew of God's future incarnation by the spirit of prophecy or by faith, [[13:17|have desired to see|cupierunt videre]], that is, wished, had it been possible, to see [[13:17|the things that you see|quæ vos videtis]], namely Christ in the flesh, and His life and signs; [[13:17|and have not seen them|et non viderunt]] present before them, with bodily sight, as you do. Hence also Simeon, the just man[[Luke 2:25||]], because of his longing to see Christ, [[Luke 2:26|had received an answer from the Holy Ghost, that he should not see death|responsum accepit a Spiritu Sancto non visurum se mortem]], until he should see [[Luke 2:26|the Christ of the Lord|Christum Domini]].

paras.t: Sed quæritur, de quo visu dicat Salvator, Prophetas et justos voluisse videre quæ viderunt Apostoli, et non viderunt. Non enim videtur de spirituali visu posse intelligi, quia Prophetæ visione intellectuali et imaginaria viderunt omnia quæ de Christo prænuntiaverunt. Intelligentia enim opus est in visione, ut Daniel ait. Unde quum Isaias Babylonis vastitatem prædiceret: Corrui, inquit, quum viderem. Multo magis vidit Christum in spiritu, quando dicebat de ejus incarnatione, Puer natus est nobis, et multa similia. Jeremias quoque, quum dixit: Quare quasi colonus venturus es in terra? Tunc enim imaginaria visione vidit Christum. Denique Salvator ipse inquit: Abraham pater vester exsultavit ut videret diem meum; vidit, et gavisus est. Nec videtur posse intelligi de visu corporali, quia de illo non intelligitur quod Apostolis dictum est: Vestri beati oculi, quia vident. Sic enim Judas et reprobi Judæi viderunt. Puto ergo quod intelligendum sit verbum prædictum de visu interiori conjuncto visui exteriori. Utroque enim visu optaverunt videre quæ Apostoli utroque visu intuiti sunt. Si autem fiat vis in hoc quod ait, Multi Prophetæ et justi, et non, Omnes Prophetæ et justi; dici posset, quod quamvis majores Sancti ac vates viderunt quæ viderunt Apostoli, non tamen alii omnes minores. Vel respondendum, quod licet Prophetæ ac justi viderunt quædam eorum quæ et Apostoli, non tamen tam multa, nec ita distincte ac circumstantionaliter. Et hoc maxime verum est, si hoc quod Christus ait Apostolis, Quæ vos videtis, referatur ad totum tempus quo Christus cum eis in terra conversatus est, usque ad horam ascensionis: et hoc modo, ut arbitror, intelligendum est.
paras.en: But it is asked of what sight the Saviour is speaking when He says that the Prophets and just men wished to see what the Apostles saw, and did not see it. It does not seem that it can be understood of spiritual sight, since the Prophets saw by intellectual and imaginary vision [that is, vision in the mind and in images, as distinct from bodily sight] all that they foretold of Christ. For [[Dan 10:1|there is need of understanding in a vision|Intelligentia enim est opus in visione]], as Daniel says. So when Isaias foretold the laying waste of Babylon, he says: "I fell down when I saw it"[[Is 21:3||]]. Much more did he see Christ in the spirit when he said of His incarnation, [[Is 9:6|a CHILD IS BORN to us|Puer natus est nobis]], and many like things. Jeremias too, when he said: [[Jer 14:8|why wilt thou be as a stranger in the land|Quare quasi colonus venturus es in terra]]? For then he saw Christ in an imaginary vision. And finally the Saviour Himself says: [[John 8:56|Abraham your father rejoiced that he might see my day: he saw it and was glad|Abraham pater vester exsultavit ut videret diem meum; vidit, et gavisus est]]. Nor does it seem that it can be understood of bodily sight, since what was said to the Apostles is not understood of that: [[13:16|blessed are your eyes, because they see|Vestri beati oculi, quia vident]]. For in that way Judas and the reprobate Jews saw. I think, therefore, that the saying is to be understood of inward sight joined to outward sight. For with both kinds of sight they wished to see what the Apostles beheld with both. But if weight is put on His saying "many prophets and just men", and not "all the prophets and just men", it could be said that although the greater saints and seers saw what the Apostles saw, yet not all the others, the lesser ones. Or it should be answered that although the Prophets and just men saw some of the things the Apostles saw, yet not so many, nor so distinctly and in all their circumstances. And this is most of all true if what Christ says to the Apostles, [[13:17|the things that you see|Quæ vos videtis]], is referred to the whole time during which Christ lived with them on earth, up to the hour of the Ascension; and so, I think, it is to be understood.

paras.t: Voluerunt quoque et audire verba sapientiæ ex ore meo, quæ auditis, qui me ad libitum interrogatis, et responsionem piam ac informationem recipitis; et non audierunt, eo modo ut vos, nec ita perfecte. Multa tamen documentorum Christi revelata fuerunt Prophetis.
paras.en: They wished also [[13:17|to hear|audire]] the words of wisdom from My mouth, [[13:17|the things that you hear|quæ auditis]], you who question Me as you please and receive a kind answer and instruction; [[13:17|and have not heard them|et non audierunt]] in the way you do, nor so perfectly. Many of Christ's teachings, however, were revealed to the Prophets.

paras.t: Vos ergo audite parabolam, id est interpretationem seu expositionem parabolæ, seminantis, id est Christi, qui per seminantem designavit se ipsum. Omnis homo qui audit corporali auditu verbum regni, id est sermonem de regno cœlesti, et non intelligit verbum hoc, id est, virtutem et sensum verborum cordi suo non imprimit, nec sagaciter pensat; venit malus, id est diabolus in malitia obstinatus, non essentia, sed voluntate malignus. Venit autem per tentationis congressum. Et rapit, id est, aufert, seu infructuosum facit, et oblivioni tradi procurat, quod seminatum est in corde ejus, id est verbum prædicationis infusum menti hominis talis. Et homo tam negligens, est qui secus viam seminatus est, id est, quem supra figuravi per eum in quem cecidit semen verbi cœlestis, secus viam sæculi hujus: juxta sensum præhabitum. Et dicitur homo seminatus, id est semine tali perfusus, quemadmodum terra dicitur corporaliter seminata.
paras.en: [[13:18|Hear you therefore the parable|Vos ergo audite parabolam]], that is, the interpretation or explanation of the parable, [[13:18|of the sower|seminantis]], that is, of Christ, who signified Himself by the sower. Every man [[13:19|When any one heareth the word of the kingdom|Omnis qui audit verbum regni]]: who hears with bodily hearing the word of the kingdom, that is, the message of the heavenly kingdom, [[13:19|and understandeth it not|et non intelligit]], that is, does not impress the force and sense of the words on his heart, nor weigh them shrewdly; [[13:19|there cometh the wicked one|venit malus]], that is, the devil, obstinate in malice, wicked not in his essence but in his will. He comes by the assault of temptation. [[13:19|and catcheth away|Et rapit]], that is, takes away, or makes fruitless and contrives to have forgotten, [[13:19|that which was sown in his heart|quod seminatum est in corde ejus]], that is, the word of preaching poured into the mind of such a man. And so negligent a man [[13:19|this is he that received the seed by the way side|est qui secus viam seminatus est]], that is, the one I figured above by him on whom the seed of the heavenly word fell, beside the way of this world, in the sense given before. And a man is said to be "sown", that is, sprinkled with such seed, just as the earth is said, in the bodily sense, to be sown.

paras.t: Qui autem supra petrosa seminatus est, id est, in corde duro ac saxeo semen verbi recepit, quem figuravi per eum in quem semen cecidit supra petrosa, id est arida duraque corda, hic est qui verbum Dei audit, et continuo cum gaudio suscipit illud in anima, tanquam sibi proficuum, per cujus susceptionem evadat periculum. Non habet autem in se radicem, id est habitualem gratiæ fecunditatem, ac stabile fidei fundamentum, seu firmum propositum; sed est temporalis, id est inconstans, ad modicum tempus perseverans in bono, sicut arundo vento agitata, et pulvis a vento projectus. Facta autem, id est sibi illata vel imminente, tribulatione ab invisibilibus hostibus, et persecutione a visibilibus inimicis, propter verbum, id est ob id quod verbum Dei recepit, et implere disponit; vel, Propter verbum exstinguendum, id est, ut verbum Dei tollant de corde ejus; continuo scandalizatur, id est, ex verbis seu factis illorum in peccata prolabitur, non resistens viriliter, relinquens viam justitiæ, ne patiatur adversa, vel ut consequatur delectabilia.
paras.en: [[13:20|And he that received the seed upon stony ground|Qui autem supra petrosa seminatus est]], that is, who received the seed of the word in a hard and stony heart, whom I figured by him on whom the seed fell upon stony ground, that is, dry and hard hearts, [[13:20|is he that heareth the word|hic est qui verbum Dei audit]] of God, [[13:20|and immediately receiveth it with joy|et continuo cum gaudio suscipit illud]] in his soul, as something profitable to him, by receiving which he may escape danger. [[13:21|Yet hath he not root in himself|Non habet autem in se radicem]], that is, the habitual fruitfulness of grace, and a steady foundation of faith, or a firm purpose; [[13:21|but is only for a time|sed est temporalis]], that is, inconstant, persevering in good for a little while, like [[Matt 11:7|a reed shaken with the wind|arundo vento agitata]], and like dust driven by the wind[[Ps 1:4||]]. [[13:21|and when there ariseth tribulation|facta autem tribulatione]], that is, when it is brought upon him or threatens, from invisible foes, [[13:21|and persecution|et persecutione]] from visible enemies, [[13:21|because of the word|propter verbum]], that is, because he has received the word of God and means to fulfil it; or, because of the word, in order to put it out, that is, so that they may take the word of God out of his heart; [[13:21|he is presently scandalized|continuo scandalizatur]], that is, through their words or deeds he slips into sins, not resisting manfully, leaving the way of justice so as not to suffer adversity, or so as to gain pleasant things.

paras.t: Qui autem seminatus est in spinis, id est, qui verbum Dei recepit in corde punctionibus temporalium curarum repleto, hic est qui verbum Dei audit; et sollicitudo sæculi istius, id est superflua cura acquirendi vel retinendi res mundanas, videlicet honorem, famam, voluptatem, et fallacia divitiarum, id est fallaces divitiæ, quæ sufficientiam quamdam promittunt, sed conferre non valent, suosque amatores æternis cruciatibus ingerunt: imo quo plus crescunt, tanto majus desiderium in corde avari accendunt, et eum quotidie insufficientiorem ac miserabiliorem efficiunt. Bene ergo vocantur fallaces. Unde Sapiens inquit: Creaturæ factæ sunt in tentationem, et in muscipulam pedibus insipientium. Vel, Fallacia divitiarum, id est deceptoria affectio quam divitiæ temporales causant in animo hominis. Blandiuntur enim, sed pungunt, quia cum labore acquiruntur, cum timore amittendi possidentur, cum tristitia amittuntur. Suffocat verbum Dei, id est, memoriam auditi sermonis aufert ab anima, quæ tanto amplius obliviscitur divinorum, quanto plus in terrenis occupatur, transitoriisque inhæret: et sine fructu boni operis ac spiritualis delectationis efficitur verbum Dei in tali corde diffusum.
paras.en: [[13:22|And he that received the seed among thorns|Qui autem seminatus est in spinis]], that is, who received the word of God in a heart full of the prickings of temporal cares, [[13:22|is he that heareth the word|hic est qui verbum Dei audit]] of God; [[13:22|and the care of this world|et sollicitudo sæculi istius]], that is, superfluous care to gain or keep worldly things, namely honour, reputation, pleasure, [[13:22|and the deceitfulness of riches|et fallacia divitiarum]], that is, deceitful riches, which promise a kind of sufficiency but cannot give it, and thrust their lovers into eternal torments; indeed, the more they grow, the greater the desire they kindle in the miser's heart, and they make him daily less satisfied and more wretched. Rightly, then, are they called deceitful. Hence the Wise Man says: Creatures are made a temptation, and [[Wis 14:11|a snare to the feet of the unwise|in muscipulam pedibus insipientium]]. Or, the deceitfulness of riches, that is, the deceptive attachment that temporal riches cause in a man's mind. For they flatter, but they prick: they are gained with toil, possessed with fear of losing them, and lost with sorrow. [[13:22|choketh up the word|Suffocat verbum]] of God, that is, takes the memory of the message heard away from the soul, which forgets divine things the more, the more it is busied with earthly things and clings to passing ones; [[13:22|and he becometh fruitless|et sine fructu efficitur]]: the word of God spread in such a heart is made without the fruit of good works and of spiritual delight.

paras.t: Qui vero in terram bonam seminatus est, id est, qui significatur per eum qui semen recepit in terra fecunda, seu ille qui corde devoto verbum Dei audivit, hic est qui audit verbum Dei aure corporali atque mentali, et intelligit illud, et fructum affert, id est, opera bona producit verbum in tali anima seminatum, et facit, aliud quidem centesimum, id est, verbum in cordibus quorumdam facit fructum centesimum, aliud autem facit fructum sexagesimum, aliud vero tricesimum: sicut expositum est, utpote secundum diversam dispositionem ac diligentiam recipientium.
paras.en: [[13:23|But he that received the seed upon good ground|Qui vero in terram bonam seminatus est]], that is, he who is signified by the one who received the seed in fruitful soil, or he who heard the word of God with a devout heart, [[13:23|is he that heareth the word|hic est qui audit verbum]] of God with the bodily ear and the ear of the mind, [[13:23|and understandeth|et intelligit]] it, [[13:23|and beareth fruit|et fructum affert]], that is, the word sown in such a soul produces good works, [[13:23|and yieldeth the one an hundredfold|et facit aliud quidem centesimum]], that is, the word in the hearts of some yields fruit a hundredfold, [[13:23|and another sixty|aliud autem facit fructum sexagesimum]], [[13:23|and another thirty|aliud vero tricesimum]], as has been explained, that is, according to the different dispositions and diligence of those who receive it.

paras.t: Posuit Christus hoc loco quatuor genera hominum audientium verbum Dei, et quatuor differentias seminis: quorum quartum genus dumtaxat salvatur, nam pauci electi; et quarta pars seminis solum fructificat. Verumtamen, quod hic dictum est de generibus audientium, ad litteram intelligitur de Judæis, quibus Christus in propria sermocinabatur persona, et paucos convertit ex eis. Mystice vero intelligi potest de ceteris gentibus.
paras.en: Christ has here set out four kinds of men who hear the word of God, and four differences of seed: of these only the fourth kind is saved, for [[Matt 20:16|few chosen|pauci electi]][[Matt 22:14||]]; and only the fourth part of the seed bears fruit. What is said here of the kinds of hearers, however, is understood literally of the Jews, to whom Christ spoke in His own person, and of whom He converted few. Mystically it can be understood of the other nations.

paras.t: Subinde Salvator comparat regnum cœlorum, id est militantem Ecclesiam, aliis rebus. Aliam parabolam proposuit Christus illis, videlicet turbis in littore stantibus, eo exsistente in navi, dicens: Simile factum est regnum cœlorum, id est status militantis Ecclesiæ, homini qui seminavit bonum semen in agro suo, etc. Quum ipse unigenitus Filius Dei, sapientia Patris æterni, post pauca proprio ore parabolam istam exponat, non debemus explanationem illius anticipando præcurrere. Differenda est ergo elucidatio præsentis parabolæ, usque ad locum ubi a Christo exponitur, et accedendum ad tertiæ parabolæ interpretationem.
paras.en: Next the Saviour compares the kingdom of heaven, that is, the Church militant, to other things. [[13:24|Another parable he proposed to them|Aliam parabolam proposuit Christus illis]], Christ did, namely to the crowds standing on the shore, while He was in the boat, [[13:24|saying: The kingdom of heaven is likened|dicens: Simile factum est regnum cœlorum]], that is, the state of the Church militant, [[13:24|to a man that sowed good seed in his field|homini qui seminavit bonum semen in agro suo]], etc. Since the only-begotten Son of God Himself, the Wisdom of the eternal Father, explains this parable with His own lips a little later[[13:37||]], we must not run ahead and anticipate His explanation. The explanation of this parable must therefore be put off until the place where Christ expounds it, and we go on to the interpretation of the third parable.

paras.t: Aliam parabolam, ordine tertiam, proposuit eis, scilicet turbis, dicens: Simile est regnum cœlorum, id est Ecclesia militans, maxime primitiva, quæ fuit parva quantitate seu numero, sed magna virtute: ideo subditur, grano sinapis, de quo sinapium exprimitur, quod granum sinapis accipiens homo agricola, seminat in agro suo. Quod granum minimum quidem est omnibus seminibus, id est inter omnia semina valde permodicum, ut patet ad oculum; quum autem creverit granum istud in agro, majus est omnibus oleribus, id est, in altius germen crescendo exsurgit, quam alia semina herbarum seu olerum, et fit arbor, id est, per modum arboris crescit in altum, ita ut volucres cœli, præsertim parvæ vel mediocres aves, veniant et habitent in ramis ejus, quiescendo sub illis. Quemadmodum ergo hoc granum quantitate permodicum crescit in altum, sic Ecclesia in principio sui contempta, et numero parva, crevit in populum infinitum, seu Ecclesiam toto orbe diffusam, quando in omnem terram exivit prædicatio Apostolorum, ita ut sub ramis ejus, id est sub documentis atque auxiliis Ecclesiæ, habitent volucres cœli, id est animæ contemplantes cœlestia, vel principes et magnates hujus sæculi ad fidem conversi. Sic ergo per hominem seminantem intelligitur Christus, vel prædicator ipsius; per granum, Ecclesia primitiva; per agrum, orbis terrarum, per quem longe ac late diffunduntur ac seminantur fideles, ita ut per Malachiam Dominus dicat: Ab ortu solis usque ad occasum, magnum est nomen meum in gentibus. Unde in Isaia scriptum est: Florebit et germinabit Israel, et implebunt faciem orbis semine.
paras.en: [[13:31|Another parable he proposed unto them, saying|Aliam parabolam … proposuit eis … dicens]] (the third in order), namely to the crowds: [[13:31|The kingdom of heaven is like|Simile est regnum cœlorum]], that is, the Church militant, above all the early Church, which was small in size or number but great in power; so it is added, [[13:31|to a grain of mustard seed|grano sinapis]], from which mustard is pressed, [[13:31|which a man took and sowed in his field|quod … accipiens homo … seminat in agro suo]], a farmer. [[13:32|Which is the least indeed of all seeds|Quod granum minimum quidem est omnibus seminibus]], that is, very small among all seeds, as is plain to the eye; [[13:32|but when it is grown up|quum autem creverit]], this grain in the field, [[13:32|it is greater than all herbs|majus est omnibus oleribus]], that is, it springs up into a taller shoot than the other seeds of plants or herbs, [[13:32|and becometh a tree|et fit arbor]], that is, grows up tall in the manner of a tree, [[13:32|so that the birds of the air come, and dwell in the branches thereof|ita ut volucres cœli, præsertim parvæ vel mediocres aves, veniant et habitent in ramis ejus]], especially small and middling birds, resting beneath them. As, then, this grain, very small in size, grows up tall, so the Church, despised at her beginning and few in number, grew into a countless people, a Church spread through the whole world, when the preaching of the Apostles went out into all the earth[[Ps 18:5||]], so that under her branches, that is, under the teachings and helps of the Church, the birds of the air dwell, that is, souls contemplating heavenly things, or the princes and great men of this world converted to the faith. So by the man sowing is understood Christ, or His preacher; by the grain, the early Church; by the field, the world, through which the faithful are spread and sown far and wide, so that the Lord says through Malachias: [[Mal 1:11|from the rising of the sun even to the going down, my name is great among the Gentiles|Ab ortu solis usque ad occasum, magnum est nomen meum in gentibus]]. Hence it is written in Isaias: [[Is 27:6|Israel shall blossom and bud, and they shall fill the face of the world with seed|Florebit et germinabit Israel, et implebunt faciem orbis semine]].

paras.t: Hieronymus, per regnum cœlorum intelligit Evangelii prædicationem, vel notitiam Scripturarum; per hominem seminantem, Christum, vel quemlibet alium qui in agrum proprii cordis mittit verbum Dei, quod significari dicit per granum sinapis. Sicut igitur granum sinapis parvum crescit in altum, sic prædicatio Evangelii primo valde contempta, et omnibus scientiis magis derisa, crevit per omnes nationes, ita quod sub ramis, id est diversis dogmatibus ejus, prædicti volucres morentur et conquiescant, omnisque sæcularis scientia et philosophorum doctrina minorata est sub ea, eique subjecta.
paras.en: Jerome understands by the kingdom of heaven the preaching of the Gospel, or the knowledge of the Scriptures; by the man sowing, Christ, or anyone else who puts the word of God into the field of his own heart, which word he says is signified by the grain of mustard seed. As, then, the small grain of mustard seed grows up tall, so the preaching of the Gospel, at first greatly despised and mocked more than all other learning, grew through all nations, so that under its branches, that is, its various doctrines, the birds just named abide and rest, and all worldly learning and the teaching of the philosophers has been made less beneath it and subject to it.

paras.t: Aliam, utpote quartam, parabolam locutus est eis: Simile est regnum cœlorum, id est Ecclesia militans, fermento quod acceptum mulier faciens massam pro panibus conficiendis, abscondit, id est, locavit ac miscuit, in farinæ satis tribus, id est tribus mensuris farinæ aqua conspersæ, seu massæ, vel azymi. Satum autem, secundum Hieronymum, est mensura Palæstinæ, unum modium cum dimidio capiens. Donec fermentatum est totum, id est, tamdiu dimisit mulier fermentum in massa, quousque tota fermento permixta est, atque conveniens facta ut de ea fieret panis. Hoc ad litteram planum est. Spiritualiter vero, per fermentum intelligitur evangelicæ legis doctrina, per quam corda hominum bonum sortiuntur saporem, ut gustent quam dulcis est Dominus, et recte de omnibus judicent, quemadmodum massa ex commixtione fermenti redditur apta ut de ea saporosi panes effici possint. Mulier vero, est Sapientia Dei incarnata, vel ipsa Ecclesia ac prædicatorum diligentia. Tria sata significant diversa loca in quibus fideles conversi sunt; vel carnem, sensualitatem, et rationalem animæ partem; vel partem intellectualem, vim concupiscibilem, et irascibilem. His tribus satis, hæc mulier infudit Evangelii documenta, donec totum fermentaretur, id est, tria hæc convenirent ac consentirent in idem, Deo unanimiter serviendo, ita ut caro et sensualitas rationi, et ratio Deo obediant, sicque simul sint unum in Christo, et unus panis, sicut Apostolus dicit: Unus panis, unum corpus multi sumus. Quamvis autem doctrina evangelica non sit subjective nisi in rationali parte animæ, redundat tamen effectumque habet in sensitiva parte et carne, et sic in eis abscondi dicitur vel infundi.
paras.en: [[13:33|Another parable he spoke to them|Aliam, utpote quartam, parabolam locutus est eis]] (the fourth, that is): [[13:33|The kingdom of heaven is like to leaven|Simile est regnum cœlorum, id est Ecclesia militans, fermento]], that is, the Church militant, [[13:33|which a woman took|quod acceptum mulier]], making a lump of dough for baking loaves, [[13:33|and hid|abscondit]], that is, put and mixed, [[13:33|in three measures of meal|in farinæ satis tribus]], that is, in three measures of flour sprinkled with water, a lump of dough, or unleavened bread. A satum, according to Jerome, is a measure of Palestine holding a modius and a half. [[13:33|until the whole was leavened|Donec fermentatum est totum]], that is, the woman left the leaven in the dough until the whole was mixed with the leaven and made fit to be made into bread. This is plain in the letter. Spiritually, by the leaven is understood the teaching of the Gospel law, by which the hearts of men acquire a good savour, so that they taste how sweet the Lord is[[Ps 33:9||]] and judge rightly of all things, just as the dough, by being mixed with leaven, is made fit for savoury loaves to be made from it. The woman is the Wisdom of God incarnate, or the Church herself and the diligence of preachers. The three measures signify the different places in which the faithful were converted; or the flesh, the sensuality, and the rational part of the soul; or the intellectual part, the concupiscible power and the irascible [the faculties of desire and of resistance to difficulty in the scholastic division of the soul]. Into these three measures this woman poured the teachings of the Gospel until the whole was leavened, that is, until these three agreed and consented in one thing, serving God with one mind, so that the flesh and the sensuality obey reason and reason obeys God, and so together they are one in Christ, and one bread, as the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 10:17|we, being many, are one bread, one body|Unus panis, unum corpus multi sumus]]. And although the teaching of the Gospel is subjectively [that is, as in its proper subject] only in the rational part of the soul, it overflows and has its effect in the sensitive part and the flesh, and so it is said to be hidden or poured into them.

paras.t: Sed quum dicat Apostolus, Epulemur, non in fermento veteri, neque in fermento malitiæ ac nequitiæ; rursusque, Modicum fermentum totam massam corrumpit: quæritur, quomodo regnum cœlorum, id est status vel doctrina Ecclesiæ, assimiletur fermento. Et respondendum, quod in fermento sunt duo, videlicet quædam humorum corruptio, et calor inclusus seu virtus latens interius. Quantum ad primum, procedit comparatio Pauli; quantum ad secundum, comparatio Christi.
paras.en: But since the Apostle says, [[1 Cor 5:8|let us feast, not with the old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness|Epulemur, non in fermento veteri, neque in fermento malitiæ ac nequitiæ]], and again, [[1 Cor 5:6|a little leaven corrupteth the whole lump|Modicum fermentum totam massam corrumpit]], it is asked how the kingdom of heaven, that is, the state or teaching of the Church, can be likened to leaven. The answer is that there are two things in leaven: a certain corruption of the moistures, and an enclosed heat or power hidden within. Paul's comparison proceeds from the first; Christ's from the second.

paras.t: Hæc omnia locutus est Jesus in parabolis ad turbas, propter causas superius assignatas. Et subditur jam alia ratio: Et sine parabolis non loquebatur eis, hac vice, vel in isto sermone, ut adimpleretur quod dictum est per Prophetam David vel Asaph, dicentem, in psalmo qui incipit, Attendite, popule meus, legem meam: Aperiam in parabolis os meum, eructabo abscondita a constitutione mundi. Ultimam partem hujus versiculi, nostra translatio habet sic: Loquar propositiones ab initio. Patet ergo, quod duo primi versiculi psalmi illius in persona Christi dicantur, qui in parabolis nunc locutus describitur, et eructavit, id est, discipulis suis manifestavit atque deprompsit, abscondita, id est parabolarum istarum interpretationes, seu mysteria regni cœlorum, quæ a constitutione mundi homines latuerunt, sicut jam dixit quod multi Prophetæ et justi voluerunt audire quæ ipsi audierunt, nec audierunt.
paras.en: [[13:34|All these things Jesus spoke in parables to the multitudes|Hæc omnia locutus est Jesus in parabolis ad turbas]], for the reasons given above. And now another reason is added: [[13:34|and without parables he did not speak to them|Et sine parabolis non loquebatur eis]] on this occasion, or in this discourse, [[13:35|That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet|ut adimpleretur quod dictum est per Prophetam]], David or Asaph, [[13:35|saying|dicentem]], in the psalm which begins [[Ps 77:1|Attend, O my people, to my law|Attendite, popule meus, legem meam]]: [[13:35|I will open my mouth in parables, I will utter things hidden from the foundation of the world|Aperiam in parabolis os meum, eructabo abscondita a constitutione mundi]]. The last part of this verse our translation has thus: [[Ps 77:2|I will utter propositions from the beginning|Loquar propositiones ab initio]]. It is plain, then, that the first two verses of that psalm are spoken in the person of Christ, who is described as now speaking in parables, and who [[13:35|will utter|eructabo]] [Latin eructavit, literally "belched forth", that is, poured out from within], that is, made known and brought out to His disciples, [[13:35|things hidden|abscondita]], that is, the interpretations of these parables, or the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, which were hidden from men from the foundation of the world; as He has already said that many prophets and just men wished to hear what the disciples heard, and did not hear it[[13:17||]].

13.title: Prosecutio expositionis præsentis capituli, ab eo loco quo dicitur: Tunc dimissis turbis, venit in domum
13.title_en: Continuation of the exposition of this chapter, from the place where it says: Then having sent away the multitudes, he came into the house

paras.t: Tunc, videlicet præscripto sermone ad populum circa mare habito ac finito, dimissis turbis, quæ dignæ non erant audire mysteria regni cœlestis, venit Jesus a navi in domum. Et accesserunt ad eum discipuli ejus, dicentes: Edissere, id est expone, nobis parabolam zizaniorum agri, id est in qua mentionem fecisti de zizaniis quæ nascuntur in agro. Quamvis Matthæus solum recitet discipulos quæsisse expositionem hujus parabolæ, creditur tamen quod aliarum quoque parabolarum expositionem quærebant, secundum quod Marcus habet, quod seorsum discipulis suis disserebat omnia.
paras.en: [[13:36|Then|Tunc]], that is, when the discourse described above, given to the people by the sea, had been held and finished, [[13:36|having sent away the multitudes|dimissis turbis]], who were not worthy to hear the mysteries of the heavenly kingdom, Jesus [[13:36|came into the house|venit in domum]] from the boat. [[13:36|and his disciples came to him, saying|Et accesserunt ad eum discipuli ejus, dicentes]]: [[13:36|Expound|Edissere]], that is, explain, [[13:36|to us the parable of the cockle of the field|nobis parabolam zizaniorum agri]], that is, the one in which You spoke of the cockle that springs up in the field. Although Matthew records only that the disciples asked for the explanation of this parable, it is believed that they asked for the explanation of the other parables as well, according to what Mark has, that [[Mark 4:34|apart, he explained all things to his disciples|seorsum discipulis suis disserebat omnia]].

paras.t: Porro ad habendum intellectum expositionis parabolæ zizaniorum, necesse est textum parabolæ supra omissum, hoc loco repetere. Sic enim ait Salvator: Simile factum est regnum cœlorum homini qui seminavit bonum semen in agro suo. Quum autem dormirent homines, venit inimicus ejus, et superseminavit zizania in medio tritici, et abiit. Quum autem crevisset herba, et fructum fecisset, tunc apparuerunt et zizania. Accedentes autem servi patrisfamilias, dixerunt ei: Domine, nonne bonum semen seminasti in agro tuo? Unde ergo habet zizania? Et ait illis: Inimicus homo hoc fecit. Servi autem dixerunt ei: Vis, imus, et colligimus ea? Et ait: Non, ne forte colligentes zizania, eradicetis simul et triticum. Sinite utraque crescere usque ad messem; et in tempore messis dicam messoribus: Colligite primum zizania, et alligate ea in fasciculos ad comburendum, triticum autem congregate in horreum meum. Hucusque textus parabolæ. Quam Christus exponens, adjecit:
paras.en: To understand the explanation of the parable of the cockle, it is necessary to repeat here the text of the parable passed over above. For the Saviour says: [[13:24|The kingdom of heaven is likened to a man that sowed good seed in his field|Simile factum est regnum cœlorum homini qui seminavit bonum semen in agro suo]]. [[13:25|But while men were asleep, his enemy came and oversowed cockle among the wheat and went his way|Quum autem dormirent homines, venit inimicus ejus, et superseminavit zizania in medio tritici, et abiit]]. [[13:26|And when the blade was sprung up, and had brought forth fruit, then appeared also the cockle|Quum autem crevisset herba, et fructum fecisset, tunc apparuerunt et zizania]]. [[13:27|And the servants of the good man of the house coming said to him. Sir, didst thou not sow good seed in thy field? Whence then hath it cockle?|Accedentes autem servi patrisfamilias, dixerunt ei: Domine, nonne bonum semen seminasti in agro tuo? Unde ergo habet zizania?]]? [[13:28|And he said to them: An enemy hath done this. And the servants said to him: Wilt thou that we go and gather it up?|Et ait illis: Inimicus homo hoc fecit. Servi autem dixerunt ei: Vis, imus, et colligimus ea?]]? [[13:29|And he said: No, lest perhaps gathering up the cockle, you root up the wheat also|Et ait: Non, ne forte colligentes zizania, eradicetis simul et triticum]]. [[13:30|Suffer both to grow until the harvest, and in the time of the harvest I will say to the reapers: Gather up first the cockle, and bind it into bundles to burn, but the wheat gather ye into my barn|Sinite utraque crescere usque ad messem; et in tempore messis dicam messoribus: Colligite primum zizania, et alligate ea in fasciculos ad comburendum, triticum autem congregate in horreum meum]]. So far the text of the parable. Explaining it, Christ added:

paras.t: Qui seminat bonum semen, est Filius hominis, hoc est, per hominem bonum semen serentem intelligitur Christus. Ager autem, est mundus, id est terra hujus peregrinationis, in qua homines degunt, et exsules sunt. Bonum vero semen, quod Christus seminavit in mundo, hi sunt filii regni, hoc est homines electi, quos Christus mittit ac spargit per omnia climata mundi, quemadmodum semina mittuntur in agris. De hoc semine Christi seu spiritualibus filiis ejus, scriptum est: Si posuerit pro peccato animam suam, videbit semen longævum. Zizania autem, sunt filii nequam, id est reprobi, præsertim hæretici, et persecutores Ecclesiæ. Inimicus autem qui seminavit ea, videlicet ista zizania, est diabolus: cujus suggestione et machinatione surrexerunt et perversa dogmata invenerunt hæretici; cujus etiam inspiratione alii reprobi se contra Ecclesiam erexerunt. Dicitur autem diabolus homo, non propter veritatem naturæ, sed propter similitudinem culpæ.
