Unde de semine ejus prædicto, Joannes: Qui peccat, inquit, ex diabolo est; et iterum: Jam Antichristi multi nati sunt; ex nobis prodierunt, sed non erant ex nobis. Hinc de Judæis Christus testatur: Vos ex patre diabolo estis. Dicuntur autem homines mali seminari vel esse ex dæmone, non creatione, sed pravitatis imitatione, juxta illud Sapientis: Imitantur illum qui sunt ex parte illius. Messis vero, usque ad quam simul crescunt et vivunt in hoc mundo electi ac reprobi, consummatio sæculi est, id est finis mundi, vel dies judicii, in quo electi in palatio Dei ponentur velut in horreo. Messores autem, qui bonos ac malos ad judicium deducent, et eos ab invicem separabunt, angeli sunt, non mali, sed boni.
paras.en: [[13:37|He that soweth the good seed is the Son of man|Qui seminat bonum semen, est Filius hominis]], that is, by the man sowing good seed Christ is understood. [[13:38|And the field is the world|Ager autem, est mundus]], that is, the land of this pilgrimage, in which men live and are exiles. [[13:38|And the good seed|Bonum vero semen]], which Christ sowed in the world, [[13:38|are the children of the kingdom|hi sunt filii regni]], that is, the elect, whom Christ sends and scatters through every region of the world, as seeds are cast into the fields. Of this seed of Christ, or His spiritual children, it is written: [[Is 53:10|if he shall lay down his life for sin, he shall see a longlived seed|Si posuerit pro peccato animam suam, videbit semen longævum]]. [[13:38|And the cockle are the children of the wicked one|Zizania autem, sunt filii nequam]], that is, the reprobate, above all heretics and the persecutors of the Church. [[13:39|And the enemy that sowed them|Inimicus autem qui seminavit ea]], namely this cockle, [[13:39|is the devil|est diabolus]]: at whose suggestion and contriving heretics arose and devised perverse doctrines, and at whose prompting other reprobates rose up against the Church. The devil is called a man [an enemy "man" (homo), as in v. 28] not because he truly has that nature, but because of likeness in guilt. Hence John says of his seed just mentioned: [[1 John 3:8|He that committeth sin is of the devil|Qui peccat, inquit, ex diabolo est]]; and again: [[1 John 2:18|even now there are become many Antichrists|Jam Antichristi multi nati sunt]]; [[1 John 2:19|They went out from us but they were not of us|ex nobis prodierunt, sed non erant ex nobis]]. Hence Christ testifies of the Jews: [[John 8:44|You are of your father the devil|Vos ex patre diabolo estis]]. Wicked men are said to be sown by the demon, or to be of him, not by creation but by imitating his wickedness, according to that saying of the Wise Man: [[Wis 2:25|they follow him that are of his side|Imitantur illum qui sunt ex parte illius]]. [[13:39|But the harvest|Messis vero]], until which the elect and the reprobate grow and live together in this world, [[13:39|is the end of the world|consummatio sæculi est]], that is, the end of the world, or the day of judgment, on which the elect will be placed in God's palace as in a barn. [[13:39|And the reapers|Messores autem]], who will lead the good and the wicked to judgment and separate them from one another, [[13:39|are the angels|angeli sunt]]: not the wicked angels, but the good.

paras.t: Sicut ergo colliguntur a messoribus zizania, id est inutiles herbæ, seu folia, et igni comburuntur; sic erit in consummatione sæculi. Mittet Filius hominis angelos suos, qui sibi subjecti sunt, etiam secundum naturam assumptam, ut Verbo unitam; et colligent, hoc est auferent, de regno ejus, id est de ecclesia electorum, seu bonis fidelibus, omnia scandala, hoc est persecutiones et tentationes, per quas boni frequenter scandalizantur; vel, Omnia scandala, id est scandalizatores aliorum, qui generant scandala, qui tunc ab electis loco et præmio separabuntur; et eos qui faciunt iniquitatem, id est ceteros operarios malos, hypocritas, simulatores et callidos iram Dei provocantes. Et mittent eos in caminum ignis, Christo dicente: Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum. Tunc enim angeli sancti exsecutores judicii, omnes reprobos, homines atque diabolos, in infernalis ignis fornacem projicient. Unde in Apocalypsi legitur: Projectus est draco ille magnus, serpens antiquus. Et alio loco ait Joannes: Cruciabitur iniquus igne et sulfure, et fumus tormentorum ejus ascendet in sæcula sæculorum. Ministerio itaque sanctorum angelorum dispositive agentium, fiet suscitatio mortuorum, quorum cineres angeli colligent, et suscitatos ad judicii locum perducent, reprobos ab electis segregabunt, et damnatos in pœnas retrudent. Ibi erit fletus et stridor dentium. Hoc supra expositum est, capitulo octavo.
paras.en: [[13:40|Even as cockle therefore is gathered up|Sicut ergo colliguntur a messoribus zizania]] by the reapers, that is, useless plants or leaves, [[13:40|and burnt with fire: so shall it be at the end of the world|et igni comburuntur; sic erit in consummatione sæculi]]. [[13:41|The Son of man shall send his angels|Mittet Filius hominis angelos suos]], who are subject to Him even according to the nature He assumed, as united to the Word; [[13:41|and they shall gather|et colligent]], that is, take away, [[13:41|out of his kingdom|de regno ejus]], that is, out of the church of the elect, or from the good faithful, [[13:41|all scandals|omnia scandala]], that is, the persecutions and temptations by which the good are often scandalized; or, all scandals, that is, those who scandalize others, who cause scandals, who will then be separated from the elect in place and reward; [[13:41|and them that work iniquity|et eos qui faciunt iniquitatem]], that is, the other evil workers, hypocrites, [[Job 36:13|Dissemblers and crafty men prove the wrath of God|simulatores et callidos iram Dei provocantes]]. [[13:42|And shall cast them into the furnace of fire|Et mittent eos in caminum ignis]], when Christ says: [[Matt 25:41|you cursed, into everlasting fire|Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum]]. For then the holy angels, the executors of the judgment, will cast all the reprobate, men and devils, into the furnace of hellfire. Hence we read in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 12:9|that great dragon was cast out, that old serpent|Projectus est draco ille magnus, serpens antiquus]]. And in another place John says: the wicked [[Apoc 14:10|shall be tormented with fire and brimstone|Cruciabitur iniquus igne et sulfure]], [[Apoc 14:11|and the smoke of their torments, shall ascend up for ever and ever|et fumus tormentorum ejus ascendet in sæcula sæculorum]]. So by the ministry of the holy angels, acting in preparation [that is, disposing things, while the raising itself is God's work], the raising of the dead will take place: the angels will gather their ashes, lead them, once raised, to the place of judgment, separate the reprobate from the elect, and thrust the damned down into their punishment. [[13:42|there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth|Ibi erit fletus et stridor dentium]]. This was explained above, in the eighth chapter[[Matt 8:12||]].

paras.t: Tunc, videlicet statim peracto vel durante judicio, et illis in caminum ignis seu infernum, qui comparatur ardenti et fumoso camino, projectis, fulgebunt justi in corpore per dotem claritatis, quæ tanto copiosior erit in corporibus glorificatis quanto eorum animæ Deum clarius videbunt, sicut sol iste sensibilis, non solum sicut nunc lucet, sed sicut tunc lucebit quando lux solis erit septempliciter, sicut lux septem dierum*. Estque probabile quod claritas corporis glorificati excedit claritatem solarem, quoniam opera gratiæ excedunt opera naturæ. Vel, Sicut sol spiritualis, videlicet Christus, de quo in Malachia Dominus perhibet: Orietur vobis, inquiens, timentibus nomen meum, Sol justitiæ. Corpora namque electorum assimilabuntur claritati corporis Christi, prout dicit Apostolus: Salvatorem exspectamus Dominum Jesum, qui reformabit corpus humilitatis nostræ, configuratum corpori claritatis suæ. Denique, sicut corpora electorum fulgida erunt ut sol, sic corpora reproborum obscurissima erunt, secundum quod animæ eorum omni lumine interiori, quantum ad rectum usum, omnino privantur. [*In regno Patris eorum.]
paras.en: [[13:43|Then|Tunc]], that is, as soon as the judgment is over, or while it is going on, and when those others have been cast into the furnace of fire, that is, hell, which is compared to a burning and smoking furnace, [[13:43|shall the just shine|fulgebunt justi]] in the body through the endowment of brightness [one of the four "endowments" (dotes) of the glorified body], which will be the more abundant in glorified bodies the more clearly their souls see God, [[13:43|as the sun|sicut sol]]: this visible sun, not only as it shines now, but as it will shine then, when [[Is 30:26|the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days|lux solis erit septempliciter, sicut lux septem dierum]] [here the edition adds in a note the words of the verse that Denis passes over: "in the kingdom of their Father"]. And it is probable that the brightness of the glorified body exceeds the brightness of the sun, since the works of grace exceed the works of nature. Or: as the spiritual sun, namely Christ, of whom the Lord declares in Malachias: [[Mal 4:2|unto you that fear my name, the Sun of justice shall arise|Orietur vobis, inquiens, timentibus nomen meum, Sol justitiæ]]. For the bodies of the elect will be made like the brightness of the body of Christ, as the Apostle says: [[Phil 3:20|we look for the Saviour|Salvatorem exspectamus]], the Lord Jesus, [[Phil 3:21|Who will reform the body of our lowness, made like to the body of his glory|qui reformabit corpus humilitatis nostræ, configuratum corpori claritatis suæ]]. Finally, as the bodies of the elect will be bright as the sun, so the bodies of the reprobate will be utterly dark, in keeping with their souls being wholly deprived of all inner light as regards its right use.

paras.t: His dictis, patet expositio hujus parabolæ, paucis exceptis, quæ tangenda sunt breviter. Quum autem dormirent homines, id est, prælati Ecclesiæ et aliorum doctores de hac vita migrarent, vel a diligenti custodia gregis sui cessarent, venit inimicus ejus, id est diabolus, adversarius Christi, et superseminavit zizania, hoc est, hæreticos et perversos misit ac miscuit, in medio tritici, id est inter electos atque Catholicos; et abiit alibi, facere aliquid mali, et cito reversurus est. Quum autem crevisset herba, hoc est semen bonum seminatum a Christo, et fructum bonæ conversationis fecisset, quum filii regni numero ac merito aucti fuissent in sæculo isto; apparuerunt inter eos et zizania, id est prædicti injusti. Accedentes autem spirituali accessu, servi patrisfamilias, hoc est famuli Christi, utpote angeli, secundum Hieronymum, vel devoti prælati ac vicarii Christi; dixerunt ei: Domine, nonne bonum semen seminasti in agro tuo, id est homines fide et opere christianos in mundo? Unde ergo habet zizania? Et ait: Inimicus homo hoc fecit, id est diabolus. Servi autem dixerunt: Vis, imus, et colligimus ea? id est, visne ut separemus et auferamus hæreticos et perversos a societate fidelium, per excommunicationem, vel tradendo eos potestati sæculari ad occidendum? Et ait: Non, ne forte colligentes zizania ista, eradicetis, id est, periculo vel occisioni exponatis, et triticum, id est electos fideles. Sinite utraque crescere usque ad messem, id est diem retributionis extremæ, seu judicii; et in tempore messis dicam messoribus, id est angelis: Colligite primum zizania, id est, antequam proferatur judicialis sententia, separate malos a bonis, et alligate ea in fasciculos, id est, per modum fasciculorum adunate eos, ad comburendum, hoc est, ut in igne gehennæ succendantur, non consumantur. Impius quippe funibus peccatorum suorum constringetur, ut Sapiens inquit. De hac impiorum colligatione scriptum est in Isaia: In die illa visitabit Dominus super militiam cœli in excelso, et super reges terræ; et congregabuntur in congregatione unius fascis in lacum, et claudentur ibi in carcere.
paras.en: With this said, the explanation of this parable is plain, except for a few points, which must be touched on briefly. [[13:25|But while men were asleep|Quum autem dormirent homines]], that is, while the prelates of the Church and the teachers of others were passing from this life, or ceasing from careful guard over their flock, [[13:25|his enemy came|venit inimicus ejus]], that is, the devil, the adversary of Christ, [[13:25|and oversowed cockle|et superseminavit zizania]], that is, sent and mingled heretics and perverse men [[13:25|among the wheat|in medio tritici]], that is, among the elect and the Catholics; [[13:25|and went his way|et abiit]] elsewhere, to do some other evil, and he will soon be back. [[13:26|And when the blade was sprung up|Quum autem crevisset herba]], that is, the good seed sown by Christ, [[13:26|and had brought forth fruit|et fructum bonæ conversationis fecisset]] of good living, when the children of the kingdom had increased in number and merit in this world, [[13:26|then appeared also the cockle|apparuerunt inter eos et zizania]] among them, that is, the unjust just mentioned. [[13:27|And the servants of the good man of the house coming|Accedentes autem spirituali accessu, servi patrisfamilias]], coming spiritually, that is, the servants of Christ, namely the angels, according to Jerome, or devout prelates and vicars of Christ, [[13:27|said to him. Sir, didst thou not sow good seed in thy field|dixerunt ei: Domine, nonne bonum semen seminasti in agro tuo]], that is, men Christian in faith and works, in the world? [[13:27|Whence then hath it cockle|Unde ergo habet zizania]]? [[13:28|And he said to them: An enemy hath done this|Et ait: Inimicus homo hoc fecit]], that is, the devil. [[13:28|And the servants said to him: Wilt thou that we go and gather it up|Servi autem dixerunt: Vis, imus, et colligimus ea?]]? That is, do You wish us to separate and remove heretics and perverse men from the fellowship of the faithful, by excommunication, or by handing them over to the secular power to be put to death? [[13:29|And he said: No, lest perhaps gathering up the cockle, you root up|Et ait: Non, ne forte colligentes zizania ista, eradicetis]], that is, expose to danger or death, [[13:29|the wheat also|et triticum]], that is, the elect faithful. [[13:30|Suffer both to grow until the harvest|Sinite utraque crescere usque ad messem]], that is, the day of final reward, or of judgment; [[13:30|and in the time of the harvest I will say to the reapers|et in tempore messis dicam messoribus]], that is, to the angels: [[13:30|Gather up first the cockle|Colligite primum zizania]], that is, before the judicial sentence is pronounced, separate the wicked from the good, [[13:30|and bind it into bundles|et alligate ea in fasciculos]], that is, gather them together after the manner of bundles, [[13:30|to burn|ad comburendum]], that is, that they may be set alight, not consumed, in the fire of Gehenna. For the wicked man [[Prov 5:22|is fast bound with the ropes of his own sins|funibus peccatorum suorum constringetur]], as the Wise Man says. Of this binding together of the wicked it is written in Isaias: [[Is 24:21|in that day the Lord shall visit upon the host of heaven on high, and upon the kings of the earth|In die illa visitabit Dominus super militiam cœli in excelso, et super reges terræ]]; [[Is 24:22|And they shall be gathered together as in the gathering of one bundle into the pit, and they shall be shut up there in prison|et congregabuntur in congregatione unius fascis in lacum, et claudentur ibi in carcere]].

paras.t: Circa hunc locum quæritur, an hæretici sint sustinendi. Et videtur quod imo, quum Christus dicat: Sinite utraque simul crescere usque ad messem. Hieronymus quoque hic dicit: Monemur ne cito amputemus fratrem, quoniam fieri potest ut ille qui hodie noxio depravatus est dogmate, cras resipiscat. Oppositum videtur ex eo quod ait Apostolus: Auferte malum de medio fratrum vestrorum. Et secundum apostolica documenta, prohibemur hæreticos salutare, et cum quibusdam perversis cibum accipere. Ad hanc quæstionem respondet Thomas, quod circa hæreticum duo pensantur, videlicet ejus iniquitas, et Ecclesiæ pietas. Quantum ad primum, meretur non solum excommunicari, sed occidi, quum multo gravius sit fidem corrumpere, quam falsare pecuniam: et tamen falsatores pecuniæ secundum jura occiduntur. Quantum ad secundum, non decet hæreticum statim damnare, sed ad veritatem pro posse reducere. Ideo Ecclesia non immediate et subito, sed post primam et secundam correptionem damnat hæreticum, sicut ad Titum docet Apostolus. Si vero ex tunc in suo errore manserit pertinax, separat eum Ecclesia a se per excommunicationis sententiam, et relinquit eum sæculari judicio morti tradendum. Unde alio loco dicit Hieronymus: Secandæ sunt putridæ carnes, et scabiosa ovis a caula repellenda est, ne tota domus, massa, corpus et pecora, ardeant, corrumpantur, putrescant. Arius, in Alexandria una scintilla fuit; sed quoniam non statim oppressus est, totum orbem ejus flamma depopulata est. Itaque, quod Dominus ait, zizania non esse tollenda, sed sinenda ut crescant cum tritico, si per zizania intelligantur hæretici, tunc intelligendum est, in eo casu quando videlicet exstirpari non possunt sine eradicatione seu periculo tritici, quando videlicet non sunt aperti, vel satis noti, vel potentes habent defensores. Unde dicit Hieronymus: Monet Dominus ne ubi quid ambiguum, cito proferamus sententiam.
paras.en: On this passage it is asked whether heretics are to be tolerated. And it seems that they are, since Christ says: [[13:30|Suffer both to grow until the harvest|Sinite utraque simul crescere usque ad messem]]. Jerome too says here: "We are warned not to cut off a brother quickly, since it may be that he who today is corrupted by a harmful doctrine will come to his senses tomorrow." The opposite seems to follow from what the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 5:13|Put away the evil one|Auferte malum]] from the midst of your brethren. And according to the apostolic teaching we are forbidden to greet heretics[[2 John 1:10||]] [the margin seems to read Tit. iii, 10 here; the forbidding of greeting is in 2 John 10], and to take food with certain perverse men[[1 Cor 5:11||]]. To this question Thomas answers [Summa Theologiae II-II, q. 11, a. 3, as the margin notes] that two things are to be weighed regarding a heretic: his wickedness, and the Church's mercy. As to the first, he deserves not only to be excommunicated but to be put to death, since it is far graver to corrupt the faith than to counterfeit money: and yet counterfeiters of money are put to death according to the laws. As to the second, it is not fitting to condemn a heretic at once, but to bring him back to the truth as far as possible. Therefore the Church condemns a heretic not immediately and suddenly, but after the first and second admonition, as the Apostle teaches in writing to Titus[[Tit 3:10||]]. But if after that he remains obstinate in his error, the Church separates him from herself by the sentence of excommunication, and leaves him to the secular judgment to be put to death. Hence Jerome says in another place: "Rotten flesh must be cut away, and the mangy sheep driven from the fold, lest the whole house, lump, body and flock burn, be corrupted, rot and perish. Arius was a single spark in Alexandria; but because he was not put out at once, his flame laid waste the whole world." So when the Lord says that the cockle is not to be pulled up but left to grow with the wheat, if heretics are understood by the cockle, it is to be understood of the case when they cannot be rooted out without the uprooting or danger of the wheat, namely when they are not open, or not well enough known, or have powerful defenders. Hence Jerome says: "The Lord warns us not to pass sentence quickly where something is doubtful."

paras.t: Sequitur quinta parabola. Simile est regnum cœlorum, hoc est præmium Beatorum in patria, thesauro abscondito in agro. Nam sicut propter talem thesaurum possidendum omnia venduntur, sic propter adipiscendum regnum cœlorum omnia temporalia deseruntur. Ideo subditur: quem thesaurum qui invenit homo, abscondit, tanquam pretiosum clenodium, et præ gaudio illius, id est ex dilectione et amore thesauri inventi, vadit, et vendit omnia quæ habet, et emit agrum illum, ut habeat jus possidendi thesaurum ex integro. Olim enim thesauri in agro inventi, quamvis propter temporis longitudinem ignorabatur cujus fuissent, tamen propter communem hominum pacem pro media parte fuerunt dominorum agri. Ager ergo est vita activa, vel sacra Scriptura, in quibus thesaurus iste, videlicet beatitudo cœlestis, quodammodo latet et continetur ut merces in merito. Homo autem thesaurum reperiens, est quicumque devotus, qui cum Apostolo omnia arbitratur ut stercora, ut Christum lucrifaciat. Vel, thesaurus est Christi divinitas; ager, caro ipsius.
paras.en: The fifth parable follows. [[13:44|The kingdom of heaven is like unto a treasure hidden in a field|Simile est regnum cœlorum, hoc est præmium Beatorum in patria, thesauro abscondito in agro]]: the kingdom, that is, the reward of the Blessed in the fatherland. For as everything is sold in order to possess such a treasure, so all temporal things are given up in order to gain the kingdom of heaven. So it is added: [[13:44|Which a man having found, hid it|quem thesaurum qui invenit homo, abscondit]], the treasure, as a precious jewel, [[13:44|and for joy thereof|et præ gaudio illius]], that is, out of delight in and love for the treasure he has found, [[13:44|goeth, and selleth all that he hath, and buyeth that field|vadit, et vendit omnia quæ habet, et emit agrum illum]], so as to have the right to possess the treasure entire. For in former times treasures found in a field, although because of the length of time it was not known whose they had been, nevertheless, for the sake of peace among men, belonged half to the owners of the field. The field, then, is the active life, or holy Scripture, in which this treasure, namely heavenly blessedness, in a manner lies hidden and is contained, as the reward in the merit. The man who finds the treasure is any devout person who, with the Apostle, counts all things as dung that he may gain Christ[[Phil 3:8||]]. Or: the treasure is the divinity of Christ; the field, His flesh.

paras.t: Iterum simile est regnum cœlorum, id est Ecclesia militans, homini negotiatori, quærenti bonas margaritas, id est lapides pretiosos. Inventa autem una pretiosa margarita, id est gemma quadam dignissima, qualis est jaspis, abiit, et vendidit omnia quæ habuit, et emit eam, ut carius venderet ipsam, vel tanquam prænobile bonum possideret. Sic Ecclesia et quilibet veraciter christianus, quærens pretiosas margaritas, hoc est virtutes præclaras et cardinales, et veteris Testamenti Scripturas, unam vero pretiosissimam inveniens, scilicet christianæ legis doctrinam, vel consiliorum evangelicorum perfectionem, vel increatam Dei sapientiam, Dominum Jesum, vendit vel vilipendit cuncta terrena, ut margaritam istam obtineat, sicut testatur Apostolus: Omnia arbitror detrimentum, propter eminentem scientiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi. Pretiosior nempe est sapientia cunctis opibus; et omnia quæ desiderantur, huic non valent comparari.
paras.en: [[13:45|Again the kingdom of heaven is like to a merchant seeking good pearls|Iterum simile est regnum cœlorum, id est Ecclesia militans, homini negotiatori, quærenti bonas margaritas]]: the kingdom, that is, the Church militant; pearls, that is, precious stones. [[13:46|Who when he had found one pearl of great price|Inventa autem una pretiosa margarita]], that is, a most noble gem, such as jasper, [[13:46|went his way, and sold all that he had, and bought it|abiit, et vendidit omnia quæ habuit, et emit eam]], so as to sell it again at a higher price, or to possess it as an exceedingly noble good. So the Church, and every true Christian, seeking precious pearls, that is, the bright and cardinal virtues and the Scriptures of the Old Testament, and finding one most precious, namely the teaching of the Christian law, or the perfection of the Gospel counsels, or the uncreated Wisdom of God, the Lord Jesus, sells or holds cheap all earthly things in order to obtain this pearl, as the Apostle testifies: [[Phil 3:8|I count all things to be but loss for the excellent knowledge of Jesus Christ|Omnia arbitror detrimentum, propter eminentem scientiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi]], our Lord. For wisdom [[Prov 3:15|is more precious than all riches: and all the things that are desired, are not to be compared to her|Pretiosior … est … cunctis opibus; et omnia quæ desiderantur, huic non valent comparari]][[Prov 8:11||]].

paras.t: Postremo, septima et ultima parabola subditur. Simile est regnum cœlorum, id est Ecclesia militans, in qua Deus per fidem et gratiam regnat: quæ et ipsa regnat in nomine Christi, sæculare ac spirituale dominium atque judicium habens et faciens; de qua Petrus apostolus: Vos, inquit, genus electum, regale sacerdotium; quæ in Apocalypsi fatetur, loquens ad Christum: Fecisti nos Deo nostro regnum et sacerdotes, et regnabimus super terram. De hoc regno dixit Archangelus de Christo ad Virginem: Regnabit in domo Jacob in æternum, et regni ejus non erit finis. Itaque regnum istud simile est sagenæ, seu reti, missæ a piscatoribus in mare, ut capiat pisces, et ex omni genere piscium congreganti, hoc est, bonos et malos pisces capienti, vel quosdam de omni specie piscium. Quam sagenam, quum impleta esset piscibus talibus, educentes piscatores, et secus littus, hoc est juxta ripam aquæ, sedentes, elegerunt ex sagena bonos pisces in vasa sua, malos autem foras miserunt, id est, penitus abjecerunt, et bestiis ac avibus ad devorandum dederunt. Sic modo Ecclesia continet bonos et malos, et quosdam de omni genere hominum. Mystice etiam per sagenam exprimitur prædicatio Apostolorum et successorum ipsorum, qui ex verbis utriusque Testamenti sermonem per modum retis texentes, miserunt illum in mundum istum, qui magno procellosoque mari assimilatur, et congregaverunt intra Ecclesiam quosdam de omni natione, pluresque reprobos quam electos. Unde in vocatione priorum Apostolorum dictum est: Venite post me, et faciam vos fieri piscatores hominum.
paras.en: Lastly, the seventh and final parable is added. [[13:47|Again the kingdom of heaven is like|Simile est regnum cœlorum]], that is, the Church militant, in which God reigns through faith and grace, and which herself also reigns in the name of Christ, having and exercising temporal and spiritual dominion and judgment; of whom the Apostle Peter says: [[1 Pet 2:9|you are a chosen generation, a kingly priesthood|Vos, inquit, genus electum, regale sacerdotium]]; and who in the Apocalypse declares, speaking to Christ: [[Apoc 5:10|hast made us to our God a kingdom and priests, and we shall reign on the earth|Fecisti nos Deo nostro regnum et sacerdotes, et regnabimus super terram]]. Of this kingdom the Archangel said to the Virgin, of Christ: [[Luke 1:32|he shall reign in the house of Jacob for ever|Regnabit in domo Jacob in æternum]], [[Luke 1:33|And of his kingdom there shall be no end|et regni ejus non erit finis]]. This kingdom, then, is like [[13:47|to a net cast into the sea|sagenæ missæ in mare]], a dragnet cast by fishermen into the sea to catch fish, [[13:47|and gathering together of all kinds of fishes|et ex omni genere piscium congreganti]], that is, catching good and bad fish, or some of every kind of fish. [[13:48|Which, when it was filled, they drew out|Quam sagenam, quum impleta esset piscibus talibus, educentes]], the net filled with such fish, the fishermen, [[13:48|and sitting by the shore|et secus littus sedentes]], that is, by the water's edge, [[13:48|they chose out the good into vessels|elegerunt … bonos … in vasa]] of theirs out of the net, [[13:48|but the bad they cast forth|malos autem foras miserunt]], that is, threw them right away and gave them to beasts and birds to eat. So now the Church holds good and bad, and some of every kind of men. Mystically, too, the net expresses the preaching of the Apostles and their successors, who, weaving their discourse like a net out of the words of both Testaments, cast it into this world, which is likened to a great and stormy sea, and gathered into the Church some of every nation, and more reprobate than elect. Hence at the calling of the first Apostles it was said: [[Matt 4:19|Come ye after me, and I will make you to be fishers of men|Venite post me, et faciam vos fieri piscatores hominum]].

paras.t: Præterea ipsemet Christus declarat cur Ecclesia comparetur tali sagenæ. Sic erit in consummatione sæculi, quantum ad hominum separationem ab invicem, quando agni ponentur a dextris, et hædi a sinistris, sicut nunc dictum est de piscium separatione. Nam tunc exibunt angeli a summo cœlo, et missi a Christo separabunt malos de medio justorum, hoc est de tota universitate electorum, et mittent eos in caminum ignis. Ibi erit fletus et stridor dentium. Hoc totum jam evidenter expositum est. Itaque Ecclesia per modum sagenæ nunc natat et fluctuat in hoc mari magno ac spatioso; et sæpe fluctibus tribulationum et aquis tentationum ita afficitur atque torquetur, ut clamet cum sancto David: Salvum me fac, Deus, quoniam intraverunt aquæ usque ad animam meam; veni in altitudinem maris, et tempestas demersit me. Nunc quoque nescitur qui pisces sint electi, et qui reprobi. Porro, in fine sæculi, Christo ad judicium descendente, sagena ista quasi ad littus trahitur, quum omnes ante Christum in valle Josaphat ducuntur ac præsentantur: tuncque boni manifeste secernentur a malis.
paras.en: Moreover, Christ Himself declares why the Church is compared to such a net. [[13:49|So shall it be at the end of the world|Sic erit in consummatione sæculi]], as regards the separation of men from one another, when the lambs will be set on the right and the goats on the left[[Matt 25:33||]], as has just been said of the separation of the fish. For then [[13:49|The angels shall go out|exibunt angeli]] from the height of heaven, and, sent by Christ, [[13:49|shall separate the wicked from among the just|separabunt malos de medio justorum]], that is, from the whole company of the elect, [[13:50|And shall cast them into the furnace of fire: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth|et mittent eos in caminum ignis. Ibi erit fletus et stridor dentium]]. All this has already been plainly explained. So the Church now swims and tosses like a net in this great and wide sea[[Ps 103:25||]]; and she is often so beset and racked by the waves of tribulation and the waters of temptation that she cries out with holy David: [[Ps 68:2|Save me, O God: for the waters are come in even unto my soul|Salvum me fac, Deus, quoniam intraverunt aquæ usque ad animam meam]]; [[Ps 68:3|I am come into the depth of the sea, and a tempest hath overwhelmed me|veni in altitudinem maris, et tempestas demersit me]]. Now, too, it is not known which fish are elect and which reprobate. But at the end of the world, when Christ comes down to judgment, this net is drawn as it were to the shore, when all are led and presented before Christ in the valley of Josaphat: and then the good will be openly sorted out from the wicked.

paras.t: Intellexistis hæc omnia, scilicet parabolas istas et interpretationes earum? Hoc Apostolis dicitur: qui tamen apud Marcum referuntur a Christo reprehensi, eo quod primam parabolam non intellexerunt. Dicunt ei: Etiam. Ait illis: Ideo, hoc est, ex quo ad vos, tanquam ad aliorum magistros, spectat hæc omnia intelligere, propterea omnis scriba doctus in regno cœlorum, hoc est quilibet prædicator et prælatus, præsertim episcopus, in militanti Ecclesia, similis est homini patrifamilias qui profert de thesauro suo nova et vetera, vestimenta, utensilia, alimenta, talenta. Quemadmodum enim talis paterfamilias unicuique de filiis ac familiis suis dat secundum quod indiget, et capere potest, vel dignus est; sic scriba doctus de quo nunc sermo est, unumquemque de grege suo pascit ac instruit, prout capere valet, secundum quod Paulus lacte potasse se dicit eos qui solidum non poterant capere cibum. In divinis enim Scripturis invenitur quod omni statui congruit. Hujusmodi itaque scriba, profert de thesauro suo, hoc est de plenitudine gratiæ, perfectionis, et scientiæ sibi divinitus distributæ (thesaurus enim desiderabilis in ore sapientis, secundum Salomonem), nova et vetera, hoc est utriusque Testamenti eloquia, sermonem suum confirmans auctoritatibus novi et veteris legis. Unde in Canticis ait Ecclesia: Omnia poma nova ac vetera, dilecte mi, servavi tibi. Debent ergo majores prælati in utraque lege esse periti: imo secundum deiformem theologorum ducem sacratissimum Dionysium, ad episcopos pertinet ut sint adeo docti, quod difficillima quæque et omnes subditorum dubitationes solvere possint.
paras.en: [[13:51|Have ye understood all these things|Intellexistis hæc omnia]], namely these parables and their interpretations? This is said to the Apostles, who nevertheless are reported in Mark to have been rebuked by Christ because they had not understood the first parable[[Mark 4:13||]]. [[13:51|They say to him: Yes|Dicunt ei: Etiam]]. [[13:52|He said unto them: Therefore|Ait illis: Ideo]], that is, since it belongs to you, as the teachers of others, to understand all these things, [[13:52|every scribe instructed in the kingdom of heaven|omnis scriba doctus in regno cœlorum]], that is, every preacher and prelate, above all a bishop, in the Church militant, [[13:52|is like to a man that is a householder, who bringeth forth out of his treasure new things and old|similis est homini patrifamilias qui profert de thesauro suo nova et vetera]]: clothing, utensils, food, money [Latin talenta]. For as such a householder gives to each of his children and household what he needs and can take, or deserves, so the instructed scribe now spoken of feeds and teaches each one of his flock as he is able to take it, as Paul says he gave milk to drink to those who could not take solid food[[1 Cor 3:2||]]. For in the divine Scriptures is found what suits every state. Such a scribe, then, [[13:52|bringeth forth out of his treasure|profert de thesauro suo]], that is, from the fullness of grace, perfection and knowledge bestowed on him by God (for [[Prov 21:20|There is a treasure to be desired|thesaurus enim desiderabilis]] in the mouth of the wise, according to Solomon) [Denis's wording; the Vulgate has "in the dwelling of the just"], [[13:52|new things and old|nova et vetera]], that is, the sayings of both Testaments, confirming his discourse with authorities from the new law and the old. Hence the Church says in the Canticle: [[Cant 7:13|all fruits: the new and the old, my beloved, I have kept for thee|Omnia poma nova ac vetera, dilecte mi, servavi tibi]]. The greater prelates, therefore, ought to be skilled in both laws: indeed, according to the godlike leader of theologians, the most holy Dionysius, it belongs to bishops to be so learned that they can resolve all the hardest questions and all the doubts of their subjects.

paras.t: Et factum est, quum consummasset, hoc est, perfecte terminasset, Jesus parabolas istas septem, non solum eas, sed etiam earum mysteria seu interpretationes disserendo discipulis, transiit inde, recedens a domo in qua locutus est ista. Et veniens in patriam suam, videlicet Galilæam, in qua conceptus, nutritus, atque moratus est, docebat eos, videlicet compatriotas et concives suos in urbe Nazareth, secundum Hieronymum, in synagogis eorum, ita ut mirarentur Nazareni, et dicerent: Unde huic sapientia hæc et virtutes, hoc est miracula? quasi dicerent: Quis dedit ei tanta dona? Noverant enim quod non habuit sapientiam istam per studium, juxta illud Joannis septimo: Unde hic scit litteras, quum non didicerit? Virtutem quoque miraculorum æstimabant sibi non esse collatam a Deo, propter ignobilitatem parentelæ. Unde subditur:
paras.en: [[13:53|And it came to pass: when Jesus had finished these parables|Et factum est, quum consummasset, hoc est, perfecte terminasset, Jesus parabolas istas]]: finished, that is, brought perfectly to an end, these seven parables, by explaining to the disciples not only the parables but also their mysteries or interpretations, [[13:53|he passed from thence|transiit inde]], leaving the house in which He had spoken these things. [[13:54|And coming into his own country|Et veniens in patriam suam]], namely Galilee, in which He was conceived, brought up and lived, [[13:54|he taught them|docebat eos]], namely His fellow countrymen and fellow citizens in the town of Nazareth, according to Jerome, [[13:54|in their synagogues, so that they wondered and said|in synagogis eorum, ita ut mirarentur Nazareni, et dicerent]], the Nazarenes did: [[13:54|How came this man by this wisdom and miracles|Unde huic sapientia hæc et virtutes]]? (virtues, that is, miracles); as if to say: Who gave Him such great gifts? For they knew that He did not have this wisdom from study, according to that saying in the seventh chapter of John: [[John 7:15|How doth this man know letters, having never learned|Unde hic scit litteras, quum non didicerit]]? The power of miracles, too, they reckoned had not been given Him by God, because of the lowliness of His kindred. So it is added:

paras.t: Nonne hic est fabri filius, scilicet ipsius Joseph (qui fertur fuisse faber lignarius)? Marci sexto ita habetur: Nonne hic est faber, filius Mariæ? Vocabant ergo Jesum fabrum: vel despective, sicut communiter fit quum filiis improperatur officium patrum (vocantur nomine talis officii, ut si filius fullonis promoveatur in episcopum, invidi dicunt, Ille fullo); vel, quia Jesus patrem suum putativum frequenter adjuvit in suo officio: quod Nazarenos istos non latuit. Nam usque ad tricesimum annum habitavit cum eis. Nonne mater ejus dicitur Maria, et fratres ejus sunt Jacobus, et Joseph, et Simon, et Judas? De istis fratribus dictum est supra, quod fuerunt consobrini Christi, et filii Mariæ uxoris Cleophæ, sororis Virginis gloriosæ, ut dicit Hieronymus in libro contra Helvidium hæreticum. S. Thomas in uno loco ait, quod illi qui in Evangelio appellantur fratres Christi, fuerunt filii Joseph de alia conjuge. Alibi dicit, quod Joseph creditur virgo fuisse: quod Beda et alii communiter asserunt; et sic fratres isti fuerunt Christi nepotes. Quum enim in cruce commiserit Matrem suam virginem virgini, quum esset adulta, probabile est quod juvenculam non commiserit, nisi virgini sponso. Et sorores ejus, id est cognatæ, nonne apud nos sunt, hoc est inter nos habitando?
paras.en: [[13:55|Is not this the carpenter's son|Nonne hic est fabri filius]], namely of Joseph himself (who is said to have been a carpenter)? In the sixth chapter of Mark it reads thus: [[Mark 6:3|Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary|Nonne hic est faber, filius Mariæ]]? So they called Jesus a carpenter: either contemptuously, as commonly happens when sons are taunted with their fathers' trade (they are called by the name of that trade, so that if a fuller's son is raised to be a bishop, the envious say, "That fuller"); or because Jesus often helped His putative father in his trade, which these Nazarenes knew well. For He lived among them up to His thirtieth year. [[13:55|Is not his mother called Mary, and his brethren James, and Joseph, and Simon, and Jude|Nonne mater ejus dicitur Maria, et fratres ejus sunt Jacobus, et Joseph, et Simon, et Judas?]]? Of these brethren it was said above[[Matt 12:46||]] that they were Christ's cousins, the sons of Mary the wife of Cleophas, the sister of the glorious Virgin, as Jerome says in his book against the heretic Helvidius. St Thomas says in one place that those who are called Christ's brethren in the Gospel were sons of Joseph by another wife. Elsewhere he says that Joseph is believed to have been a virgin, which Bede and others commonly affirm; and so these brethren were Christ's kinsmen [Latin nepotes, here in the wider sense of relatives]. For since on the cross He entrusted His virgin Mother to a virgin[[John 19:26||]] when she was a grown woman, it is probable that He did not entrust her as a young girl to any but a virgin spouse. [[13:56|And his sisters|Et sorores ejus]], that is, His kinswomen, [[13:56|are they not all with us|nonne apud nos sunt]], that is, living among us?

paras.t: Et scandalizabantur in eo, id est, ex consideratione humilis genealogiæ cognationisque Christi, in peccatum prolapsi sunt, æstimantes quod sapientiam et virtutes habuerit a diabolo potius quam a Deo. In quo patet infinita eorum cæcitas atque perversitas, quum multi Prophetarum illitterati et egeni exstiterint, et tamen prophetali sapientia Deo miserante impleti sunt, ut Amos agricola vellicans sycomoros, Jeremias puer. Jesus autem dixit eis: Non est Propheta sine honore, nisi in patria sua, et in domo, id est familia sua: non quod alibi ubique honoretur, vel ab omnibus suis compatriotis spernatur; sed quia communiter sic est, quod a suis magis contemnitur, quam ab aliis. Et hoc ex invidia oritur, vel superbia: quia homines male pati possunt, ut compares sui præferantur eis; et compatriotæ melius sciunt imperfectum alicujus quam alii, et frequenter convertunt oculum mentis ad considerationem ejus quod homo fuit tempore pueritiæ, vel quum eis similis videbatur. Et non fecit ibi virtutes multas, hoc est multa miracula, saltem hac vice, propter incredulitatem illorum, videlicet, quia indigni erant, et etiam ne faceret eos majori damnationi obnoxios. Fecit tamen ibi quædam miracula, ne excusationem suæ infidelitatis haberent. Unde Marcus habet: Et non poterat ibi virtutem ullam facere, scilicet potentia ordinata, quia non decuit, nisi paucos infirmos impositis manibus curavit.
paras.en: [[13:57|And they were scandalized in his regard|Et scandalizabantur in eo]], that is, considering Christ's lowly descent and kindred, they fell into sin, thinking that He had His wisdom and powers from the devil rather than from God. In this their boundless blindness and perversity is plain, since many of the Prophets were unlettered and poor, and yet by God's mercy were filled with prophetic wisdom: as Amos, a husbandman plucking sycamore figs[[Amos 7:14||]], and Jeremias, a child[[Jer 1:6||]]. [[13:57|But Jesus said to them: A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country, and in his own house|Jesus autem dixit eis: Non est Propheta sine honore, nisi in patria sua, et in domo]], that is, his own household: not that he is honoured everywhere else, or despised by all his countrymen, but because it is commonly so, that he is despised more by his own than by others. And this springs from envy, or pride: for men can hardly bear that their equals should be preferred to them; and a man's countrymen know his imperfection better than others do, and often turn the eye of the mind to what he was in the time of his boyhood, or when he seemed like them. [[13:58|And he wrought not many miracles there|Et non fecit ibi virtutes multas]]: virtues, that is, many miracles, at least on this occasion, [[13:58|because of their unbelief|propter incredulitatem illorum]], that is, because they were unworthy, and also so as not to make them liable to greater damnation. Yet He did some miracles there, so that they should have no excuse for their unbelief. Hence Mark has: [[Mark 6:5|he could not do any miracles there|non poterat ibi virtutem ullam facere]], namely by His ordered power [that is, God's power as it acts according to the order He has chosen, as distinct from His absolute power], because it was not fitting, [[Mark 6:5|only that he cured a few that were sick, laying his hands upon them|nisi paucos infirmos impositis manibus curavit]].

14.title: Expositio capituli quartidecimi: In illo tempore, audivit Herodes tetrarcha famam Jesu, etc.
14.title_en: Exposition of the fourteenth chapter: At that time Herod the Tetrarch heard the fame of Jesus, etc.

paras.t: In illo tempore, audivit Herodes Antipas, filius Herodis Ascalonitæ, cujus tempore natus est Christus, qui et infantes occidit, tetrarcha, id est princeps quartæ partis regni. Nam patre ejus mortuo, divisum est regnum Judææ in quatuor partes: quarum duæ datæ sunt Archelao filio prædicti Herodis; tertia pars, Philippo; quarta, huic Herodi data est ab imperatore Romano. Famam Jesu, id est rumorem miraculorum, documentorum, et operum Christi. Et ait pueris, id est satellitibus suis vel sibi familiariter junctis: Hic Jesus, de quo audio tanta, est Joannes Baptista. Sciebat enim Herodes Joannem virum sanctum et justum fuisse, ut habet Marcus. Idcirco, audiens tanta de Christo, putavit quod ipse esset idem justus et sanctus, quasi Deus non haberet nisi unum excellentem ministrum in mundo. Ipse Joannes, quem ego decollavi, surrexit a mortuis. Ex hoc patet quod iste Herodes, sicut et pater ejus, legem Moysis acceptavit. Et ideo virtutes, hoc est præcedentia merita seu opera virtuosa Joannis, operantur in eo, id est, sunt causa quod tanta mirabilia agit. Quamvis enim Joannes ante mortem suam nullum fecerat signum, æstimavit tamen Herodes, quod post resurrectionem miracula faceret, quasi ad statum meliorem promotus. Et quia de morte Joannis jam tactum est, Evangelista describit causam, modum et ordinem suæ occisionis.
paras.en: [[14:1|At that time|In illo tempore]] [[14:1|Herod|Herodes]] Antipas, the son of Herod of Ascalon, in whose time Christ was born and who also killed the infants[[Matt 2:16||]], [[14:1|the Tetrarch|tetrarcha]], that is, prince of the fourth part of the kingdom, [[14:1|heard|audivit]]. For on his father's death the kingdom of Judea was divided into four parts: two of them were given to Archelaus, the son of the said Herod; the third part to Philip; the fourth was given to this Herod by the Roman emperor. He heard [[14:1|the fame of Jesus|Famam Jesu]], that is, the report of Christ's miracles, teachings and works. [[14:2|And he said to his servants|Et ait pueris]], that is, to his guards, or to those close to him: This Jesus, of whom I hear such things, [[14:2|is John the Baptist|est Joannes Baptista]]. For Herod knew that John had been a holy and just man, as Mark has it[[Mark 6:20||]]. Therefore, hearing such things of Christ, he thought that He was that same just and holy man, as if God had only one outstanding minister in the world. John himself, whom I beheaded, [[14:2|he is risen from the dead|surrexit a mortuis]]. From this it is plain that this Herod, like his father, accepted the law of Moses. [[14:2|and therefore mighty works|Et ideo virtutes]], that is, John's preceding merits or virtuous works, [[14:2|shew forth themselves in him|operantur in eo]], that is, are the cause of his doing such wonders. For although John had worked no sign before his death, Herod nevertheless reckoned that after his resurrection he worked miracles, as one raised to a better state. And since the death of John has now been touched on, the Evangelist describes the cause, manner and order of his killing.

paras.t: Herodes autem per servos suos tenuit, hoc est, comprehendit ac cepit, Joannem, et alligavit eum, et posuit in carcerem, propter Herodiadem uxorem fratris sui, id est ad instantiam Herodiadis conjugis Philippi, qui fuit frater Herodis: cujus legitimam conjugem nomine Herodiadem, abstulit iste Herodes, et secum in adulterio sedit. Vel, Propter Herodiadem, hoc est propter amorem carnalem quem habuit ad eam: quam tanto carnalitatis ardore amavit, quod increpationem de hoc ferre non potuit. Vel, Propter Herodiadem, id est, ad hunc finem, ut Joanne occiso, cum illa quietius ac securius delectaretur. Dicebat enim illi, puta Herodi, Joannes: Non licet tibi, qui legem Moysis recepisti, habere eam in conjugem: quia hoc prohibet lex, ne quis uxorem fratris, illo vivente, accipiat. Et volens Herodes illum, id est Joannem, occidere, timuit populum, ne insurgeret contra ipsum, si Joannem occideret, quia sicut prophetam eum habebant, id est, Joannem reputavit populus communis esse prophetam. Unde dictio illa, Sicut, hoc loco dicit non tantum similitudinem, sed etiam veritatem. Marcus habet, quod Herodes metuebat Joannem, sciens eum virum sanctum et justum; et custodiebat eum, et audito eo, multa faciebat, et libenter eum audiebat. Quibus verbis Marcus præmisit: Herodias autem insidiabatur Joanni, volens occidere eum, nec poterat. Cujus impotentiæ causam Marcus assignans, dicit quæ allegata est: Herodes enim metuebat Joannem. Ex quibus patet, quod mulier ista nefaria, primo concepit odium contra Joannem suæ concupiscentiæ inimicum. Videns enim quod Herodes Joannem libenter audivit, eoque audito multa operabatur, cœpit timere ne propter prædicationem Joannis, Herodes eam abjiceret, et primo redderet viro. Quod ergo nunc dicitur, quod Herodes quærebat Joannem occidere, intelligendum est processisse ex Herodiadis suggestione. Effeminatus quippe Herodes in tantum victus est luxuriosæ mulieris concupiscentia et amore, quod contra legem et propriæ rationis judicium acquievit mulieri, et insidiabatur Joanni, quem ante libenter audivit ac timuit.
paras.en: [[14:3|For Herod had apprehended John|Herodes autem per servos suos tenuit, hoc est, comprehendit ac cepit, Joannem]] through his servants, that is, seized and took him, [[14:3|and bound him, and put him into prison|et alligavit eum, et posuit in carcerem]], [[14:3|because of Herodias, his brother's wife|propter Herodiadem uxorem fratris sui]], that is, at the urging of Herodias, the wife of Philip, who was Herod's brother: this Herod took away his lawful wife, Herodias by name, and lived with her in adultery. Or, because of Herodias, that is, because of the carnal love he had for her: he loved her with such a heat of the flesh that he could not bear to be rebuked for it. Or, because of Herodias, that is, to this end, that with John killed he might take his pleasure with her more quietly and safely. [[14:4|For John said to him|Dicebat enim illi, puta Herodi, Joannes]], namely to Herod: [[14:4|It is not lawful for thee|Non licet tibi]], who have received the law of Moses, [[14:4|to have her|habere eam]] as wife: for the law forbids anyone to take his brother's wife while the brother is alive[[Lev 18:16||]][[Lev 20:21||]]. [[14:5|And having a mind to put him to death|Et volens illum occidere]], Herod, him, that is, John, [[14:5|he feared the people|timuit populum]], lest they should rise against him if he killed John, [[14:5|because they esteemed him as a prophet|quia sicut prophetam eum habebant]], that is, the common people held John to be a prophet. So the word "as" here expresses not only likeness but truth. Mark has it that [[Mark 6:20|Herod feared John, knowing him to be a just and holy man: and kept him, and when he heard him, did many things: and he heard him willingly|Herodes metuebat Joannem, sciens eum virum sanctum et justum; et custodiebat eum, et audito eo, multa faciebat, et libenter eum audiebat]]. Before these words Mark put: [[Mark 6:19|Now Herodias laid snares for him: and was desirous to put him to death and could not|Herodias autem insidiabatur Joanni, volens occidere eum, nec poterat]]. Giving the cause of her inability, Mark says what has been quoted: [[Mark 6:20|For Herod feared John|Herodes enim metuebat Joannem]]. From this it is plain that this wicked woman first conceived hatred against John as the enemy of her lust. For seeing that Herod heard John willingly and did many things when he had heard him, she began to fear that because of John's preaching Herod would cast her off and give her back to her first husband. So what is said here, that Herod sought to kill John, is to be understood as having come from Herodias's prompting. For Herod, made womanish, was so overcome by his lust and love for this wanton woman that, against the law and the judgment of his own reason, he gave in to the woman and laid snares for John, whom he had formerly heard willingly and feared.

paras.t: Die autem natalis, id est anniversario die nativitatis Herodis, saltavit, hoc est, chorizando tripudiavit, filia Herodiadis, ex alio viro, in medio aulæ seu alterius loci, vel in medio eorum qui aderant; et placuit Herodi saltans filia meretricis, et saltatio ejus. Unde, id est ex qua vana complacentia, cum juramento pollicitus est, id est promisit, ei dare quodcumque postulasset ab eo, quamvis mediam regni partem. At illa puella præmonita a matre sua Herodiade, a qua petivit consilium, dicens: Quid petam? Et illa: Caput Joannis. Da mihi, inquit puella Herodi, hic, hoc est in loco præsenti, in disco, caput Joannis Baptistæ: quod fieri non potuit, nisi decapitaretur. Et contristatus est rex Herodes, quod tam inconsulte jurasset ac promisisset, et quod illa tam crudeliter postulasset. Quidam dicunt quod Romani abstulerunt a Judæis nomen regium. Et tamen hoc loco Herodes dominus Judæorum, dicitur rex. Propter juramentum autem quod fecit puellæ, ne videretur perjurus, et eos qui pariter recumbebant, id est, simul cum ipso manducabant. Fecit enim cœnam principibus, et tribunis, et primis Galilææ. Itaque, propter istos, ne in tantorum virorum præsentia videretur perjurus et mendax, vel ne ipsi turbarentur, quia fortassis consenserunt Herodiadi in mortem Joannis, jussit dari caput Joannis puellæ nequissimæ.
paras.en: [[14:6|But on Herod's birthday|Die autem natalis]], that is, on the anniversary of Herod's birth, [[14:6|the daughter of Herodias danced|saltavit filia Herodiadis]], that is, leapt in a round dance, her daughter by another husband, [[14:6|before them|in medio]], in the middle of the hall or some other place, or in the midst of those present; [[14:6|and pleased Herod|et placuit Herodi]], the harlot's daughter as she danced, and her dancing. [[14:7|Whereupon|Unde]], that is, from that empty delight, [[14:7|he promised with an oath, to give her whatsoever she would ask of him|cum juramento pollicitus est, id est promisit, ei dare quodcumque postulasset ab eo]], even if it were half his kingdom[[Mark 6:23||]]. [[14:8|But she being instructed before by her mother|At illa puella præmonita a matre sua]], Herodias, whose advice she sought, saying: [[Mark 6:24|What shall I ask|Quid petam]]? And she said: [[Mark 6:24|The head of John|Caput Joannis]]. [[14:8|said: Give me here in a dish the head of John the Baptist|Da mihi, inquit, hic in disco caput Joannis Baptistæ]]: give me, the girl says to Herod, here, that is, in this place; which could not be done unless he were beheaded. [[14:9|And the king was struck sad|Et contristatus est rex]], Herod, because he had sworn and promised so rashly, and because she had asked so cruelly. Some say that the Romans had taken the royal title away from the Jews; and yet here Herod, lord of the Jews, is called king. [[14:9|yet because of his oath|Propter juramentum autem]], which he made to the girl, lest he should seem to be forsworn, [[14:9|and for them that sat with him at table|et eos qui pariter recumbebant]], that is, who were eating with him. For he made a supper [[Mark 6:21|for the princes, and tribunes, and chief men of Galilee|principibus, et tribunis, et primis Galilææ]]. So, because of these, lest he should seem forsworn and a liar in the presence of such great men, or lest they should be put out (for perhaps they had agreed with Herodias on John's death), [[14:9|he commanded it to be given|jussit dari]]: the head of John, to the most wicked girl.

paras.t: Secundum Hieronymum, et alios plures, Herodes cum Herodiade ordinavit quomodo posset Joannem occidere; et invento concordi consilio, fecit convivium, in quo filia Herodiadis tripudiaret: qua saltante, finxit se rex ultra modum delectatum in saltatione illius, moxque jurando promisit dare ei quod peteret. Qua caput Joannis petente, simulavit se rex contristari, ut populus haberet eum excusatum de morte Joannis, quum tamen corde gauderet. Et hoc alii probant: Primo, quia ut scribitur hic, Herodes ante saltationem, accubitum, et postulationem puellæ, voluit Joannem occidere. Secundo, quoniam nisi optasset mortem Joannis, non occidisset eum propter juramentum, quia sub promissione hujusmodi non intelligitur aliquod illicitum cadere. Tertio, quia non est probabile quod propter saltationem promitteret puellæ tantum donum. Verumtamen Augustinus sentire videtur, quod Herodes vere metuebat et libenter audiebat Joannem, et ex animo tristis effectus est postulatione illa audita: quod littera hujus capituli et verbis Marci magis consonare apparet. Quod igitur dicitur, Herodem voluisse occidere Joannem, intelligi potest de voluntario permixto involuntario, quomodo Pilatus voluit crucifigere Christum: quem utique voluntarie crucifixit, aliter non peccasset: sed erat voluntarium illud involuntario mixtum. Denique, sicut juxta Salomonem, vult et non vult piger, si talis vult et non vult, hoc quoque quod vult, efficit cum mœrore, quemadmodum negotiator cum tristitia projicit merces in mare. Habuit ergo displicentiam contra Joannem, propter increpationem ipsius, et inclinationem ad occidendum eum, propter Herodiadis preces; sed non tantum, quod absolute decrevit vel optavit eum occidere, secundum Augustinum: ideo contristatus est audita petitione petulantis puellæ. Ad secundum dici potest, quod reges, principes et superbi, volunt promissa ac juramenta sua implere, quamvis illicita, ne ab hominibus judicentur perjuri aut mentientes. Et quod opponitur: Si puella petisset caput patris et matris, Herodes non consensisset, ergo quod juravit puellæ dare quidquid peteret, insidiando fecit: hoc solveretur, dicendo quod intentio Herodis non erat absolute promittere, sed dummodo non esset penitus irrationabile et absurdum. Ideo enim dixit: Licet dimidium regni mei. Quasi diceret: Si aliquid majus petieris, non præstarem. Ad tertium diceretur, quod reges quum vino calefacti sint, faciliter inclinantur ad promittendum, ut patet de Assuero, quomodo promiserat Esther. Quamvis autem caput Joannis dare saltanti, fuit maxime irrationabile, tamen Herodes non reputavit hoc tam irrationabile ut alia multa.
paras.en: According to Jerome and many others, Herod arranged with Herodias how he might kill John; and having agreed on a plan, he gave a banquet at which Herodias's daughter was to dance. When she danced, the king pretended to be delighted beyond measure with her dancing, and at once promised on oath to give her what she asked. When she asked for John's head, the king pretended to be sad, so that the people would hold him excused for John's death, though at heart he rejoiced. And these others prove it: first, because, as is written here, Herod wanted to kill John before the dancing, the banquet and the girl's request; second, because unless he had wished for John's death, he would not have killed him on account of his oath, since nothing unlawful is understood to fall under a promise of that kind; third, because it is not likely that he would have promised the girl so great a gift for a dance. Augustine, however, seems to hold that Herod truly feared John and heard him willingly, and was made sad in his heart when he heard that request; and this appears to agree better with the letter of this chapter and with the words of Mark. So when it is said that Herod wished to kill John, this can be understood of a willing mixed with unwilling, in the way that Pilate willed to crucify Christ: he certainly crucified Him willingly, or he would not have sinned; but that willing was mixed with unwilling. Indeed, as according to Solomon [[Prov 13:4|The sluggard willeth, and willeth not|vult et non vult piger]], if such a man wills and does not will, what he does will he carries out with grief, as a merchant throws his goods into the sea with sorrow. So Herod felt displeasure against John because of his rebuke, and an inclination to kill him because of Herodias's entreaties; but not so much that he decided or wished outright to kill him, according to Augustine; and so he was saddened when he heard the request of the impudent girl. To the second argument it can be said that kings, princes and the proud want to fulfil their promises and oaths, even unlawful ones, so as not to be judged by men to be perjurers or liars. And as for the objection, "If the girl had asked for the head of her father or mother, Herod would not have consented; so his swearing to give the girl whatever she asked was part of a plot", this would be answered by saying that Herod's intention was not to promise absolutely, but provided the request was not wholly unreasonable and absurd. That is why he said: [[Mark 6:23|though it be the half of my kingdom|Licet dimidium regni mei]]; as if to say: If you asked for anything greater, I would not grant it. To the third it would be said that kings, when warmed with wine, are easily inclined to make promises, as is plain of Assuerus and how he had promised Esther[[Esth 5:6||]]. And although giving John's head to a dancer was utterly unreasonable, Herod did not think it as unreasonable as many other things.

paras.t: Misitque spiculatorem, et decollavit per manum illius Joannem in carcere. Et allatum est caput ejus in disco, et datum est puellæ, et tulit matri suæ Herodiadi, ut viso capite increpatoris sui, gloriaretur de condigna vindicta. O qualia sunt judicia Dei! Et quomodo permittit Deus justus et sanctus, electos suos in præsenti sæculo tribulari, a reprobis opprimi, multis injuriis affici! Scit enim quam salubre et meritorium hoc eis exsistat. Ecce sanctissimum virum, consanguineum Christi, præconem, præcursorem, baptistam Salvatoris, quo inter natos mulierum major non fuit, permisit ad suggestionem adulteræ incarcerari, ad instantiam petulantis ac vilis puellæ occidi. Nemo ergo servorum Christi murmuret, contristetur, aut pusillanimis fiat, dum adversitatibus atque injuriis fatigatur. Multæ enim tribulationes justorum; et tanquam aurum in fornace probavit Deus electos.
paras.en: [[14:10|And he sent|Misitque]] an executioner, [[14:10|and beheaded John in the prison|et decollavit Joannem in carcere]] by his hand. [[14:11|And his head was brought in a dish: and it was given to the damsel, and she brought it to her mother|Et allatum est caput ejus in disco, et datum est puellæ, et tulit matri suæ]], Herodias, so that on seeing the head of her rebuker she might glory in a fitting revenge. O what are the judgments of God! How the just and holy God permits His elect in this present world to be afflicted, oppressed by the reprobate, and visited with many injuries! For He knows how wholesome and meritorious this is for them. Behold, the holiest of men, Christ's kinsman, the herald, forerunner and baptizer of the Saviour, than whom [[Matt 11:11|among them that are born of women a greater|inter natos mulierum major]] there was not, He allowed to be imprisoned at the prompting of an adulteress and killed at the demand of an impudent and worthless girl. Let none of Christ's servants, then, murmur, be saddened, or lose heart when worn down by adversities and injuries. For [[Ps 33:20|Many are the afflictions of the just|Multæ enim tribulationes justorum]]; and [[Wis 3:6|As gold in the furnace, he hath proved them|tanquam aurum in fornace probavit]], God, His elect.

paras.t: Et accedentes discipuli ejus, puta Joannis, tulerunt corpus ejus de carcere, vel loco carceri propinquo, et sepelierunt illud, in urbe Sebaste, ut dicitur, quæ olim vocabatur Samaria. Nec dubium quin fecerint planctum magnum super tam dilectum et sanctum magistrum. Et venientes nuntiaverunt Jesu de occisione Joannis. Noverant enim Jesum esse cognatum et amicum Joannis præcipuum. Quod quum audisset Jesus: non quod tunc illud primo cognovit, quippe quum ipse omnia præterita, præsentia, et futura, a primo suæ conceptionis instanti agnoverit; sed tunc ostendit se illud cognoscere, faciendo quod subditur, secessit inde, videlicet a patria sua seu Nazareth, in navicula, ut pauper et humilis, vili et humili vehiculo navigaret trans fretum seu mare Galilææ, ut patet in Joanne. In locum desertum seorsum: non quasi timens ab Herode occidi, quem poterat solo nutu destruere; sed quasi cedens furori hostis, dansque exemplum vicissim declinandi persecutionem, et ut die divinitus præordinato pateretur in Jerusalem, sicut frequenter prædixit. Et quum audissent turbæ Jesum transisse ad locum hunc, secutæ sunt eum pedestres de civitatibus, nec dubium quin etiam de villis atque castellis. Causam quare secutæ sunt eum, Joannes refert, videlicet, quia videbant signa quæ faciebat super his qui infirmabantur.
paras.en: [[14:12|And his disciples came and took the body|Et accedentes discipuli ejus, puta Joannis, tulerunt corpus]], John's disciples, that is, his body from the prison, or from a place near the prison, [[14:12|and buried it|et sepelierunt illud]], in the city of Sebaste, as is said, which was once called Samaria. And no doubt they made great lamentation over so beloved and holy a master. [[14:12|and came and told Jesus|Et venientes nuntiaverunt Jesu]] of John's killing. For they knew that Jesus was John's kinsman and his special friend. [[14:13|Which when Jesus had heard|Quod quum audisset Jesus]]: not that He first learned it then, since He knew all things past, present and future from the first instant of His conception; but then He showed that He knew it, by doing what follows: [[14:13|he retired from thence|secessit inde]], namely from His own country, or Nazareth, [[14:13|by a boat|in navicula]], so that, poor and lowly, He might sail in a mean and lowly craft across the strait, or sea of Galilee, as appears in John[[John 6:1||]], [[14:13|into a desert place apart|In locum desertum seorsum]]: not as if He feared being killed by Herod, whom He could destroy with a nod; but as giving way to the enemy's fury, and giving us an example of avoiding persecution in our turn, and so that He might suffer in Jerusalem on the day appointed by God, as He often foretold. [[14:13|and the multitudes having heard of it|Et quum audissent turbæ]], that Jesus had crossed to this place, [[14:13|followed him on foot out of the cities|secutæ sunt eum pedestres de civitatibus]], and no doubt from the villages and hamlets too. John gives the reason why they followed Him, namely because [[John 6:2|they saw the miracles which he did on them that were diseased|videbant signa quæ faciebat super his qui infirmabantur]].

paras.t: Et exiens Jesus, hoc est, desertum locum egrediens, et turbis quodammodo obvians, vidit turbam multam, et misertus est eis, quia erant sicut oves non habentes pastorem, secundum Marcum; et curavit languidos eorum, hoc est infirmos quos turba adduxit, et docuit turbam. Per hoc mystice designatur, quod Christus ipsius vestigia sequentibus, ejusque gratiosam præsentiam quærentibus, protinus obviet, et ultro se offerat, juxta illud: Omnis qui quærit, invenit. Vulnera vitiorum in eis curat, et lumen sapientiæ influit.
paras.en: [[14:14|And he coming forth|Et exiens Jesus]], that is, going out of the desert place and in a manner going to meet the crowds, [[14:14|saw a great multitude, and had compassion on them|vidit turbam multam, et misertus est eis]], because [[Mark 6:34|they were as sheep not having a shepherd|erant sicut oves non habentes pastorem]], according to Mark; [[14:14|and healed their sick|et curavit languidos eorum]], that is, the sick whom the crowd had brought, and taught the crowd. By this it is mystically signified that Christ at once comes to meet those who follow in His footsteps and seek His gracious presence, and offers Himself freely, according to that saying: [[Matt 7:8|he that seeketh, findeth|Omnis qui quærit, invenit]]. He heals the wounds of vices in them, and pours in the light of wisdom.

paras.t: Vespere autem facto, accesserunt ad eum discipuli ejus, dicentes: Desertus est locus in quo sumus, id est domos et cibos non habens, et hora jam præteriit, id est, tempus hujus diei ad occasum jam tendit: idcirco dimitte turbas, dando eis licentiam vel consilium revertendi ad loca habitationis, ut euntes in castella, emant sibi escas. Marcus sic habet: Ut euntes in villas et vicos. Unde per castella, alia quoque loca convenientia intelliguntur. In quo declaratur sollicitudo superflua, imperfectaque fides discipulorum, qui dabant consilium recedendi a Christo et spirituali alimento, propter corporeum cibum, et quasi fame periclitari possent quibus adfuit Christus.
paras.en: [[14:15|And when it was evening, his disciples came to him, saying: This is a desert place|Vespere autem facto, accesserunt ad eum discipuli ejus, dicentes: Desertus est locus]] where we are, that is, with no houses or food, [[14:15|and the hour is now passed|et hora jam præteriit]], that is, the time of this day is already drawing to sunset: therefore [[14:15|send away the multitudes|dimitte turbas]], giving them leave, or advice, to return to the places where they live, [[14:15|that going into the towns, they may buy themselves victuals|ut euntes in castella, emant sibi escas]]. Mark has it thus: [[Mark 6:36|that going into the next villages and towns|Ut euntes in villas et vicos]]. So by "towns" other suitable places too are understood. In this the disciples' superfluous anxiety and imperfect faith are shown, in advising the people to leave Christ and spiritual food for the sake of bodily food, as if those with whom Christ was present could be in danger of hunger.

paras.t: Jesus autem dixit eis: Non habent necesse ire ad cibos emendos; date illis vos manducare. Quæritur, cur hoc Christus dixit discipulis, quos noverat non habere cibaria tanta. Dicendum: primo, ad insinuandum quod si discipuli habuissent fidem sicut granum sinapis, certi fuissent se sola prece posse acquirere escas sufficientes turbæ a Deo; secundo, intelligi potest per modum propheticæ prænuntiationis, ut Christus dicatur dixisse discipulis, Date illis manducare, quia scivit sic esse futurum. Sciendum tamen, quod antequam Christus hæc dixit, interrogavit Philippum: Unde ememus panes ut manducent hi? ut habet Joannes. Quo respondente, Ducentorum denariorum panes non sufficiunt eis, dixit Salvator: Vos date illis manducare. Responderunt discipuli: Euntes emamus denariis ducentis panes, et dabimus illis manducare. Qui dixit: Quot panes habetis? ut in Marco habetur. Quid autem ad hoc responderint, subjungit Matthæus. Responderunt ei: Non habemus hic nisi quinque panes et duos pisces. Joannes sic habet: Respondet ei Andreas: Est puer hic unus, habens quinque panes hordeaceos et duos pisces. Itaque per synecdochen ponitur pars pro toto; vel omnes respondisse dicuntur, quia Andreas respondit pro omnibus. Qui ait eis: Afferte huc illos mihi, panes et pisces.
paras.en: [[14:16|But Jesus said to them, They have no need to go|Jesus autem dixit eis: Non habent necesse ire]] to buy food; [[14:16|give you them to eat|date illis vos manducare]]. It is asked why Christ said this to the disciples, whom He knew had no such store of food. It must be said: first, to suggest that if the disciples had had [[Matt 17:19|faith as a grain of mustard seed|fidem sicut granum sinapis]], they would have been sure that by prayer alone they could obtain from God food enough for the crowd; second, it can be understood by way of prophetic foretelling, so that Christ is said to have told the disciples, give them to eat, because He knew it would be so. It should be known, however, that before Christ said this He asked Philip: [[John 6:5|Whence shall we buy bread, that these may eat|Unde ememus panes ut manducent hi]]? as John has it. When he answered, [[John 6:7|Two hundred pennyworth of bread is not sufficient for them|Ducentorum denariorum panes non sufficiunt eis]], the Saviour said: [[Mark 6:37|Give you them to eat|Vos date illis manducare]]. The disciples answered: [[Mark 6:37|Let us go and buy bread for two hundred pence, and we will give them to eat|Euntes emamus denariis ducentis panes, et dabimus illis manducare]]. And He said: [[Mark 6:38|How many loaves have you|Quot panes habetis]]? as is found in Mark. What they answered to this Matthew adds: [[14:17|They answered him: We have not here, but five loaves, and two fishes|Responderunt ei: Non habemus hic nisi quinque panes et duos pisces]]. John has it thus: Andrew answered Him[[John 6:8||]]: [[John 6:9|There is a boy here that hath five barley loaves and two fishes|Est puer hic unus, habens quinque panes hordeaceos et duos pisces]]. So the part is put for the whole by synecdoche; or all are said to have answered because Andrew answered for all. [[14:18|Who said to them: Bring them hither to me|Qui ait eis: Afferte huc illos mihi]], the loaves and fishes.

paras.t: Et quum jussisset turbam discumbere, hoc est manducare, vel ad manducandum quiescere seu sedere, super fœnum. Erat namque fœnum multum in loco illo, nec tabulas et sedilia habuerunt. Acceptis quinque panibus et duobus piscibus, adspiciens in cœlum: non quod per elevationem corporalium oculorum suorum, interiores oculi animæ suæ plus quam ante elevarentur ad Deum per contemplationem, quem indesinenter per speciem vidit. Sed adspexit in cœlum: Primo, ut daret nobis exemplum semper recurrendi ad Deum, juxta illud in Psalmo: Oculi mei semper ad Dominum. Secundo, ad significandum quod tota virtus et efficacia sua esset a Patre, quemadmodum ait apud Joannem: Non possum ego a me ipso facere quidquam. Benedixit: in quo docuit ante comestionem benedicere cibos; et fregit, et dedit discipulis panes jam fractos; discipuli autem dederunt turbis. Denique, inter manus Christi et discipulorum multiplicati sunt panes et pisces, vel per creationem novorum panum et piscium, vel per solam eorum multiplicationem, sine alicujus materiæ conversione in panes piscesque, vel per augmentationem, convertendo aliquid in panes et pisces. De modo siquidem hujus multiplicationis, est longissima atque difficilis disputatio inter doctores.
paras.en: [[14:19|And when he had commanded the multitude to sit down|Et quum jussisset turbam discumbere]], that is, to eat, or to rest or sit down in order to eat, [[14:19|upon the grass|super fœnum]]. For [[John 6:10|there was much grass in the place|Erat namque fœnum multum in loco illo]], and they had no tables or benches. [[14:19|he took the five loaves and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven|Acceptis quinque panibus et duobus piscibus, adspiciens in cœlum]]: not that by raising His bodily eyes the inner eyes of His soul were raised to God in contemplation more than before, since He saw God unceasingly face to face. But He looked up to heaven: first, to give us an example of always having recourse to God, according to that saying in the Psalm: [[Ps 24:15|My eyes are ever towards the Lord|Oculi mei semper ad Dominum]]; second, to signify that all His power and efficacy was from the Father, as He says in John: [[John 5:30|I cannot of myself do any thing|Non possum ego a me ipso facere quidquam]]. [[14:19|he blessed|Benedixit]], in which He taught us to bless our food before eating; [[14:19|and brake, and gave the loaves to his disciples|et fregit, et dedit discipulis panes]], already broken; [[14:19|and the disciples to the multitudes|discipuli autem dederunt turbis]]. So the loaves and fishes were multiplied in the hands of Christ and the disciples, either by the creation of new loaves and fishes, or by their multiplication alone without any matter being turned into loaves and fishes, or by increase, by turning something into loaves and fishes. On the manner of this multiplication there is indeed a very long and difficult dispute among the doctors.

paras.t: Et manducaverunt omnes, et saturati sunt omnes. Et discipuli tulerunt, hoc est, colligendo a manducantibus abstulerunt, reliquias ciborum remanentes, duodecim cophinos fragmentorum plenos. Ponit continens pro contento, hoc est fragmenta sportarum duodecim. Mystica horum explanatio poni solet in Joannis evangelio. Unde ad locum illum hanc differo. Manducantium autem numerus fuit quinque millia virorum, exceptis mulieribus et parvulis, quorum numerus forsitan numerum virorum excessit. Quemadmodum vero in Numeris habetur, Viri vocantur qui vicesimum annum attigerunt, quasi potentes ad bella procedere.
paras.en: [[14:20|And they did all eat, and were filled|Et manducaverunt omnes, et saturati sunt]], all of them. [[14:20|And they took up what remained|Et discipuli tulerunt, hoc est, colligendo a manducantibus abstulerunt, reliquias]], the disciples, that is, gathered up from those eating and took away what was left of the food, [[14:20|twelve full baskets of fragments|duodecim cophinos fragmentorum plenos]]. He puts the container for the contents, that is, fragments enough for twelve baskets. The mystical explanation of these things is usually given in the Gospel of John, so I put it off to that place. [[14:21|And the number of them that did eat, was five thousand men, besides women and children|Manducantium autem numerus fuit quinque millia virorum, exceptis mulieribus et parvulis]], whose number perhaps exceeded the number of the men. As is found in Numbers, those are called men who have reached their twentieth year, as able to go out to war[[Num 1:3||]].

paras.t: Et statim jussit discipulos suos ascendere in naviculam, et præcedere eum trans fretum, videlicet ultra mare Galilææ. Imo coegit eos ad hoc, secundum Marcum: per quod patet, quod nec ad horam libenter separabantur a tam dulci ac potenti magistro. Nihilominus statim obtemperaverunt. Donec dimitteret turbas a se recedere, et tunc sequeretur discipulos. Turbæ enim noluerunt abire, nisi viso discipulorum recessu. Et dimissa turba, ascendit, imo secundum Joannem, fugit, in montem solus orare. Ratio cur fecit discipulos præcedere, et cur ipse fugit in montem prædicti deserti, exprimitur in Joanne, quo legitur: Sciens Jesus quia venturi erant, ut raperent et facerent eum regem, viso scilicet tanto miraculo, fugit in montem. In quo docuit honorem et gloriam mundi humiliter declinare. Vespere autem facto, solus erat ibi, in vertice montis. Porro, quod Christus turba dimissa ascendit montem causa orandi, ostendit quod aliorum præsentia frequenter impedit orationis instantiam ac fervorem, et quod locus sublimis seu opportunus occasionaliter proficit ad excitandum mentis fervorem in orando, laudando, contemplandoque Deum; et item, quod prælatus, prædicator ac doctor dominici gregis, semper quum potest redire debet ad locum quietum, in quo solus cum Domino occupetur, atque ab eo purgetur, illuminetur ac perficiatur, ita ut rediens, memoriam abundantiæ suavitatis Dei gustatæ suis eructuet, gratiamque perceptam aliis administret.
paras.en: [[14:22|And forthwith Jesus|Et statim]] [[14:22|obliged his disciples to go up into the boat, and to go before him over the water|jussit discipulos suos ascendere in naviculam, et præcedere eum trans fretum]], that is, across the sea of Galilee. Indeed He compelled them to it, according to Mark[[Mark 6:45||]]: from which it is plain that they did not willingly part even for an hour from so sweet and mighty a Master. Nevertheless they obeyed at once. [[14:22|till he dismissed the people|Donec dimitteret turbas]] to go away from Him, and then He would follow the disciples. For the crowds would not go away until they had seen the disciples depart. [[14:23|And having dismissed the multitude, he went into a mountain alone to pray|Et dimissa turba, ascendit in montem solus orare]]: went up, or rather, according to John, fled. The reason why He made the disciples go before Him, and why He fled into the mountain of that desert, is given in John, where we read: [[John 6:15|when he knew that they would come to take him by force and make him king|Sciens Jesus quia venturi erant, ut raperent et facerent eum regem]] (having seen so great a miracle, that is), He fled into the mountain.
