In this He taught us humbly to avoid the honour and glory of the world. [[14:23|And when it was evening, he was there alone|Vespere autem facto, solus erat ibi]], on the top of the mountain. Further, Christ's going up the mountain to pray once the crowd was dismissed shows that the presence of others often hinders the earnestness and fervour of prayer; and that a high or suitable place can help to stir up fervour of mind in praying to, praising and contemplating God; and also that the prelate, preacher and teacher of the Lord's flock ought always, when he can, to go back to a quiet place, where he may be busy alone with the Lord and be purged, enlightened and perfected by Him, so that on his return he may pour out to his people the memory of the abundance of God's sweetness that he has tasted[[Ps 144:7||]], and minister to others the grace he has received.

paras.t: Navicula autem, in qua erant discipuli, in medio mari, id est stagno prædicto: non enim fuit Magnum mare; jactabatur fluctibus, orta tempestate in aqua. Erat enim contrarius ventus navigationi eorum, nec poterant facile remigare. Ex quo figuratum est, quod carentes præsentia Christi, variis periculis subjacent, ejusque interna consolatione absente, diversæ afflictiones et tempestates tentationum oriuntur in animo. Ideo sanctus Job: Pone me (inquit) juxta te, et cujusvis manus pugnet contra me.
paras.en: [[14:24|But the boat|Navicula autem]], in which the disciples were, [[14:24|in the midst of the sea|in medio mari]], that is, of the lake already mentioned (for it was not the Great Sea [the Mediterranean]), [[14:24|was tossed with the waves|jactabatur fluctibus]], a storm having arisen on the water. [[14:24|for the wind was contrary|Erat enim contrarius ventus]] to their sailing, and they could not easily row. This figures that those who lack the presence of Christ are exposed to various dangers, and when His inward consolation is absent, various afflictions and storms of temptation arise in the soul. Therefore holy Job says: [[Job 17:3|set me beside thee, and let any man's hand fight against me|Pone me (inquit) juxta te, et cujusvis manus pugnet contra me]].

paras.t: Quarta autem vigilia noctis, id est tribus partibus noctis jam lapsis, et ultima parte ejus instante vel inchoata. Solebant enim milites tempore prælii exercitum custodientes, dividere noctem in quatuor partes, quatenus in qualibet parte una pars militum vigilaret ad custodiendum exercitum. Venit Jesus ad eos, ambulans supra mare, per agilitatis dotem, secundum Hugonem: quod tamen alii negant. Secundum Marcum, Jesus stans in terra, vidit discipulos laborantes in remigando, et tamen non statim, sed circa finem noctis venit ad eos, qui tota nocte periclitabantur: ad designandum, quod sæpe permittit electos suos ad tempus affligi, ut a venialibus purgentur, et Christi gratiam atque præsentiam invocando, ampliori gratia et gloria decorentur. Et videntes eum supra mare ambulantem, turbati sunt, propter rem prorsus insolitam, dicentes: Quia phantasma est, id est apparentia rei non exsistentis quod esse videtur. Forsan timebant ne esset spiritus malignus in specie Christi. Et præ timore clamaverunt, divinam protectionem invocando, quia timebant a dæmone illudi, et nocumentum incurrere.
paras.en: [[14:25|And in the fourth watch of the night|Quarta autem vigilia noctis]], that is, when three parts of the night had already passed and its last part was at hand or had begun. For soldiers guarding an army in time of war used to divide the night into four parts, so that in each part one section of the soldiers kept watch to guard the army. [[14:25|he came to them walking upon the sea|Venit Jesus ad eos, ambulans supra mare]], Jesus did, by the endowment of agility [one of the endowments of a glorified body, by which it moves at the soul's command without hindrance], according to Hugh; which others, however, deny. According to Mark, Jesus, standing on land, saw the disciples [[Mark 6:48|labouring in rowing|laborantes in remigando]], and yet He came to them not at once but towards the end of the night, though they were in danger all night long: to show that He often allows His elect to be afflicted for a time, so that they may be purged of venial sins and, by calling on Christ's grace and presence, be adorned with fuller grace and glory. [[14:26|And they seeing him walking upon the sea, were troubled|Et videntes eum supra mare ambulantem, turbati sunt]], because of a thing wholly unheard of, [[14:26|saying: It is an apparition|dicentes: Quia phantasma est]], that is, the appearance of a thing that does not exist as it seems to. Perhaps they feared it was an evil spirit in the likeness of Christ. [[14:26|And they cried out for fear|Et præ timore clamaverunt]], calling on God's protection, because they feared being deluded by a demon and coming to harm.

paras.t: Statimque Jesus locutus est eis, dicens: Ego sum sicut apparet, et cujus vocem cognoscitis, et qui verum esse habeo, qui olim dixi ad Moysen: Ego sum qui sum; hæc dices filiis Israel, Qui est misit me ad vos. Habete fiduciam in Deo, nolite timere inordinato pavore, a negotio perambulante in tenebris. In omnibus inveniuntur discipuli Christi usque ad Spiritus Sancti emissionem vel ascensionem, satis imperfecti ac rudes: propter quod Salvator apud Marcum ait, quia obcæcatum fuit cor eorum.
paras.en: [[14:27|And immediately Jesus spoke to them, saying|Statimque Jesus locutus est eis, dicens]]: [[14:27|it is I|Ego sum]], as it appears, whose voice you know, and who have true being, who said of old to Moses: [[Ex 3:14|I AM WHO AM|Ego sum qui sum]]; [[Ex 3:14|Thus shalt thou say to the children of Israel: HE WHO IS, hath sent me to you|hæc dices filiis Israel, Qui est misit me ad vos]]. [[14:27|Be of good heart|Habete fiduciam]] in God, [[14:27|fear ye not|nolite timere]] with disordered dread, [[Ps 90:6|the business that walketh about in the dark|a negotio perambulante in tenebris]] [the "business" of the Psalm is taken by the commentators as a demon prowling at night]. In everything Christ's disciples are found to be rather imperfect and unformed until the sending of the Holy Ghost, or the Ascension; which is why the Saviour says in Mark that [[Mark 6:52|their heart was blinded|obcæcatum fuit cor eorum]].

paras.t: Respondens autem Petrus, qui in omnibus invenitur ceteris in fide et caritate ardentior, dixit: Domine, si tu es. Hoc dixit, non amplius dubitando: alioqui non commisisset se tanto periculo, ut propter verbum ipsius inciperet ambulare supra mare. Quod igitur ait, Domine, si tu es, ex caritatis procedit ardore et fidei magnitudine, qua credidit se per potentiam vel meritum Christi posse supra aquas incedere. Jube me venire ad te super aquas, quoniam tibi obediendo, perire non valeo. At ipse Jesus ait: Veni. Et descendens Petrus de navicula, ambulabat super aquam ut veniret ad Jesum. Noverat Petrus, quod virtute Christi posset aqua sub pedibus suis consolidari, vel corpus suum levificari. Et ad magnitudinem hujus miraculi confert, quod tam Christus quam Petrus, non supra tranquillum, sed turbulentum mare deambulavit.
paras.en: [[14:28|And Peter making answer, said: Lord, if it be thou|Respondens autem Petrus, dixit: Domine, si tu es]]: Peter, who in everything is found more ardent than the rest in faith and charity. He said this no longer doubting; otherwise he would not have put himself in such danger as to begin walking on the sea at His word. So his saying, Lord, if it be Thou, comes from the ardour of his charity and the greatness of his faith, by which he believed that by the power or merit of Christ he could walk on the waters. [[14:28|bid me come to thee upon the waters|Jube me venire ad te super aquas]], since by obeying You I cannot perish. [[14:29|And he said: Come|At ipse Jesus ait: Veni]]. [[14:29|And Peter going down out of the boat walked upon the water to come to Jesus|Et descendens Petrus de navicula, ambulabat super aquam ut veniret ad Jesum]]. Peter knew that by Christ's power the water could be made firm under his feet, or his body made light. And it adds to the greatness of this miracle that both Christ and Peter walked not on a calm but on a rough sea.

paras.t: Videns vero, imo experiens, ventum validum se impellentem, timuit. Et quum cœpisset mergi, propter timorem inordinatum ex fidei imperfectione descendentem, clamavit, dicens: Domine, salvum me fac ab isto submersionis periculo. Et continuo Jesus extendens manum, apprehendit eum. Sic cunctis electis periclitantibus spiritualiter facit Christus. Nam licet ad tempus desinat eos adversitatibus agitari, tamen quum prospicit quod mox perituri sint nisi ipse succurrat, porrigit manum adjutricem. Propter quod ait Psalmista: Impulsus, eversus sum ut caderem, et Dominus suscepit me; itemque, Quum ceciderit, non collidetur, quia Dominus supponit manum suam. Et ait illi Jesus: Modicæ fidei, id est tu, Petre, modicam habens fidem, vel potius fidei actum, quantum ad præsens. Modicam enim fidem habere videtur, in quo passiones partis sensitivæ fidei actum impediunt sive obnubilant. Quare dubitasti, id est, incertus fuisti de mea custodia, et tua conservatione? quasi mergi posset, qui me jubente super aquas progreditur, quum ego per Isaiam testatus sum: Quum transieris per aquas, tecum ero, et flumina non operient te. Nondum fuerat Petrus tantus in fide, ut cum Psalmista dicere posset: Nam et si ambulavero in medio umbræ mortis, non timebo mala, quoniam tu mecum es.
paras.en: [[14:30|But seeing the wind strong|Videns vero, imo experiens, ventum validum]], or rather feeling it drive against him, [[14:30|he was afraid|timuit]]. [[14:30|and when he began to sink|Et quum cœpisset mergi]], because of a disordered fear arising from imperfect faith, [[14:30|he cried out, saying: Lord, save me|clamavit, dicens: Domine, salvum me fac]] from this danger of drowning. [[14:31|And immediately Jesus stretching forth his hand took hold of him|Et continuo Jesus extendens manum, apprehendit eum]]. So Christ does with all His elect when they are in spiritual danger. For though for a time He lets them be tossed by adversities, yet when He sees that they will soon perish unless He helps them, He holds out a helping hand. Therefore the Psalmist says: [[Ps 117:13|Being pushed I was overturned that I might fall: but the Lord supported me|Impulsus, eversus sum ut caderem, et Dominus suscepit me]]; and again: [[Ps 36:24|When he shall fall he shall not be bruised, for the Lord putteth his hand under him|Quum ceciderit, non collidetur, quia Dominus supponit manum suam]]. [[14:31|and said to him: O thou of little faith|Et ait illi Jesus: Modicæ fidei]], that is, you, Peter, having little faith, or rather little act of faith, for the present. For a man seems to have little faith when the passions of the sensitive part hinder or cloud the act of faith. [[14:31|why didst thou doubt|Quare dubitasti]], that is, why were you uncertain of My keeping and your preservation? As if one could sink who goes forward on the waters at My command, when I have testified through Isaias: [[Is 43:2|When thou shalt pass through the waters, I will be with thee, and the rivers shall not cover thee|Quum transieris per aquas, tecum ero, et flumina non operient te]]. Peter was not yet so great in faith that he could say with the Psalmist: [[Ps 22:4|For though I should walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I will fear no evils, for thou art with me|Nam et si ambulavero in medio umbræ mortis, non timebo mala, quoniam tu mecum es]].

paras.t: Et quum ascendisset Jesus cum Petro in naviculam, cessavit ventus, haud dubium quin Christo jubente. Sic Christo per internam visitationem redeunte ad cor quod ad tempus dispensative reliquit, redit tranquillitas animi, delectaturque anima in multitudine pacis.
paras.en: [[14:32|And when they were come up into the boat, the wind ceased|Et quum ascendisset Jesus cum Petro in naviculam, cessavit ventus]]: when Jesus had come up with Peter, the wind ceased, no doubt at Christ's command. So when Christ returns by an inward visitation to a heart He has left for a time by His providence, calm of mind returns, and the soul [[Ps 36:11|shall delight in abundance of peace|delectaturque anima in multitudine pacis]].

paras.t: Qui autem in navicula erant, videlicet alii discipuli, et ut dicit Hieronymus, vectores et nautæ, venerunt, et genibus flexis, vel proni super asseres, adoraverunt eum. Si crediderunt eum esse verum Deum, adoraverunt eum adoratione latriæ. Et certum est, quod nec Apostoli habuerunt firmam et fixam fidem de hoc, usque post resurrectionem. Nondum enim sciebant minora de Christo, ut quod esset passurus pro mundo, vel resurrecturus a morte. Dicentes: Vere Filius Dei es. Si adoraverunt eum ut verum Deum, vocabant eum Filium Dei naturalem et unicum; si autem adoraverunt eum adoratione duliæ, quasi hominem excellentem, ut Joab David regem, vocabant eum Filium Dei per gratiam singularem. Communiter vero affirmant doctores, quod adoraverunt eum adoratione latriæ, quasi Filium Dei naturalem, verumque Deum. Sed si in hac fide stabiliti fuissent, non tam facile postea dubitassent, sicut in sequenti dicetur capitulo; et præsertim tempore passionis, quando verba credentium mulierum videbantur eis deliramenta.
paras.en: [[14:33|And they that were in the boat came and adored him|Qui autem in navicula erant, venerunt, et adoraverunt eum]]: those in the boat, namely the other disciples and, as Jerome says, the passengers and sailors, came and, on bended knees, or bowed down upon the planks, adored Him. If they believed Him to be true God, they adored Him with the adoration of latria [the worship due to God alone]. And it is certain that not even the Apostles had a firm and settled faith about this until after the resurrection. For they did not yet know lesser things about Christ, such as that He was to suffer for the world, or rise from death[[Luke 18:31||]]. [[14:33|saying: Indeed thou art the Son of God|Dicentes: Vere Filius Dei es]]. If they adored Him as true God, they called Him the natural and only Son of God; but if they adored Him with the adoration of dulia [the honour given to a creature], as an excellent man, as Joab did King David[[2 Kings 14:22||]], they called Him Son of God by singular grace. The doctors commonly affirm, however, that they adored Him with the adoration of latria, as the natural Son of God and true God. But if they had been settled in this faith, they would not have doubted so easily afterwards, as will be said in the next chapter; and above all at the time of the Passion, when the words of the women who believed seemed to them idle tales[[Luke 24:11||]].

paras.t: Et quum transfretassent, id est, ultra mare istud navigassent Jesus et ejus discipuli, venerunt in terram Genesar: de qua dictum est supra. Et quum cognovissent eum viri loci illius, vel ex solo rumore, quia famosus erat, vel ex adspectu, vel, quod potius tenendum est, quoniam Jesus jam semel fuit in regione illa, in qua liberavit duos a dæmonibus, qui ingressi in porcos præcipitaverunt eos in mare: quod factum omnibus terræ illius innotuit; miserunt in universam regionem illam, colligendo et adducendo ad Jesum omnes infirmos, sicut subjungitur, et obtulerunt ei omnes male habentes. Ex consideratione enim prædicti miraculi, et aliorum signorum quæ perceperunt facta a Christo, firmiter crediderunt quod posset quoscumque infirmos curare. Et rogabant eum infirmi, vel alii pro infirmis, ut vel fimbriam vestimenti ejus tangerent, ut sanarentur, corporis sui sanctissimi tactu se reputantes indignos, nec oportere illud contingere, sed sufficere tactum extremæ partis vestis ipsius, propter excellentiam suæ sanctitatis. Quibus Christus libenter assensit. Et quicumque tetigerunt fimbriam, salvi facti sunt ab incommodo seu languore mentis et corporis. Virtus nempe (Luc. vi, 19) exivit de eo, et redundans in corpus seque diffundens per vestem, sanavit omnes, ut dictum est.
paras.en: [[14:34|And having passed the water|Et quum transfretassent]], that is, when Jesus and His disciples had sailed across this sea, [[14:34|they came into the country of Genesar|venerunt in terram Genesar]], of which we have spoken above[[Matt 8:28||]]. [[14:35|And when the men of that place had knowledge of him|Et quum cognovissent eum viri loci illius]], either from report alone, since He was famous, or by sight, or, which is rather to be held, because Jesus had already been once in that region, where He freed two men from devils, who went into the swine and drove them headlong into the sea[[Matt 8:28||]], a deed that became known to everyone in that land; [[14:35|they sent into all that country|miserunt in universam regionem illam]], gathering and bringing all the sick to Jesus, as follows: [[14:35|and brought to him all that were diseased|et obtulerunt ei omnes male habentes]]. For considering that miracle and the other signs they learned Christ had done, they firmly believed He could cure any sick. [[14:36|And they besought him|Et rogabant eum]], the sick, or others for the sick, [[14:36|that they might touch but the hem of his garment|ut vel fimbriam vestimenti ejus tangerent]], so as to be healed, thinking themselves unworthy to touch His most holy body, and that there was no need to touch it, but that it was enough to touch the edge of His clothing, because of the excellence of His holiness. To this Christ gladly agreed. [[14:36|And as many as touched, were made whole|Et quicumque tetigerunt fimbriam, salvi facti sunt]], as many as touched the hem, from their ailment or sickness of mind and body. For [[Luke 6:19|virtue went out from him|Virtus nempe (Luc. vi, 19) exivit de eo]] and overflowing into His body and spreading through His clothing, [[Luke 6:19|healed all|sanavit omnes]], as has been said.

15.title: Declaratio capituli quintidecimi: Tunc accesserunt ad eum ab Jerosolymis Scribæ et Pharisæi
15.title_en: Explanation of the fifteenth chapter: Then came to him from Jerusalem scribes and Pharisees

paras.t: Tunc accesserunt ad eum, cujus vestimentorum contactu sanabantur infirmi, ab Jerosolymis Scribæ et Pharisæi dicentes: Quare discipuli tui transgrediuntur traditiones, id est ordinationes morales, seniorum, id est factas seu institutas a senioribus (qui præerant populo Judæorum, et successerunt septuaginta senibus electis a Moyse, de quibus in libro Numerorum legitur)? Hi seniores ordinaverunt ne Judæi comederent manibus communibus, hoc est non lotis: quod discipuli Christi interdum non servaverunt. Nec tenebantur ad hoc, quoniam sub summi dispensatoris magisterio erant, qui poterat eos ab hac ordinatione absolvere: nam et ipsemet Christus sæpe non lotis manibus manducavit, ut Lucas habet. Non enim lavant manus suas quum panem manducant, id est, quando ad mensam accessuri sunt. Per panem autem designat Scriptura quemlibet cibum. Ipse autem Jesus respondens, ait illis: Quare et vos transgredimini mandatum Dei, propter traditionem vestram, id est ut observetis vestras institutiones? Non ex impatientia, sed zelo justitiæ taliter Christus respondet, innocentes excusando, et invidos ac prævaricatores accusando: Primo, ad ostendendum quod indigni sunt alios de parvis accusare, qui magnis subjacent vitiis. Secundo, ut adimpleretur quod per Isaiam de ipso prædictum est: Judicabit in justitia pauperes, et arguet in æquitate pro mansuetis terræ; et in Psalmo, Judicabit pauperes populi, et salvos faciet filios pauperum, et humiliabit calumniatorem. Quomodo autem Scribæ ac Pharisæi transgressi sunt divinum mandatum, subjungitur.
paras.en: [[15:1|Then came to him|Tunc accesserunt ad eum]], to Him by the touch of whose clothing the sick were healed, [[15:1|from Jerusalem scribes and Pharisees, saying|ab Jerosolymis Scribæ et Pharisæi dicentes]]: [[15:2|Why do thy disciples transgress the tradition|Quare discipuli tui transgrediuntur traditiones]], that is, the rules of conduct, [[15:2|of the ancients|seniorum]], that is, made or laid down by the elders (who were over the Jewish people and succeeded the seventy elders chosen by Moses, of whom we read in the book of Numbers[[Num 11:24||]])? These elders ordained that the Jews should not eat [[Mark 7:2|with common, that is, with unwashed hands|manibus communibus, hoc est non lotis]], which Christ's disciples sometimes did not observe. Nor were they bound to it, since they were under the teaching of the supreme Dispenser, who could release them from this ordinance; for Christ Himself often ate with unwashed hands, as Luke has it[[Luke 11:38||]]. [[15:2|For they wash not their hands when they eat bread|Non enim lavant manus suas quum panem manducant]], that is, when they are about to come to table. By "bread" Scripture means any food. [[15:3|But he answering, said to them: Why do you also transgress the commandment of God for your tradition|Ipse autem Jesus respondens, ait illis: Quare et vos transgredimini mandatum Dei, propter traditionem vestram]], that is, so as to keep your own ordinances? Christ answers in this way not out of impatience but out of zeal for justice, excusing the innocent and accusing the envious and the transgressors: first, to show that those who are subject to great vices are unworthy to accuse others of small things; second, that what was foretold of Him by Isaias might be fulfilled: [[Is 11:4|he shall judge the poor with justice, and shall reprove with equity the meek of the earth|Judicabit in justitia pauperes, et arguet in æquitate pro mansuetis terræ]]; and in the Psalm: [[Ps 71:4|He shall judge the poor of the people, and he shall save the children of the poor: and he shall humble the oppressor|Judicabit pauperes populi, et salvos faciet filios pauperum, et humiliabit calumniatorem]]. How the scribes and Pharisees transgressed the divine commandment is added next.

paras.t: Nam Deus dixit, id est, per Moysen jussit: Honora patrem tuum et matrem, carnales, non solum reverentiam exhibendo tanquam principiis exsistentiæ tuæ, sed etiam necessaria ministrando quum indigent. Quamvis enim per se et secundum communem cursum, non debeant filii parentibus thesaurizare, sed econtra, ut dicit Apostolus; tamen per accidens, scilicet in causa necessitatis et notabilis indigentiæ, hoc oportet: imo in causa necessitatis, magis succurrendum esset parentibus quam uxori aut filiis propriis, secundum Thomam. Et, Qui maledixerit patri vel matri, verbo vel facto, vel aperta rebellione, morte moriatur, id est, secundum legem occidatur. Hæc erat pœna maledicentium suis parentibus. Unde in Ecclesiastico scriptum est: Quam malæ famæ est, qui relinquit patrem! et est maledictus a Deo, qui exasperat matrem.
paras.en: [[15:3|For God said|Nam Deus dixit]], that is, commanded through Moses: [[15:4|Honour thy father and mother|Honora patrem tuum et matrem]][[Ex 20:12||]], your fleshly parents, not only by showing them reverence as the source of your existence, but also by supplying their needs when they are in want. For although in itself and in the ordinary course [[2 Cor 12:14|neither ought the children to lay up for the parents|non debeant filii parentibus thesaurizare]], but the other way round, as the Apostle says, yet incidentally, namely in a case of necessity and notable want, they must do so: indeed, in a case of necessity one should rather help one's parents than one's own wife or children, according to Thomas. [[15:4|And: He that shall curse father or mother|Et, Qui maledixerit patri vel matri]], by word or deed, or by open rebellion, [[15:4|let him die the death|morte moriatur]][[Ex 21:17||]][[Lev 20:9||]], that is, let him be put to death according to the law. This was the penalty for those who cursed their parents. Hence it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 3:18|Of what an evil fame is he that forsaketh his father: and he is cursed of God that angereth his mother|Quam malæ famæ est, qui relinquit patrem! et est maledictus a Deo, qui exasperat matrem]].

paras.t: Vos autem dicitis, hoc est, prædictum præceptum false exponendo, alios vestra traditione ita instruitis: Quicumque filius dixerit patri, vel matri indigenti, Munus quodcumque est ex me, id est, quidquid ego obtulero Deo, seu omne munus quod ex mea devotione Deo offertur vel consecratur, tibi proderit, id est, tibi utilius erit, quam si illud tibi præstarem, quia proficiet ad spiritualem salutem, quæ melior est quam corporalis nutritio. Ad hujus intellectum, sciendum quod sacerdotes, Scribæ ac Pharisæi avaritiæ dediti, ut majores oblationes acquirerent, impietatem suam quadam religione palliabant, dicentes, quod melius esset Deo offerre quæ parentibus danda erant, quam conferre ea parentibus: primo, quoniam Deus esset pater summus ac principalis, de quo Isaias ait, Tu, Domine, pater noster; secundo, quia hoc magis prodesset saluti parentum. Dixerunt ergo, quod quando filii dicerent parentibus egenis, Munus quodcumque est ex me, vel a me Deo promissum, oblatum, vel consecratum, vobis proderit magis, quam si illud in usus vestros expenderetis; tunc filii non tenerentur parentibus victualia ministrare, quamvis indigerent. Et hoc etiam idcirco dixerunt Scribæ et Pharisæi, ut parentes sic esse putantes, non auderent bona filiorum Deo oblata contingere, ne sacrilegii crimen incurrerent. Sed ista Scribarum assertio falsa est: non enim vult Deus sibi offerri ea quæ aliis debentur. Parentibus autem tenentur filii ministrare necessaria vitæ in casu prædicto.
paras.en: [[15:5|But you say|Vos autem dicitis]], that is, by expounding that commandment falsely you teach others by your tradition as follows: [[15:5|Whosoever shall say to father or mother|Quicumque filius dixerit patri, vel matri]], whatever son says to his father or his mother in want, [[15:5|The gift whatsoever proceedeth from me|Munus quodcumque est ex me]], that is, whatever I offer to God, or every gift that is offered or consecrated to God out of my devotion, [[15:5|shall profit thee|tibi proderit]], that is, will be more useful to you than if I gave it to you, because it will profit your spiritual salvation, which is better than bodily nourishment. To understand this, it should be known that the priests, scribes and Pharisees, being given to avarice, in order to get larger offerings cloaked their impiety with a kind of religion, saying that it was better to offer to God what should have been given to parents than to give it to the parents: first, because God is the highest and chief Father, of whom Isaias says, [[Is 63:16|thou, O Lord, art our father|Tu, Domine, pater noster]]; second, because this would profit the parents' salvation more. So they said that when sons told their needy parents, "Whatever gift is from me, or is promised, offered or consecrated by me to God, will profit you more than if you spent it on your own needs", then the sons were not bound to supply their parents with food, even if they were in want. And the scribes and Pharisees said this also so that the parents, thinking it was so, would not dare touch their sons' goods offered to God, lest they incur the crime of sacrilege. But this assertion of the scribes is false: for God does not want to be offered what is owed to others. And in the case described, sons are bound to supply their parents with the necessities of life.

paras.t: Porro, quod subditur, et non honorificabit patrem suum aut matrem suam, dupliciter intelligi potest: Primo, Et non honorificabit, id est, filius ista dicendo parentibus, vel bona sua Deo vovendo, non tenetur nec debet honorificare seu necessaria ministrare patri aut matri. Secundo sic: Et non honorificabit, id est, quicumque filius vestram traditionem sequitur, non honorificabit veraciter suos parentes, dando eis victum atque vestitum dum indigent, sicut lex præcepit, sicque transgreditur divinum præceptum, sequendo vestrum errorem. Ideo subditur: et irritum, id est vacuum et false intellectum ac prævaricatum, fecistis mandatum Dei de honoratione parentum, propter traditionem vestram jam dictam, quia per illam inducitis aliquos ad falsum intellectum atque crudelem transgressionem divini præcepti, evacuatisque illud: et ita agitis contra præceptum Moysis in Deuteronomio, ubi ait, Non adjicietis ad verbum quod ego loquor, nec auferetis ex eo; et fecistis homines potius obedire vobis quam Deo.
paras.en: Further, what follows, [[15:6|And he shall not honour his father or his mother|et non honorificabit patrem suum aut matrem suam]], can be understood in two ways. First: and he shall not honour, that is, a son who says this to his parents, or vows his goods to God, is not bound and ought not to honour his father or mother, or supply their needs. Second, thus: and he shall not honour, that is, whatever son follows your tradition will not truly honour his parents by giving them food and clothing when they are in want, as the law commanded; and so he transgresses the divine commandment by following your error. So it is added: [[15:6|and you have made void the commandment of God for your tradition|et irritum fecistis mandatum Dei propter traditionem vestram]]: made void, that is, empty, falsely understood and broken, the commandment of God about honouring parents, by your tradition just mentioned; for by it you lead some to a false understanding and a cruel transgression of the divine commandment, and you empty it of force. And so you act against the commandment of Moses in Deuteronomy, where he says: [[Deut 4:2|You shall not add to the word that I speak to you, neither shall you take away from it|Non adjicietis ad verbum quod ego loquor, nec auferetis ex eo]]; and you have made men obey you rather than God.

paras.t: Hypocritæ, qui aliud estis, et aliud simulatis, bene prophetavit de vobis Isaias, dicens: Populus hic, a foris religiosus, sed intus vitiosus, labiis me honorat, ore laudando Deum ac prædicando divina, cor autem eorum longe est a me, non locali distantia, quum ego ubique sim et omnia penetrem, sed dissimilitudine, quia peccata eorum dividunt inter me et eos. Unde Sapiens inquit: Longe est Dominus ab impiis; et Osee, Dereliquerunt (ait) Dominum in non custodiendo. Sine causa autem, id est inaniter, colunt me exteriori obsequio solum, quia non est meritorium opus hujusmodi, nec perducit ad ultimum finem, qui est vita æterna, docentes doctrinas, id est exhortationes, et mandata hominum, humano spiritu, non Spiritu Sancto loquentium, id est traditiones seniorum suorum divino mandato contrarias.
paras.en: [[15:7|Hypocrites|Hypocritæ]], who are one thing and pretend another, [[15:7|well hath Isaias prophesied of you, saying|bene prophetavit de vobis Isaias, dicens]][[Is 29:13||]]: [[15:8|This people|Populus hic]], religious without but vicious within, [[15:8|honoureth me with their lips|labiis me honorat]], praising God with the mouth and preaching divine things, [[15:8|but their heart is far from me|cor autem eorum longe est a me]]: not by distance of place, since I am everywhere and pierce all things, but by unlikeness, because their sins divide between Me and them[[Is 59:2||]]. Hence the Wise Man says: [[Prov 15:29|The Lord is far from the wicked|Longe est Dominus ab impiis]]; and Osee: [[Osee 4:10|they have forsaken the Lord in not observing|Dereliquerunt (ait) Dominum in non custodiendo]]. [[15:9|And in vain|Sine causa autem]], that is, to no purpose, [[15:9|do they worship me|colunt me]] with outward service only, because such a work is not meritorious and does not lead to the last end, which is eternal life; [[15:9|teaching doctrines|docentes doctrinas]], that is, exhortations, [[15:9|and commandments of men|et mandata hominum]] speaking by a human spirit and not by the Holy Ghost, that is, the traditions of their elders, contrary to the divine commandment.

paras.t: Et convocatis ad se turbis, dixit eis Jesus: Audite, et intelligite, id est, diligenter advertite quæ dico: Non quod intrat in os, id est cibus corporalis, qui ore accipitur, coinquinat hominem inquinatione peccati, quantum est ex natura cibi, quoniam omnis creatura Dei bona est, et nihil rejiciendum quod cum gratiarum actione sumitur, sanctificatur enim per verbum Dei. Nihilominus cibus potest esse materia vel occasio spiritualis immunditiæ, ratione prohibitionis vel immoderantiæ; sed tunc origo et radix inquinationis est ab anima, non a cibo. Sicque multi cibi erant in lege prohibiti. Apostolus quoque vetat idolothyta, seu idolis immolata, comedere, ne alii scandalizentur. Sed quod procedit ex ore, videlicet verbum inordinatum, seu superstitiosa traditio, hoc coinquinat hominem intus in anima. Unde Jacobus inquit: Universitas iniquitatis lingua constituitur in membris nostris; et Paulus, Corrumpunt (inquit) mores bonos colloquia prava.
paras.en: [[15:10|And having called together the multitudes unto him, he said to them|Et convocatis ad se turbis, dixit eis]], Jesus: [[15:10|Hear ye and understand|Audite, et intelligite]], that is, pay careful attention to what I say. [[15:11|Not that which goeth into the mouth|Non quod intrat in os]], that is, bodily food, which is taken by the mouth, [[15:11|defileth a man|coinquinat hominem]] with the defilement of sin, as far as the nature of the food goes, since [[1 Tim 4:4|every creature of God is good, and nothing to be rejected that is received with thanksgiving|omnis creatura Dei bona est, et nihil rejiciendum quod cum gratiarum actione sumitur]], [[1 Tim 4:5|For it is sanctified by the word of God|sanctificatur enim per verbum Dei]]. Nevertheless food can be the matter or occasion of spiritual uncleanness, by reason of a prohibition or of excess; but then the origin and root of the defilement is from the soul, not from the food. And so many foods were forbidden in the law[[Lev 11:1||]]. The Apostle too forbids eating things offered to idols, lest others be scandalized[[1 Cor 8:13||]]. [[15:11|but what cometh out of the mouth|Sed quod procedit ex ore]], namely a disordered word, or a superstitious tradition, [[15:11|this defileth a man|hoc coinquinat hominem]] within, in the soul. Hence James says: [[Jas 3:6|a world of iniquity. The tongue is placed among our members|Universitas iniquitatis lingua constituitur in membris nostris]]; and Paul: [[1 Cor 15:33|Evil communications corrupt good manners|Corrumpunt (inquit) mores bonos colloquia prava]].

paras.t: Tunc accedentes discipuli ejus, dixerunt ei. Discipuli adhuc tenebantur humano timore, idcirco ne Christus gravius offenderet Scribas ac Pharisæos, vel contra se eos provocaret, accesserunt ad Jesum, dicentes: Scis quia Pharisæi audito hoc verbo, Non quod intrat in os coinquinat hominem, etc., scandalizati sunt, id est ad ruinam culpæ inducti, videlicet indignati et seditionem movere optantes in turba contra Christum, quasi infringeret legem, quæ aliquos cibos vocat immundos? Christus autem non scandalizavit eos directe, quoniam scandalum activum est dictum vel factum minus rectum præbens alteri occasionem ruinæ; sed illi ex sua perversitate scandalizati sunt, non volentes acquiescere sanæ doctrinæ.
paras.en: [[15:12|Then came his disciples, and said to him|Tunc accedentes discipuli ejus, dixerunt ei]]. The disciples were still held by human fear; so, lest Christ should offend the scribes and Pharisees more gravely, or provoke them against Himself, they came to Jesus, saying: [[15:12|Dost thou know that the Pharisees, when they heard this word|Scis quia Pharisæi audito hoc verbo]], Not that which goeth into the mouth defileth a man, etc., [[15:12|were scandalized|scandalizati sunt]], that is, led into the ruin of sin, namely made indignant and eager to stir up the crowd against Christ, as if He were breaking the law, which calls some foods unclean? But Christ did not scandalize them directly, since active scandal is a less upright word or deed that gives another occasion of ruin [the scholastic definition of scandal]; they were scandalized by their own perversity, not wishing to accept sound teaching.

paras.t: At ille respondens discipulis suis, ait: Omnis plantatio, id est generatio plantata, vel doctrina humanitus adinventa atque erronea, quam non plantavit, id est, per gratiam prædestinationis non fundavit, vel per lumen sapientiæ non inspiravit nec stabilivit, Pater meus cœlestis, eradicabitur, id est, reprobabitur atque damnabitur, sicut per Isaiam prædictum est: Turbabis eos, et ventus tollet, et aura disperget eos; et iterum, Et quidem neque satus, neque radicatus in terra truncus eorum, repente flavit in eos, et aruerunt. Unde Ecclesiastes: Quasi umbra (inquit) prætereant, qui non timent faciem Domini.
paras.en: [[15:13|But he answering, said|At ille respondens discipulis suis, ait]] to His disciples: [[15:13|Every plant|Omnis plantatio]], that is, every planted generation, or every doctrine devised by man and erroneous, [[15:13|which my heavenly Father hath not planted|quam non plantavit, id est, per gratiam prædestinationis non fundavit, vel per lumen sapientiæ non inspiravit nec stabilivit, Pater meus cœlestis]], that is, has not founded by the grace of predestination, or has not inspired or established by the light of wisdom, [[15:13|shall be rooted up|eradicabitur]], that is, shall be rejected and condemned, as was foretold through Isaias: [[Is 41:16|Thou shalt fan them, and the wind shall carry them away, and the whirlwind shall scatter them|Turbabis eos, et ventus tollet, et aura disperget eos]] [Denis's wording, "Thou shalt trouble them", differs slightly from the Vulgate]; and again: [[Is 40:24|And surely their stock was neither planted, nor sown, nor rooted in the earth: suddenly he hath blown upon them, and they are withered|Et quidem neque satus, neque radicatus in terra truncus eorum, repente flavit in eos, et aruerunt]]. Hence Ecclesiastes says: [[Eccles 8:13|as a shadow let them pass away that fear not the face of the Lord|Quasi umbra (inquit) prætereant, qui non timent faciem Domini]].

paras.t: Sed quæritur, si omnis plantatio non plantata a Deo eradicatur, et plantata a Deo non eradicatur, quomodo ad Synagogam Dominus dicat per Jeremiam: Ego te plantavi vineam electam, et conversa es in amaritudinem vitis alienæ. Et in Psalmo: Vineam de Ægypto transtulisti, ejecisti gentes, et plantasti eam. Et post pauca: Ut quid destruxisti maceriam ejus, et vindemiant eam omnes qui prætergrediuntur viam? Exterminavit eam aper de silva. Denique Apostolus Corinthiis scribens: Ego, inquit, plantavi. Numquid non illa plantatio eradicata est? Insuper, quidquid essentiæ vel exsistentiæ est in rebus, a Deo Patre profluxit. Ergo omnis plantatio ab eo plantata est: præsertim quum Jeremias de impiis dicat, Plantasti eos, et proficiunt. Et respondendum, quod Synagoga a Deo plantata fuit, quantum ad receptionem temporalium bonorum, et habitationem in terra promissionis; multique Judæorum, quantum ad bona gratiæ, plantati fuerunt divinitus. Unde quod de plantatione et destructione Synagogæ allegatum est, non oportet accipere de eisdem numero, sed specie. Apostolus quoque plantavit instrumentaliter, Deus principaliter. Propter quod ait: Dei cooperatores sumus. Interea omne exsistens potest dici plantatum a Deo, quantum ad esse naturale, quod recepit a primo universorum fontali principio. Nunc autem fit sermo de plantatione seu interiori fundatione mentis a Deo per gratiam, sine qua nemo finaliter stabilitur. Ad quod pertinet quod ait Salvator: Nemo potest venire ad me, nisi fuerit ei datum a Patre meo; et denuo, Nemo (inquit) venit ad me, nisi Pater meus traxerit eum. Alii eradicantur, juxta illud: Tollatur impius, ne videat gloriam Dei, juxta LXX. Separantur enim a consortio electorum, et regione viventium. Hinc scriptum est: Adulterinæ plantationes non dabunt radices altas.
paras.en: But it is asked: if every plant not planted by God is rooted up, and one planted by God is not rooted up, how is it that the Lord says to the Synagogue through Jeremias: [[Jer 2:21|I planted thee a chosen vineyard|Ego te plantavi vineam electam]], and thou art turned into the bitterness of a strange vine? And in the Psalm: [[Ps 79:9|Thou hast brought a vineyard out of Egypt: thou hast cast out the Gentiles and planted it|Vineam de Ægypto transtulisti, ejecisti gentes, et plantasti eam]]. And a little after: [[Ps 79:13|Why hast thou broken down the hedge thereof, so that all they who pass by the way do pluck it|Ut quid destruxisti maceriam ejus, et vindemiant eam omnes qui prætergrediuntur viam]]? [[Ps 79:14|The boar out of the wood hath laid it waste|Exterminavit eam aper de silva]]. And the Apostle, writing to the Corinthians, says: [[1 Cor 3:6|I have planted|Ego te plantavi]]. Was that planting not rooted up? Moreover, whatever there is of essence or existence in things has flowed from God the Father; so every plant has been planted by Him: especially since Jeremias says of the wicked, [[Jer 12:2|Thou hast planted them|Plantasti eos]], and they prosper. The answer is that the Synagogue was planted by God as regards receiving temporal goods and dwelling in the land of promise; and many of the Jews were planted by God as regards the goods of grace. So what has been brought forward about the planting and the destroying of the Synagogue need not be taken of the same individuals, but of the same kind. The Apostle too planted as an instrument, God as the principal agent; which is why he says: [[1 Cor 3:9|For we are God's coadjutors|Dei cooperatores sumus]]. Again, everything that exists can be said to be planted by God as regards its natural being, which it received from the first fountain-principle of all things. But here the talk is of planting, that is, the inward founding of the mind by God through grace, without which no one is finally made firm. To this belongs what the Saviour says: [[John 6:66|no man can come to me, unless it be given him by my Father|Nemo potest venire ad me, nisi fuerit ei datum a Patre meo]]; and again: [[John 6:44|No man can come to me|Nemo (inquit) venit ad me]] unless My Father draw him. Others are rooted up, according to that saying: Let the wicked be taken away, that [[Is 26:10|he shall not see the glory of the Lord|ne videat gloriam Dei]] [Denis quotes the Septuagint reading, as the margin notes]. For they are separated from the fellowship of the elect and from the land of the living. Hence it is written: [[Wis 4:3|bastard slips shall not take deep root|Adulterinæ plantationes non dabunt radices altas]].

paras.t: Sinite illos, hoc est, dimittite Scribas ac Pharisæos incorrigibiles scandalizari, errare, turbari, quatenus qui in sordibus est sordescat adhuc, et peccator adjiciat ad peccandum. Non enim propter scandalum aliorum vitandum, omittenda est veritas vitæ, justitiæ vel doctrinæ, secundum Hieronymum. Unde ait Gregorius: Quum de veritate scandalum oritur, utilius nasci permittitur quam veritas deseratur. Verumtamen scandalum pusillorum vitandum est magis quam Pharisæorum, sicut infra dicetur. Cæci sunt corde, id est lumine veræ sapientiæ, et rectæ intelligentiæ Scripturarum privati: excæcavit enim eos rancor eorum, quia in malevolam animam non introibit sapientia. Duces cæcorum, hoc est doctores, magistri et prælati carnalium, litteralium atque errantium Judæorum. Unde convenit eis illud Isaiæ: Speculatores ejus cæci omnes, videntes vana; ipsi pastores ignoraverunt intelligentiam. Cæcus autem prælatus seu doctor non illuminatus a Spiritu Sancto, si cæco gregi vel subdito ignoranti, ducatum præstet, inducendo eum ad ambulandum per vias suas, seu ad sequendum opera et judicia sua, ambo in foveam cadunt, id est, in vitia præcipitantur, et tandem in locum gehennæ labuntur, quemadmodum scriptum est: Secundum judicem populi, sic et ministri ejus. Hinc Jeremias inquit: Quia stulte egerunt pastores, ideo omnis grex eorum dissipatus est. Maximum ergo beneficium Dei est, habere doctum ac virtuosum prælatum, quia ut contestatur Gregorius, Quum pastor per abrupta graditur, necesse est ut grex in præcipitium ducatur. Utinam tales dicerent illud Isaiæ: Non sum medicus, et in domo mea non est panis; nolite me constituere principem populi.
paras.en: [[15:14|Let them alone|Sinite illos]], that is, leave the incorrigible scribes and Pharisees to be scandalized, to err and to be troubled, so that [[Apoc 22:11|he that is filthy, let him be filthy still|qui in sordibus est sordescat adhuc]], and [[Ecclus 3:29|the sinner will add sin to sin|peccator adjiciat ad peccandum]]. For the truth of life, of justice or of doctrine is not to be given up in order to avoid scandal to others, according to Jerome. Hence Gregory says: "When scandal arises from the truth, it is better to let the scandal arise than to abandon the truth." Yet the scandal of the little ones is to be avoided more than that of the Pharisees, as will be said below. [[15:14|they are blind|Cæci sunt]] in heart, that is, deprived of the light of true wisdom and of the right understanding of the Scriptures: for [[Wis 2:21|their own malice blinded them|excæcavit enim eos rancor eorum]] [Denis has "rancour" where the Vulgate has "malice"], since [[Wis 1:4|wisdom will not enter into a malicious soul|in malevolam animam non introibit sapientia]]. [[15:14|and leaders of the blind|Duces cæcorum]], that is, the teachers, masters and prelates of the carnal, literal-minded and erring Jews. So that saying of Isaias fits them: [[Is 56:10|His watchmen are all blind|Speculatores ejus cæci omnes]], [[Is 56:10|seeing vain things|videntes vana]]; [[Is 56:11|the shepherds themselves knew no understanding|ipsi pastores ignoraverunt intelligentiam]]. [[15:14|And if the blind lead the blind|si cæco ducatum præstet]]: if a blind prelate or teacher, not enlightened by the Holy Ghost, leads a blind flock or an ignorant subject, bringing him to walk in his ways, or to follow his works and judgments, [[15:14|both fall into the pit|ambo in foveam cadunt]], that is, are hurled into vices and at last slip down into the place of Gehenna; as it is written: [[Ecclus 10:2|As the judge of the people is himself, so also are his ministers|Secundum judicem populi, sic et ministri ejus]]. Hence Jeremias says: [[Jer 10:21|Because the pastors have done foolishly|Quia stulte egerunt pastores]], therefore [[Jer 10:21|all their flock is scattered|omnis grex eorum dissipatus est]]. It is, then, the greatest benefit from God to have a learned and virtuous prelate, since, as Gregory testifies, "When the shepherd walks over steep places, the flock must be led to the precipice." Would that such men would say that word of Isaias: [[Is 3:7|I am no healer, and in my house there is no bread|Non sum medicus, et in domo mea non est panis]]; [[Is 3:7|make me not ruler of the people|nolite me constituere principem populi]].

paras.t: Respondens autem Petrus, dixit ei, videlicet Christo: Edissere, hoc est expone, nobis parabolam istam, qua dixisti: Non quod intrat in os coinquinat hominem, etc. Quod tamen non fuit parabola, sed manifesta sententia. Sed Petrus, quoniam rudis fuit sicut et socii ejus, et quoniam Christus solitus fuit parabolice loqui, putavit istud per parabolam dictum, quæritque mysticum intellectum in sermone perspicuo. Ideo meretur audire: Adhuc et vos, Apostoli, sine intellectu, id est actu intellectus, videlicet sine debita consideratione, estis? Solus Petrus interrogavit; sed quia de consilio et in persona condiscipulorum sciscitatus est, idcirco omnibus increpatorie dicitur, Adhuc et vos sine intellectu estis? Pro quo in Marco scriptum est: Adhuc et vos imprudentes estis?
paras.en: [[15:15|And Peter answering, said to him|Respondens autem Petrus, dixit ei]], namely to Christ: [[15:15|Expound to us this parable|Edissere nobis parabolam istam]]: expound, that is, explain, the parable in which You said, Not that which goeth into the mouth defileth a man, etc. Yet this was not a parable but a plain statement. But Peter, being unformed like his companions, and since Christ was accustomed to speak in parables, thought it was said in a parable, and looks for a mystical sense in a clear saying. So he deserves to hear: [[15:16|Are you also yet without understanding|Adhuc et vos sine intellectu estis?]], you Apostles: without understanding, that is, without the act of understanding, namely without due consideration? Peter alone asked; but because he inquired on the advice and in the person of his fellow disciples, it is said to all by way of rebuke: Are you also yet without understanding? For which it is written in Mark: [[Mark 7:18|So are you also without knowledge|Adhuc et vos imprudentes estis]]?

paras.t: Non intelligitis, quod merito intelligeretis, quasi rem planam, quia omne alimentum quod in os intrat, id est, a comedente ori imponitur ad alendum, in ventrem vadit, qui est locus ciborum, sicut mare aquarum, et in secessum emittitur? non totum, sed quantum ad partes impuras atque superfluas; purior tamen pars alimenti post completam digestionem in corpus convertitur comedentis. Hanc auctoritatem allegant pro se Magister et Petrus Comestor, cum aliis: qui dicunt nihil de alimento converti in veritatem substantiæ aliti, ita quod in primis parentibus fuit, secundum eos, tota substantia carnis posterorum. Præterea ponderandum quod hoc loco asserit S. Hieronymus: Omnia, inquit, Evangeliorum loca, apud hæreticos et perversos scandalis plena sunt. Ex hac nempe sententia, quidam perversissimi homines dixerunt Jesum fuisse idiotam, et physicæ ignarum, ex eo quod dicat, Omne quod intrat in os, in ventrem vadit, etc., quasi acceptæ escæ non diffunderentur per medullas, venas, nervos ac artus. Sed isti, dum sapientiam Dei ignaram fuisse comprobare nituntur, propriam manifestant præsumptionem atque insaniam. Nonne in tota Scriptura canonica, imo et in communi usu locutionis, frequens et celebris est modus loquendi per synecdochen? Et illa Christus jam utitur.
paras.en: [[15:17|Do you not understand|Non intelligitis]], as you might rightly understand, it being a plain matter, [[15:17|that whatsoever entereth into the mouth|quia omne alimentum quod in os intrat]], all food, that is, which the eater puts into his mouth for nourishment, [[15:17|goeth into the belly|in ventrem vadit]], which is the place of food as the sea is of waters, [[15:17|and is cast out into the privy|et in secessum emittitur]]? Not all of it, but as to its impure and superfluous parts; the purer part of the food, after digestion is complete, is turned into the body of the one who eats. The Master [Peter Lombard, the Master of the Sentences] and Peter Comestor, with others, cite this text for their view: they say that nothing of food is turned into the true substance of the one nourished, so that, according to them, the whole substance of the flesh of their descendants was in our first parents. Further, what St Jerome asserts at this place should be weighed: "All the passages of the Gospels," he says, "are full of stumbling-blocks for heretics and perverse men." For from this saying some most perverse men said that Jesus was unlearned and ignorant of natural science, because He says, whatsoever entereth into the mouth goeth into the belly, etc., as if food taken in were not spread through the marrow, veins, sinews and limbs. But these men, while they try to prove that the Wisdom of God was ignorant, show their own presumption and madness. Is not speaking by synecdoche [naming a part for the whole] a frequent and familiar manner of speech throughout canonical Scripture, and indeed in ordinary usage? And Christ uses it here.

paras.t: Quæ autem procedunt de ore, videlicet verba illicita, de corde exeunt, id est, ab intellectu et voluntate causantur: quia ut ait Plato, ad hoc datus est nobis sermo, ut mutuæ voluntatis fiant indicia; et ea coinquinant hominem, inferendo maculam culpæ. De corde enim exeunt cogitationes malæ, quæ sunt verba mentalia, et exprimuntur per verba vocalia; sicque cogitationes procedunt de ore per verba vocalia, quæ sunt cogitationum indicia; homicidia, adulteria, fornicationes, et ceteri vitiosi concubitus, furta, falsa testimonia, blasphemiæ: quæ etiam dicuntur de ore procedere, in quantum aliquis per verba inducitur ad ista peccata. Hæc vitia sunt quæ coinquinant, id est, interius maculant, hominem, ita ut anima ejus dæmonibus similis sit. [Non lotis autem manibus manducare non coinquinat hominem.]
paras.en: [[15:18|But the things which proceed out of the mouth|Quæ autem procedunt de ore]], namely unlawful words, [[15:18|come forth from the heart|de corde exeunt]], that is, are caused by the understanding and the will: for, as Plato says, speech was given us so that it might be the sign of our wills to one another; [[15:18|and those things defile a man|et ea coinquinant hominem]], by bringing on the stain of guilt. [[15:19|For from the heart come forth evil thoughts|De corde enim exeunt cogitationes malæ]], which are words of the mind and are expressed by spoken words; and so thoughts come out of the mouth through spoken words, which are the signs of thoughts; [[15:19|murders, adulteries, fornications|homicidia, adulteria, fornicationes]], and other sinful unions, [[15:19|thefts, false testimonies, blasphemies|furta, falsa testimonia, blasphemiæ]]: and these too are said to come out of the mouth inasmuch as someone is led into these sins by words. [[15:20|These are the things that defile a man|Hæc vitia sunt quæ coinquinant, id est, interius maculant, hominem]]: these are the vices that defile, that is, stain within, a man, so that his soul is like the demons. [[15:20|But to eat with unwashed hands doth not defile a man|Non lotis autem manibus manducare non coinquinat hominem]] [the edition gives these words of the verse in brackets, without comment].

paras.t: Ex his infert Hieronymus: Ergo principale animæ, non secundum Platonem, in cerebro, sed secundum Christum, in corde est. Sed hoc facile solveretur ab aliis. Nam Christus hic accipit cor pro mente, quemadmodum et Psalmista, dicendo: Confitebor tibi, Domine, in toto corde meo. Sic enim et alibi adstruit: Beati mundo corde. Plato vero accipit cor pro parte corporis, sicut et Aristoteles, dicens, quod cor est primum vivens et ultimum moriens. Insuper dicit Hieronymus: Arguendi sunt hi qui cogitationes malas dicunt immitti a dæmone, et non propria nasci voluntate. Diabolus enim adjutor et incensor cogitationum malarum esse potest, non auctor. Si autem in insidiis positus, levem cogitationum nostrarum scintillam suis fomitibus inflammaverit, non debemus opinari eum cordis quoque occulta rimari, sed ex corporis habitu et gestibus æstimare quid versemus intrinsecus. Verbi gratia: si pulchram mulierem viderit nos crebro respicere, intelligit cor nostrum amoris jaculo vulneratum.
paras.en: From this Jerome infers: "So the ruling part of the soul is not in the brain, as Plato holds, but in the heart, as Christ says." But others would easily answer this. For Christ here takes the heart for the mind, as the Psalmist also does when he says: [[Ps 9:2|I will give praise to thee, O Lord, with my whole heart|Confitebor tibi, Domine, in toto corde meo]][[Ps 110:1||]][[Ps 137:1||]]. So too He asserts elsewhere: [[Matt 5:8|Blessed are the clean of heart|Beati mundo corde]]. Plato, however, takes the heart for a part of the body, as does Aristotle when he says that the heart is the first thing to live and the last to die. Jerome says further: "Those are to be refuted who say that evil thoughts are put into us by the devil and do not arise from our own will. The devil can be the helper and kindler of evil thoughts, not their author. If, lying in wait, he has fanned a slight spark of our thoughts with his tinder, we must not suppose that he also searches the secrets of the heart, but that he guesses from the bearing and gestures of the body what we are turning over within. For example, if he sees us looking again and again at a beautiful woman, he understands that our heart has been wounded by the dart of love."

paras.t: Et egressus inde, videlicet a terra Genesar, et a conventiculis Scribarum ac Pharisæorum, Jesus secessit cum discipulis suis in partes Tyri et Sidonis, quæ erant urbes famosæ, antiquæ, magnæ et opulentæ. Et ecce mulier Chananæa genere, id est de stirpe Chananæorum progenita: nam prædictæ urbes ad terram Chanaan pertinebant; a finibus, id est locis seu terminis, illis egressa corpore et anima: corpore, quoniam domum suam exivit ut quæreret Jesum; anima, quoniam Chananæorum incredulitatem ac impietatem deseruit, credens in Christum; clamavit: quia ex vehementi affectu in verba erupit, et propter magnitudinem necessitatis suæ oblita est femineæ verecundiæ, clamans sine rubore: nam excessivus amor rationem non pensat. Dicens ei: Miserere mei, Domine, fili David. Perceperat mulier ista miracula Christi, audiveratque eum appellari filium David. Filia mea male, id est graviter, a dæmonio vexatur.
paras.en: [[15:21|And Jesus went from thence|Et egressus inde Jesus]], namely from the land of Genesar and from the gatherings of the scribes and Pharisees, [[15:21|and retired into the coast of Tyre and Sidon|secessit in partes Tyri et Sidonis]] with His disciples: famous, ancient, great and wealthy cities. [[15:22|And behold a woman of Canaan|Et ecce mulier Chananæa]] by race, that is, born of the stock of the Canaanites, for these cities belonged to the land of Canaan, [[15:22|who came out of those coasts|a finibus illis egressa]], that is, from those places or borders, coming out in body and in soul: in body, since she left her house to seek Jesus; in soul, since she left the unbelief and impiety of the Canaanites, believing in Christ; [[15:22|crying out|clamavit]], because out of vehement feeling she burst into words, and for the greatness of her need forgot womanly modesty, crying out without blushing: for excessive love does not weigh reason. [[15:22|said to him: Have mercy on me, O Lord, thou son of David|Dicens ei: Miserere mei, Domine, fili David]]. This woman had learned of Christ's miracles, and had heard Him called the son of David. [[15:22|my daughter is grievously troubled by a devil|filia mea male a dæmonio vexatur]]: grievously, that is, badly.

paras.t: Qui non respondit ei verbum, non ex superbia vel contemptu: sed ratione mysterii, ut designaret se primo ac principaliter advenisse ad loquendum ac subveniendum populo Israel; et quia jam ante præcepit discipulis, In viam gentium ne abieritis. Hæc autem mulier gentilis erat, genere Syrophœnissa, hoc est de Syria Phœnicis. Ideo etiam non respondit, ut illa instantius peteret, et ardentius postulando copiosius exaudiretur. Et accedentes discipuli ejus, dixerunt ei*: Dimitte eam, id est, exaudiendo age quod rogat, ut revertatur, quia clamat post nos, sequens vestigia nostra. Ex quo patet, quod ista contigerunt in via. Sed quæstio tunc occurrit: nam Marcus inquit, quod mulier ista venit et procidit coram Christo in domo. Respondetur, quod primo venit in domum, et quum ibi exaudita non esset, secuta est Christum in via. Porro discipuli orant pro ea, vel clamore ejus attædiati, vel necessitati ejus compassi, vel fide ejus devotioneque moti. Mulier ista non clamavit nisi ad Jesum, et tamen discipuli dicunt, Clamat post nos. Jam enim reputaverunt se unum cum Christo in Deo. Ipse autem respondens discipulis, ait: Non sum missus primo ac principaliter, et ad prædicandum ac operandum prodigia in propria persona, nisi ad oves quæ perierunt domus Israel, id est ad oves familiæ Israeliticæ perditas per peccatum originale et actuale, videlicet ad populum Judæorum, quibus Christus primo per se ipsum usque ad diem passionis, deinde diu per Apostolos prædicavit, donec illis penitus obstinatis et inexcusabiliter induratis, justa facta est ad gentes transmigratio. Unde Christus in propria persona parum prædicasse gentibus legitur. Interdum tamen parum prædicavit et signa fecit in gentibus, ex superabundanti, et ad figurandum quod postea prædicandum esset eis Evangelium regni. [*Rogabant eum dicentes.]
paras.en: [[15:23|Who answered her not a word|Qui non respondit ei verbum]]: not out of pride or contempt, but for the sake of a mystery, to show that He had come first and principally to speak to and help the people of Israel; and because He had already commanded the disciples: [[Matt 10:5|Go ye not into the way of the Gentiles|In viam gentium ne abieritis]]. But this woman was a Gentile, [[Mark 7:26|a Syrophenician born|genere Syrophœnissa]], that is, from Syria of Phoenicia. He also did not answer so that she would ask more urgently and, by asking more ardently, be heard more abundantly. [[15:23|And his disciples came|Et accedentes discipuli ejus]] and said to Him [the edition notes the Vulgate's words: "and besought him, saying"]: [[15:23|Send her away|Dimitte eam]], that is, by hearing her do what she asks, so that she goes back, [[15:23|for she crieth after us|quia clamat post nos]], following in our footsteps. From this it is plain that these things happened on the road. But then a question arises: for Mark says that this woman came and fell down before Christ in a house[[Mark 7:25||]]. The answer is that she first came into the house, and when she was not heard there, she followed Christ on the road. The disciples pray for her, either wearied by her crying, or pitying her need, or moved by her faith and devotion. This woman cried out only to Jesus, and yet the disciples say: She crieth after us. For they already reckoned themselves one with Christ in God. [[15:24|And he answering, said|Ipse autem respondens discipulis, ait]] to the disciples: [[15:24|I was not sent|Non sum missus]] first and principally, and to preach and work wonders in My own person, [[15:24|but to the sheep, that are lost of the house of Israel|nisi ad oves quæ perierunt domus Israel]], that is, to the sheep of the household of Israel lost through original and actual sin, namely to the Jewish people, to whom Christ preached first Himself until the day of His Passion, and then for a long time through the Apostles, until, when they were wholly obstinate and inexcusably hardened, there was a just passing over to the Gentiles. Hence Christ is read to have preached little to the Gentiles in His own person. Yet at times He did preach a little and work signs among the Gentiles, out of superabundance, and to prefigure that the Gospel of the kingdom was afterwards to be preached to them.

paras.t: At illa venit, et adoravit eum. Non est probabile quod putaverit eum verum Deum, quum nec discipuli hoc putaverint, sicut ostendi, et Beda fatetur, sed Prophetam et hominem sanctum, vel etiam Messiam. Adoravit itaque eum eo modo quo mulier Thecuitis David regem, dicens: Domine, adjuva me. Mulier ista filiam suam petit juvari atque sanari: et tamen ait, Adjuva me: primo, quoniam calamitatem propriæ filiæ reputavit ut suam; secundo, quoniam scivit filiam suam non posse sanari principaliter, nisi a Deo, ideo orat ut per Jesum impetret quod per se impetrare a Deo non potuit. Sic nempe et Martha locuta est: Domine, scio quia quæcumque poposceris a Deo, dabit tibi Deus.
paras.en: [[15:25|But she came and adored him|At illa venit, et adoravit eum]]. It is not likely that she thought Him true God, since not even the disciples thought so, as I have shown and as Bede declares; but she took Him for a Prophet and a holy man, or even the Messias. So she adored Him in the way the woman of Thecua adored King David[[2 Kings 14:4||]], [[15:25|saying: Lord, help me|dicens: Domine, adjuva me]]. This woman asks that her daughter be helped and healed, and yet she says, Help me: first, because she counted her daughter's calamity as her own; second, because she knew that her daughter could not be healed principally except by God, and so she prays that through Jesus she may obtain what she could not obtain from God by herself. So indeed Martha spoke too: Lord, I know that [[John 11:22|whatsoever thou wilt ask of God, God will give it thee|quæcumque poposceris a Deo, dabit tibi Deus]].

paras.t: Qui respondens ait, difficultatem quamdam monstrando: Non est bonum sumere panem filiorum, et mittere canibus. Hoc ad litteram ita est, et tamen iste non est sensus litteralis seu principaliter intentus, nec mulier ita intellexit. Spiritualiter ergo exponendum est: Non est bonum, id est justum ac ordinatum, sumere panem filiorum, id est spiritualia alimenta seu beneficia Dei, videlicet gratiam doctrinæ, et opera miraculorum Judæis promissa ac impendenda, qui filii nominantur, propter cultum et fidem unius Dei: et mittere canibus, id est dona ista impertiri gentilibus, qui propter idololatriæ insaniam et sanguinis atque cadaverum immolatorum esum, canibus comparantur. Hinc de populo Israel Dominus ait: Puer Israel, et dilexi eum. In Jeremia quoque: Ephraim, inquit, primogenitus meus. Verum, per filios hoc loco præsertim significantur electi Judæi, quales fuerunt discipuli. Non enim reputantur in semine Abrahæ, nisi qui credunt, secundum Apostolum. At illa dixit: Etiam, Domine, ita est ut dicis, et etiam fieri decet quod postulo; nam et catelli, id est parvi catuli seu caniculi, edunt de micis, id est fragmentis, quæ cadunt de mensa dominorum suorum. Hoc litteraliter ita est; sed sicut Christus metaphorice loquitur, sic et mulier metaphorice, subtiliterque, et valde pertinenter respondit. Ut sit sensus: Sicut parvuli canes sustentantur fragmentis cibi dominorum suorum, sic decet me gentilem catello similem, aliquid gratiæ Judæorum sortiri, ut ad instantiam meam filia mea sanetur.
paras.en: [[15:26|Who answering, said|Qui respondens ait]], showing a certain difficulty: [[15:26|It is not good to take the bread of the children, and to cast it to the dogs|Non est bonum sumere panem filiorum, et mittere canibus]]. In the letter this is so; and yet this is not the literal sense, or the one principally intended, nor did the woman understand it so. So it must be explained spiritually: it is not good, that is, just and orderly, to take the bread of the children, that is, the spiritual food or benefits of God, namely the grace of doctrine and the works of miracles promised and to be given to the Jews, who are called children because of their worship of and faith in the one God; and to cast it to the dogs, that is, to share these gifts with the Gentiles, who for the madness of idolatry and their eating of blood and of the carcasses of sacrifices are compared to dogs. Hence the Lord says of the people of Israel: [[Osee 11:1|Israel was a child, and I loved him|Puer Israel, et dilexi eum]]. And in Jeremias too: [[Jer 31:9|Ephraim is my firstborn|Ephraim, inquit, primogenitus meus]]. But by the children here are chiefly signified the elect Jews, such as the disciples were; for only those who believe are counted in the seed of Abraham, according to the Apostle[[Rom 4:12||]]. [[15:27|But she said: Yea, Lord|At illa dixit: Etiam, Domine]], it is as You say, and yet what I ask is also fitting to be done; [[15:27|for the whelps also|nam et catelli]], that is, little dogs or puppies, [[15:27|eat of the crumbs|edunt de micis]], that is, the scraps, [[15:27|that fall from the table of their masters|quæ cadunt de mensa dominorum suorum]]. Literally this is so; but as Christ speaks metaphorically, so the woman answered metaphorically, subtly and very much to the point. So the sense is: as little dogs are kept alive by the scraps of their masters' food, so it is fitting that I, a Gentile like a little dog, should receive some of the grace of the Jews, so that at my request my daughter may be healed.

paras.t: Tunc respondens Jesus, ait illi: O mulier, magna est fides tua, id est firma et integra, bonis operibus ceterisque virtutibus adornata, quoniam toties repulsa, et quasi vilipensa a me, quia canibus comparata, non cessas fideliter, humiliter, prudenter, ac patientissime postulare: dignum est ergo ut tibi aperiam januam pietatis. Fiat tibi sicut vis, id est, sicut petisti, sic impleatur. Hunc Christi sermonem mox effectus secutus est: nam sequitur: Et sanata est filia ejus, id est a dæmonio liberata, ex illa hora, hoc est, statim quum Christus locutus est, Fiat tibi sicut vis. Denique, quo Christus videbatur huic mulieri asperior foris in verbis et gestibus, eo fuit ei benignior intus per operationem occultam, per inspirationem ac illustrationem internam. Alioqui, quomodo mulier ista tantam fidem, humilitatem, patientiam atque prudentiam habuisset? Sed quæritur, si verum est quod dixit Salvator, Non est bonum sumere panem filiorum et mittere canibus: ergo ipse faciendo oppositum, videtur fecisse non bene. Et respondendum, quod verbum Christi intelligendum erat in generali, tamen in casu bonum fuit oppositum: sicut et Moyses jussit ne Ammonitæ et Moabitæ intrarent in ecclesiam Dei. Nihilominus Ruth Moabites et Achior Ammonites, propter virtutes suas et devotionem ad Deum Israel, statim admissi sunt ad ritum Judæorum: et sic et mulier ista ex singulari devotione obtinet quod communiter aliis condonandum non fuit.
paras.en: [[15:28|Then Jesus answering, said to her: O woman, great is thy faith|Tunc respondens Jesus, ait illi: O mulier, magna est fides tua]], that is, firm and whole, adorned with good works and the other virtues; for though so often repulsed, and as it were made light of by Me, being compared to dogs, you do not cease to ask faithfully, humbly, prudently and most patiently: it is fitting, then, that I open to you the door of mercy. [[15:28|be it done to thee as thou wilt|Fiat tibi sicut vis]], that is, as you have asked, so let it be fulfilled. The effect followed this word of Christ at once, for it follows: [[15:28|and her daughter was cured|Et sanata est filia ejus]], that is, freed from the demon, [[15:28|from that hour|ex illa hora]], that is, as soon as Christ said, be it done to thee as thou wilt. So the harsher Christ seemed outwardly to this woman in His words and bearing, the kinder He was to her inwardly by a hidden working, by inward inspiration and enlightening. Otherwise, how would this woman have had such faith, humility, patience and prudence? But it is asked: if what the Saviour said is true, It is not good to take the bread of the children and to cast it to the dogs, then in doing the opposite He seems not to have done well. The answer is that Christ's word was to be understood generally, but in this case the opposite was good: as Moses commanded that the Ammonites and Moabites should not enter the church of God[[Deut 23:3||]]; nevertheless Ruth the Moabitess[[Ruth 1:16||]][[Ruth 2:10||]][[Ruth 4:10||]] and Achior the Ammonite[[Jdt 14:6||]], for their virtues and devotion to the God of Israel, were at once admitted to the rites of the Jews. And so this woman too, by her singular devotion, obtains what was not to be granted to others in general.

paras.t: Mystice, per mulierem hanc figuratur Ecclesia, quæ gentilitate relicta, incedit et clamat ad Christum pro sanatione filiæ sui, hoc est animarum, seu particularium Ecclesiarum, pro qua Apostoli ac ceteri Sancti intercedunt ad Dominum. Et consideranda est hic mutatio dexteræ Excelsi: quomodo Judæi, qui filii dicebantur, nunc canes vocantur (sicut de eis ait Christus in Psalmo, Quoniam circumdederunt me canes multi; et Apostolus, Videte canes, videte malos operarios, videte concisionem); gentiles vero, qui canes erant, jam filii nuncupantur.
paras.en: Mystically, this woman figures the Church, which, having left the Gentile world behind, comes forward and cries to Christ for the healing of her daughter, that is, of souls, or of particular Churches; and for her the Apostles and the other Saints intercede with the Lord. And here we should consider [[Ps 76:11|the change of the right hand of the most High|mutatio dexteræ Excelsi]]: how the Jews, who were called children, are now called dogs (as Christ says of them in the Psalm: [[Ps 21:17|many dogs have encompassed me|circumdederunt me canes multi]]; and the Apostle: [[Phil 3:2|Beware of dogs: beware of evil workers: beware of the concision|Videte canes, videte malos operarios, videte concisionem]]); while the Gentiles, who were dogs, are now named children.

paras.t: Et quum transisset inde Jesus, hoc est a partibus Tyri et Sidonis ad Judæam revertendo, venit secus mare Galilææ; et ascendens in montem, sedebat ibi, quatenus ab omnibus videretur, audiretur, faciliusque posset ad ipsum esse accessus. Per quod figuratum est, quod prædicator et custos dominici gregis, omnisque vicarius Christi, ascendere debet arcem contemplationis, apicemque spiritualis conversationis. Et accesserunt ad eum turbæ multæ, habentes secum mutos, claudos, cæcos, debiles. Si per debiles intelligerentur communiter omnes alii a prædictis ægrotis, adjectum non esset, et alios multos, videlicet languidos. Sicut ergo per claudos intelliguntur qui uno claudicant pede, sic per debiles, qui unam manum habent invalidam. Ecce ponit hoc loco velut sub compendio Evangelista multa miracula Christi, quæ si sigillatim recitarentur, facerent magnum volumen: et simile ponit frequenter. Ex quo patet majestas et gloria Salvatoris, qui tam innumerabilia operatus est signa, ut nemo in veteri Testamento queat ei æquari. Pensemus Eliæ et Elisei miracula, et sciemus quam minora ac rariora sint signa eorum prodigiis Christi. Sed et modus agendi incomparabiliter differt in eis. Et projecerunt eos ad pedes ejus, et curavit eos solum imperio, ita ut turbæ mirarentur, videntes, id est audientes, mutos, hoc est, qui muti fuerunt, loqui. Visus in Scripturis, pro quocumque sensu accipitur. Videntes etiam claudos ambulantes, cæcos videntes. Et magnificabant, id est, magnum ac omnipotentem esse professi sunt, Deum Israel, qui tanta ac talia operabatur per Jesum.
paras.en: [[15:29|And when Jesus had passed away from thence|Et quum transisset inde Jesus]], that is, going back from the parts of Tyre and Sidon to Judea, [[15:29|he came nigh the sea of Galilee: and going up into a mountain, he sat there|venit secus mare Galilææ; et ascendens in montem, sedebat ibi]], so as to be seen and heard by all, and so that they might come to Him more easily. This figures that the preacher and guardian of the Lord's flock, and every vicar of Christ, ought to climb the height of contemplation and the summit of a spiritual life. [[15:30|And there came to him great multitudes, having with them the dumb, the blind, the lame, the maimed|Et accesserunt ad eum turbæ multæ, habentes secum mutos, claudos, cæcos, debiles]]. If by "the maimed" were meant in general all others besides the sick already named, there would not have been added [[15:30|and many others|et alios multos]], namely the sick. So as by the lame are meant those who limp on one foot, so by the maimed are meant those who have one hand disabled. See how the Evangelist here gives, as in summary, many miracles of Christ which, if they were told one by one, would make a great volume; and he often does the like. From this the majesty and glory of the Saviour are plain, who worked signs so countless that no one in the Old Testament can be compared with Him. Let us weigh the miracles of Elias and Eliseus, and we shall know how much smaller and rarer their signs are than the wonders of Christ. And their manner of acting differs beyond comparison. [[15:30|and they cast them down at his feet, and he healed them|Et projecerunt eos ad pedes ejus, et curavit eos]] by His command alone, [[15:31|So that the multitudes marvelled seeing the dumb speak|ita ut turbæ mirarentur, videntes, id est audientes, mutos, hoc est, qui muti fuerunt, loqui]]: seeing, that is, hearing, the dumb, that is, those who had been dumb, speak. In the Scriptures "seeing" is used for any sense. Seeing also [[15:31|the lame walk, the blind see|claudos ambulantes, cæcos videntes]]. [[15:31|and they glorified the God of Israel|et magnificabant Deum Israël]], that is, confessed Him great and almighty, who worked such great things through Jesus.

paras.t: Ipse autem Jesus, convocatis discipulis suis, quibus tanquam familiaribus et amicis secreta sua pandebat, dixit: Misereor super turbam, hoc est, indigentiæ populi hujus condoleo, caritatis ac pietatis affectu, quia jam triduo perseverant mecum, id est, per tres dies mecum manserunt in solitudine et sub dio. In quo declaratur amor eorum ad Christum, et devotio ad doctrinam atque miracula ejus. Et non habent quod manducent, ideo dignum est ut eis provideam, tanquam pastor bonus: de quo Dominus prædixit per Ezechielem, dicens, Suscitabo super gregem meum pastorem unum, qui pascat eum, David servum meum, id est Christum, ut omnes exponunt. Et dimittere eos jejunos nolo, ne deficiant, id est fame periclitentur, in via, redeundo ad propria. Quidam enim ex eis de longe venerunt, ut Marcus habet.
paras.en: [[15:32|And Jesus called together his disciples|Ipse autem Jesus, convocatis discipulis suis]], to whom, as His intimates and friends, He opened His secrets, [[15:32|and said: I have compassion on the multitudes|dixit: Misereor super turbam]], that is, I grieve with the need of this people, with a feeling of charity and pity, [[15:32|because they continue with me now three days|quia jam triduo perseverant mecum]], that is, they have stayed with Me three days in the wilderness and under the open sky. In this their love for Christ, and their devotion to His teaching and miracles, is shown. [[15:32|and have not what to eat|Et non habent quod manducent]]; so it is fitting that I provide for them, as the good shepherd, of whom the Lord foretold through Ezechiel, saying: [[Ezech 34:23|I WILL SET UP ONE SHEPHERD OVER THEM, and he shall feed them, even my servant David|Suscitabo super gregem meum pastorem unum, qui pascat eum, David servum meum]], that is, Christ, as all explain it. [[15:32|and I will not send them away fasting, lest they faint in the way|et dimittere eos jejunos nolo, ne deficiant in via]]: faint, that is, be in danger from hunger, on the road home. For [[Mark 8:3|some of them came from afar off|Quidam enim ex eis de longe venerunt]], as Mark has it.

paras.t: Et dicunt ei discipuli: Unde ergo nobis in deserto panes tantos, id est, ex quo vis populum istum reficere, qualiter acquiremus in eremo hac escam ad hoc sufficientem, ut saturemus turbam tantam? quasi dicant: Hoc nobis impossibile est. Discipuli tanquam magistro suo familiarissimi, pluraliter responderunt. Christus quippe singulariter dixit, Dimittere eos jejunos nolo; discipuli vero in persona sua ac Christi responderunt, Unde nobis, id est tibi et discipulis tuis? In quo patet eorum imperfectio, quia non consideraverunt potentiam Christi, qui paulo ante de quinque panibus piscibusque duobus, quinque millia hominum saturavit. Et ait illis Jesus: Quot panes habetis? Non quasi ignorans interrogat, sed ut ex discipulorum responsione, futuri miraculi magnificentia pateat, et ipse in faciendo miraculo ordinate procedat. At illi dixerunt: Septem, et paucos numero pisciculos.
paras.en: [[15:33|And the disciples say unto him: Whence then should we have so many loaves in the desert|Et dicunt ei discipuli: Unde ergo nobis in deserto panes tantos]], that is, since You wish to feed this people, how shall we get in this wilderness food enough for it, [[15:33|as to fill so great a multitude|ut saturemus turbam tantam]]? As if to say: this is impossible for us. The disciples, as most intimate with their Master, answered in the plural. For Christ said in the singular, I will not send them away fasting; but the disciples answered in their own person and Christ's, Whence should we have, that is, You and Your disciples? In this their imperfection is plain, since they did not consider the power of Christ, who a little before had fed five thousand men with five loaves and two fishes[[Matt 14:21||]]. [[15:34|And Jesus said to them: How many loaves have you|Et ait illis Jesus: Quot panes habetis]]? He does not ask as if He did not know, but so that from the disciples' answer the greatness of the coming miracle may be plain, and He Himself may proceed in order in working the miracle. [[15:34|But they said: Seven, and a few little fishes|At illi dixerunt: Septem, et paucos numero pisciculos]].
