paras.t: Et præcepit turbæ ut discumberent super terram. Et accipiens Jesus septem panes et pisces, quantitate permodicos, et gratias agens secundum assumptam humanitatem, Deo Patri, seu toti supergloriosissimæ Trinitati omnium bonorum liberalissimo fonti, fregit, et frangendo multiplicavit, secundum quod Deus potestate immensa, sicut superius dictum est de quinque panum benedictione, fractione et multiplicatione; et dedit discipulis suis, qui acceperunt de manibus ejus, seu loco ubi reposuit panes, non jam septem panes dumtaxat, sed tot quot suffecerunt populo tanto. Et discipuli dederunt populo. Et comederunt omnes, et saturati sunt, id est sufficienter, non gulose, refecti. Et quod superfuit de fragmentis, videlicet reliquias panum ac pisciculorum, tulerunt, id est, collegerunt discipuli, septem sportas plenas, hoc est materiam septem sportas implentem. Erant autem qui manducaverunt, quatuor millia hominum, extra parvulos, hoc est præter eos qui erant sub anno vicesimo, et mulieres. In quo utique signo ostensa est omnipotentia Christi.
paras.en: [[15:35|And he commanded the multitude to sit down upon the ground|Et præcepit turbæ ut discumberent super terram]]. [[15:36|And taking the seven loaves and the fishes|Et accipiens Jesus septem panes et pisces]], very small in quantity, [[15:36|and giving thanks|et gratias agens]], according to the humanity He had assumed, to God the Father, or to the whole most supremely glorious Trinity, the most liberal fountain of all good things, [[15:36|he brake|fregit]], and in breaking multiplied them, as God, by His boundless power, as was said above of the blessing, breaking and multiplication of the five loaves; [[15:36|and gave to his disciples|et dedit discipulis suis]], who received from His hands, or from the place where He set them down, no longer just seven loaves but as many as sufficed for so great a people. [[15:36|and the disciples gave to the people|Et discipuli dederunt populo]]. [[15:37|And they did all eat, and had their fill|Et comederunt omnes, et saturati sunt]], that is, were fed sufficiently, not greedily. [[15:37|And they took up|tulerunt]], that is, the disciples gathered, what was left of the fragments, namely the remains of the loaves and little fishes, [[15:37|seven baskets full|septem sportas plenas]], that is, enough to fill seven baskets. [[15:38|And they that did eat, were four thousand men, beside children|Erant autem qui manducaverunt, quatuor millia hominum, extra parvulos]], that is, besides those under twenty years of age, [[15:38|and women|et mulieres]]. By this sign certainly the almighty power of Christ was shown.

paras.t: Porro hujus miraculi, sicut et superioris de quinque panibus, aliqualis fuit figura, quod in libro Regum de Eliseo recolitur, qui de panibus primitiarum centum viros cibavit, et superabundavit. Mystice, per hanc corporalem refectionem quatuor millium de septem panibus et paucis pisciculis, designatur spiritualis refectio populi christiani, doctrinam quatuor Evangeliorum tenentis, et quatuor virtutes cardinales habentis: qui septem panibus, id est septiformi gratia seu septem donis Spiritus Sancti reficitur; et paucis pisciculis, id est ceteris donis gratis datis, quæ comparatione dictorum bonorum minima sunt, quum possint haberi a malis, et tamen conferuntur a Spiritu Sancto, sicut testatur Apostolus: Alii per Spiritum Sanctum datur sermo sapientiæ, alii sermo scientiæ; alii gratia sanitatum, alii operatio virtutum. Hæc autem sunt pauca numero. Hos autem cibos obtulit Christus hominibus per sanctos Apostolos, per quorum manuum impositionem dabatur Spiritus Sanctus, et quorum prædicatione illuminatæ ac Spiritu Sancto repletæ sunt gentes.
paras.en: Further, this miracle, like the earlier one of the five loaves, had a kind of figure in what is recorded in the book of Kings of Eliseus, who fed a hundred men with loaves of the firstfruits, and there was some left over[[4 Kings 4:42||]]. Mystically, this bodily feeding of four thousand with seven loaves and a few little fishes signifies the spiritual feeding of the Christian people, who hold the teaching of the four Gospels and have the four cardinal virtues: they are fed with seven loaves, that is, with sevenfold grace, or the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost; and with a few little fishes, that is, with the other graces given freely [gratiae gratis datae, gifts given for the good of others], which are very small compared with the goods just named, since they can be had by the wicked, and yet they are bestowed by the Holy Ghost, as the Apostle testifies: [[1 Cor 12:8|To one indeed, by the Spirit, is given the word of wisdom: and to another, the word of knowledge|Alii per Spiritum Sanctum datur sermo sapientiæ, alii sermo scientiæ]]; to another [[1 Cor 12:9|the grace of healing|gratia sanitatum]], to another [[1 Cor 12:10|the working of miracles|operatio virtutum]]. These are few in number. Christ offered this food to men through the holy Apostles, by the laying on of whose hands the Holy Ghost was given[[Acts 8:17||]][[Acts 19:6||]], and by whose preaching the nations were enlightened and filled with the Holy Ghost.

paras.t: Denique, quod Christus dixit se misereri turbæ ipsum triduo imitanti, hoc significat, quod Christus omnibus vere pœnitentibus et contritis, omnibus mundi hujus delicias fugientibus, crucem suam portantibus, secretum locum petentibus causa contemplationis, lacrimationis ac austerioris conversationis (qui dicere possunt cum Psalmista, Similis factus sum pelecano solitudinis; itemque, Ecce elongavi fugiens, et mansi in solitudine): his, inquam, Christus miseretur, peccata indulgendo, gratiarum opulentiam influendo, intus loquendo et consolando, quemadmodum ait per Osee: Ecce, inquiens, ego lactabo eam, et ducam eam in solitudinem, et loquar ad cor ejus. Propter quod ait Apostolus: Sicut pro Christo abundant tribulationes nostræ, ita per Christum abundat consolatio nostra. Oportet ergo Christum in solitudinem sequi, fugiendo, tacendo et quiescendo, cum eo stabiliter die et nocte perseverare, carnales atque humanas consolationes vitando: et tunc Christus conspiciens quia a nobis ipsis non habemus quod manducemus, hoc est, quo spiritualiter confortemur, non dimittet nos jejunos, sed alet nos ad satietatem, ita ut totum capere nequeamus, nec ultra deficiamus in via peregrinationis hujus exsilii, sed cœlesti confortati viatico perducamur ad patriam.
paras.en: Lastly, Christ's saying that He had compassion on the crowd that had followed Him for three days signifies that Christ has compassion on all who are truly penitent and contrite, all who flee the delights of this world, carry their cross, and seek a secluded place for contemplation, tears and a more austere life (who can say with the Psalmist: [[Ps 101:7|I am become like to a pelican of the wilderness|Similis factus sum pelecano solitudinis]]; and again: [[Ps 54:8|Lo, I have gone far off flying away; and I abode in the wilderness|Ecce elongavi fugiens, et mansi in solitudine]]): on these, I say, Christ has compassion, forgiving their sins, pouring in an abundance of graces, speaking within them and consoling them, as He says through Osee: [[Osee 2:14|behold I will allure her, and will lead her into the wilderness: and I will speak to her heart|Ecce, inquiens, ego lactabo eam, et ducam eam in solitudinem, et loquar ad cor ejus]]. Hence the Apostle says: As our tribulations abound for Christ, [[2 Cor 1:5|so also by Christ doth our comfort abound|ita per Christum abundat consolatio nostra]]. We must, then, follow Christ into the wilderness, by flight, silence and rest, persevering steadily with Him day and night and avoiding carnal and human consolations; and then Christ, seeing that we have nothing of our own to eat, that is, nothing to strengthen us spiritually, will not send us away fasting, but will feed us to the full, so that we cannot take it all in, and shall no longer faint on the road of this pilgrimage of exile, but, strengthened by heavenly food for the journey, shall be brought to our fatherland.

15.title: Expositio capituli sextidecimi: Et dimissa turba, ascendit in naviculam
15.title_en: Exposition of the sixteenth chapter: And having dismissed the multitude, he went up into a boat

paras.t: Et dimissa turba, quam in fine præcedentis capituli legitur refecisse, quæ refecta remeavit ad propria, ascendit Jesus in naviculam cum discipulis suis. Raro legitur Christus Dominus majestatis ascendisse in navim, sed in naviculam, ut sicut in aliis, ita in hoc quoque humilitatis exemplum præberet. Et venit in fines, id est loca, Magedan, ubi ut in libris Regum habetur, Josias rex Juda occurrit Nechao Pharaoni regi Ægypti, a cujus sagittariis letaliter læsus est. Sed huic videtur contrarium, quod in Marco asseritur: Statim ascendens navim, venit in partes Dalmanutha. Et respondendum, quod eadem terra est, habens nomina duo, ut aliqui dicunt; alii dicunt quod sint loca contigua, et ergo Christus exsistens in confinio horum locorum, in utroque fuisse describitur.
paras.en: [[15:39|And having dismissed the multitude|Et dimissa turba]], which we read at the end of the preceding chapter that He had fed, and which, having been fed, went back home, Jesus [[15:39|went up into a boat|ascendit Jesus in naviculam]] with His disciples. Christ, the Lord of majesty, is seldom read to have gone up into a ship, but into a boat, so that in this too, as in other things, He might give an example of humility. [[15:39|and came into the coasts of Magedan|et venit in fines Magedan]]: coasts, that is, places; where, as is found in the books of Kings, Josias king of Juda went to meet Nechao Pharao king of Egypt, by whose archers he was mortally wounded[[4 Kings 23:29||]][[2 Par 35:23||]]. But against this seems to be what is asserted in Mark: [[Mark 8:10|And immediately going up into a ship|Statim ascendens navim]], [[Mark 8:10|he came into the parts of Dalmanutha|venit in partes Dalmanutha]]. The answer is that it is the same land with two names, as some say; others say that they are neighbouring places, and so Christ, being on the border between them, is described as being in both.

15.note: The first part of Art. XXIX, the exposition of chapter 16, which begins with Matthew 15:39 (shown here); the rest is in chapter 16.

16.title: Expositio capituli sextidecimi: Et dimissa turba, ascendit in naviculam
16.title_en: Exposition of the sixteenth chapter: And having dismissed the multitude, he went up into a boat

paras.t: Et accesserunt ad eum Pharisæi et Sadducæi tentantes Christum, id est, experimentum sumere cupientes, an ipse esset Christus, vel quærentes reprehendere eum in aliquo verbo vel facto. Et rogaverunt eum insidiose ac perfida mente, ut signum de cœlo, id est aliquam supernaturalem mutationem in corporibus superioribus, vel apparitionem angelicam, ostenderet eis, per quod scire possent, quod Messias venisset, et quod ipse esset Messias.
paras.en: [[16:1|And there came to him the Pharisees and Sadducees tempting|Et accesserunt ad eum Pharisæi et Sadducæi tentantes]] Christ, that is, wishing to make trial whether He was the Christ, or seeking to catch Him out in some word or deed. [[16:1|and they asked him|Et rogaverunt eum]], with a crafty and faithless mind, [[16:1|to shew them a sign from heaven|ut signum de cœlo, id est aliquam supernaturalem mutationem in corporibus superioribus, vel apparitionem angelicam, ostenderet eis]], that is, some supernatural change in the higher bodies, or an appearance of angels, by which they could know that the Messias had come and that He was the Messias.

paras.t: At ille respondens, ait eis: Facto vespere, id est de sero, dicitis interdum: Serenum erit, id est, cras erit aura pulchra, rubicundum est enim cœlum, id est, rubeus quidam color apparet in cœlo, ex incidentia lucis solaris permodicæ super vapores elevatos in aere, in quibus est rubor prædictus, non in cœlestibus corporibus. Talis autem dispositio signum est futuræ serenitatis, quia vapores subtiles ac modici sunt, qui non resolvuntur in pluvias. Interdum tamen contingit oppositum ex causa superveniente. Et mane dicitis sæpe: Hodie tempestas erit, id est aura turbulenta seu pluviosa, rutilat enim, id est, coruscationibus fulget, vel rubore quodam coloratur, triste cœlum, id est nubibus obductum. Et dicitur cœlum rutilum ac rubeum, quia in nubibus est qualitas ista fulgoris sive ruboris: et dicitur cœlum triste, quia talibus qualitatibus in aere exsistentibus, ex adspectu cœli generatur tristitia quædam in anima; sicut opposito modo dicitur lætum, quum adest serenitas aeris. Hæ itaque dispositiones apparentes in cœlo, sunt signa tempestatis instantis.
paras.en: [[16:2|But he answered and said to them: When it is evening|At ille respondens, ait eis: Facto vespere]], that is, late in the day, [[16:2|you say|dicitis]] at times: [[16:2|It will be fair weather|Serenum erit]], that is, tomorrow the weather will be fine, [[16:2|for the sky is red|rubicundum est enim cœlum]], that is, a reddish colour appears in the sky, from the falling of the faint sunlight on vapours raised in the air, in which this redness is, not in the heavenly bodies. Such a condition is a sign of fair weather to come, because the vapours are thin and slight and do not turn into rain; though sometimes the opposite happens from some cause supervening. [[16:3|And in the morning|Et mane]] you often say: [[16:3|To day there will be a storm|Hodie tempestas erit]], that is, turbulent or rainy weather, [[16:3|for the sky is red and lowering|rutilat enim, id est, coruscationibus fulget, vel rubore quodam coloratur, triste cœlum]]: red, that is, flashing with lightning or coloured with a kind of redness; lowering [Latin triste, "sad"], that is, covered with clouds. The sky is called glowing and red because this quality of brightness or redness is in the clouds; and it is called sad because, when such qualities are in the air, a certain sadness arises in the soul from the look of the sky, just as in the opposite way it is called glad when the air is clear. These conditions appearing in the sky, then, are signs of an approaching storm.

paras.t: Faciem ergo cœli, id est prædictas dispositiones apparentes in cœlo: quæ facies cœli vocantur, quoniam per modum vultus in superficie apparent, et primo ingerunt se oculis intuentis; dijudicare, id est ab invicem distinguere, et ex eis futura quædam conjicere, nostis; signa autem temporum, id est argumenta atque indicia quibus pateat tempus primi adventus Christi jam esse impletum, meque esse Christum, non potestis dijudicare et scire? Hoc ait Salvator increpando et exprobrando, quasi dicat: Merito attenderetis signa prophetiæ prænuntiata de Christi adventu jam esse completa in me. In Danielis etenim prophetia, tempus adventus Christi et passionis ejus prætaxatum fuit, Gabriele dicente: Post hebdomades sexaginta duas occidetur Christus. Similiter in Genesi, per ablationem sceptri a Juda: quod Herodis tempore erat completum. Sic nempe prædixit patriarcha Jacob: Non auferetur sceptrum de Juda, et dux de femore ejus, donec veniat qui mittendus est. Item quod Isaias prædixit: Tunc aperientur oculi cæcorum, et aures surdorum patebunt; tunc saliet claudus sicut cervus, etc. Testimonium quoque Joannis, de quo Isaias et Malachias vaticinati fuerunt, fuit manifestum signum adventus Christi: similiter, trium Magorum oblatio, Innocentium occisio, atque miracula Christi, de quibus ait Salvator: Opera quæ ego facio in nomine Patris mei, testimonium perhibent de me: et rursus: Si non facio opera Dei, nolite credere mihi; si autem facio, et si mihi non vultis credere, operibus credite. Increpat ergo Judæos, quod ex omnibus his non consideraverunt eum esse Messiam.
paras.en: [[16:3|You know then how to discern the face of the sky|Faciem ergo cœli, id est prædictas dispositiones apparentes in cœlo: quæ facies cœli vocantur, quoniam per modum vultus in superficie apparent, et primo ingerunt se oculis intuentis; dijudicare, id est ab invicem distinguere, et ex eis futura quædam conjicere, nostis]]: the face of the sky, that is, the conditions just described appearing in the sky, which are called the face of the sky because they appear on its surface like a countenance and are the first thing to meet the eyes of one looking at it; to discern, that is, to distinguish them from one another and to forecast some future things from them; [[16:3|and can you not know the signs of the times|signa autem temporum, id est argumenta atque indicia quibus pateat tempus primi adventus Christi jam esse impletum, meque esse Christum, non potestis dijudicare et scire?]]? That is, the proofs and indications by which it is plain that the time of Christ's first coming is now fulfilled, and that I am the Christ. The Saviour says this rebuking and reproaching them, as if to say: You ought rightly to attend to the signs foretold in prophecy of the coming of Christ, now fulfilled in Me. For in the prophecy of Daniel the time of Christ's coming and of His Passion was set beforehand, when Gabriel said: [[Dan 9:26|after sixty-two weeks Christ shall be slain|Post hebdomades sexaginta duas occidetur Christus]]. Likewise in Genesis, by the taking away of the sceptre from Juda, which was fulfilled in Herod's time; for so the patriarch Jacob foretold: [[Gen 49:10|The sceptre shall not be taken away from Juda, nor a ruler from his thigh, till he come that is to be sent|Non auferetur sceptrum de Juda, et dux de femore ejus, donec veniat qui mittendus est]]. Again, what Isaias foretold: [[Is 35:5|Then shall the eyes of the blind be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped|Tunc aperientur oculi cæcorum, et aures surdorum patebunt]]; [[Is 35:6|Then shall the lame man leap as a hart|tunc saliet claudus sicut cervus]], etc. The testimony of John too, of whom Isaias[[John 1:23||]] and Malachias[[Mal 3:1||]] prophesied, was a plain sign of Christ's coming; likewise the offering of the three Magi[[Matt 2:1||]], the killing of the Innocents[[Matt 2:16||]], and the miracles of Christ, of which the Saviour says: [[John 10:25|the works that I do in the name of my Father, they give testimony of me|Opera quæ ego facio in nomine Patris mei, testimonium perhibent de me]]; and again: [[John 10:37|If I do not the works of my Father, believe me not|Si non facio opera Dei, nolite credere mihi]]; [[John 10:38|But if I do, though you will not believe me, believe the works|si autem facio, et si mihi non vultis credere, operibus credite]]. So He rebukes the Jews because from all these things they did not perceive that He was the Messias.

paras.t: Generatio mala et adultera signum quærit; et signum non dabitur ei, nisi signum Jonæ prophetæ. Hoc supra habitum atque expositum est. Et relictis illis incredulis, divinoque signo indignis, abiit Jesus, ingrediens navim cum discipulis suis, et transfretans, ut Marcus habet. Et quum venissent discipuli ejus, et etiam ipse, trans fretum, obliti sunt panes accipere, hoc est, tunc adverterunt se ex oblivione non sumpsisse panes antequam transfretare inciperent. Forte tam occupati fuerunt circa cibum animæ, quod corporalem cibum secum ferre obliti sunt. Habuerunt tamen unum panem, secundum Marcum. Et quæri potest, ubi dimiserint septem illos cophinos, fragmentis ciborum impletos, de quibus in fine præcedentis capituli dictum est. Dici potest, quod cibos illos dederunt egenis ad propria redeuntibus, ut haberent escas in via, quia nonnulli eorum de longe (teste Marco) venerunt.
paras.en: [[16:4|A wicked and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign: and a sign shall not be given it, but the sign of Jonas the prophet|Generatio mala et adultera signum quærit; et signum non dabitur ei, nisi signum Jonæ prophetæ]]. This was dealt with and explained above[[Matt 12:39||]]. [[16:4|And he left them, and went away|Et relictis illis, abiit]], Jesus, leaving them in their unbelief and unworthy of a divine sign, and went on board a ship with His disciples and crossed over, as Mark has it[[Mark 8:13||]]. [[16:5|And when his disciples were come over the water, they had forgotten to take bread|Et quum venissent discipuli ejus, et etiam ipse, trans fretum, obliti sunt panes accipere]]: when His disciples, and He too, had come over, that is, they then noticed that through forgetfulness they had not taken bread before they began to cross. Perhaps they were so taken up with the food of the soul that they forgot to bring bodily food with them. Yet they had one loaf, according to Mark[[Mark 8:14||]]. And it may be asked where they had left those seven baskets filled with fragments of food, spoken of at the end of the preceding chapter. It can be said that they gave that food to the needy returning home, so that they would have food on the way, since some of them had come from afar, as Mark testifies[[Mark 8:3||]].

paras.t: Qui Christus dixit: Intuemini, hoc est, prudenter discernite, et cavete a fermento Pharisæorum et Sadducæorum. Quomodo autem intelligendum sit hoc, Christus post pauca exponit; nec decet ejus expositionem anticipare. Marcus addit, dicens: Et a fermento Herodis. At illi cogitabant, et ex prævia cogitatione loquebantur, inter se dicentes: Quia panes non accepimus: hoc est, quoniam panem materialem non sumpsimus nobiscum, ideo admonet nos, ne emamus vel accipiamus panem fermentatum a Pharisæis et Sadducæis. Rudes namque discipuli æstimabant magistrum loqui de pane materiali, et de provisione solita corporei cibi. Ideo increpantur, sicut subjungitur.
paras.en: [[16:6|Who said to them: Take heed|Qui Christus dixit: Intuemini]], Christ, that is, discern prudently, [[16:6|and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees|et cavete a fermento Pharisæorum et Sadducæorum]]. How this is to be understood Christ explains a little later, and it is not fitting to anticipate His explanation. Mark adds: [[Mark 8:15|and of the leaven of Herod|Et a fermento Herodis]]. [[16:7|But they thought within themselves, saying|At illi cogitabant, et ex prævia cogitatione loquebantur, inter se dicentes]], and from the thought that went before they spoke: [[16:7|Because we have taken no bread|Quia panes non accepimus]], that is, because we have not brought material bread with us, He warns us not to buy or take leavened bread from the Pharisees and Sadducees. For the unformed disciples thought their Master was speaking of material bread and the usual provision of bodily food. So they are rebuked, as follows.

paras.t: Sciens autem Jesus cogitationes et verba eorum: quæ inter se susurrando dixerunt voce submissa, ne audirentur ab eo; sed eum nil latuit, et cogitationes eorum prodendo divinitatem suam ostendit, et dixit eis: Quid cogitatis inter vos, modicæ fidei, id est, qui modicam fidem habetis, quoniam æstimatis quod monuerim vos de corporalis alimenti provisione, quasi non possem vobis supernaturaliter providere? Quid ergo cogitatis me loqui de corporali fermento vitando? Quia panes non habetis, ideoque putatis me vos exhortari de pane materiali. Nondum intelligitis signa quæ vidistis, per quæ omnipotentiam meam merito cognosceretis? Neque recordamini quinque panum multiplicatorum et expositorum per manus vestras, in quinque millia hominum, præter pueros et mulieres? et non recordamini quot cophinos sumpsistis, id est, quot sportas de fragmentis implestis? Neque recordamini septem panum in quatuor millia hominum, et quot sportas sumpsistis? Tanquam dicat: Si ista sagaciter pensaretis, sciretis utique quia non de materiali fermento locutus sum. Ideo subditur: Quare non intelligitis, quod merito intelligeretis, in quo apparet imperfectio vel negligentia vestra, quia non de pane corporeo dixi vobis istud: Cavete a fermento Pharisæorum et Sadducæorum? Tunc intellexerunt discipuli, quia non dixerit Christus, esse cavendum a fermento panum, id est pane fermentato, seu fermento corporeo, sed a doctrina Pharisæorum et Sadducæorum.
paras.en: [[16:8|And Jesus knowing it|Sciens autem Jesus]]: knowing their thoughts and their words, which they whispered among themselves in a low voice so as not to be heard by Him; but nothing was hidden from Him, and by revealing their thoughts He showed His divinity; [[16:8|said|dixit]] to them: [[16:8|Why do you think within yourselves, O ye of little faith|Quid cogitatis inter vos, modicæ fidei]], that is, you who have little faith, since you think I warned you about providing bodily food, as if I could not provide for you supernaturally? Why then do you think I am speaking of avoiding bodily leaven, [[16:8|for that you have no bread|Quia panes non habetis]], and so you think I am exhorting you about material bread? [[16:9|Do you not yet understand|Nondum intelligitis]] the signs you have seen, by which you might rightly know My almighty power? [[16:9|neither do you remember the five loaves among five thousand men|neque recordamini quinque panum in quinque millia hominum]], loaves multiplied and set out by your hands, besides children and women? [[16:9|and how many baskets you took up|et non recordamini quot cophinos sumpsistis]], that is, how many baskets you filled with fragments? [[16:10|Nor the seven loaves, among four thousand men, and how many baskets you took up|Neque recordamini septem panum in quatuor millia hominum, et quot sportas sumpsistis?]]? As if to say: if you weighed these things shrewdly, you would surely know that I was not speaking of material leaven. So it is added: [[16:11|Why do you not understand|Quare non intelligitis]], as you rightly should (in which your imperfection or negligence appears), [[16:11|that it was not concerning bread I said to you: Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees|quia non de pane corporeo dixi vobis istud: Cavete a fermento Pharisæorum et Sadducæorum?]]? [[16:12|Then they understood that he said not that they should beware of the leaven of bread|Tunc intellexerunt discipuli, quia non dixerit Christus, esse cavendum a fermento panum]], that is, leavened bread or bodily leaven, [[16:12|but of the doctrine of the Pharisees and Sadducees|sed a doctrina Pharisæorum et Sadducæorum]].

paras.t: Ecce hic ponitur expositio metaphoricæ locutionis Christi. Itaque per fermentum, propter suam corruptionem, designatur infecta et falsa doctrina istorum, a qua Christus admonet esse cavendum. Quandoque etiam per fermentum notatur simulatio sanctitatis: ut quum ait Salvator, Cavete a fermento Pharisæorum, quod est hypocrisis.
paras.en: See, here the explanation of Christ's metaphorical saying is given. By leaven, because of its corruption, is signified the tainted and false teaching of these men, which Christ warns must be avoided. Sometimes, too, leaven denotes the pretence of holiness, as when the Saviour says: [[Luke 12:1|Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy|Cavete a fermento Pharisæorum, quod est hypocrisis]].

paras.t: Venit autem Jesus in partes, id est ad loca vicina, Cæsareæ Philippi, id est civitatis quam Philippus frater Herodis Antipæ qui decollavit Joannem, vocavit Cæsaream, ad honorem Tiberii Cæsaris, a quo recepit quartam partem regni patris sui Herodis Ascalonitæ, videlicet unam tetrarchiam. Hæc urbs olim (ut fertur) vocabatur Lais: quam, sicut in libro Judicum recitatur, filii Dan destruxerunt, reparatamque vocaverunt nomine patris sui Dan. Quam Philippus iste amplificans et emendans, vocavit Cæsaream; et postea dicta est Paneas. Fuit quoque secundum historias, alia Cæsarea Palæstinæ, in qua Cornelius centurio mansisse narratur. Et interrogabat discipulos, non velut ignorans, sed ut discipulorum fidem corroboraret, et ex eorum responsione convenientia documenta inferret. Quem dicunt homines esse Filium hominis, scilicet me? Secundum quosdam, Christus non dicit, Quem dicunt me esse? sed, Quem dicunt Filium hominis? ne de se jactanter interrogare videretur. Sed quum aliquid tale a quocumque doctore catholico dicitur, cujus oppositum in Scriptura canonica invenitur, ingenti cautela uti oportet, magisque sequi oportet Scripturam quam verba doctoris. Sic in præsenti. Nam in Marco legitur Christum quæsisse: Quem me dicunt homines esse? Et in Luca: Quem me dicunt turbæ?
paras.en: [[16:13|And Jesus came into the quarters of Cesarea Philippi|Venit autem Jesus in partes Cæsareæ Philippi]]: quarters, that is, the neighbouring places; of Cesarea Philippi, that is, of the city which Philip, brother of Herod Antipas who beheaded John, named Cesarea in honour of Tiberius Caesar, from whom he received the fourth part of the kingdom of his father, Herod of Ascalon, namely one tetrarchy. This city was once (so it is said) called Lais; as is told in the book of Judges, the sons of Dan destroyed it and, having rebuilt it, called it by the name of their father Dan[[Judg 18:29||]]. This Philip enlarged and improved it and called it Cesarea; and afterwards it was called Paneas. There was also, according to the histories, another Cesarea, of Palestine, in which Cornelius the centurion is said to have lived[[Acts 10:1||]]. [[16:13|and he asked his disciples|Et interrogabat discipulos]], not as if He did not know, but to strengthen the disciples' faith, and to draw fitting lessons from their answer: [[16:13|Whom do men say that the Son of man is|Quem dicunt homines esse Filium hominis]], that is, Me? According to some, Christ does not say "Whom do they say that I am?" but "Whom do they say the Son of man is?", lest He should seem to ask boastfully about Himself. But when something of this kind is said by any Catholic doctor whose opposite is found in canonical Scripture, great caution must be used, and Scripture must be followed rather than the words of the doctor. So here: for in Mark we read that Christ asked: [[Mark 8:27|Whom do men say that I am|Quem me dicunt homines esse]]? And in Luke: [[Luke 9:18|Whom do the people say that I am|Quem me dicunt turbæ]]?

paras.t: At illi dixerunt: Alii dicunt Filium hominis, seu te, esse Joannem Baptistam: sicut Herodes, qui dixit: Quem ego decollavi Joannem, ipse surrexit a mortuis, et ideo virtutes operantur in eo. Ista fuit rudis opinio. Nam tempore decollationis Joannis, Christus habuit triginta circiter annos. De hoc dictum est supra. Alii autem dicunt te esse Eliam. Quemadmodum enim sacerdotes suspicati sunt Joannem Baptistam esse Eliam, dicentes, Elias es tu? propter solitariæ vitæ austeritatem, et vestium parilitatem; sic aliqui putaverunt Jesum esse Eliam: primo, quia Elias creditur rediturus ad populum Judæorum, juxta illud Malachiæ prophetæ, Ecce ego mittam vobis Eliam; secundo, propter miraculorum eminentiam; tertio, propter veritatis atque justitiæ insuperabilem zelum. Alii vero Jeremiam: vel propter vitæ sanctitatem, quoniam Jeremias sanctificatus fuit in utero; vel propter eximiam caritatem ad populum, sicut de Jeremia scriptum est, Hic est fratrum amator; vel propter patientiam inconcussam. Aut unum ex Prophetis, videlicet Isaiam, vel aliquem talem, propter eloquentiam. Putabant enim aliquem Prophetarum surrexisse a mortuis, juxta illud Lucæ: Quia Propheta unus de prioribus surrexit. Dicit illis Jesus: Vos autem, quorum non est circa communia languere, qui non tam homines quam dii estis, et documenta mea ac opera melius aliis nostis, quem me esse dicitis? id est, quid sentitis et affirmatis de me?
paras.en: [[16:14|But they said: Some|At illi dixerunt: Alii]] say that the Son of man, that is, You, is [[16:14|John the Baptist|Joannem Baptistam]]: like Herod, who said: [[Mark 6:16|John whom I beheaded, he is risen again from the dead|Quem ego decollavi Joannem, ipse surrexit a mortuis]], [[Matt 14:2|and therefore mighty works shew forth themselves in him|et ideo virtutes operantur in eo]]. That was a crude opinion, for at the time of John's beheading Christ was about thirty years old. Of this we have spoken above. [[16:14|and other some Elias|alii autem Eliam]]: others say You are Elias. For as the priests suspected that John the Baptist was Elias, saying, [[John 1:21|Art thou Elias|Elias es tu]]? because of the austerity of his solitary life and the likeness of his clothing, so some thought that Jesus was Elias: first, because Elias is believed to be coming back to the Jewish people, according to that saying of the prophet Malachias, [[Mal 4:5|Behold, I will send you Elias|Ecce ego mittam vobis Eliam]]; second, because of the greatness of His miracles; third, because of His unconquerable zeal for truth and justice. [[16:14|and others Jeremias|Alii vero Jeremiam]]: either because of the holiness of His life, since Jeremias was sanctified in the womb[[Jer 1:5||]]; or because of His exceptional love for the people, as it is written of Jeremias, [[2 Mach 15:14|This is a lover of his brethren|Hic est fratrum amator]]; or because of His unshaken patience. [[16:14|or one of the prophets|Aut unum ex Prophetis]], namely Isaias, or some such, because of His eloquence. For they thought that one of the Prophets had risen from the dead, according to that saying of Luke: [[Luke 9:19|one of the former prophets is risen again|Propheta unus de prioribus surrexit]][[Luke 9:8||]]. [[16:15|Jesus saith to them: But whom do you say that I am|Dicit illis Jesus: Vos autem, quem me esse dicitis?]]? But you, who are not to languish among common opinions, who are not so much men as gods, and who know My teachings and works better than others, whom do you say that I am? That is, what do you think and affirm of Me?

paras.t: Respondens Simon Petrus, dixit ei. Petrus tanquam principalis, pro omnibus dat responsum. Tu es Christus, Filius Dei vivi. Christus est nomen personæ in duabus naturis subsistentis, in divina videlicet et humana. Itaque, Tu es Christus, id est rex Messias, mundi Salvator, oleo exsultationis, plenitudine gratiæ, chrismate spirituali excellentissime unctus; Filius Dei unicus, unigenitus, naturalis, non adoptivus; Dei vivi, id est, vere viventis vita beata: quod additur ad differentiam hominum mortuorum, qui a gentibus colebantur ut dii, ut Jupiter, Apollo, Minerva, Diana: qui quantum ad corpus omnino defuncti sunt; quantum vero ad animam mortui sunt morte culpæ ac pœnæ, quæ est mors secunda. Respondens autem Jesus, dixit ei: Beatus es beatitudine viæ, beatitudine inchoata, beatitudine spei et gratiæ, Simon: quod interpretatur obediens; Bar Jona, id est filius Joannis. Sic enim dictus est pater ejus. Unde in Joanne Salvator ait: Simon Joannis, diligis me? Vel, Bar Jona, id est filius columbæ, videlicet Spiritus Sancti, qui per columbam significatur. Quia caro et sanguis, id est Judæi, de quorum sanguine natus es; vel, Caro et sanguis non revelavit tibi, id est, a te ipso non invenisti quod professus es, dicens quod sim Christus, Filius Dei vivi. Simili modo Paulus testatur: Non acquievi carni et sanguini. Sed Pater meus, qui in cœlis est, a quo est omne datum optimum, et omne donum perfectum. Nemo enim novit Filium, nisi Pater, et cui revelaverit Pater.
paras.en: [[16:16|Simon Peter answered and said|Respondens Simon Petrus, dixit]] to Him. Peter, as the chief, gives the answer for all: [[16:16|Thou art Christ, the Son of the living God|Tu es Christus, Filius Dei vivi]]. Christ is the name of a Person subsisting in two natures, namely the divine and the human. So: Thou art Christ, that is, the King Messias, the Saviour of the world, anointed most excellently [[Heb 1:9|with the oil of gladness|oleo exsultationis]], with the fullness of grace, with spiritual chrism; [[16:16|the Son|Filius]] of God, the only, only-begotten, natural, not adopted Son; [[16:16|of the living God|Dei vivi]], that is, of God truly living with the life of blessedness: which is added to distinguish Him from the dead men who were worshipped as gods by the Gentiles, such as Jupiter, Apollo, Minerva and Diana, who as to the body are wholly dead, and as to the soul are dead with the death of guilt and punishment, [[Apoc 21:8|which is the second death|quæ est mors secunda]][[Apoc 20:14||]]. [[16:17|And Jesus answering said to him: Blessed art thou|Respondens autem Jesus, dixit ei: Beatus es]] with the blessedness of the way [that is, of this life, as distinct from the blessedness of heaven], a blessedness begun, the blessedness of hope and grace, [[16:17|Simon|Simon]], which is interpreted "obedient"; [[16:17|Bar-Jona|Bar Jona]], that is, son of John, for so his father was called; hence in John the Saviour says: [[John 21:15|Simon, son of John, lovest thou me|Simon Joannis, diligis me]]? Or Bar-Jona, that is, son of the dove, namely of the Holy Ghost, who is signified by the dove. [[16:17|because flesh and blood|Quia caro et sanguis]], that is, the Jews, of whose blood you were born; or flesh and blood [[16:17|hath not revealed it to thee|non revelavit tibi]], that is, you did not find out by yourself what you have confessed, saying that I am the Christ, the Son of the living God. In the same way Paul testifies: [[Gal 1:16|I condescended not to flesh and blood|Non acquievi carni et sanguini]]. [[16:17|but my Father who is in heaven|Sed Pater meus, qui in cœlis est]], from whom is [[Jas 1:17|Every best gift and every perfect gift|omne datum optimum, et omne donum perfectum]]. For [[Matt 11:27|no one knoweth the Son but the Father|Nemo enim novit Filium, nisi Pater]], and he to whom the Father reveals Him.

paras.t: Et ego dico tibi, hoc est, tuæ confessioni qua mihi dixisti, Tu es Christus, vicissitudinem et præmium reddo, et dico, dicendoque facio, quoniam meum dixisse fecisse est: Quia tu es Petrus, id est principalis, et in fide firmus; vel, Petrus, id est vere Petre, qui es Christi dignus confessor. Sic ergo imponitur ei novum nomen, propter fidei suæ confessionem, et dicitur Petrus, qui Simon vocabatur. Et super hanc petram, hoc est fidei hujus firmitatem et fundamentum; vel, Super hanc petram quam confessus es, hoc est super me ipsum, lapidem angularem, montem altissimum: de quo ait Apostolus, Fundamentum aliud nemo potest ponere, præter id quod positum est, quod est Christus Jesus. Ædificabo, hoc est, spiritualiter collocabo ac confirmabo, Ecclesiam meam, id est congregationem fidelium, corda eorum per fidem, caritatem et gratiam, mihi inseparabiliter connectendo, ita ut omnes sint unum corpus mysticum, unaque domus: juxta illud Pauli apostoli, Scias quomodo oporteat te conversari in domo Dei, quæ est Ecclesia Dei vivi, columna et fundamentum veritatis. In hac igitur fide, quod Jesus est Christus, Filius Dei vivi, fundatur atque salvatur Ecclesia, præsertim quum in nomine Christi, tota superbeatissima Trinitas intelligatur, videlicet Pater ungens, Filius unctus, Spiritus Sanctus unctio. Hinc Joannes in Canonica: Omnis, inquit, qui credit quoniam Jesus est Christus, ex Deo natus est; et rursus, Quis est qui vincit mundum, nisi qui credit quoniam Jesus est Christus? Et portæ inferi, hoc est ea quæ ducunt ad pœnas inferni, videlicet tentationes diaboli, doctrinæ fallaces, et vitia; vel ea quæ propter suam pœnalitatem comparantur portis vel pœnis inferni, videlicet tribulationes adversariorum, persecutiones tyrannorum, et reliqua præsentis vitæ incommoda; non prævalebunt adversus eam, id est contra totam Ecclesiam supra prædictam petram spiritualiter ædificatam. Non enim poterunt eam a fide avertere, a Deo abstrahere, dæmonum servituti subjicere, quoad se totam, hoc est quantum ad electos, in quibus præsertim consistit Ecclesia. De quibus Joannes: Omnis, inquit, qui natus est ex Deo, non peccat, sed generatio Dei conservat illum. In eadem quoque epistola ait Joannes: Qui natus est ex Deo non peccat (finaliter scilicet) quoniam semen ejus manet in eo. Talibus quippe Christus promisit: Ecce ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus, usque ad consummationem sæculi. Hanc potestatem habet Ecclesia, non a se per naturam, sed per gratiam Christi, de quo profitetur Apostolus: Omnia possum in eo qui me confortat.
paras.en: [[16:18|And I say to thee|Et ego dico tibi]], that is, to your confession, in which you said to Me, Thou art Christ, I give a return and a reward, and I say, and in saying I do, since for Me to have said is to have done: [[16:18|That thou art Peter|Quia tu es Petrus]], that is, chief and firm in faith; or, Peter, that is, truly a rock [Latin petra], you who are a worthy confessor of Christ. So a new name is given him because of the confession of his faith, and he who was called Simon is called Peter. [[16:18|and upon this rock|Et super hanc petram]], that is, upon the firmness and foundation of this faith; or, upon this rock which you have confessed, that is, upon Myself, the corner stone[[Is 28:16||]][[Eph 2:20||]], the highest mountain, of whom the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 3:11|other foundation no man can lay, but that which is laid: which is Christ Jesus|Fundamentum aliud nemo potest ponere, præter id quod positum est, quod est Christus Jesus]]. [[16:18|I will build|Ædificabo]], that is, will spiritually set in place and make firm, [[16:18|my church|Ecclesiam meam]], that is, the congregation of the faithful, joining their hearts inseparably to Myself through faith, charity and grace, so that all are one mystical body and one house: according to that saying of the apostle Paul: [[1 Tim 3:15|that thou mayest know how thou oughtest to behave thyself in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth|Scias quomodo oporteat te conversari in domo Dei, quæ est Ecclesia Dei vivi, columna et fundamentum veritatis]]. On this faith, then, that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the living God, the Church is founded and saved; especially since in the name of Christ the whole most blessed Trinity is understood, namely the Father who anoints, the Son who is anointed, the Holy Ghost who is the anointing. Hence John says in his Epistle: [[1 John 5:1|Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ, is born of God|Omnis, inquit, qui credit quoniam Jesus est Christus, ex Deo natus est]]; and again: [[1 John 5:5|Who is he that overcometh the world, but he that believeth that Jesus is|Quis est qui vincit mundum, nisi qui credit quoniam Jesus est]] the Christ? [[16:18|and the gates of hell|Et portæ inferi]], that is, the things that lead to the pains of hell, namely the devil's temptations, false teachings and vices; or the things which for their painfulness are compared to the gates, or pains, of hell, namely the tribulations caused by adversaries, the persecutions of tyrants and the other hardships of the present life, [[16:18|shall not prevail against it|non prævalebunt adversus eam]], that is, against the whole Church built spiritually upon the rock just named. For they will not be able to turn her from the faith, draw her away from God, or subject her to the slavery of demons as regards the whole of her, that is, as regards the elect, in whom above all the Church consists. Of them John says: [[1 John 5:18|whosoever is born of God sinneth not: but the generation of God preserveth him|Omnis, inquit, qui natus est ex Deo, non peccat, sed generatio Dei conservat illum]]. In the same epistle John also says: [[1 John 3:9|Whosoever is born of God committeth not sin|Qui natus est ex Deo non peccat]] (finally, that is), [[1 John 3:9|for his seed abideth in him|quoniam semen ejus manet in eo]]. To such indeed Christ promised: [[Matt 28:20|behold I am with you all days, even to the consummation of the world|Ecce ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus, usque ad consummationem sæculi]]. The Church has this power not of herself by nature, but through the grace of Christ, of whom the Apostle declares: [[Phil 4:13|I can do all things in him who strengtheneth me|Omnia possum in eo qui me confortat]].

paras.t: Et tibi dabo claves regni cœlorum. Huic loco paulisper immorari oportet. Primo ergo pensandum, quod sicut in corporalibus, clavis vocatur instrumentum quo janua regulariter aperitur, ita in spiritualibus seu sacramento Pœnitentiæ, clavis appellatur potestas qua obstaculum ingrediendi regnum cœleste aufertur. Hoc autem obstaculum duplex est, scilicet macula, et reatus seu obligatio ad pœnam. Clavis ergo, ut nunc sumitur, est potestas ligandi et solvendi, qua ecclesiasticus judex indignos excludit a regno, et dignos ad illud admittit. Quæ potestas est in Deo Trinitate per auctoritatem, in Christo homine per excellentiam, in ministris Ecclesiæ per instrumentalem administrationem. Quidam vero dixerunt, quod sint duæ claves realiter condistinctæ, videlicet scientia infusa seu acquisita, per quam sacerdos judicat quis dignus, et quis indignus consistat, et potestas admittendi ad regnum vel excludendi a regno: sic tamen, ut scientia dicatur clavis minus principalis, et in ordine ad aliam clavem, sine qua nec clavis esset. Et hæc videtur fuisse opinio Magistri in libro quarto. Alii probabilius dicunt, quod et communius jam tenetur, quod non ipsa scientia, sed auctoritas utendi scientia ad discernendum inter bonum et malum, sit clavis: quæ potest esse sine scientia, et econtra, quemadmodum in sæcularibus judiciis quidam habent auctoritatem judicandi non habentes juris scientiam, et quidam vice versa habent scientiam juris, non autem auctoritatem exercendi judicium. Et clarum est, quod scientia necessario exigitur ad debitum usum clavis istius.
paras.en: [[16:19|And I will give to thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven|Et tibi dabo claves regni cœlorum]]. We must dwell on this place for a little. First, then, it should be considered that as among bodily things a key is the instrument by which a door is ordinarily opened, so among spiritual things, or in the sacrament of Penance, the key is the power by which the obstacle to entering the heavenly kingdom is removed. This obstacle is twofold, namely the stain, and the guilt or liability to punishment. The key, then, as it is taken here, is the power of binding and loosing, by which the ecclesiastical judge shuts out the unworthy from the kingdom and admits the worthy to it. This power is in God the Trinity by authority, in Christ as man by excellence, and in the ministers of the Church by instrumental administration. Some have said that there are two keys really distinct, namely knowledge, infused or acquired, by which the priest judges who is worthy and who unworthy, and the power of admitting to the kingdom or shutting out from it; but in such a way that knowledge is called the less principal key, ordered to the other key, without which it would not be a key at all. And this seems to have been the opinion of the Master [Peter Lombard] in his fourth book. Others say more probably, and this is now more commonly held, that the key is not knowledge itself but the authority to use knowledge in discerning between good and evil; and this can exist without knowledge, and the other way round, just as in secular courts some have the authority to judge without having knowledge of the law, and some, conversely, have knowledge of the law but not authority to exercise judgment. And it is clear that knowledge is necessarily required for the due use of this key.

paras.t: Porro, Hieronymus ait hoc loco, quod sicut in veteri Testamento jubebantur leprosi ostendere se sacerdotibus, ut si lepram haberent, a sacerdote immundi fierent, non quod sacerdotes legales leprosos faciant, et immundos, sed quod habeant notitiam leprosi et non leprosi, possintque discernere quis mundus vel immundus sit: quomodo ergo ibi sacerdos leprosum facit immundum, sic in novo Testamento ligat vel solvit episcopus vel sacerdos, non eos qui insontes seu innocentes sunt, vel qui noxii; sed pro officio suo, quum peccatorum audierit varietates, scit qui ligandus sit, vel qui solvendus. Verum, juxta hanc assertionem, non videretur sacerdos novæ legis (ut quidam objiciunt) majorem habere efficaciam atque virtutem quam sacerdos legalis, nec sacramenta novæ legis facerent (ut videtur) quod significant. Considerandum ergo, quod secundum Magistrum, quarto libro Sententiarum, sacerdotibus novæ legis commissa est auctoritas remittendi peccata, vel retinendi, non ut propria auctoritate hoc faciant, sed Dei operationem vitia remittentis ostendant, quasi ipsius ministri. Hæc autem ostensio tribus modis efficitur: Primo, ostendendo eam, non ut præsentem, sed promittendo tanquam futuram, sine hoc quod aliquid operentur ad eam: sicque sacramenta veteris legis ostendebant Dei operationem, et significabant eam. Unde sacerdos legalis ostendebat dumtaxat, nil operabatur ad culpæ remissionem. Secundo, fit ostensio ut sacerdotes significent operationem Dei tanquam præsentem, et nil operentur ad eam. Et ita aliqui asserunt, sacramenta novæ legis solum ostendere infusionem gratiæ quam Deus confert in sacramentorum dispensatione: sicque potestas clavium tantum ostenderet collationem gratiæ seu remissionem culpæ factam in sacramento Pœnitentiæ. Tertio, fit ut sacerdotes significent præsentem operationem Dei in remissionem culpæ, aliquid operando ad eam instrumentaliter et dispositive, quantum in ipsis est, licet interdum culpa sit ante remissa. Et istud communius nunc tenetur, quod scilicet virtute clavium minister Ecclesiæ cooperetur hoc modo ad remissionem peccati: quod etiam verbis Christi magis consonare videtur, quibus ait apud Joannem, Quorum remiseritis peccata, remittuntur eis, et quorum retinueritis, retenta sunt. Unde nunc quoque subjungitur:
paras.en: Further, Jerome says at this place that as in the Old Testament lepers were commanded to show themselves to the priests[[Lev 13:9||]], so that if they had leprosy they might be declared unclean by the priest (not that the priests of the Law make men lepers and unclean, but that they have knowledge of who is a leper and who is not, and can discern who is clean or unclean), so, in the way the priest there makes the leper unclean, in the New Testament the bishop or priest binds or looses, not those who are guiltless or innocent, or those who are guilty; but in virtue of his office, when he has heard the various kinds of sins, he knows who is to be bound and who loosed. But according to this assertion (as some object), the priest of the new law would not seem to have greater efficacy and power than the priest of the Law, nor would the sacraments of the new law (as it seems) effect what they signify. It should be considered, then, that according to the Master, in the fourth book of the Sentences, the priests of the new law have been entrusted with the authority to remit or retain sins, not so as to do this by their own authority, but so as to show forth, as His ministers, the working of God who remits sins. This showing forth happens in three ways. First, by showing it not as present but by promising it as future, without doing anything towards it: and so the sacraments of the old law showed forth God's working and signified it; hence the priest of the Law only showed it, and did nothing towards the remission of guilt. Second, the showing is such that the priests signify God's working as present, and do nothing towards it; and so some assert that the sacraments of the new law only show forth the infusion of grace which God bestows in the dispensing of the sacraments; and so the power of the keys would only show forth the bestowal of grace or the remission of guilt brought about in the sacrament of Penance. Third, it is such that the priests signify God's present working for the remission of guilt, doing something towards it instrumentally and by way of disposition, as far as lies in them, although sometimes the guilt has been remitted beforehand. And this is now more commonly held, namely that by the power of the keys the minister of the Church cooperates in this way in the remission of sin; and this seems to agree better with the words of Christ in John: [[John 20:23|Whose sins you shall forgive, they are forgiven them: and whose sins you shall retain, they are retained|Quorum remiseritis peccata, remittuntur eis, et quorum retinueritis, retenta sunt]]. So now it is added:

paras.t: Et quodcumque ligaveris super terram, id est, quemcumque a regno excluseris, excommunicaveris, inabsolutum dimiseris, servato recto processu seu debito clavium usu. Ait nempe Theologus ultimo Ecclesiasticæ hierarchiæ capitulo, quod sacerdotes uti debent virtutibus hierarchiæ sibi collatis, secundum quod Divinitas moverit eos, quoniam agens instrumentale non sortitur efficaciam, nisi prout a principali agente movetur. Propter quod dicit Apostolus: Secundum potestatem quæ data est mihi in ædificationem, non in destructionem. Erit ligatum et in cœlis, id est, ratum et approbatum erit coram Deo. Et quodcumque solveris super terram, id est, quemcumque in Ecclesia militanti absolveris, ad regnum admiseris, erit solutum et in cœlis, id est, a Deo dimissum erit et ratum, servato, ut tactum est, ordinato processu, ut vere pœnitens et contritus absolvatur, non is qui in voluntate manet peccati. Hanc autem potestatem Christus dedit Apostolis omnibus, ut aliqui dicunt, quando post resurrectionem insufflavit in eos, et dixit: Accipite Spiritum Sanctum, quorum remiseritis peccata, etc. Denique secundum Thomam, et alios multos, duæ præfatæ claves non differunt secundum essentiam, sed per comparationem ad actum, ita ut duæ dicantur, propter actus diversos. Imo secundum Thomam, potestas ista, seu clavis, realiter idem est quod character, seu ordo sacerdotalis vel virtus conficiendi: et secundum hoc Christus dedit hanc potestatem Apostolis in Cœna, quando ordinavit, id est fecit eos sacerdotes, dicendo: Hoc facite in meam commemorationem.
paras.en: [[16:19|And whatsoever thou shalt bind upon earth|Et quodcumque ligaveris super terram]], that is, whomever you shut out from the kingdom, excommunicate, or leave unabsolved, keeping the right procedure, or the due use of the keys. For the Theologian [Dionysius the Areopagite] says in the last chapter of the Ecclesiastical Hierarchy that priests must use the hierarchical powers conferred on them as the Godhead moves them, since an instrumental agent has no efficacy except as it is moved by the principal agent. Hence the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 13:10|according to the power which the Lord hath given me unto edification and not unto destruction|Secundum potestatem quæ data est mihi in ædificationem, non in destructionem]]. [[16:19|it shall be bound also in heaven|Erit ligatum et in cœlis]], that is, it will be ratified and approved before God. [[16:19|and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth|Et quodcumque solveris super terram]], that is, whomever in the Church militant you absolve and admit to the kingdom, [[16:19|it shall be loosed also in heaven|erit solutum et in cœlis]], that is, it will be forgiven by God and ratified: keeping, as has been said, the ordered procedure, so that the truly penitent and contrite is absolved, not one who remains in the will to sin. Christ gave this power to all the Apostles, as some say, when after the resurrection He breathed on them and said: [[John 20:22|Receive ye the Holy Ghost|Accipite Spiritum Sanctum]], [[John 20:23|Whose sins you shall forgive|quorum remiseritis peccata]], etc. Finally, according to Thomas and many others, the two keys spoken of do not differ in essence, but in relation to their act, so that they are called two because of their different acts. Indeed, according to Thomas, this power or key is really the same as the character, or priestly order, or the power of consecrating; and accordingly Christ gave this power to the Apostles at the Supper, when He ordained them, that is, made them priests, saying: [[Luke 22:19|Do this for a commemoration of me|Hoc facite in meam commemorationem]].

paras.t: Tunc Jesus præcepit discipulis suis, ut nemini dicerent quia ipse esset Christus. Mirum videtur, cur Christus istud præcepit. Si enim noluit prædicari se esse Christum, cur misit et permisit Joannem Baptistam prædicare ejus adventum? Et cur ipsemet interdum respondit se esse Christum? dicendo: Ego veni in nomine Patris mei, et non recepistis me; et, Qui credit in me, non morietur in æternum; et, Ego et Pater unum sumus. Supra quoque capitulo decimo legitur, quod misit Apostolos prædicare suum adventum. Ad quod Hieronymus, Ambrosius, aliique expositores diversimode responderunt, et satis obscure. Videtur autem hoc modo posse responderi, quod Christus noluit suum adventum penitus publicari, ne sua passio impediretur: quia si cognovissent, nunquam Dominum gloriæ crucifixissent. Noluit etiam suum adventum penitus taceri et occultari, ne Judæi excusationem haberent. Ideo per Annam prophetissam, per Simeonem justum, per Magos, per Præcursorem, per discipulos, per propria verba atque miracula, interdum insinuavit se esse Christum, secundum congruentiam causæ, loci et temporis. Unde interdum præcepit miracula sua taceri, aliquando manifestari. Nunc ergo jussit taceri se esse Christum, ne Judæi audientes quod esset Filius Dei, et postea videntes eum occidi, scandalizarentur. Idcirco jam subditur:
paras.en: [[16:20|Then he commanded his disciples, that they should tell no one that he was|Tunc Jesus præcepit discipulis suis, ut nemini dicerent quia ipse esset]] the Christ. It seems strange that Christ commanded this. For if He did not wish it to be preached that He was the Christ, why did He send John the Baptist and allow him to preach His coming? And why did He Himself sometimes answer that He was the Christ, saying: [[John 5:43|I am come in the name of my Father, and you receive me not|Ego veni in nomine Patris mei, et non recepistis me]]; and, He that [[John 11:26|believeth in me shall not die for ever|credit in me, non morietur in æternum]]; and, [[John 10:30|I and the Father are one|Ego et Pater unum sumus]]? And above, in the tenth chapter, we read that He sent the Apostles to preach His coming[[Matt 10:7||]]. To this Jerome, Ambrose and other expositors have answered in various ways, and rather obscurely. It seems, however, that it can be answered thus: Christ did not wish His coming to be fully published, lest His Passion be hindered; for [[1 Cor 2:8|if they had known it, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory|si cognovissent, nunquam Dominum gloriæ crucifixissent]]. Nor did He wish His coming to be wholly passed over in silence and hidden, lest the Jews have an excuse. So through Anna the prophetess, Simeon the just, the Magi, the Forerunner, the disciples, and His own words and miracles, He sometimes made it known that He was the Christ, as the cause, place and time made fitting. Hence He sometimes commanded His miracles to be kept quiet, and sometimes to be made known. Now, then, He ordered that it be kept quiet that He was the Christ, lest the Jews, hearing that He was the Son of God and afterwards seeing Him put to death, should be scandalized. So it is now added:

paras.t: Exinde, id est statim post hæc verba, in quibus ostendit se verum Christum, Dei Filium, verumque Deum, habentem potentiam dandi claves regni cœlorum, cœpit Jesus ostendere, per Scripturas Prophetarum, vel aliis modis, discipulis suis, quia oporteret eum ire, tempore præordinato atque præfixo a Patre, Jerosolymam. Hoc autem oportuit non necessitate coactionis, sed ut impleretur præordinatio Dei, qui per Christi passionem proposuit mundum redimere. Oportuit ergo necessitate conditionata, necessitate consequentiæ, et necessitate finis. Et multa pati, id est verba blasphema ac dira supplicia, a senioribus Judæorum, et Scribis, et Pharisæis, qui erant clerici Judæorum, et principibus sacerdotum Anna et Caipha, et occidi, ut implerentur Scripturæ, et nostra delicta solverentur, non propter propriam culpam: sicut in Psalmo testatur, Quæ non rapui, tunc exsolvebam; et tertia die resurgere. Hoc ad consolationem discipulorum adjecit, ne propter passionis ejus auditum inconsolabiliter tristarentur.
paras.en: [[16:21|From that time|Exinde]], that is, immediately after these words in which He showed that He was the true Christ, the Son of God and true God, having power to give the keys of the kingdom of heaven, [[16:21|Jesus began to shew to his disciples|cœpit Jesus ostendere discipulis suis]], by the Scriptures of the Prophets or in other ways, [[16:21|that he must go to Jerusalem|quia oporteret eum ire Jerosolymam]], at the time foreordained and fixed by the Father. This He must do, not by the necessity of compulsion, but so that God's foreordaining might be fulfilled, who purposed to redeem the world through Christ's Passion. So He must, by conditional necessity, necessity of consequence, and necessity of the end [scholastic terms: necessary given God's decree, not compelled]. [[16:21|and suffer many things|Et multa pati]], that is, blasphemous words and dreadful torments, [[16:21|from the ancients and scribes|a senioribus Judæorum, et Scribis]] of the Jews, and the Pharisees, who were the clergy of the Jews, [[16:21|and chief priests|et principibus sacerdotum]] Annas and Caiphas, [[16:21|and be put to death|et occidi]], that the Scriptures might be fulfilled and our sins be paid for, not for any fault of His own, as He testifies in the Psalm: [[Ps 68:5|then did I pay that which I took not away|Quæ non rapui, tunc exsolvebam]]; [[16:21|and the third day rise again|et tertia die resurgere]]. This He added for the consolation of the disciples, lest on hearing of His Passion they should be sad beyond consolation.

paras.t: Et assumens eum Petrus seorsum, ne magistrum in præsentia discipulorum arguere videretur, quia non debet subditus superiorem suum publice increpare. Vel ideo sumpsit eum seorsum, ut ei familiarius atque audacius seu fiducialius loqueretur, sicut moris est amicorum in secreto securius colloqui. Cœpit increpare, non quasi de culpa, sed increpare, id est verbis reprimere per modum dissuadentis, illum suum prædilectum magistrum, a quo tam dulcia verba immediate audivit, Beatus es, Simon Bar Jona; dicens: Absit a te, Domine, ut tanta patiaris, qui culpam non habes, quum et pœna culpæ debeatur; non erit hoc malum pœnæ tibi innocenti. Ex quo patet, quod Petrus nondum agnovit ex Scripturis, quod Christus pro mundi salute fuerit occidendus.
paras.en: [[16:22|And Peter taking him|Et assumens eum Petrus]] aside, so as not to seem to reprove his Master in the presence of the disciples, since a subject ought not to rebuke his superior in public. Or he took Him aside so as to speak to Him more familiarly and boldly, or confidently, as friends are accustomed to talk more freely in private. [[16:22|began to rebuke him|Cœpit increpare]]: not as if for a fault, but rebuke, that is, hold Him back with words by way of dissuading, his dearly loved Master, from whom he had just heard such sweet words, Blessed art thou, Simon Bar-Jona; [[16:22|saying: Lord, be it far from thee|dicens: Absit a te, Domine]] to suffer such things, You who have no fault, since punishment is owed to fault; [[16:22|this shall not be unto thee|non erit hoc]]: this evil of punishment shall not be yours, who are innocent. From this it is plain that Peter had not yet learned from the Scriptures that Christ was to be put to death for the salvation of the world.

paras.t: Qui conversus, id est, vultum suum ad Petrum convertens, ut eum districtius increparet, et adspectu suo terrifico perterreret: nam per tristitiam vultus corrigitur animus delinquentis; dixit Petro: Vade post me, id est, sensum tuum relinque, et sequere me, voluntatemque tuam conforma præordinationi divinæ, satana, id est, adversator meus, imo omnium inimice, quantum ad hoc quod passionem meam, ex qua mundi salus dependet, niteris impedire, et meo sermoni conaris resistere; scandalum es mihi, id est, quantum in te est, suggeris mihi malum culpæ, et occasionem ruinæ, ut non obediam Deo Patri, qui decrevit mea passione mundum salvare; quia non sapis ea quæ Dei sunt, id est, divina nondum intelligis, nec secundum Deum afficeris, habendo cognitionem formatam ac sapidam, affectionesque spirituales secundum influentiam Spiritus Sancti. Sic quoque ait Apostolus: Animalis homo non percipit ea quæ sunt Spiritus Dei. Sed ea quæ hominum, hoc est, humanum sensum et naturalem affectum sectaris, optando ne patiar. Ex naturali ergo amore, et quadam pia compassione, Petrus hæc dixit; nec peccavit mortaliter. Præterea constat ex his, quod sicut Jesus blandus erat in commendando quæ bona sunt, sic terribilis erat in increpando illicita. Quod secundum congruentiam loci, causæ, ac temporis, imitari debet prælatus, et omnis Christi vicarius. Veritas enim neminem palpat. Unde ad Titum dicit Apostolus: Dure increpa illos. Non tamen semper hoc expedit. Propter quod dicit Apostolus: Servum Domini non oportet litigare, sed docibilem esse ad omnes, patientem, cum modestia corripientem.
paras.en: [[16:23|Who turning|Qui conversus]], that is, turning His face to Peter, so as to rebuke him more sternly and frighten him with His terrible look, for [[Eccles 7:4|by the sadness of the countenance the mind of the offender is corrected|per tristitiam vultus corrigitur animus delinquentis]], [[16:23|said to Peter: Go behind me|dixit Petro: Vade post me]], that is, leave your own way of thinking and follow Me, and conform your will to the divine foreordaining, [[16:23|Satan|satana]], that is, My adversary, indeed the enemy of all, in that you are trying to hinder My Passion, on which the salvation of the world depends, and to resist My word; [[16:23|thou art a scandal unto me|scandalum es mihi]], that is, as far as in you lies, you suggest to Me the evil of sin and an occasion of ruin, that I should not obey God the Father, who has decreed to save the world by My Passion; [[16:23|because thou savourest not the things that are of God|quia non sapis ea quæ Dei sunt]], that is, you do not yet understand divine things, nor are you moved according to God, having a formed and savouring knowledge [Latin sapere, both "to know" and "to taste"] and spiritual affections according to the inflowing of the Holy Ghost. So too the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 2:14|the sensual man perceiveth not these things that are of the Spirit of God|Animalis homo non percipit ea quæ sunt Spiritus Dei]]. [[16:23|but the things that are of men|Sed ea quæ hominum]], that is, you follow human sense and natural affection, in wishing that I should not suffer. Peter said this, then, out of natural love and a kind of devout compassion, and did not sin mortally. Further, it is clear from this that as Jesus was gentle in commending what is good, so He was terrible in rebuking what is unlawful. The prelate, and every vicar of Christ, ought to imitate this as place, cause and time make fitting; for the truth flatters no one. Hence the Apostle says to Titus: [[Tit 1:13|rebuke them sharply|Dure increpa illos]]. Yet this is not always expedient; which is why the Apostle says: [[2 Tim 2:24|the servant of the Lord must not wrangle: but be mild toward all men, apt to teach, patient|Servum Domini non oportet litigare, sed docibilem esse ad omnes, patientem]], [[2 Tim 2:25|With modesty admonishing|cum modestia corripientem]].

paras.t: Tunc Jesus dixit discipulis suis, et etiam aliis. Unde Lucas ait: Dixit autem ad omnes. Et Marcus: Convocata, inquit, turba cum discipulis suis, dixit ad eos. Si quis vult post me venire, hoc est mea vestigia sequi, meis virtutibus conformari, ad perfectionem pertingere, ad patriam cœlestem post me intrare, abneget semetipsum, id est, propriam voluntatem relinquat, Deo obediat, concupiscentias vincat. Hoc est, secundum Apostolum, deponere veterem hominem cum actibus suis, et induere novum, qui secundum Deum creatus est in sanctitate et justitia. Et tollat crucem suam, hoc est, tribulationes, adversitates, tentationes, æquanimiter atque viriliter perferat, se ipsum quotidie per opera pœnitentiæ mortificet, et omne genus martyrii pro fide et æquitate pati paratus sit, quemadmodum scriptum est: Quoniam propter te mortificamur tota die. Propter quod Paulus: Semper, inquit, mortificationem Jesu in corpore nostro circumferentes, ut et vita Jesu manifestetur in carne nostra mortali. Hoc agit qui sapienter pensat illud Apostoli: Non sunt condignæ passiones hujus temporis ad futuram gloriam; et, Omnes qui volunt pie vivere in Christo, persecutionem patientur. Et sequatur me, perseverando in bonis usque in finem. Istud ad omnes pertinet: quoniam teste Joanne, Qui se dicit in Christo manere, debet sicut ille ambulavit, et ipse ambulare. Si vero quod dictum est, Abneget semetipsum, intelligatur sic, ut propriam voluntatem prorsus abjiciat, obedientiam promittendo homini superiori propter Deum, tunc erit consilium.
paras.en: [[16:24|Then Jesus said to his disciples|Tunc Jesus dixit discipulis suis]], and to others too. Hence Luke says: [[Luke 9:23|And he said to all|Dixit autem ad omnes]]. And Mark: [[Mark 8:34|calling the multitude together with his disciples, he said to them|Convocata, inquit, turba cum discipulis suis, dixit ad eos]]. [[16:24|If any man will come after me|Si quis vult post me venire]], that is, follow in My footsteps, be conformed to My virtues, reach perfection, and enter the heavenly fatherland after Me, [[16:24|let him deny himself|abneget semetipsum]], that is, give up his own will, obey God, overcome his desires. This is, according to the Apostle, [[Col 3:9|stripping yourselves of the old man with his deeds|deponere veterem hominem cum actibus suis]], and to [[Eph 4:24|put on the new man, who according to God is created in justice and holiness|induere novum, qui secundum Deum creatus est in sanctitate et justitia]][[Col 3:10||]]. [[16:24|and take up his cross|Et tollat crucem suam]], that is, bear tribulations, adversities and temptations calmly and manfully, mortify himself daily by works of penance, and be ready to suffer every kind of martyrdom for the faith and for justice; as it is written: [[Ps 43:22|for thy sake we are killed all the day long|propter te mortificamur tota die]]. Hence Paul says: [[2 Cor 4:10|Always bearing about in our body the mortification of Jesus, that the life also of Jesus may be made manifest|Semper, inquit, mortificationem Jesu in corpore nostro circumferentes, ut et vita Jesu manifestetur]] [[2 Cor 4:11|in our mortal flesh|in carne nostra mortali]]. He does this who wisely weighs that saying of the Apostle: [[Rom 8:18|the sufferings of this time are not worthy to be compared with the glory to come|Non sunt condignæ passiones hujus temporis ad futuram gloriam]]; and: [[2 Tim 3:12|all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution|Omnes qui volunt pie vivere in Christo, persecutionem patientur]]. [[16:24|and follow me|Et sequatur me]], persevering in good to the end. This belongs to all, since, as John testifies: [[1 John 2:6|He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also to walk even as he walked|Qui se dicit in Christo manere, debet sicut ille ambulavit, et ipse ambulare]]. But if what was said, let him deny himself, is understood to mean that he should cast off his own will entirely by promising obedience to a human superior for God's sake, then it will be a counsel [that is, a counsel of perfection, as distinct from a precept binding all].

paras.t: Qui enim voluerit voluntate perfecta et efficaci, quæ procedit in opus dum potest, animam suam salvam facere, hoc est a damnatione æterna eripere, atque ad veram felicitatem perducere, perdet eam, id est, in præsenti vita eam vitaliter salubriterque occidet, privatum amorem exstirpando, delectabilia hujus vitæ spernendo, et animam propriam propter Christum in omnibus affligendo, vel morti corporali eam exponendo propter justitiam, ita ut cum Apostolo dicere possit: Vivo autem, jam non ego, vivit vero in me Christus, id est, nil ago secundum privatum amorem, sed omnia secundum caritatem divinam, propter vitam æternam. Porro quod iste sit verus ac proprius intellectus hujus scripturæ, innotescit ex eo quod subditur: Qui autem perdiderit animam suam, hoc modo eam despiciendo et affligendo quasi non esset sua, propter me, id est amore mei, et ad hoc ut præmium consequatur a me, inveniet eam, id est, in futuro sæculo ipsam salvam habebit ac feliciter possidebit, juxta illud: E cœlo ista possideo, sed propter Deum nunc ista despicio, quia in futuro ea recipere spero. Ad hoc pertinet quod alibi ait Salvator: Qui odit animam suam in hoc mundo, in vitam æternam custodit eam. Sic ergo debet homo animam suam salubriter perdere propter sui ipsius salutem. Cujus ratio assignatur:
paras.en: [[16:25|For he that will save his life|Qui enim voluerit animam suam salvam facere]]: he that wills it with a perfect and effective will, which goes on to the deed when it can, to save his soul, that is, to snatch it from eternal damnation and bring it to true happiness, [[16:25|shall lose it|perdet eam]], that is, in the present life will put it to death in a life-giving and wholesome way, rooting out self-love, despising the pleasures of this life, afflicting his own soul in all things for Christ's sake, or exposing it to bodily death for justice, so that he can say with the Apostle: [[Gal 2:20|I live, now not I: but Christ liveth in me|Vivo autem, jam non ego, vivit vero in me Christus]], that is, I do nothing according to self-love, but all things according to divine charity, for the sake of eternal life. That this is the true and proper sense of this text is made known from what follows: [[16:25|and he that shall lose his life|Qui autem perdiderit animam suam]], despising and afflicting it in this way as if it were not his own, [[16:25|for my sake|propter me]], that is, for love of Me, and so as to obtain a reward from Me, [[16:25|shall find it|inveniet eam]], that is, in the world to come will have it saved and possess it in happiness, according to that saying: [[2 Mach 7:11|These I have from heaven|E cœlo ista possideo]], but for God's sake I now despise them, because I hope to receive them again in the future. To this belongs what the Saviour says elsewhere: [[John 12:25|he that hateth his life in this world keepeth it unto life eternal|Qui odit animam suam in hoc mundo, in vitam æternam custodit eam]]. So a man ought to lose his soul in a wholesome way, for his own salvation. The reason is given:

paras.t: Quid enim prodest homini, si mundum universum lucretur, omnia temporalia acquirendo, deliciis affluendo, alios sibi subjiciendo, vel etiam aliis prædicando ac proficiendo, animæ vero suæ detrimentum, id est damnationem, casum seu nocumentum in spiritualibus, patiatur per negligentiam propriam, non faciendo quæ docuit? Hoc non solum non proficit, sed plurimum deficit, perdendo bonum spirituale propter corporale, felicitatem æternam propter rem temporalem. Ordo ergo caritatis requirit, ut unusquisque post Deum primo ac maxime amet se ipsum in Deo, et propriæ satagat providere saluti, sciens quoniam unusquisque onus suum portabit, et pro se ipso redditurus est rationem. Verumtamen multi sunt qui docent, et non faciunt, qui aliorum magis quam proprios observant, ponderant, increpantque defectus, qui totum mundum volunt salvare, et tamen palpant se ipsos. Talibus clamat Apostolus: Qui alium doces, te ipsum non doces; qui gloriaris in lege, per prævaricationem legis Deum inhonoras. Aut quam dabit, hoc est, dare poterit, homo commutationem, id est redemptionem seu pretium, pro anima sua, si contigerit eam damnari? Nullam utique. Ideo nil proficit, si totum mundum lucretur, et eam neglexerit. Propter quod ait Psalmista: Non dabit Deo placationem suam, et pretium redemptionis animæ suæ. Job quoque ait: Non credet impius frustra, quod aliquo pretio redimendus sit. Exteriorum vero rerum damna potest homo aliqua commutatione recompensare ac recuperare.
paras.en: [[16:26|For what doth it profit a man, if he gain the whole world|Quid enim prodest homini, si mundum universum lucretur]], by acquiring all temporal things, abounding in delights, subjecting others to himself, or even by preaching to others and doing them good, [[16:26|and suffer the loss of his own soul|animæ vero suæ detrimentum patiatur?]]: loss, that is, damnation, a fall or harm in spiritual things, through his own negligence, by not doing what he taught? This not only profits nothing but is a very great loss, losing spiritual good for bodily, eternal happiness for a temporal thing. The order of charity, then, requires that after God each one should first and most love himself in God, and take pains to provide for his own salvation, knowing that [[Gal 6:5|every one shall bear his own burden|unusquisque onus suum portabit]], and will render account for himself[[Rom 14:12||]]. Yet there are many who teach and do not do[[Matt 23:3||]], who watch, weigh and rebuke the failings of others more than their own, who want to save the whole world and yet flatter themselves. To such the Apostle cries: Thou [[Rom 2:21|that teachest another, teachest not thyself|Qui alium doces, te ipsum non doces]]; [[Rom 2:23|Thou, that makest thy boast of the law, by transgression of the law dishonourest God|qui gloriaris in lege, per prævaricationem legis Deum inhonoras]]. [[16:26|Or what exchange shall a man give for his soul|aut quam dabit homo commutationem pro anima sua?]]: shall give, that is, will be able to give; exchange, that is, redemption or price, for his soul, if it should be damned? None at all. So it profits nothing if he gain the whole world and neglect his soul. Hence the Psalmist says: [[Ps 48:8|he shall not give to God his ransom|Non dabit Deo placationem suam]], [[Ps 48:9|Nor the price of the redemption of his soul|et pretium redemptionis animæ suæ]]. And Job says: [[Job 15:31|He shall not believe, being vainly deceived by error, that he may be redeemed with any price|Non credet impius frustra, quod aliquo pretio redimendus sit]]. But the loss of outward things a man can make good and recover by some exchange.

paras.t: Quod autem homo non possit aliquam commutationem dare pro anima sua, ostenditur ex districtione divini judicii. Filius enim hominis venturus est in die novissimo ad judicium, in gloria Patris sui, id est in majestate et potestate quam habet a Patre, cum angelis suis, qui tunc visibiliter apparebunt, secundum Gregorium; et tunc reddet unicuique secundum opera ejus, id est secundum exigentiam meritorum suorum: per operationem, actum interiorem et exteriorem intelligendo, videlicet cogitationes, affectiones, locutiones et operationes, imo et operum debitorum omissiones, quia et arbor quæ non facit opera bona, excidetur et in ignem mittetur. Multi tamen salvabuntur sine operibus propriis, scilicet pueri baptizati ante discretionis annos defuncti. Loquitur ergo Salvator de adultis et ratione utentibus. Hinc scriptum est in Job: Absit a Deo impietas; opus enim hominis reddet ei, et juxta vias singulorum restituet.
paras.en: That a man cannot give any exchange for his soul is shown from the strictness of the divine judgment. [[16:27|For the Son of man shall come|Filius enim hominis venturus est]] on the last day to judgment, [[16:27|in the glory of his Father|in gloria Patris sui]], that is, in the majesty and power that He has from the Father, [[16:27|with his angels|cum angelis suis]], who will then appear visibly, according to Gregory; [[16:27|and then will he render to every man according to his works|et tunc reddet unicuique secundum opera ejus]], that is, according to what his merits require: understanding by works the inward and outward act, namely thoughts, affections, words and deeds, and indeed the omission of works that were owed, since [[Matt 3:10|Every tree therefore that doth not yield good fruit, shall be cut down, and cast into the fire|arbor quæ non facit opera bona, excidetur et in ignem mittetur]]. Many, however, will be saved without works of their own, namely baptized children who die before the years of discretion; so the Saviour is speaking of adults who have the use of reason. Hence it is written in Job: [[Job 34:10|far from God be wickedness|Absit a Deo impietas]]; [[Job 34:11|For he will render to a man his work, and according to the ways of every one he will reward them|opus enim hominis reddet ei, et juxta vias singulorum restituet]].
