paras.t: Sed quoniam dura erant quæ de Christi passione ejusque imitatione prædicta sunt, et discipuli eis auditis, tremefacti ac desolati fuerunt, idcirco subditur consolatio pia, qua ipsis promittitur visio ejus in præsenti sæculo quod in futuro visuri sunt. Amen dico vobis, sunt quidam de hic stantibus, id est quidam discipulorum meorum, qui non gustabunt mortem, hoc est, morituri non sunt, donec videant Filium hominis venientem in regno suo, id est, ascendentem ad regnum cœleste: quod omnes Apostoli in die ascensionis viderunt. Vel, Venientem in regno suo, id est in Ecclesia militanti, in qua Christus spiritualiter venit per gratiosam inhabitationem et piam subventionem, quando post resurrectionem numerus credentium quotidie mirabiliter augebatur. Adhuc namque viventibus Apostolis, prædicata atque recepta fuit fides per omnes principales partes mundi. Vel, Venientem in regno suo, hoc est, apparentem in tali claritate qualem habebit in regno cœlesti. Talem quippe viderunt eum Petrus, Jacobus et Joannes in transfiguratione. Vel, In regno suo, id est in corpore glorificato, in quo semper regnabit. In illo enim viderunt eum discipuli post resurrectionem, quamvis non apparuerit eis in forma gloriosa.
paras.en: But since what had been said of Christ's Passion and of imitating Him was hard, and the disciples on hearing it were shaken and desolate, a loving consolation is added, in which they are promised a sight in this present world of what they are to see in the world to come. [[16:28|Amen I say to you, there are some of them that stand here|Amen dico vobis, sunt quidam de hic stantibus]], that is, some of My disciples, [[16:28|that shall not taste death|qui non gustabunt mortem]], that is, will not die, [[16:28|till they see the Son of man coming in his kingdom|donec videant Filium hominis venientem in regno suo]], that is, going up to the heavenly kingdom, which all the Apostles saw on the day of the Ascension. Or, coming in His kingdom, that is, in the Church militant, in which Christ comes spiritually by His gracious indwelling and loving help, when after the resurrection the number of believers grew wonderfully day by day[[Acts 5:14||]]. For while the Apostles were still alive the faith was preached and received through all the principal parts of the world. Or, coming in His kingdom, that is, appearing in such brightness as He will have in the heavenly kingdom; for so Peter, James and John saw Him at the Transfiguration. Or, in His kingdom, that is, in His glorified body, in which He will reign for ever; for the disciples saw Him in it after the resurrection, although He did not appear to them in glorious form.

16.note: Art. XXIX begins with Matthew 15:39; that paragraph is shown in chapter 15.

17.title: Explanatio capituli septimidecimi: Et post dies sex, assumpsit Jesus Petrum, et Jacobum, et Joannem fratrem ejus
17.title_en: Explanation of the seventeenth chapter: And after six days Jesus taketh unto him Peter and James, and John his brother

paras.t: Qui id quod in fine præcedentis capituli Christus promisit de visione sui in regno suo, exponunt de visione Christi in forma gloriosa, dicunt quod in hujus capituli exordio ostenditur Christus illam promissionem implesse. Et post dies sex a promissione et sermocinatione in præcedenti capitulo factis, assumpsit Jesus Petrum, et Jacobum, et Joannem fratrem ejus, tanquam familiariores et cariores: qui et resuscitationi puellæ interfuerunt, et nocte passionis a Christo assumpti atque seorsum ducti fuerunt. Quidam sentire videntur, quod Jacobus qui transfigurationi interfuit, fuerit Jacobus primus Jerosolymitarum episcopus, scilicet Jacobus Minor, filius Alphæi. Sed quia hoc loco aperte asseritur quod fuerat Jacobus frater Joannis, simpliciter dicendum quod fuit Jacobus Major, filius Zebedæi, ab Herode occisus. Quandocumque autem doctores catholici aliud asserunt cujus contrarium manifeste habetur in Scriptura canonica, certum est quod dicant hoc, non recolentes nec attendentes quemadmodum Scriptura sacra contineat. Et si eam attendissent, nequaquam sic affirmassent. Unde in talibus non oportet deliberare quid respondeatur. Quæritur, quomodo dicat Matthæus, Post dies sex, assumpsit Jesus, etc., quum Lucas dicat, Post dies fere octo. Respondendum, quod Lucas commemorat diem prædictæ promissionis et diem impletionis, Matthæus vero et Marcus dies intermedios computant. Ideo tres assumpsit, ut in ore trium testium staret hujus transfigurationis testimonium, et propter sanctæ Trinitatis mysterium designandum, et propter ternarii numeri perfectionem. Omnia namque super tria ponimus, secundum Philosophum.
paras.en: Those who explain what Christ promised at the end of the preceding chapter, about the sight of Himself in His kingdom, as the sight of Christ in glorious form, say that at the beginning of this chapter Christ is shown to have fulfilled that promise. [[17:1|And after six days|Et post dies sex]] from the promise and discourse given in the preceding chapter, [[17:1|Jesus taketh unto him Peter and James, and John his brother|assumpsit Jesus Petrum, et Jacobum, et Joannem fratrem ejus]], as the more intimate and dearer ones, who were also present at the raising of the girl[[Mark 5:37||]], and on the night of the Passion were taken by Christ and led apart[[Matt 26:37||]]. Some seem to think that the James who was present at the Transfiguration was James the first bishop of Jerusalem, that is, James the Less, son of Alpheus. But since it is plainly asserted here that it was James the brother of John, it must simply be said that it was James the Greater, son of Zebedee, who was killed by Herod[[Acts 12:2||]]. Whenever Catholic doctors assert something whose contrary is plainly found in canonical Scripture, it is certain that they say it without recalling or attending to what holy Scripture contains; had they attended to it, they would never have affirmed it so. So in such matters there is no need to deliberate over what answer to give. It is asked how Matthew says, after six days Jesus taketh unto him, etc., when Luke says, [[Luke 9:28|about eight days after|Post dies fere octo]]. The answer is that Luke counts the day of the promise and the day of its fulfilment, while Matthew and Mark[[Mark 9:1||]] count the days in between. He took three, so that the testimony of this Transfiguration might stand in the mouth of three witnesses[[Deut 19:15||]], to signify the mystery of the holy Trinity, and because of the perfection of the number three: for, according to the Philosopher [Aristotle], we set all things upon three.

paras.t: Et duxit illos in montem excelsum, videlicet in montem Thabor, seorsum ab aliis discipulis; et transfiguratus, hoc est in splendidiorem formam seu gloriosiorem figuram ac qualitatem mutatus, est ante eos, videlicet in conspectu eorum, quibus ostendere voluit gloriam quam ipse post resurrectionem fuerat habiturus, et quam dabit in resurrectione futura suis electis. In hac transfiguratione Christi, nec substantia suæ humanitatis, nec quantitas sui corporis est mutata; sed qualitas dignior seu claritas admiranda superinducta est corpori.
paras.en: [[17:1|and bringeth them up into a high mountain apart|Et duxit illos in montem excelsum, videlicet in montem Thabor, seorsum]]: namely Mount Thabor, apart from the other disciples; [[17:2|And he was transfigured before them|et transfiguratus est ante eos]]: transfigured, that is, changed into a more splendid form, or a more glorious shape and quality; before them, that is, in their sight, to whom He wished to show the glory that He was to have after the resurrection, and which He will give His elect in the resurrection to come. In this Transfiguration of Christ neither the substance of His humanity nor the size of His body was changed; but a nobler quality, or a wonderful brightness, was brought upon His body.

paras.t: Et resplenduit facies ejus sicut sol. Si illa claritas tanta fuit, quanta post resurrectionem erit, dubium nullum est quin facies ejus incomparabiliter clarior fuerit sole, præsertim quum de ceteris scriptum sit, quia fulgebunt sicut sol in regno Patris sui. Denique, secundum commune dictum doctorum, in resurrectione futura dotes corporum glorificatorum erunt ex redundantia beatitudinis animarum in corpora: quod intelligendum videtur per modum causæ meritoriæ, non effective ex parte animarum. Anima autem Christi in primo instanti suæ creationis ac unionis cum Verbo, erat vere ac fruitive beata. Idcirco, nisi ex divinæ dispensationis moderamine retracta atque dilata fuisset redundantia beatitudinis animæ ejus in sacratissimum corpus ipsius, omnes quatuor dotes corporis gloriosi fuissent in corpore Christi a primo suæ formationis instanti; sed fuit dispensative dilata. Aliquando tamen fuit permissa, scilicet in transfiguratione. Porro, secundum Hugonem, Christus ante passionem successive seu diversis temporibus assumpsit quatuor corporis dotes, videlicet: subtilitatem in nativitate, egrediendo de clauso dulcissimæ Virginis utero; agilitatem, ambulando super aquarum fluenta; claritatem, in transfiguratione; impassibilitatem, in consecratione seu porrectione corporis sui in Cœna. Alii tamen communiter tenent oppositum, maxime quantum ad dotem impassibilitatis tempore Cœnæ. Tale enim corpus dedit Apostolis, quale tunc habuit. Et quum de ratione dotis sit, ut habeatur et insit per modum qualitatis fixæ ac permanentis, non transeuntis; propterea claritas ista, licet secundum essentiam fuerit ejusdem rationis cum claritate quæ ponitur dos, tamen non habuit ibi modum rationemque dotis, quia non inerat permanenter.
paras.en: [[17:2|And his face did shine as the sun|Et resplenduit facies ejus sicut sol]]. If that brightness was as great as it will be after the resurrection, there is no doubt that His face was incomparably brighter than the sun, especially since it is written of the others that they [[Matt 13:43|shall the just shine as the sun, in the kingdom of their Father|fulgebunt sicut sol in regno Patris sui]]. Further, according to the common teaching of the doctors, in the resurrection to come the endowments of glorified bodies [the four dotes: brightness, impassibility, agility and subtlety] will come from the overflow of the souls' blessedness into the bodies: which seems to be understood by way of meritorious cause, not of efficient cause on the part of the souls. Now the soul of Christ, in the first instant of its creation and union with the Word, was truly blessed and enjoyed God. Therefore, had not the overflow of His soul's blessedness into His most sacred body been held back and delayed by the governance of the divine dispensation, all four endowments of the glorious body would have been in Christ's body from the first instant of its formation; but it was delayed by dispensation. At times, however, it was allowed, namely in the Transfiguration. Further, according to Hugh, Christ before the Passion took on the four endowments of the body one after another, at different times: subtlety at His birth, in coming forth from the closed womb of the most sweet Virgin; agility, in walking on the waters; brightness, in the Transfiguration; impassibility, in consecrating or handing over His body at the Supper. Others, however, commonly hold the opposite, especially as regards the endowment of impassibility at the time of the Supper; for He gave the Apostles such a body as He then had. And since it belongs to the nature of an endowment that it is had and is present after the manner of a fixed and permanent quality, not a passing one, this brightness, although in essence it was of the same kind as the brightness that counts as an endowment, nevertheless did not have the manner and nature of an endowment there, because it was not present permanently.

paras.t: Vestimenta autem ejus facta sunt alba sicut nix. De modo hujus albefactionis dubitatio est. Augustinus enim videtur asserere, quod claritas seu albedo apparens in vestibus, non erat subjective in eis, sed ex illustratione aeris candida apparebant ac alba, quemadmodum ea pars cœli cui sol est vicinior. Verumtamen satis probabile est, quod ad declarandam futuram glorificationem corporum electorum in se et in mansionibus suis, etiam vestimenta Christi fuerunt veraciter immutata et clarificata: quod et Scripturis magis consonare censetur. Scribitur namque in Marco: Vestimenta ejus facta sunt splendentia et candida nimis velut nix, qualia fullo super terram non potest candida facere. Et Lucas: Vestitus (inquit) ejus factus est albus refulgens. Hoc quoque sentit Hieronymus, si verba ejus bene pensentur. Ait enim, quod in transfiguratione non est substantia mutata, sed splendor vultui additus. Quod probat eo quod substantia vestium non sit mutata, quæ tamen splendidæ factæ fuerunt. Clarum est autem, quod argumentatio ista nulla esset, nisi et vestes vere clarificatæ fuissent. Hoc quoque sciendum, quod licet Lucas dicat quod species vultus Christi facta sit altera, non tamen sic intelligendum est, quasi sola facies sit clarificata, sed tota caro, quemadmodum in resurrectione futurum est.
paras.en: [[17:2|and his garments became white as snow|Vestimenta autem ejus facta sunt alba sicut nix]]. There is doubt about the manner of this whitening. For Augustine seems to assert that the brightness or whiteness appearing in the garments was not in them as in its subject, but that they appeared bright and white from the lighting up of the air, as does the part of the sky nearest the sun. Yet it is quite probable that, to show forth the future glorification of the bodies of the elect in themselves and in their dwellings, Christ's garments too were truly changed and made bright; and this is judged to agree better with the Scriptures. For it is written in Mark: [[Mark 9:2|his garments became shining and exceeding white as snow|Vestimenta ejus facta sunt splendentia et candida nimis velut nix]], [[Mark 9:2|so as no fuller upon earth can make white|qualia fullo super terram non potest candida facere]]. And Luke: [[Luke 9:29|his raiment|Vestitus]] (he says) [[Luke 9:29|became white and glittering|factus est albus refulgens]]. Jerome too holds this, if his words are weighed well. For he says that in the Transfiguration the substance was not changed, but splendour was added to the countenance; and he proves this by the fact that the substance of the garments was not changed, though they were made shining. It is clear, however, that this argument would be worthless unless the garments too had truly been made bright. This also should be known: although Luke says that [[Luke 9:29|the shape of his countenance was altered|species vultus Christi facta sit altera]], it is not to be understood as if the face alone were made bright, but the whole flesh, as will be in the resurrection.

paras.t: Et ecce, res valde notabilis, nam apparuerunt eis, videlicet Petro, Jacobo et Joanni, Moyses et Elias. Hi præ ceteris cum Christo adfuerunt: Primo, ut per Moysen vere defunctum et Eliam nondum mortuum, ostenderetur Christus judex ac Dominus vivorum et mortuorum. Secundo, propter specialem conformitatem eorum cum Christo: nam sicut Moyses veteris, sic Christus novæ legis est collator, et Elias secundum ejus præcurret adventum. Tertio, ad designandum Christi perfectionem. Per Moysen nempe, qui mansuetus erat præ omnibus hominibus habitantibus super terram, et Eliam rigorosissimum, qui surrexit velut ignis, et maximus divini honoris ac legis exstitit æmulator, significatur quod Christus simul mitissimus atque justissimus fuit, et in tantum zelatus est pro Patris honore, ut transgressores constantissime increparet, et propter Patrem glorificandum pro hominum salute vitam suam exponeret morti. Quarto, propter eminentiam dignitatis ac miraculorum et sanctitatis Moysis et Eliæ. Quinto, ut ostendatur Christus non esse legis solutor, sed impletor, et Prophetarum verificator: cujus oppositum imposuerunt ei Judæi. Insuper Moyses et Elias vere et personaliter aderant, non secundum similitudinem quamdam, vel angeli in forma eorum, ut aliqui dicunt. De Moyse enim aliqui dicunt, quod surrexit ad horam, apparens in proprio corpore: quod videtur esse de mente Hieronymi, qui ait quod Moyses resurrexit ab inferis. Alii probabiliter dicunt, quod apparuit in corpore assumpto et sibi adaptato, eo modo quo angeli. De Elia vero certum est, quod divina virtute, forsan angelico ministerio, adductus sit de paradiso terrestri sicut subsistit, in anima et corpore. Tamen uterque eorum apparuit tunc in magna claritate, et ampliori quam Elias ante vel postea habuit. Unde Lucas ait, quod apparuerunt cum Christo in majestate. Cum eo loquentes. Sermocinationis illius materiam exprimit Lucas: Et dicebant excessum quem completurus erat in Jerusalem: id est, de Christi passione loquebantur, cum Christo gratias referendo, et pro mundi salute orando, de Judæorum quoque perversitate dolendo ac admirando. Dicitur autem passio Christi excessus, propter ejus excessivum dolorem, et quia ex amore excessivo ad nos pati dignatus est, vel propter excessivam impietatem Judæorum in eum.
paras.en: [[17:3|And behold|Et ecce]], a very remarkable thing, [[17:3|there appeared to them Moses and Elias|apparuerunt eis, videlicet Petro, Jacobo et Joanni, Moyses et Elias]], to Peter, James and John, that is. These two were present with Christ rather than others: first, so that by Moses, who had truly died, and Elias, who has not yet died, Christ might be shown to be the judge and Lord of the living and the dead[[Acts 10:42||]]. Second, because of their special likeness to Christ: for as Moses was the giver of the old law, so Christ is of the new, and Elias will go before His second coming[[Mal 4:5||]]. Third, to signify Christ's perfection. For by Moses, who was [[Num 12:3|exceeding meek above all men that dwelt upon earth|mansuetus erat præ omnibus hominibus habitantibus super terram]], and by Elias, most severe, who [[Ecclus 48:1|stood up, as a fire|surrexit velut ignis]] and was the greatest zealot for God's honour and law[[3 Kings 19:10||]][[1 Mach 2:58||]], it is signified that Christ was at once most gentle and most just, and so zealous for His Father's honour that He rebuked transgressors most steadfastly, and to glorify the Father exposed His life to death for the salvation of men. Fourth, because of the eminence of the dignity, the miracles and the holiness of Moses and Elias. Fifth, to show that Christ is not the destroyer of the law but its fulfiller, and the one who makes the Prophets true, the opposite of which the Jews charged Him with. Moreover, Moses and Elias were truly present in person, not in some likeness, nor were they angels in their form, as some say. Of Moses some say that he rose for the hour, appearing in his own body: which seems to be Jerome's mind, who says that Moses rose from the underworld. Others say, with probability, that he appeared in a body assumed and fitted to him, in the way angels do. Of Elias it is certain that by divine power, perhaps through the ministry of angels, he was brought from the earthly paradise as he exists, in soul and body. Yet both of them then appeared in great brightness, greater than Elias had before or afterwards. Hence Luke says that they appeared with Christ [[Luke 9:31|in majesty|in majestate]]. [[17:3|talking with him|Cum eo loquentes]]. Luke states the matter of that conversation: [[Luke 9:31|they spoke of his decease that he should accomplish in Jerusalem|dicebant excessum quem completurus erat in Jerusalem]], that is, they spoke of Christ's Passion, giving thanks with Christ and praying for the salvation of the world, and grieving and marvelling at the perversity of the Jews. Christ's Passion is called a "decease" [Latin excessus, "going out", also "excess"] because of its excessive pain, and because out of excessive love for us He deigned to suffer, or because of the excessive impiety of the Jews towards Him.

paras.t: Respondens autem Petrus, qui verba Moysis et Eliæ audivit de Christi passione, ut aliqui dicunt. Tamen Lucas habet, quod Petrus et qui cum eo erant, somno erant gravati: et antequam Lucas describit evigilationem eorum, recitat de collocutione Christi, Moysis atque Eliæ. Unde certum non habeo, an colloquentium verba audierit: quæ tamen postea eum cognovisse ex revelatione certissimum est. Dixit ad Jesum: Domine, bonum, id est delectabile et honestum, est nos, videlicet te, Moysen, Eliam, et nos tuos discipulos, hic esse, videlicet in monte, ut videamus te in tanta majestate et gloria, Moysen quoque et Eliam excellentissimos viros in tanto decore. Si vis. Reverenter et sobrie loquitur Petrus, quantum ad hoc quod defert Domino suo, non absolute, sed conditionaliter loquens, quia inferior suam semper debet voluntatem subjicere beneplacito domini sui in licitis et honestis. Unde et Christus in passione oravit: Pater, si vis (inquiens) transfer calicem istum a me. Faciamus hic tria tabernacula, id est habitacula in quibus stabiliter perseveremus. Forte talia tabernacula voluit facere, qualia habebantur in veteri Testamento, videlicet de frondibus atque tentoriis, quæ facile fiunt. Tibi unum, Moysi unum, et Eliæ unum. Quare non dixit, Faciamus hic sex tabernacula? Forte ideo, quia putavit in illis tribus tabernaculis se et duos condiscipulos suos recipi posse ac commorari: sic tamen, ut ipse esset in tabernaculo sui magistri carissimi. Secundum Lucam et Marcum, Petrus hæc dixit, nesciens quid diceret: quia præ excessiva dilectione, dulcedine et devotione in Christum, loquebatur quasi in ecstasi, et sine consideratione considerandorum. Nihilominus, secundum Marcum, causa hujus nescientiæ, fuit nimius timor ex insolito visu. Timor autem immoderatus impedit valde usum rationis et linguæ, juxta illud Job: Auferat Dominus a me virgam suam, et pavor ejus non me terreat; neque enim possum metuens respondere. Nihilominus ordinata tristitia, vel non multum excessiva, confert ad veritatis contemplationem, in quantum dissolutionem, vanitatem, et inconsideratam libertatem aufert. Propter quod Isaias inquit: Domine, in angustia requisierunt te, in tribulatione murmuris doctrina tua eis. Secundum Hieronymum, Petrus hæc dicens erravit. Primo enim errasse videtur, quod in contemplatione humanitatis Christi voluit contentari sive quiescere, quum tamen beatitudo in divinitatis suæ contemplatione essentialiter sita sit, quam tunc Petrus non vidit. Secundo, quod in terra et non potius in cœlo, locum mansionis quæsivit, quum tamen dicat Apostolus: Non habemus hic manentem civitatem, sed futuram inquirimus. Tertio, quod aliorum discipulorum oblivisci videbatur, et de præsentium contentari salute. Sed utique, si Petrus voluit ibi ad tempus cum Christo sic transfigurato commorari, non penitus errasse dicendus est.
paras.en: [[17:4|And Peter answering|Respondens autem Petrus]], who heard the words of Moses and Elias about Christ's Passion, as some say. Yet Luke has it that [[Luke 9:32|Peter and they that were with him were heavy with sleep|Petrus et qui cum eo erant, somno erant gravati]], and before Luke describes their waking he tells of the conversation of Christ, Moses and Elias. So I do not hold it as certain whether he heard the words of those talking together; that he afterwards knew them by revelation is quite certain. [[17:4|said to Jesus: Lord, it is good|Dixit ad Jesum: Domine, bonum]], that is, delightful and fitting, [[17:4|for us|est nos]], namely You, Moses, Elias and us Your disciples, [[17:4|to be here|hic esse]], namely on the mountain, so that we may see You in such majesty and glory, and Moses and Elias, most excellent men, in such splendour. [[17:4|if thou wilt|Si vis]]. Peter speaks reverently and soberly, deferring to his Lord, speaking not absolutely but conditionally, because an inferior ought always to submit his will to the good pleasure of his lord in lawful and honourable things. Hence Christ too prayed in His Passion: [[Luke 22:42|Father, if thou wilt, remove this chalice from me|Pater, si vis (inquiens) transfer calicem istum a me]]. [[17:4|let us make here three tabernacles|Faciamus hic tria tabernacula]], that is, dwellings in which we may stay for good. Perhaps he wanted to make such tabernacles as there were in the Old Testament, of branches and coverings, which are easily made[[Lev 23:40||]]. [[17:4|one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias|Tibi unum, Moysi unum, et Eliæ unum]]. Why did he not say, Let us make six tabernacles here? Perhaps because he thought that he and his two fellow disciples could be received and stay in those three tabernacles: in such a way, however, that he himself would be in the tabernacle of his dearest Master. According to Luke and Mark, Peter said this [[Luke 9:33|not knowing what he said|nesciens quid diceret]]: for out of excessive love, sweetness and devotion towards Christ he spoke as if in ecstasy, without considering what should be considered. Yet according to Mark the cause of this not knowing was excessive fear at the unaccustomed sight[[Mark 9:5||]]. And immoderate fear greatly hinders the use of reason and of the tongue, according to that saying of Job: [[Job 9:34|Let him take his rod away from me, and let not his fear terrify me|Auferat Dominus a me virgam suam, et pavor ejus non me terreat]]; [[Job 9:35|for I cannot answer while I am in fear|neque enim possum metuens respondere]]. Yet an ordered sadness, or one not very excessive, helps the contemplation of truth, inasmuch as it removes dissipation, vanity and thoughtless licence. Hence Isaias says: [[Is 26:16|Lord, they have sought after thee in distress, in the tribulation of murmuring thy instruction was with them|Domine, in angustia requisierunt te, in tribulatione murmuris doctrina tua eis]]. According to Jerome, Peter erred in saying this. First, he seems to have erred in wishing to be content or to rest in contemplating Christ's humanity, whereas blessedness lies essentially in the contemplation of His divinity, which Peter did not then see. Second, in seeking a place to dwell on earth rather than in heaven, whereas the Apostle says: [[Heb 13:14|we have not here a lasting city: but we seek one that is to come|Non habemus hic manentem civitatem, sed futuram inquirimus]]. Third, in seeming to forget the other disciples and to be content with the salvation of those present. But surely, if Peter wished to stay there for a time with Christ thus transfigured, he is not to be said to have erred altogether.

paras.t: Adhuc eo, videlicet Petro, loquente verba prædicta, ecce nubes lucida, id est pulchra et clara, non ex grossis vaporibus causata, sed talis, qualis recepit Jesum in hora ascensionis ab oculis discipulorum, ut in Actibus legitur; obumbravit, id est, temperanter operuit eos. Difficile forte apparet ad quos referendum sit hoc. Immediate enim de Christo, Moyse et Elia facta est mentio, sicque videtur obumbratio ista referenda ad eos. Verumtamen, si ea quæ Lucas scribit diligenter pensemus, invenimus Moysen et Eliam ante nubis apparitionem recessisse: nam ibi habetur, quod quum Moyses et Elias discederent, Petrus dixit: Bonum est nos hic esse. Nubes ergo obumbravit eos, id est Petrum, Jacobum et Joannem, ne oculi eorum claritate corporis Christi omnino repercuterentur et obtunderentur. Et ecce vox Patris de nube sonuit, dicens: Hic est Filius meus dilectus, in quo mihi bene complacui. Hoc ipsum supra scriptum ac diligenter expositum est. Ipsum audite auribus cordis et corporis, quoniam ipse est veritas infallibilis, sapientia increata, magister perfectus, doctor salvificus, qui ait: Qui audit verba mea, et credit ei qui misit me, habet vitam æternam. Hunc magistrum esse audiendum, prænuntiavit Moyses in Deuteronomio: Prophetam, inquiens, suscitabit vobis Dominus tanquam me; ipsum audietis; et erit, omnis qui non audierit verba Prophetæ illius, exterminabitur de populo suo. Denique similis apparitio et testificatio factæ sunt in Christi baptismo ac transfiguratione. Utrobique namque ostensa est Trinitas superbenedicta, videlicet: Pater, in voce, quæ angelico ministerio creditur formata; Filius, in humanitate; Spiritus Sanctus, ibi in specie columbæ, hic autem in nube. Quemadmodum enim Spiritus Sanctus per columbam designatur propter simplicitatem et innocentiam ceterasque bonas proprietates columbæ; sic figuratur per nubem: quia, ut nubes refrigerat et defendit a solis calore, sic Spiritus Sanctus ab igne concupiscentiæ et omnium tentationum fervore. Propter quod in Isaia per nubem exprimitur gratia Spiritus Sancti, quum dicitur: Creabit Dominus super omnem locum montis Sion, et ubi invocatus est, nubem per diem. Quum ergo Christus sit nobis causa gratiæ in præsenti, et gloriæ in futuro, idcirco in ejus baptismo et transfiguratione apparuit Trinitas. Et Pater de Filio testimonium protulit, quia baptismus Christi fuit figura et causa nostræ regenerationis, qua in præsenti renascimur gratiam acquirendo, ejusque transfiguratio figura fuit nostræ glorificationis in futuro. Unde per nubem lucidam hic apparentem, intelligi potest claritas visionis divinæ, qua electi ab omni adversitate tutantur, juxta illud Apocalypsis et Isaiæ: Non esurient neque sitient amplius, et non percutiet eos æstus et sol.
paras.en: [[17:5|And as he was yet speaking|Adhuc eo, videlicet Petro, loquente]], Peter, that is, the words just given, [[17:5|behold a bright cloud|ecce nubes lucida]], that is, fair and clear, not caused by thick vapours, but such as [[Acts 1:9|a cloud received him out of their sight|recepit Jesum in hora ascensionis ab oculis discipulorum]] at the hour of the Ascension, as we read in the Acts, [[17:5|overshadowed them|obumbravit eos]], that is, covered them gently. It is perhaps hard to see to whom this is to be referred. For Christ, Moses and Elias have just been mentioned, and so it seems this overshadowing is to be referred to them. Yet if we weigh carefully what Luke writes, we find that Moses and Elias had withdrawn before the cloud appeared: for there it is said that as Moses and Elias were departing, Peter said: It is good for us to be here[[Luke 9:33||]]. So the cloud overshadowed them, that is, Peter, James and John, lest their eyes should be wholly struck and dazzled by the brightness of Christ's body. [[17:5|And lo a voice out of the cloud, saying: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased|Et ecce vox … de nube … dicens: Hic est Filius meus dilectus, in quo mihi bene complacui]]: the voice of the Father sounded. This was written and carefully explained above[[Matt 3:17||]]. [[17:5|hear ye him|Ipsum audite]] with the ears of the heart and of the body, since He is infallible truth, uncreated wisdom, the perfect master, the saving teacher, who says: [[John 5:24|he who heareth my word and believeth him that sent me hath life everlasting|Qui audit verba mea, et credit ei qui misit me, habet vitam æternam]]. That this Master was to be heard Moses foretold in Deuteronomy: A Prophet the Lord will raise up to you like me; [[Deut 18:15|him thou shalt hear|ipsum audietis]][[Deut 18:19||]]; and [[Acts 3:23|it shall be, that every soul which will not hear that prophet shall be destroyed from among the people|erit, omnis qui non audierit verba Prophetæ illius, exterminabitur de populo suo]][[Acts 3:22||]] [Denis's words are closer to St Peter's quotation of Moses in the Acts, which the margin also cites]. Further, a like appearance and testimony took place at Christ's baptism and at His Transfiguration[[Matt 3:16||]]. For in both the most blessed Trinity was shown: the Father in the voice, which is believed to have been formed by the ministry of angels; the Son in His humanity; the Holy Ghost, there in the form of a dove, here in the cloud. For as the Holy Ghost is signified by the dove because of the simplicity, innocence and other good properties of the dove, so He is figured by the cloud: because, as a cloud cools and shields from the heat of the sun, so the Holy Ghost shields from the fire of concupiscence and the heat of all temptations. Hence in Isaias the grace of the Holy Ghost is expressed by a cloud, when it is said: [[Is 4:5|the Lord will create upon every place of mount Sion, and where he is called upon, a cloud by day|Creabit Dominus super omnem locum montis Sion, et ubi invocatus est, nubem per diem]]. Since, then, Christ is for us the cause of grace in the present and of glory in the future, the Trinity appeared at His baptism and Transfiguration. And the Father bore witness to the Son, because Christ's baptism was the figure and cause of our regeneration, by which we are reborn in the present by receiving grace, and His Transfiguration was the figure of our glorification in the future. So by the bright cloud appearing here can be understood the brightness of the divine vision, by which the elect are protected from all adversity, according to that saying of the Apocalypse and of Isaias: [[Apoc 7:16|They shall no more hunger nor thirst|Non esurient neque sitient amplius]], [[Is 49:10|neither shall the heat nor the sun strike them|non percutiet eos æstus et sol]].

paras.t: Et audientes discipuli vocem quam Deus majestatis de nube intonuit, ceciderunt in faciem suam; more Prophetarum, qui frequenter corruisse leguntur, auditis sermonibus revelationis divinæ; et timuerunt valde: quia hoc naturale est, ut homo propter suæ naturæ fragilitatem terreatur, auditis divinæ majestatis sermonibus. Hinc in Exodo filii Israel dicunt ad Moysen: Loquere tu nobis, et audiemus: non loquatur nobis Dominus, ne forte moriamur. Et in Deuteronomio habetur: Quid est omnis caro, ut audiat vocem Domini Dei viventis? Et accessit Jesus, et tetigit eos, Moyse et Elia jam ad loca sua unde adducti erant reversis; dixitque eis: Surgite, non solum a terra, sed et a pristina imperfectione, et nolite timere, inordinato pavore propter vocem cœlestem, sed potius de vestræ fidei certificatione, et mea dignitate vobis jam revelata, gaudete: sicut Daniel et Ezechiel tactu angelico se levatos et confortatos fuisse testantur. Levantes autem oculos suos Apostoli, neminem viderunt, nisi solum Jesum. Abierant etenim Moyses et Elias ante prædicta, ne vel ab eis vel ad aliquem eorum crederetur vox facta de nube.
paras.en: [[17:6|And the disciples hearing|Et audientes discipuli]] the voice which the God of majesty thundered from the cloud, [[17:6|fell upon their face|ceciderunt in faciem suam]], after the manner of the Prophets, who are often read to have fallen down on hearing the words of divine revelation[[Is 21:3||]][[Ezech 2:1||]][[Dan 8:17||]]; [[17:6|and were very much afraid|et timuerunt valde]]: for it is natural that man, because of the frailty of his nature, should be terrified on hearing the words of the divine majesty. Hence in Exodus the children of Israel say to Moses: [[Ex 20:19|Speak thou to us, and we will hear: let not the Lord speak to us, lest we die|Loquere tu nobis, et audiemus: non loquatur nobis Dominus, ne forte moriamur]]. And in Deuteronomy we have: [[Deut 5:26|What is all flesh, that it should hear the voice of the living God|Quid est omnis caro, ut audiat vocem Domini Dei viventis]]? [[17:7|And Jesus came and touched them|Et accessit Jesus, et tetigit eos]], Moses and Elias having now gone back to the places from which they had been brought; [[17:7|and said to them: Arise|dixitque eis: Surgite]], not only from the ground but from your former imperfection, [[17:7|and fear not|et nolite timere]] with a disordered dread because of the heavenly voice, but rather rejoice at the confirming of your faith and at My dignity now revealed to you: as Daniel and Ezechiel testify that they were raised up and strengthened by the touch of an angel[[Dan 8:18||]][[Ezech 2:2||]]. [[17:8|And they lifting up their eyes, saw no one, but only Jesus|Levantes autem oculos suos Apostoli, neminem viderunt, nisi solum Jesum]], the Apostles. For Moses and Elias had gone away before this, lest the voice from the cloud should be believed to come from them or to be addressed to either of them.

paras.t: Et descendentibus illis de monte, præcepit eis Jesus, dicens: Nemini dixeritis visionem, id est id quod jam in monte vidistis, donec Filius hominis a mortuis resurgat. Hoc Christus præcepit: primo, ut doceat nos occultare propriam excellentiam, quousque in præsenti vivimus sæculo; secundo, ne res illa propter suam magnitudinem putaretur incredibilis; tertio, ne tempore passionis graviter scandalizarentur, qui ante ædificari poterant ex transfigurationis revelatione.
paras.en: [[17:9|And as they came down from the mountain, Jesus charged them, saying: Tell the vision to no man|Et descendentibus illis de monte, præcepit eis Jesus, dicens: Nemini dixeritis visionem]], that is, what you have now seen on the mountain, [[17:9|till the Son of man be risen from the dead|donec Filius hominis a mortuis resurgat]]. Christ commanded this: first, to teach us to hide our own excellence as long as we live in this present world; second, lest that thing, because of its greatness, should be thought incredible; third, lest at the time of the Passion those should be gravely scandalized who before could be edified by the revelation of the Transfiguration.

paras.t: Et interrogaverunt eum discipuli, dicentes: Quid ergo Scribæ dicunt, quod Eliam oportet primum venire? id est: Si transfiguratio ista glorificatio tua est, quomodo dicunt doctores Judæorum, quod Elias venturus est primum, id est, antequam appareas in gloria? Noverant Scribæ ex testimonio Malachiæ, quod Elias præcedet secundum Christi adventum, seu diem judicii, in quo Christus gloriosus omnibus monstrabitur. Quoniam ergo prædicti tres Apostoli transfigurationem Christi quam viderant, putabant esse gloriam in qua ad judicandum venturus est, ita quod transfiguratio illa esset indicium consummationis mundi atque extremi judicii de proximo imminentis, ideo sciscitabantur Christum qualiter intelligenda esset Scribarum assertio de adventu Eliæ ante diem judicii. Viderant quippe Eliam, sed mirabantur quod tam subito abiit, quem Scribæ testantur manifeste venturum et prædicaturum Judæis. Interrogatio igitur Apostolorum ex quodam errore procedit, quia putabant instare diem judicii, finemque sæculi. Christus tamen clementer instruit eos, sicut subjungitur.
paras.en: [[17:10|And his disciples asked him, saying: Why then do the scribes say that Elias must come first|Et interrogaverunt eum discipuli, dicentes: Quid ergo Scribæ dicunt, quod Eliam oportet primum venire]]? That is: if this Transfiguration is Your glorification, how is it that the teachers of the Jews say that Elias is to come first, that is, before You appear in glory? The scribes knew from the testimony of Malachias[[Mal 4:5||]] that Elias will go before Christ's second coming, or the day of judgment, on which Christ will be shown to all in glory. Since, then, these three Apostles thought that the Transfiguration of Christ which they had seen was the glory in which He is to come to judge, so that it was a sign that the end of the world and the last judgment were close at hand, they asked Christ how the scribes' assertion about the coming of Elias before the day of judgment was to be understood. For they had seen Elias, but they wondered that he had gone away so suddenly, he whom the scribes declare will come openly and preach to the Jews. The Apostles' question, then, comes from a certain error, since they thought that the day of judgment and the end of the world were at hand. Yet Christ kindly instructs them, as follows.

paras.t: At ille respondens, ait illis, videlicet Petro, Jacobo et Joanni: Elias quidem venturus est, quemadmodum Scribæ affirmant, quia secundum meum præcurret adventum, sicut Joannes primum, et restituet omnia, id est, totum genus Judæorum reducet ad Deum, convertendo eos ad Christum. Aperiet namque Antichristi mendacia: quo facto Judæi fidem recipient. Unde in Malachia legitur: Convertet cor patrum ad filios, et cor filiorum ad patres. Sic ergo ait Salvator, Elias restituet omnia, quomodo alibi de se profitetur, Si exaltatus fuero, omnia traham ad me ipsum. Elias autem minister erit restitutionis illius, non actor principalis, sed instrumentalis. Dico autem vobis, quia Elias jam venit, non personaliter, sed æquivalenter, videlicet alius in virtute et spiritu ejus, et non cognoverunt eum Judæi increduli, scilicet Scribæ, sacerdotes ac Pharisæi, dicentes de Joanne, quia dæmonium habet. Et quamvis Herodes et alii quidam maligni aliqualiter Joannem noverunt (sciebat enim Herodes, quod esset vir justus et sanctus), dicuntur tamen eum non cognovisse: primo, quoniam nescierunt quod esset Christi præcursor; secundo, quoniam documenta et opera ejus finaliter reprobaverunt. Sed fecerunt in eum quæcumque voluerunt, id est, multipliciter persecuti sunt ipsum. Nam et Herodes de consensu, et forsan consilio, Scribarum, Pharisæorum ac sacerdotum, Joannem incarceravit et decollavit. Sic et Filius hominis passurus est ab eis supplicium crucis: quia in passione idem Herodes sprevit Christum, albaque veste illusum reddidit voluntati Pilati, qui tandem procurantibus Judæis crucifixit Christum. Denique Christus loquitur de diversis injustis generaliter, quasi de eisdem, secundum quod una ponitur generatio omnium reproborum, cui ait Salvator: Venient hæc omnia, scilicet omnis sanguis innocenter effusus, super generationem istam. Tunc intellexerunt discipuli tres prædicti, quia de Joanne Baptista dixisset eis illa quæ de præterito Eliæ adventu narravit, per Eliam intelligendo ac designando Joannem, propter proprietatum similitudinem, non propter personæ unitatem. Nam et Joannes a Judæis interrogatus, Elias es tu? respondit, Non.
paras.en: [[17:11|But he answering, said to them|At ille respondens, ait illis]], to Peter, James and John, that is: [[17:11|Elias indeed shall come|Elias quidem venturus est]], as the scribes affirm, for he will go before My second coming, as John did before the first, [[17:11|and restore all things|et restituet omnia]], that is, will bring the whole Jewish race back to God by converting them to Christ. For he will lay bare the lies of Antichrist, and when this is done the Jews will receive the faith. Hence we read in Malachias: [[Mal 4:6|he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers|Convertet cor patrum ad filios, et cor filiorum ad patres]]. So the Saviour says, Elias shall restore all things, in the way that He says of Himself elsewhere: If I be lifted up, [[John 12:32|will draw all things to myself|omnia traham ad me ipsum]]. Elias will be the minister of that restoring, not its principal agent but an instrument. [[17:12|But I say to you, that Elias is already come|Dico autem vobis, quia Elias jam venit]], not in person, but in equivalent, namely another in his power and spirit, [[17:12|and they knew him not|et non cognoverunt eum]], the unbelieving Jews, namely the scribes, priests and Pharisees, who said of John, [[Matt 11:18|He hath a devil|dæmonium habet]]. And although Herod and some other wicked men knew John in some way (for Herod knew that he was a just and holy man[[Mark 6:20||]]), they are nevertheless said not to have known him: first, because they did not know that he was the forerunner of Christ; second, because in the end they rejected his teaching and works. [[17:12|But have done unto him whatsoever they had a mind|Sed fecerunt in eum quæcumque voluerunt]], that is, persecuted him in many ways. For Herod, with the consent and perhaps on the advice of the scribes, Pharisees and priests, imprisoned and beheaded John. [[17:12|So also the Son of man shall suffer from them|Sic et Filius hominis passurus est ab eis]] the punishment of the cross: for in the Passion the same Herod set Christ at nought and, having mocked Him with a white garment, gave Him back to the will of Pilate[[Luke 23:11||]], who at last, at the Jews' urging, crucified Christ[[Luke 23:23||]]. Christ is speaking generally of different wicked men as if of the same ones, inasmuch as all the reprobate are taken as one generation, to which the Saviour says: [[Matt 23:36|all these things shall come upon this generation|venient hæc omnia super generationem istam]], namely all the blood shed innocently. [[17:13|Then the disciples understood, that he had spoken to them of John the Baptist|Tunc intellexerunt discipuli tres prædicti, quia de Joanne Baptista dixisset eis]], the three disciples, that is: what He told of the past coming of Elias He had said of John, understanding and signifying John by Elias, because of the likeness of their qualities, not because they were one person. For John too, when asked by the Jews, [[John 1:21|Art thou Elias|Elias es tu]]? answered, No.

17.title: Explanatio residuæ partis hujus capituli, ab eo loco quo dicitur: Et quum venisset Jesus ad turbam
17.title_en: Explanation of the rest of this chapter, from the place where it says: And when he was come to the multitude

paras.t: Et quum venisset Jesus ad turbam, id est die sequenti a transfiguratione prædicta, accessit ad eum homo genibus provolutus, id est genua flectens, ante eum, dicens: Domine, miserere filio meo, liberando eum a sua miseria, quia lunaticus est, id est, secundum lunationes seu tempore noviluniorum furit tanquam arrepticius; et male patitur, id est, dire vexatur a dæmone. Cur autem aliquis nuncupetur lunaticus, plenius dictum est supra. Nam sæpe cadit in ignem, et crebro in aquam, id est, a diabolo ipsum apprehendente in ignem et aquam projicitur, ut occidatur. Unde Marcus clarius dicit: Ubicumque apprehenderit eum spiritus, allidit eum, et spumat, et stridet dentibus, et arescit. Et obtuli eum discipulis tuis, non tamen Petro, Jacobo et Joanni, sed eis qui transfigurationi non interfuerunt; et non potuerunt curare eum a prædictis incommodis et a dæmonio. Hujus impotentiæ causa fuit, tam incredulitas patris quam discipulorum, sicut dicetur.
paras.en: [[17:14|And when he was come to the multitude|Et quum venisset Jesus ad turbam]], Jesus, that is, on the day after the Transfiguration just told, [[17:14|there came to him a man falling down on his knees before him saying|accessit ad eum homo genibus provolutus ante eum, dicens]]: falling down on his knees, that is, kneeling: [[17:14|Lord, have pity on my son|Domine, miserere filio meo]], by freeing him from his misery, [[17:14|for he is a lunatic|quia lunaticus est]], that is, according to the phases of the moon, or at the time of the new moons, he raves like one possessed; [[17:14|and suffereth much|et male patitur]], that is, is cruelly tormented by the demon. Why someone is called a lunatic was explained more fully above[[Matt 4:24||]]. [[17:14|for he falleth often into the fire, and often into the water|Nam sæpe cadit in ignem, et crebro in aquam]], that is, he is thrown into the fire and the water by the devil who seizes him, so that he may be killed. Hence Mark says more clearly: [[Mark 9:17|wheresoever he taketh him, dasheth him: and he foameth and gnasheth with the teeth and pineth away|Ubicumque apprehenderit eum spiritus, allidit eum, et spumat, et stridet dentibus, et arescit]]. [[17:15|And I brought him to thy disciples|Et obtuli eum discipulis tuis]], not, however, to Peter, James and John, but to those who were not present at the Transfiguration; [[17:15|and they could not cure him|et non potuerunt curare eum]] of these ills and of the demon. The cause of this inability was the unbelief both of the father and of the disciples, as will be said.

paras.t: Respondens autem Jesus, ait: O generatio incredula et perversa, id est, infideles et iniqui. Hoc dicit ad patrem lunatici et ad similes ei. Quousque ero vobiscum, inter vos corporaliter conversando? usquequo patiar vos, id est incredulitatem perversitatemque vestram? quasi dicat, Non diu. Vel hoc dicit, significans se desiderare reverti ad Patrem, et ut malos digne redarguat, ac suæ justitiæ zelum ostendat seque de hominum pravitate monstret dolere. Non autem dicit hæc quasi impatiens et tædio victus, vel quasi ante tempus divinitus præordinatum mori desiderans, sed potius loquitur affectu ac more prudentissimi medici, qui contrariantibus suæ artis remediis durius loquitur. Afferte huc illum lunaticum ad me. Ut curatio et modus suæ curationis omnibus innotescat, ideo fecit eum Christus adduci ad se, quem utique poterat curare absentem. Et increpavit illum Jesus, vel puerum, eo quod aliquid forte commisit, propter quod diabolus in eum potestatem accepit, vel (quod verius est) dæmonem. Unde Marcus ait: Comminatus est spiritui immundo; et Lucas, Increpavit (inquit) spiritum immundum. Et exiit ab eo dæmonium: quod secundum Marcum, erat surdum et mutum, quoniam fecit puerum surdum et ad loquendum impotentem; et curatus est puer a dæmonio, a surditate et mutitate, ex illa hora, qua Jesus dæmoni jussit exire a puero.
paras.en: [[17:16|Then Jesus answered and said: O unbelieving and perverse generation|Respondens autem Jesus, ait: O generatio incredula et perversa]], that is, you unbelieving and wicked. He says this to the lunatic's father and to those like him. [[17:16|how long shall I be with you|Quousque ero vobiscum]], living bodily among you? [[17:16|How long shall I suffer you|usquequo patiar vos]], that is, your unbelief and perversity? As if to say: not long. Or He says this to signify that He longs to return to the Father, and so as to rebuke the wicked as they deserve, show the zeal of His justice, and show that He grieves at the depravity of men. He does not say this as one impatient and overcome by weariness, or as one wishing to die before the time appointed by God, but rather speaks with the feeling and in the manner of a most prudent physician, who speaks more harshly to those who oppose the remedies of his art. [[17:16|Bring him hither to me|Afferte huc illum lunaticum ad me]], the lunatic. Christ had him brought to Him, though He could certainly have cured him in his absence, so that the cure and the manner of the cure might be known to all. [[17:17|And Jesus rebuked him|Et increpavit illum Jesus]]: either the boy, because perhaps he had committed something on account of which the devil received power over him, or (which is truer) the demon. Hence Mark says: [[Mark 9:24|he threatened the unclean spirit|Comminatus est spiritui immundo]]; and Luke: [[Luke 9:43|Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit|Increpavit (inquit) spiritum immundum]]. [[17:17|and the devil went out of him|Et exiit ab eo dæmonium]], which according to Mark was deaf and dumb[[Mark 9:24||]], since it made the boy deaf and unable to speak; [[17:17|and the child was cured from that hour|et curatus est puer ex illa hora]], of the demon, of deafness and dumbness, from the hour in which Jesus ordered the demon to go out of the boy.

paras.t: Tunc accesserunt discipuli ad Jesum secreto, et dixerunt: Quare nos non potuimus ejicere illum dæmonem a puero isto? Superius dictum est, quod Jesus dedit discipulis potestatem super omnia dæmonia; imo super omnem virtutem inimici, secundum Lucam: quomodo ergo nunc dicitur, quod non potuerunt dæmonem istum expellere? Et respondendum, quod illa potestatis collatio intelligenda erat, nisi discipuli ponerent obicem. Dicit illis Jesus: Propter incredulitatem vestram: non quod simpliciter infideles fuerint, sed quia in fidei perfectione defecerunt. Quemadmodum enim ex consequentibus innotescit, ceteri discipuli videntes quod Jesus Petrum, Jacobum et Joannem specialiter duxit seorsum in montem, humanum aliquid passi sunt, videlicet motum invidiæ atque superbiæ, dolentes illos sibi præferri; ob hoc quoque meruerunt incurrere quamdam hæsitationem in fide. Porro, quod propter incredulitatem suam non potuerint ejicere dæmonem, declarat Salvator. Amen quippe dico vobis, si habueritis fidem sicut granum sinapis, id est, quæ tali grano compararetur (cui superius comparatum est regnum cœlorum), quatenus sicut hujusmodi granum parvum est quantitate, maximumque virtute, sic fides vestra in se vigorosa, fecunda ac fortis consistat, dicetis monti huic, Transi hinc, id est, de loco isto transferaris virtute divina; et transibit, quo jusseritis. Per hoc exemplum innuit Christus, quod fidei nihil impossibile sit. Et quamvis tale quid raro factum legatur, tamen verum est quod ait Salvator. Nam si ratio id exigeret, Deus montem transferret ad instantiam verbi in fide perfecti. Majora quoque fecerunt discipuli quam esset montis translatio, mortuos suscitando, a nativitate claudos et cæcos sanando, arcana cordium reserando. Quidam per montem, ratione elationis, intelligunt dæmonem, quem viri perfecti solo verbo transire et fugere cogunt. Unde de impio legitur apud Jeremiam: Ecce ego ad te, mons pestifer, ait Dominus, qui corrumpis universam terram.
paras.en: [[17:18|Then came the disciples to Jesus secretly, and said: Why could not we cast him out|Tunc accesserunt discipuli ad Jesum secreto, et dixerunt: Quare nos non potuimus ejicere illum]], the demon, from this boy? It was said above that Jesus gave the disciples power over all demons[[Matt 10:1||]], and indeed, according to Luke, [[Luke 10:19|upon all the power of the enemy|super omnem virtutem inimici]]: how then is it now said that they could not drive out this demon? The answer is that that bestowal of power was to be understood as holding unless the disciples put an obstacle in its way. [[17:19|Jesus said to them: Because of your unbelief|Dicit illis Jesus: Propter incredulitatem vestram]]: not that they were simply unbelievers, but because they fell short in the perfection of faith. For, as is made known from what follows, the other disciples, seeing that Jesus had taken Peter, James and John apart up the mountain, felt something human, namely a stirring of envy and pride, grieving that those three were preferred to themselves; and for this they deserved to fall into a certain hesitation in faith. The Saviour then declares that it was because of their unbelief that they could not cast out the demon. [[17:19|For, amen I say to you, if you have faith as a grain of mustard seed|Amen quippe dico vobis, si habueritis fidem sicut granum sinapis]], that is, faith that could be compared to such a grain (to which the kingdom of heaven was compared above[[Matt 13:31||]]), so that, as such a grain is small in size and very great in power, so your faith in itself may be vigorous, fruitful and strong, [[17:19|you shall say to this mountain: Remove from hence|dicetis monti huic, Transi hinc]], that is, be carried from this place by divine power, [[17:19|and it shall remove|et transibit]], where you command. By this example Christ suggests that nothing is impossible to faith. And although such a thing is seldom read to have been done, what the Saviour says is nevertheless true; for if reason required it, God would move a mountain at the word of one perfect in faith. And the disciples did greater things than the moving of a mountain, raising the dead, healing those lame and blind from birth, and laying open the secrets of hearts. Some understand by the mountain, by reason of its pride, the demon, whom perfect men force by a word alone to depart and flee. Hence we read of the wicked one in Jeremias: [[Jer 51:25|Behold I come against thee, thou destroying mountain, saith the Lord, which corruptest the whole earth|Ecce ego ad te, mons pestifer, ait Dominus, qui corrumpis universam terram]].

paras.t: Hoc autem genus dæmonum non ejicitur ab obsessis, nisi per orationem et jejunium, id est virtute et merito orationis et abstinentiæ, quæ sunt effectus fidei tam perfectæ, ut grano sinapis merito comparetur. Diversorum etenim dæmonum varia est potestas, et diversi de diversis vitiis tentant homines. Unde quidam dicuntur spiritus fornicationis, alii spiritus invidiæ, alii spiritus superbiæ. Genus itaque dæmonum ad quod pertinebat dæmon iste, fortiter imprimit se hominibus quos obsidet. Et aliqui dicunt, quod tentet de vitio carnis: propter quod non ejicitur, nisi oratione atque jejunio, quibus carnales concupiscentiæ refrenantur. Insuper, per orationem, quæ est elevatio mentis in Deum, et per jejunium, quod est castigatio corporis, datur intelligi quod hoc dæmonum genus non ejiciatur, nisi ab hominibus notabiliter virtuosis, mente et corpore depuratis. Hinc beatissimi anachoretæ testati sunt, unumquemque facile illi posse dominari dæmonio, qui vicerit passionem et culpam de qua dæmon hujusmodi tentat.
paras.en: [[17:20|But this kind|Hoc autem genus]] of demons [[17:20|is not cast out|non ejicitur]] from the possessed [[17:20|but by prayer and fasting|nisi per orationem et jejunium]], that is, by the power and merit of prayer and abstinence, which are the effects of a faith so perfect that it is rightly compared to a grain of mustard seed. For the power of different demons differs, and different demons tempt men to different vices. So some are called spirits of fornication, others spirits of envy, others spirits of pride. The kind of demons to which this demon belonged presses itself hard upon the men it possesses; and some say that it tempts to the vice of the flesh, which is why it is cast out only by prayer and fasting, by which the desires of the flesh are curbed. Further, by prayer, which is the raising of the mind to God, and by fasting, which is the chastising of the body, we are given to understand that this kind of demon is cast out only by men of notable virtue, purified in mind and body. Hence the most blessed anchorites have testified that anyone can easily master the demon who has overcome the passion and the sin to which that demon tempts.

paras.t: Conversantibus autem eis, videlicet Jesu et ejus discipulis, in Galilæa, dixit illis Jesus: Filius hominis tradendus est in manus hominum, et occident eum, et tertia die resurget. Adversis ac tristibus læta permiscet, ut mœrorem lætitia temperet. Ideo de sua passione prædicens, de gloria resurrectionis mox addidit. Frequenter quoque prænuntiat se passurum, ne inopinate captus putetur, et jacula prævisa minus feriant, ipsique discipuli, quum viderint verificata quæ prædixit, constabiliantur in fide. Et contristati sunt vehementer: et tanto vehementius, quanto in ejus amore magis fervebant, et quanto invitius separabantur a tam dulci magistro, a tam pio patrono atque fidelissimo defensore ac provisore, et quia agnoverant sanctitatem ac innocentiam ejus. Et quoniam nondum spirituales erant perfecte, nec resurrectionis gloriam diligenter pensabant, idcirco tanto magis de Christi occisione dolebant, quanto illam in se ipsa sub ratione pœnæ ac mali et nocumenti, non sub ratione remedii et salutis, pensabant. Nec tamen audebant suadere oppositum, scientes quid Petrus oppositum consulens, paulo ante audisset, videlicet, Vade post me, satana, quia non sapis quæ Dei sunt.
paras.en: [[17:21|And when they abode together in Galilee|Conversantibus autem eis in Galilæa]], Jesus and His disciples, that is, [[17:21|Jesus said to them: The Son of man shall be betrayed into the hands of men|dixit illis Jesus: Filius hominis tradendus est in manus hominum]]: [[17:22|And they shall kill him, and the third day he shall rise again|et occident eum, et tertia die resurget]]. He mingles glad things with adverse and sad ones, so as to temper sorrow with joy: so, foretelling His Passion, He at once added the glory of the resurrection. He often foretells that He will suffer, too, lest He be thought to have been taken unawares, so that darts foreseen may wound less, and so that the disciples themselves, when they see fulfilled what He foretold, may be made firm in faith. [[17:22|And they were troubled exceedingly|Et contristati sunt vehementer]]: and the more exceedingly, the more fervent they were in their love for Him, the more unwillingly they were to be parted from so sweet a Master, so loving a patron, so faithful a defender and provider, and because they knew His holiness and innocence. And since they were not yet perfectly spiritual, and did not weigh carefully the glory of the resurrection, they grieved over Christ's killing all the more because they considered it in itself, as punishment, evil and harm, and not as remedy and salvation. Yet they did not dare to urge the opposite, knowing what Peter had heard a little before when he advised the opposite, namely: [[Matt 16:23|Go behind me, Satan|Vade post me, satana]], [[Matt 16:23|because thou savourest not the things that are of God|quia non sapis quæ Dei sunt]].

paras.t: Et quum venissent Capharnaum Jesus ejusque discipuli, accesserunt qui didrachma accipiebant, ad Petrum, id est exactores tributi quod vocabatur didrachma, hoc est duplex drachma. Drachma vero (ut dicitur) est octava pars unciæ, valens sex obolos. Exactores ergo seu collectores tributorum ex parte imperatoris commorantes in urbe præcipua Galilææ, puta Capharnaum, non accedunt ad Jesum, propter reverentiam ejus, quem noverant tanta operari miracula, et tantum honorari a populo, sed ad Petrum, tanquam principalem inter discipulos. Et dixerunt ei: Magister vester, hic Jesus, non solvit didrachma? id est, soletne dare tributum, sicut ordinaverunt Romani? Ait Petrus: Etiam. Et quum intrasset Petrus in domum, ut diceret Christo verba exactorum, prævenit eum Jesus, ut ostenderet se omnia scire, dicens: Quid tibi videtur, Simon? Quærit, non ignorans quid responsurus sit Petrus, sed ut ex ejus responsione convenientius instruat eum, et optima proferat documenta. Reges terræ a quibus accipiunt tributum vel censum? a filiis suis, an ab alienis ceteris sibi subjectis?
paras.en: [[17:23|And when they were come to Capharnaum|Et quum venissent Capharnaum]], Jesus and His disciples, [[17:23|they that received the didrachmas, came to Peter|accesserunt qui didrachma accipiebant, ad Petrum]], that is, the collectors of the tax called the didrachma, that is, the double drachma. A drachma (so it is said) is an eighth of an ounce, worth six obols. So the collectors of the taxes on the emperor's behalf, living in the chief city of Galilee, Capharnaum, do not approach Jesus, out of reverence for Him, whom they knew to work such great miracles and to be so honoured by the people, but Peter, as the chief among the disciples. [[17:23|and said to him: Doth not your master pay the didrachma|Et dixerunt ei: Magister vester, hic Jesus, non solvit didrachma?]]? Your Master, this Jesus, that is: is He accustomed to pay the tax, as the Romans have ordained? [[17:24|He said: Yes|Ait Petrus: Etiam]]. [[17:24|And when he was come into the house|Et quum intrasset Petrus in domum]], Peter, to tell Christ the words of the collectors, [[17:24|Jesus prevented him, saying: What is thy opinion, Simon|prævenit eum Jesus, dicens: Quid tibi videtur Simon?]]? He went before him, to show that He knew all things. He asks, not as if He did not know what Peter would answer, but so as to instruct him more fittingly from his answer and to bring out the best lessons. [[17:24|The kings of the earth, of whom do they receive tribute or custom, of their own children, or of strangers|Reges terræ a quibus accipiunt tributum vel censum? a filiis suis, an ab alienis]], the others subject to them?

paras.t: Et ille dixit: Ab alienis. Dixit illi Jesus: Ergo liberi sunt filii, a persolutione tributi ac census sui, filii regum. Per hoc Christus intendebat concludere se liberum esse a dando tributa, tanquam Filium Regis regum, nulli legi humanæ de necessitate subjectum: de quo fertur in Psalmo: Deus, judicium tuum regi da, et justitiam tuam filio regis. Denique advertendum, quod libertas est duplex: Una spiritualis: sicque omnes Christiani facti sunt liberi, quia per Christi passionem sunt a potestate diaboli et jugo peccati erepti. Propter quod ait Salvator: Si filius vos liberaverit, vere liberi eritis. Alia corporalis: et ita fideles tenentur ad tributa, quemadmodum dicit Apostolus: Cui tributum, tributum; cui vectigal, vectigal. Unde Christus alibi: Reddite, inquit, quæ sunt Cæsaris Cæsari, et quæ sunt Dei Deo.
paras.en: [[17:25|And he said: Of strangers. Jesus said to him: Then the children are free|Et ille dixit: Ab alienis. Dixit illi Jesus: Ergo liberi sunt filii]]: free, that is, from paying their tribute and custom, the sons of kings. By this Christ meant to conclude that He was free from paying taxes, as the Son of the King of kings, subject by necessity to no human law: of whom it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 71:2|Give to the king thy judgment, O God, and to the king's son thy justice|Deus, judicium tuum regi da, et justitiam tuam filio regis]]. It should be noted, further, that freedom is twofold. One is spiritual: and so all Christians have been made free, because through Christ's Passion they have been snatched from the power of the devil and the yoke of sin. Hence the Saviour says: [[John 8:36|If therefore the son shall make you free, you shall be free indeed|Si filius vos liberaverit, vere liberi eritis]]. The other is bodily: and so the faithful are bound to pay taxes, as the Apostle says: [[Rom 13:7|Tribute, to whom tribute is due: custom, to whom custom|Cui tributum, tributum; cui vectigal, vectigal]]. Hence Christ says elsewhere: [[Matt 22:21|Render therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar's; and to God, the things that are God's|Reddite, inquit, quæ sunt Cæsaris Cæsari, et quæ sunt Dei Deo]].

paras.t: Ut autem non scandalizemus, id est, ad ruinam peccati occasionaliter inducamus, eos qui didrachma requirunt: qui putassent Christum imperatori repugnantem, et sæculare jus violantem, nisi solvisset didrachma. Præterea Christus magis vitavit scandalum istorum quam Scribarum ac Pharisæorum, quia istorum scandalum ortum fuisset ex ignorantia qua ignorabant Jesum esse naturalem ac verum Filium Dei: ad quam notitiam non tenebantur explicite, præsertim quum essent Romani gentiles. Scandalum vero Scribarum ac Pharisæorum processit ex mera malitia. Christus quoque, sicut peccare non potuit, ita nec aliquem potuit scandalizare directe, sed occasionaliter tantum. Vade ad mare, supra quod sita fuit urbs ista Capharnaum, et mitte hamum, videlicet instrumentum quo pisces capiuntur, in aquam; et eum piscem qui primus ascenderit, id est, hamo captus inhæserit, levatusque fuerit, tolle, et aperto ore ejus, invenies staterem valentem duplex didrachma, et per consequens pro duobus sufficientem: ideo subditur, illum staterem sumens, da eis pro me et te. Christus tanquam veraciter liberalis atque largissimus, plus dedit quam illi exigebant. In hoc autem quod eo operante inventus, et secundum Hieronymum, creatus est in ore piscis stater, ostenditur omnipotentia ejus; in eo quod de inventione piscis ac stateris tam certe prædixit, monstratur omniscientia ejus, atque in utroque ejus divinitas declaratur. In eo quoque quod humanis se legibus subdidit, quum esset liberrimus Filius Regis æterni, ejus humilitas summa et vera humanitas agnoscuntur.
paras.en: [[17:26|But that we may not scandalize them|Ut autem non scandalizemus eos]], that is, lead them by occasion into the ruin of sin, those who demand the didrachma: who would have thought Christ was opposing the emperor and violating secular law if He had not paid the didrachma. Moreover, Christ avoided the scandal of these men more than that of the scribes and Pharisees, because their scandal would have arisen from ignorance, by which they did not know that Jesus was the natural and true Son of God, a knowledge they were not bound to explicitly, especially since they were Roman Gentiles; whereas the scandal of the scribes and Pharisees came from sheer malice. And Christ, as He could not sin, so He could not scandalize anyone directly, but only by occasion. [[17:26|go to the sea|Vade ad mare]], on which this city of Capharnaum stood, [[17:26|and cast in a hook|et mitte hamum]], that is, the instrument by which fish are caught, into the water; [[17:26|and that fish which shall first come up, take|et eum piscem, qui primus ascenderit, tolle]]: first come up, that is, is caught and held on the hook and drawn up; [[17:26|and when thou hast opened it's mouth, thou shalt find a stater|et aperto ore ejus, invenies staterem]], worth a double didrachma, and so enough for two: so it is added, [[17:26|take that, and give it to them for me and thee|illum staterem sumens, da eis pro me et te]]. Christ, as truly liberal and most generous, gave more than they demanded. In the stater being found, and according to Jerome created, in the fish's mouth by His working, His almighty power is shown; in His foretelling so surely the finding of the fish and the stater, His knowledge of all things is shown; and in both His divinity is declared. And in His submitting Himself to human laws, though He was the wholly free Son of the eternal King, His supreme humility and true humanity are recognized.

18.title: Explanatio capituli octavidecimi: In illa hora accesserunt discipuli ad Jesum
18.title_en: Explanation of the eighteenth chapter: At that hour the disciples came to Jesus

paras.t: In superioribus dictum est quemadmodum Christus specialiter dixerit Petro, Tibi dabo claves regni cœlorum; quomodo etiam primus fuit inter tres quos Jesus assumpsit, ut transfigurationi suæ interessent; et qualiter pro se atque pro Petro solvit tributum. Ex his atque similibus, discipuli moti sunt ad suspicandum quod Petrus omnibus eis esset præferendus: de quo minus bene contentabantur, nondum enim humilitatis apicem attigerant. Idcirco, In illa hora qua facta sunt quæ in fine præcedentis capituli scripta sunt, in Capharnaum, de persolutione tributi, accesserunt discipuli, præsertim Apostoli, ad Jesum, dicentes: Quis, putas, major est in regno cœlorum? id est, quis amplioris gratiæ et meriti est in Ecclesia militanti? et quis plenioris gloriæ et præmii est in Ecclesia triumphanti? Hoc quæsierunt, quatenus talis eis præficeretur, qui dignioris esset gratiæ in præsenti et gloriæ in futuro. Sed his obviare videtur quod apud Marcum inducitur, quemadmodum quum venissent domum, Jesus interrogavit discipulos: Quid in via tractabatis? At illi obticuerunt, videlicet præ verecundia, siquidem in via disputaverant, quis eorum esset major. Quomodo ergo nunc dicuntur accessisse et Jesum interrogasse? Responderi potest: Primo, quod videntes se a Christo deprehensos, ad tempus præ rubore silebant; post modicum temporis resumpta fiducia, sciscitati sunt Dominum. Secundo, quod aliqui tacuerunt, et alii interrogaverunt. Tertio, quod tacuerunt de sua ambitiosa disputatione, sed locuti sunt de utili quæstione.
paras.en: It was said above how Christ said to Peter in particular, [[Matt 16:19|I will give to thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven|Tibi dabo claves regni cœlorum]]; how he was also first among the three whom Jesus took to be present at His Transfiguration[[Matt 17:1||]]; and how He paid the tax for Himself and for Peter[[Matt 17:26||]]. From these and similar things the disciples were led to suspect that Peter was to be preferred to all of them, which did not please them well, for they had not yet reached the summit of humility. So [[18:1|At that hour|In illa hora]] in which the things written at the end of the preceding chapter took place, in Capharnaum, about the payment of the tax, [[18:1|the disciples came to Jesus, saying|accesserunt discipuli, præsertim Apostoli, ad Jesum, dicentes]] (the Apostles above all): [[18:1|Who, thinkest thou, is the greater in the kingdom of heaven|Quis, putas, major est in regno cœlorum]]? That is, who has the fuller grace and merit in the Church militant, and who the fuller glory and reward in the Church triumphant? They asked this so that such a one might be set over them, as being worthy of greater grace in the present and glory in the future. But against this seems to be what is told in Mark: when they had come to the house, Jesus asked the disciples, [[Mark 9:32|What did you treat of in the way|Quid in via tractabatis]]? [[Mark 9:33|But they held their peace|At illi obticuerunt]], namely for shame, [[Mark 9:33|for in the way they had disputed|siquidem in via disputaverant]] which of them was the greater. How then are they now said to have come and asked Jesus? It can be answered: first, that seeing themselves found out by Christ, they kept silent for a time out of shame, and after a little while, regaining confidence, they questioned the Lord; second, that some kept silent and others asked; third, that they kept silent about their ambitious dispute but spoke of a useful question.

paras.t: Et advocans Jesus parvulum, statuit, id est collocavit, eum in medio eorum, videlicet discipulorum, et dixit. Humilis magister, non solum verbis, sed et factis humilitatem commendans, ambitionem funditus eradicavit. Amen dico vobis, nisi conversi fueritis, id est corde salubriter immutati, videlicet a contentione, elatione et omni ambitione, ad pacem, humilitatem, obedientiam, et efficiamini sicut parvuli, id est, parvulis assimilati fueritis, quantum ad bonas proprietates eorum, amplectendo innocentiam, puritatem et humilitatem eorum, quos constat de prælatione non occupari, nec invicem invidere, non intrabitis in regnum cœlorum, quod humilibus atque pacificis est paratum. Hoc in persona Apostolorum omnibus dicitur Christianis. Sed quoniam nemo excluditur a regno cœlorum, nisi pro peccato mortali, videntur Apostoli peccasse mortaliter, quibus nunc dicitur: Nisi conversi fueritis, et efficiamini sicut parvuli, etc. Si autem dicantur non peccasse mortaliter in prædictis, tunc illud quod dicitur, Nisi conversi fueritis, intelligendum erit conditionaliter, ut sit sensus: Nisi conversi fueritis, id est, si magni fueritis in oculis propriis, elati et ambitiosi, non poteritis salvari, nisi conversi fueritis modo præfato. Unde per Jeremiam dicitur: Nolite elevari, sed date gloriam Domino Deo. Et apostolus Petrus: Deponentes, inquit, omnem malitiam et dolum et simulationem et detractionem, quasi modo geniti infantes, lac concupiscite. Denique in parvulo considerari potest minoratio sensus, et indisciplinatio morum: et sic non debemus fieri sicut parvuli, juxta illud Apostoli, Nolite pueri effici sensibus, sed malitia parvuli estote. Verumtamen nomen parvuli in Scripturis interdum in malo accipitur: ut quum Salomon ait, Aversio parvulorum interficiet eos; et Job, Parvulum (ait) occidit invidia.
paras.en: [[18:2|And Jesus, calling unto him a little child, set him in the midst of them|Et advocans Jesus parvulum, statuit, id est collocavit, eum in medio eorum]]: set, that is, placed him, in the midst of the disciples, [[18:3|And said|et dixit]]. The humble Master, commending humility not only by words but by deeds, uprooted ambition entirely. [[18:3|amen I say to you, unless you be converted|Amen dico vobis, nisi conversi fueritis]], that is, changed in heart to your salvation, namely from contention, pride and all ambition to peace, humility and obedience, [[18:3|and become as little children|et efficiamini sicut parvuli]], that is, made like little children as to their good qualities, embracing their innocence, purity and humility (for it is plain that they are not busy about precedence nor envious of one another), [[18:3|you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven|non intrabitis in regnum cœlorum]], which is prepared for the humble and peaceable. This is said to all Christians in the person of the Apostles. But since no one is shut out of the kingdom of heaven except for mortal sin, the Apostles seem to have sinned mortally, since it is now said to them: unless you be converted, and become as little children, etc. If they are said not to have sinned mortally in this, then the words "unless you be converted" must be understood conditionally, so that the sense is: unless you be converted, that is, if you are great in your own eyes, proud and ambitious, you cannot be saved unless you are converted in the way described. Hence it is said through Jeremias: [[Jer 13:15|Be not proud|Nolite elevari]], [[Jer 13:16|Give ye glory to the Lord your God|date gloriam Domino Deo]]. And the apostle Peter: [[1 Pet 2:1|laying away all malice and all guile and dissimulations|Deponentes, inquit, omnem malitiam et dolum et simulationem]] and detraction, [[1 Pet 2:2|As newborn babes, desire|quasi modo geniti infantes, lac concupiscite]] milk. Again, in a little child one can consider the lesser understanding and the undisciplined behaviour; and in this way we ought not to become as little children, according to that saying of the Apostle: [[1 Cor 14:20|do not become children in sense. But in malice be children|Nolite pueri effici sensibus, sed malitia parvuli estote]]. And the word "little one" is sometimes taken in a bad sense in the Scriptures, as when Solomon says, [[Prov 1:32|The turning away of little ones shall kill them|Aversio parvulorum interficiet eos]]; and Job: [[Job 5:2|envy slayeth the little one|Parvulum (ait) occidit invidia]].

paras.t: Quidam per parvulum istum quem Jesus statuit inter discipulos, intelligunt ipsummet Christum. Sed hoc ad litteram stare non potest, quum de parvulo isto scriptum sit apud Marcum: Quem quum amplexus esset Jesus. Certum autem est, quod non amplexabatur se ipsum.
paras.en: Some understand by this little child whom Jesus set among the disciples Christ Himself. But this cannot stand in the letter, since it is written of this child in Mark: [[Mark 9:35|Whom when he had embraced|Quem quum amplexus esset]], Jesus. And it is certain that He did not embrace Himself.

paras.t: Quicumque ergo humiliaverit se coram Deo et hominibus sicut parvulus iste, id est, omnem motum superbiæ prorsus abjecerit, et tam alienus fuerit ab elatione ut puer, consideratione divinæ majestatis atque intuitu propriæ defectuositatis, major est in regno cœlorum, quam alii minus humiles. Humilitas namque directe disponit ad profectum gratiæ in præsenti, et exaltationem incrementumque gloriæ in futuro, prout scriptum est: Deus superbis resistit, humilibus autem dat gratiam; et iterum, Humilia valde spiritum tuum, et invenies gratiam coram Deo et hominibus. Hinc in Proverbiis legitur: Humilitas præcedit gloriam, et humilem spiritu suscipiet gloria. Quanto itaque quis se magis humiliaverit pure propter Deum ex caritate, tanto sublimior erit in patria. Non quod præmium essentiale correspondeat humilitati directe, sed dispositive ac fundamentaliter, et quia majori humilitati major adest caritas.
paras.en: [[18:4|Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child|Quicumque ergo humiliaverit se sicut parvulus iste]] before God and men, that is, shall utterly cast off every movement of pride, and be as far from conceit as a child, by considering the divine majesty and looking at his own failings, [[18:4|he is the greater in the kingdom of heaven|major est in regno cœlorum]] than others who are less humble. For humility disposes directly to progress in grace in the present and to exaltation and increase of glory in the future, as it is written: [[Jas 4:6|God resisteth the proud and giveth grace to the humble|Deus superbis resistit, humilibus autem dat gratiam]][[1 Pet 5:5||]]; and again: [[Ecclus 7:19|Humble thy spirit very much|Humilia valde spiritum tuum]], and [[Ecclus 3:20|thou shalt find grace before God|invenies gratiam coram Deo]] and men. Hence we read in Proverbs: [[Prov 15:33|humility goeth before glory|Humilitas præcedit gloriam]], and [[Prov 29:23|glory shall uphold the humble of spirit|humilem spiritu suscipiet gloria]]. So the more someone humbles himself purely for God's sake out of charity, the higher he will be in the fatherland. Not that the essential reward corresponds to humility directly, but as to a disposition and foundation, and because greater charity goes with greater humility.
