paras.t: Et iratus dominus ejus, videlicet Christus, qui nunc irascitur, non per passionis commotionem inordinatam, sed justitiæ exsecutionem, tradidit eum tortoribus, puta dæmonibus, qui sunt infatigabiles impiorum punitores, saltem usque ad diem judicii, post quam omnes reprobi simul cruciabuntur a pœnis inferni, non a se invicem, ut aliqui dicunt; quoadusque redderet universum debitum, id est in æternum, quoniam in inferno exsistentes nunquam salubriter pœnitent, unde nec debitum solvunt satisfaciendo pro culpis. Sic et Pater meus cœlestis, qui est Pater meus per veram generationem, et naturæ identitatem, faciet vobis, mancipando vos pœnis æternis, si non remiseritis unusquisque fratri suo, hoc est proximo, de cordibus vestris, cordialiter diligendo injuriantem vel peccantem, et culpam penitus dimittendo, ita ut nil amaritudinis, iræ vel impatientiæ, inhæreat animæ vestræ.
paras.en: [[18:34|And his lord being angry|Et iratus dominus ejus]], namely Christ, who is now angry, not by a disordered movement of passion but by the carrying out of justice, [[18:34|delivered him to the torturers|tradidit eum tortoribus]], namely the demons, who are untiring punishers of the wicked, at least until the day of judgment, after which all the reprobate together will be tormented by the pains of hell, not by one another, as some say; [[18:34|until he paid all the debt|quoadusque redderet universum debitum]], that is, for ever, since those in hell never repent to their salvation, and so never pay the debt by making satisfaction for their sins. [[18:35|So also shall my heavenly Father do to you|Sic et Pater meus cœlestis, qui est Pater meus per veram generationem, et naturæ identitatem, faciet vobis]], who is My Father by true generation and identity of nature, handing you over to eternal punishment, [[18:35|if you forgive not every one his brother from your hearts|si non remiseritis unusquisque fratri suo, hoc est proximo, de cordibus vestris]], that is, his neighbour, loving from the heart the one who wrongs or sins against you, and forgiving the guilt entirely, so that no bitterness, anger or impatience clings to your soul.

paras.t: Videtur autem hoc loco quodammodo insinuari, quod peccata semel dimissa, redeant eadem et vindicentur, quia de servo illo prædictum est, quod dominus tradidit eum tortoribus, quousque solveret debitum universum, et subditur: Sic Pater faciet vobis. Sed ut communiter jam tenetur, peccata dimissa non redeunt eadem, nec quoad culpam nec quoad pœnam, directe et integre; sed indirecte et aliquo modo redire dicuntur, in quantum sequentia vitia graviora et damnabiliora sunt propter ingratitudinem indultæ pietatis, et propter recidivum in eadem mala, sicut et periculosius est, eamdem corporis partem vulnerari quæ læsa est semel.
paras.en: It seems, however, to be suggested in some way here that sins once forgiven return the same and are punished, since it was said of that servant that his lord handed him over to the torturers until he should pay all the debt, and it is added: so shall My Father do to you. But, as is now commonly held, forgiven sins do not return the same, neither as to guilt nor as to punishment, directly and wholly; but they are said to return indirectly and in a certain way, inasmuch as the sins that follow are graver and more damnable because of ingratitude for the mercy granted and because of falling back into the same evils; as it is also more dangerous for the same part of the body to be wounded that has been hurt once already.

19.title: Elucidatio capituli nonidecimi: Et factum est, quum consummasset Jesus sermones istos, etc.
19.title_en: Explanation of the nineteenth chapter: And it came to pass when Jesus had ended these words, etc.

paras.t: Et factum est, quum consummasset, id est implesset, Jesus sermones istos, in præcedenti capitulo recitatos, migravit a Galilæa, et venit in fines Judææ trans Jordanem, videlicet in partes seu terram duarum tribuum ac mediæ, scilicet Ruben, Gad, et Manasse. Et secutæ sunt eum turbæ multæ, propter diversas causas, ut dictum est sæpius; et curavit eos ibi, eos utique qui indigebant, non totam turbam. In quo tangit Evangelista diversa sanitatum miracula esse peracta ad præcedentis confirmationem doctrinæ: quas propter prolixitatem vitandam non recitat sigillatim. Nec solum curavit eos ab infirmitatibus corporis, sed et a languoribus animæ.
paras.en: [[19:1|And it came to pass when Jesus had ended|Et factum est, quum consummasset]], that is, fulfilled, [[19:1|these words|sermones istos]], recited in the preceding chapter, [[19:1|he departed from Galilee and came into the coasts of Judea, beyond Jordan|migravit a Galilæa, et venit in fines Judææ trans Jordanem]], namely into the parts or land of two tribes and a half, that is, Ruben, Gad, and Manasses. [[19:2|And great multitudes followed him|Et secutæ sunt eum turbæ multæ]], for various reasons, as has often been said; [[19:2|and he healed them there|et curavit eos ibi]]: those, that is, who were in need, not the whole crowd. Here the Evangelist touches on the many miracles of healing done to confirm the preceding teaching, which he does not recount one by one so as not to be long. And He healed them not only of the infirmities of the body but also of the sicknesses of the soul.

paras.t: Et accesserunt ad eum Pharisæi, tentantes eum, id est, experiri volentes an possent eum reprehendere in sermone seu responsione, et dicentes: Si, id est utrum, licet homini dimittere uxorem suam omnino, non solum quoad cohabitationem et copulam, sed etiam quantum ad vinculum, ut accipiat aliam, quacumque ex causa, id est ex qualibet causa indifferenter, vel ex levi causa, videlicet propter deformitatem, fœditatem, seu odium? Hoc dolose quærebant, volentes redarguere Christum, quidquid responderet. Si enim diceret non licere, arguerent eum blasphemiæ, quasi contradicentem sacræ Scripturæ, quoniam in Deuteronomio Moyses ait: Si acceperit homo uxorem, et non invenerit gratiam ante oculos ejus propter aliquam fœditatem, scribet libellum repudii. Et Malachias propheta: Quum odio (inquit) habueris, eam dimitte. Si autem responderet quod liceret, arguerent eum libidinis licentiatorem. Sed si, Salomone testante, frustra jacitur rete ante oculos pennatorum, multo amplius inaniter expanduntur laquei ante oculos cuncta cernentis ac infallibilis Christi. Ideo ipse tanquam sapientia Dei, responsionem suam testimonio Scripturæ sic munivit, ut pro nulla parte valeat reprehendi.
paras.en: [[19:3|And there came to him the Pharisees tempting him|Et accesserunt ad eum Pharisæi, tentantes eum]], that is, wishing to try whether they could catch Him out in His speech or answer, [[19:3|saying: Is it lawful|et dicentes: Si licet]] (that is, whether it is lawful) [[19:3|for a man to put away his wife|homini dimittere uxorem suam]] altogether, not only as to living together and intercourse but also as to the bond, so that he may take another, [[19:3|for every cause|quacumque ex causa]], that is, for any cause whatever without distinction, or for a slight cause, such as ugliness, uncleanness or hatred? They asked this craftily, wishing to refute Christ whatever He answered. For if He said it was not lawful, they would accuse Him of blasphemy, as contradicting Holy Scripture, since Moses says in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 24:1|If a man take a wife|Si acceperit homo uxorem]], [[Deut 24:1|she find not favour in his eyes, for some uncleanness: he shall write a bill of divorce|et non invenerit gratiam ante oculos ejus propter aliquam fœditatem, scribet libellum repudii]]. And the prophet Malachias says: [[Mal 2:16|When thou shalt hate her put her away|Quum odio (inquit) habueris, eam dimitte]]. But if He answered that it was lawful, they would accuse Him of licensing lust. But if, as Solomon testifies, [[Prov 1:17|a net is spread in vain before the eyes of them that have wings|frustra jacitur rete ante oculos pennatorum]], much more vainly are snares spread before the eyes of Christ, who sees all things and cannot be deceived. Therefore He, as the Wisdom of God, so fortified His answer with the testimony of Scripture that it could not be faulted in any part.

paras.t: Qui respondens, ait eis: Non legistis, vos Pharisæi, qui ceteris religiosiores esse videmini? quasi dicat: Utique legistis, sed forte non sane intellexistis. Quia qui fecit hominem ab initio, id est Deus, qui protoplastos parentes creavit circa principium mundi, sexto videlicet die, masculum et feminam creavit eos, id est, unum eorum fecit marem, et aliam feminam in adjutorium viri ad prolem procreandam.
paras.en: [[19:4|Who answering, said to them: Have ye not read|Qui respondens, ait eis: Non legistis]], you Pharisees, who seem more religious than the rest? As if to say: You have certainly read it, but perhaps you have not understood it soundly. [[19:4|that he who made man from the beginning|Quia qui fecit hominem ab initio]], that is, God, who created our first parents about the beginning of the world, namely on the sixth day, [[19:4|made them male and female|masculum et feminam creavit eos]][[Gen 1:27||]]: that is, He made one of them a man and the other a woman, as a help to the man for the begetting of offspring.

paras.t: Et dicit Deus per Adam, seu ipse Adam Deo inspirante: Propter hoc, id est ob id quod vir et mulier conditi sunt in adjutorium mutuum gratia generandi, dimittet homo patrem et matrem. Ista dimissio intelligi potest dupliciter: Primo, quoad cohabitationis separationem. Videmus namque, quod sponsus et sponsa parentum suorum domos relinquunt, et separatim cohabitant. Secundo, quoad exclusionem matrimonialis contractus, quia parentes non sunt personæ legitimæ ad contrahendum matrimonium. Relinquet ergo homo patrem et matrem, id est, filius non ducet matrem, nec filia patrem. Hoc enim semper fuit illicitum propter naturalem reverentiam quæ debetur parentibus. Et adhærebit uxori suæ, et illa suo viro, per amorem, cohabitationem atque perpetuum vinculum; et erunt duo supposita, utpote maritus et conjux, in carne una, id est in uno carnali commercio, ita quod quilibet eorum potestatem habebit corporis alterius, et nullus proprii corporis.
paras.en: [[19:4|And he said|Et dicit]]: God through Adam, or Adam himself by God's inspiration: [[19:5|For this cause|Propter hoc]][[Gen 2:24||]], that is, because man and woman were made to help each other for the sake of begetting, [[19:5|shall a man leave father and mother|dimittet homo patrem et matrem]]. This leaving can be understood in two ways. First, as to separation in dwelling: for we see that bridegroom and bride leave the houses of their parents and dwell together apart. Secondly, as to exclusion from the marriage contract, since parents are not lawful persons for contracting marriage. So [[19:5|shall a man leave father and mother|Relinquet ergo homo patrem et matrem]], that is, a son shall not marry his mother, nor a daughter her father; for this was always unlawful, because of the natural reverence owed to parents. [[19:5|and shall cleave to his wife|Et adhærebit uxori suæ]], and she to her husband, through love, living together, and a perpetual bond; [[19:5|and they two shall be|et erunt duo]] persons [supposita: in the language of the schools, individual subsisting beings], namely husband and wife, [[19:5|in one flesh|in carne una]], that is, in one fleshly union, so that each of them will have power over the other's body, and neither over his own.

paras.t: Hæc scripta sunt in Genesi. Quum enim immisisset Dominus soporem supernæ contemplationis, seu ecstasim mentis, in Adam, tulissetque unam costarum ejus, et inde fecisset Evam, ille evigilans, vel potius ad se rediens, et quod factum erat ex revelatione agnoscens, locutus est: Hoc nunc os ex ossibus meis, et caro de carne mea; propter hoc relinquet patrem, etc., sicut nunc allegatum est.
paras.en: These things are written in Genesis. For when the Lord had cast upon Adam a sleep of heavenly contemplation, or an ecstasy of mind, and had taken one of his ribs and made Eve from it[[Gen 2:21||]], he, awaking, or rather coming back to himself, and knowing by revelation what had been done, said: [[Gen 2:23|This now is bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh|Hoc nunc os ex ossibus meis, et caro de carne mea]]; [[Gen 2:24|Wherefore a man shall leave father|propter hoc relinquet patrem]], etc., as has just been cited.

paras.t: Ex quibus concludit Salvator: Itaque jam, post copulam matrimonialem, non sunt, vir ejusque uxor, duo separabilia ab invicem, sed una caro, id est, tam indissolubiliter juncti sunt, ac si essent penitus una caro. Et quodammodo sunt una caro, quoniam caro unius est in potestate alterius, et econtra, quemadmodum ait Apostolus: Vir sui corporis non habet potestatem, sed mulier; similiter mulier sui corporis potestatem non habet, sed vir. Ex his infert responsionem firmissimam. Quod ergo Deus conjunxit, hoc est virum et feminam, quos Deus tam inseparabiliter counivit, homo non separet auctoritate humana et propria voluntate, ex qualibet causa. Possunt tamen separari quoad cohabitationem et debiti solvendi obligationem, de communi eorum consensu, auctoritate Ecclesiæ, propter cultum divinum, dum alter eorum vel uterque ingredi vult religionem. Verumtamen quomodocumque separentur, vinculum matrimonii permanet altero vivente, quemadmodum ait Apostolus: Mulier alligata est legi, quamdiu vivit vir ejus.
paras.en: From which the Saviour concludes: [[19:6|Therefore now|Itaque jam]], that is, after the union of marriage, [[19:6|they are not two|non sunt duo]]: the husband and his wife are not two who can be separated from each other, [[19:6|but one flesh|sed una caro]]: that is, they are joined as indissolubly as if they were wholly one flesh. And in a way they are one flesh, since the flesh of the one is in the power of the other, and the other way round, as the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 7:4|the husband also hath not power of his own body: but the wife|Vir sui corporis non habet potestatem, sed mulier]]; and likewise [[1 Cor 7:4|The wife hath not power of her own body: but the husband|mulier sui corporis potestatem non habet, sed vir]]. From this He draws a most firm answer: [[19:6|What therefore God hath joined together|Quod ergo Deus conjunxit]], that is, the man and the woman whom God has united so inseparably, [[19:6|let no man put asunder|homo non separet]] by human authority and his own will, for any cause whatever. They can, however, be separated as to living together and the obligation of rendering the debt [that is, the marriage right], by their common consent and the authority of the Church, for the sake of divine worship, when one or both of them wishes to enter religion. Yet however they are separated, the bond of marriage remains while the other lives, as the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 7:39|A woman is bound by the law as long as her husband liveth|Mulier alligata est legi, quamdiu vivit vir ejus]].

paras.t: Dicunt illi, videlicet Pharisæi Christo, objiciendo ejus responsioni: Quid ergo, id est, si ita est ut asseris, cur Moyses, ex parte Dei, mandavit viris dare libellum repudii, id est scripturam continentem causam divortii, et dimittere? Quando enim maritus voluit uxorem dimittere, redegit in scriptis causam separationis, et dedit uxori, vel præsentavit eam superiori.
paras.en: [[19:7|They say to him|Dicunt illi]], namely the Pharisees to Christ, objecting to His answer: [[19:7|Why then|Quid ergo]], that is, if it is as you say, why [[19:7|did Moses command|Moyses mandavit]], on God's behalf, men [[19:7|to give a bill of divorce|dare libellum repudii]][[Deut 24:1||]], that is, a writing setting out the cause of the divorce, [[19:7|and to put away|et dimittere]]? For when a husband wished to put away his wife, he set down the cause of the separation in writing and gave it to the wife, or presented it to a superior.

paras.t: Ait illis Jesus: Quoniam Moyses ad, id est propter, duritiam cordis vestri permisit, non jussit, vobis dimittere uxores vestras: non quasi dimissio illa sit in se bona ac licita, sed propter deterius malum vitandum, videlicet, ne eas occideretis, quia crudeles, duri et invidi semper fuistis. Simili ratione permisit usuram ad extraneos. Ab initio autem mundi, videlicet tempore legis naturalis, non fuit sic: quia non licuit ante tempora Moysis dare libellum repudii, eo quod indivisibilitas sit de ratione matrimonii, quod sic definitur: Matrimonium est conjunctio maris et feminæ inter legitimas personas, individuam vitæ consuetudinem retinens. Dico autem vobis, quia quicumque dimiserit uxorem suam, nisi ob fornicationem, id est adulterium: propter quod dimittenda est, si perseveret in eo, ne maritus videatur ejus malitiæ consentire, et quia ex adulterio sequeretur incertitudo de prole cujus esset, ut patris; et aliam duxerit, illa vivente, mœchatur, adulterium committendo. Nam vinculum manet, ut dictum est. Et qui dimissam feminam duxerit atque cognoverit, priori viro vivente, mœchatur. Ipsa quoque sic ducta, mœchatur, sicut Apostolus ait: Si fuerit cum alio viro, vocabitur adultera.
paras.en: [[19:8|He saith to them|Ait illis]] Jesus: [[19:8|Because Moses by reason of the hardness of your heart permitted|Quoniam Moyses ad duritiam cordis vestri permisit]], not commanded, [[19:8|you to put away your wives|vobis dimittere uxores vestras]]: not as if that putting away were good and lawful in itself, but to avoid a worse evil, namely lest you should kill them, since you have always been cruel, hard and envious. For a like reason he permitted usury towards strangers[[Deut 23:19||]][[Deut 23:20||]]. [[19:8|but from the beginning|Ab initio autem]] of the world, namely in the time of the natural law, [[19:8|it was not so|non fuit sic]]: for before the time of Moses it was not lawful to give a bill of divorce, since indivisibility belongs to the very nature of marriage, which is defined thus: Marriage is the union of a man and a woman between lawful persons, maintaining an undivided partnership of life. [[19:9|And I say to you, that whosoever shall put away his wife|Dico autem vobis, quia quicumque dimiserit uxorem suam]], [[19:9|except it be for fornication|nisi ob fornicationem]], that is, adultery (for which she is to be put away if she persists in it, lest the husband seem to consent to her wickedness, and because adultery would bring uncertainty as to whose the offspring was, as to the father), [[19:9|and shall marry another|et aliam duxerit]] while she lives, [[19:9|committeth adultery|mœchatur]]; for the bond remains, as was said. [[19:9|and he that shall marry her that is put away|Et qui dimissam feminam duxerit]] and know her while her former husband lives, [[19:9|committeth adultery|mœchatur]]. She too, so married, commits adultery, as the Apostle says: [[Rom 7:3|she shall be called an adulteress, if she be with another man|vocabitur adultera si fuerit cum alio viro]].

paras.t: Dicunt ei discipuli ejus, non objiciendo, ut Pharisæi, sed ut instruantur et certificentur a summo magistro: Si ita est causa, id est negotium, hominis cum uxore, videlicet, quod insolubile vinculum permanet inter eos, nec separari possunt nisi ob fornicationem, secundum sensum prætactum, non expedit nubere: non solum ob hoc quod status matrimonialis minus meritorius est quam status virginalis, sed etiam propter servitutem, et incommoda vitæ præsentis, ut si mulier fuerit litigiosa, gulosa, inverecunda, vel gravem seu incurabilem morbum incurrat. Unde in Ecclesiastico habetur: Omnis plaga tristitia cordis, et omnis malitia nequitia mulieris; rursusque, Commorari leoni et draconi placebit, quam cum muliere nequam. Hinc dicit Apostolus: Beatior erit, si sic permanserit secundum meum consilium; et item, Tribulationem carnis habebunt hujusmodi.
paras.en: [[19:10|His disciples say unto him|Dicunt ei discipuli ejus]], not objecting like the Pharisees, but so as to be taught and made certain by the supreme Master: [[19:10|If the case|Si ita est causa]], that is, the business, [[19:10|of a man with his wife be so|hominis cum uxore]], namely, that an indissoluble bond remains between them and they cannot be separated except for fornication, in the sense touched on above, [[19:10|it is not expedient to marry|non expedit nubere]]: not only because the married state is less meritorious than the state of virginity, but also because of the servitude and the troubles of the present life, as when a wife is quarrelsome, greedy, shameless, or falls into a grave or incurable sickness. Hence it is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 25:17|The sadness of the heart is every plague: and the wickedness of a woman is all evil.|Omnis plaga tristitia cordis, et omnis malitia nequitia mulieris]]; and again, [[Ecclus 25:23|It will be more agreeable to abide with a lion and a dragon, than to dwell with a wicked woman|Commorari leoni et draconi placebit, quam cum muliere nequam]]. Hence the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 7:40|more blessed shall she be, if she so remain, according to my counsel|Beatior erit, si sic permanserit secundum meum consilium]]; and again, [[1 Cor 7:28|such shall have tribulation of the flesh|Tribulationem carnis habebunt hujusmodi]].

paras.t: Qui dixit illis suis discipulis: Non omnes capiunt, per acceptationem et saporem, verbum istud, videlicet, quod non expedit nubere: id est, omnibus non apparet hoc, nec sic sentiunt, neque virginalem continentiam apprehendunt propter suam perfectionem; sed quibus datum est, id est, quibus Dominus per gratiam dat sic sentire et operari. Nemo enim potest esse continens, nisi Deus det, ut Sapiens inquit. Denique ad hoc ostendendum, ponit Salvator triplicem continentiam: quarum tertia habetur per gratiam, et est virtuosa; aliæ duæ sunt naturales vel necessariæ. Sunt enim eunuchi qui de matris utero sic nati sunt, hoc est naturaliter frigidi, voluptatem non appetentes, seu genitalibus membris privati. Et sunt eunuchi qui facti sunt ab hominibus, id est, castrati, quorum secantur genitalia. Isti sunt corporales eunuchi, quorum continentia in se meritoria non est: si tamen sponte acceptetur, potest esse laudabilis. Et sunt eunuchi qui se ipsos castraverunt, hoc est, usum genitalium sibi voluntarie subtraxerunt, omnino caste vivendo, propter regnum cælorum, id est amore felicitatis cælestis, ut eam copiosius adipiscantur per hoc quod nunc continenter vivunt, ut spirituali dilectione fortius accendantur, divinorumque contemplationi liberius, purius, atque stabilius vacent, imo angelicam vitam ducant in carne. Qui enim sine uxore est, teste Apostolo, sollicitus est quæ sunt Domini, quomodo placeat Deo; qui autem cum uxore est, sollicitus est quæ sunt mundi, quomodo placeat uxori, et divisus est. Horum continentia sancta ac meritoria est, et tanto virtuosior quanto laboriosior. Ideo subdit: Qui potest capere, id est verba hæc perfectæ continentiæ digne intelligere, efficaciterque implere, capiat ea hoc modo. Nec enim oportet. Quoniam tam sublimis perfectio supererogationis est, non præcepti, hoc ait Salvator hortando, suosque pugiles ad pudicitiæ præmia excitando.
paras.en: [[19:11|Who said to them|Qui dixit illis]], to His disciples: [[19:11|All men take not|Non omnes capiunt]], by accepting and relishing it, [[19:11|this word|verbum istud]], namely, that it is not expedient to marry: that is, it does not seem so to all, nor do all feel so, nor do all lay hold of virginal continence for the sake of its perfection; [[19:11|but they to whom it is given|sed quibus datum est]], that is, those to whom the Lord by grace gives to feel and act so. For no one can [[Wis 8:21|be continent, except God gave it|esse continens, nisi Deus det]], as the Wise Man says. Lastly, to show this, the Saviour sets out three kinds of continence, the third of which is had through grace and is virtuous, while the other two are natural or forced. [[19:12|For there are eunuchs, who were born so from their mothers womb|Sunt enim eunuchi qui de matris utero sic nati sunt]], that is, naturally cold, not desiring pleasure, or lacking the organs of generation. [[19:12|and there are eunuchs, who were made so by men|Et sunt eunuchi qui facti sunt ab hominibus]], that is, castrated, whose organs are cut off. These are bodily eunuchs, whose continence is not meritorious in itself, though if it is willingly accepted it can be praiseworthy. [[19:12|and there are eunuchs, who have made themselves eunuchs|Et sunt eunuchi qui se ipsos castraverunt]], that is, have of their own will withdrawn from themselves the use of the organs of generation, living altogether chastely, [[19:12|for the kingdom of heaven|propter regnum cælorum]], that is, for love of heavenly happiness, so as to gain it more abundantly by living in continence now, to be more strongly kindled with spiritual love, and to give themselves to the contemplation of divine things more freely, purely and steadily; indeed, to lead the life of angels in the flesh. For, as the Apostle witnesses, [[1 Cor 7:32|He that is without a wife is solicitous for the things that belong to the Lord: how he may please God|Qui enim sine uxore est, teste Apostolo, sollicitus est quæ sunt Domini, quomodo placeat Deo]]; [[1 Cor 7:33|But he that is with a wife is solicitous for the things of the world: how he may please his wife. And he is divided.|qui autem cum uxore est, sollicitus est quæ sunt mundi, quomodo placeat uxori, et divisus est]]. The continence of these is holy and meritorious, and the more virtuous the more laborious it is. So He adds: [[19:12|He that can take|Qui potest capere]], that is, worthily understand these words of perfect continence and carry them out effectively, [[19:12|let him take it|capiat]] in this way. For it is not obligatory: since so lofty a perfection is a matter of supererogation, not of precept, the Saviour says this by way of exhortation, rousing His champions to the rewards of chastity.

paras.t: Tunc oblati sunt ei parvuli, forte a parentibus, ut manus eis imponeret, benedicendo eos hoc modo, et oraret pro eis. Judæi namque scientes Patriarchas benedixisse filiis suis per manuum impositionem, et orationem, videntesque Christi sanctitatem et efficaciam, ex devotione obtulerunt ei parvulos suos.
paras.en: [[19:13|Then were little children presented to him|Tunc oblati sunt ei parvuli]], perhaps by their parents, [[19:13|that he should impose hands upon them|ut manus eis imponeret]], blessing them in this way, [[19:13|and pray|et oraret]] for them. For the Jews, knowing that the Patriarchs had blessed their sons by the laying on of hands and by prayer, and seeing Christ's holiness and power, offered Him their little ones out of devotion.

paras.t: Discipuli autem increpabant eos, videlicet offerentes, non parvulos oblatos. Viderunt enim discipuli magistrum suum multis laboribus itineris ac sermonis lassatum. Propter quod putabant eum offerentium importunitate et oblatorum benedictione posse gravari. Chrysostomus reprehendit in hoc facto discipulos. Nam paulo ante, vocato ad se parvulo, eoque in medio constituto, hortatus fuit discipulos ad parvulorum similitudinem ac imitationem, dicendo: Nisi conversi fueritis, et efficiamini sicut parvuli, non intrabitis in regnum cælorum. Jesus autem ait eis, puta discipulis: Sinite parvulos istos, ætate et corpore parvos, et nolite eos prohibere ad me venire, ut benedicantur. Nemo ergo quantumcumque sublimis aut sapiens, pusillos contemnat et tangere dedignetur, quum videat Christum Dominum universorum, et sapientiæ fontem, parvulos tam dignanter ac dulciter recepisse, tetigisse, ac benedixisse. Talium est enim regnum cælorum. Non dicit, Istorum; sed, Talium, utpote humilium, obedientium, simplicium et castorum, qui figurantur per parvulos, et spiritualiter atque salubriter parvuli appellantur. Nihilominus, parvulorum qui remedium contra originale peccatum sortiti sunt, est regnum cælorum, secundum id quod jam sunt, et secundum præsentem justitiam, quamvis interdum crescendo pejorentur ac pereant.
paras.en: [[19:13|And the disciples rebuked them|Discipuli autem increpabant eos]], that is, those who brought them, not the little ones who were brought. For the disciples saw their Master wearied by much toil of travel and preaching, and so they thought He might be burdened by the importunity of those who brought them and by blessing those brought. Chrysostom blames the disciples in this. For a little before, having called a little child to Him and set him in the midst[[Matt 18:2||]], He had exhorted the disciples to become like little children and to imitate them, saying: [[Matt 18:3|unless you be converted, and become as little children, you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven|Nisi conversi fueritis, et efficiamini sicut parvuli, non intrabitis in regnum cælorum]]. [[19:14|But Jesus said to them|Jesus autem ait eis]], that is, to the disciples: [[19:14|Suffer the little children|Sinite parvulos]], these who are little in age and body, [[19:14|and forbid them not to come to me|et nolite eos prohibere ad me venire]], to be blessed. Let no one, then, however exalted or wise, despise the little ones and disdain to touch them, when he sees that Christ, the Lord of all and the fountain of wisdom, received, touched and blessed little children so graciously and sweetly. [[19:14|for the kingdom of heaven is for such|Talium est enim regnum cælorum]]. He does not say "of these" but "of such": that is, of the humble, obedient, simple and chaste, who are figured by little children and are called little children in a spiritual and wholesome sense. Nonetheless the kingdom of heaven belongs to the little ones who have received the remedy against original sin, according to what they now are and their present justice, although sometimes as they grow they become worse and perish.

paras.t: Et quum imposuisset illis manus suas superdignissimas, divinæ virtutis sacratissima instrumenta, parvulis benedicendo, et pro eis orando. Unde in Marco scriptum est: Complexans eos et imponens manus super illos, benedicebat eos. Abiit inde.
paras.en: [[19:15|And when he had imposed hands upon them|Et quum imposuisset illis manus]], His most worthy hands, the most sacred instruments of divine power, blessing the little ones and praying for them. Hence it is written in Mark: [[Mark 10:16|And embracing them and laying his hands upon them, he blessed them.|Complexans eos et imponens manus super illos, benedicebat eos]]. [[19:15|he departed from thence|Abiit inde]].

paras.t: Et ecce unus accedens, ait illi. Iste unus secundum Matthæum, fuit adolescens; et secundum Lucam, fuit princeps, videlicet nobilis, dives et potens, habens subjectos. Magister bone, id est, juste et sapiens, qui agis quod doces. Non enim sola doctrina, sed vita cum documentis bonum facit magistrum. Unde superius dictum est: Qui fecerit et docuerit, magnus vocabitur. Secundum quosdam, adolescens iste superbus fuit, et non voto discentis, hoc est intentione discendi, sed tentantis, interrogat. Sed obviare videtur quod apud Marcum de adolescente isto narratur, videlicet quod præcucurrit, et genu flexo coram Jesu, dixit quæ subjunguntur; et post pauca, quum adolescens dixisset se omnia præcepta a juventute servasse, subditur: Intuitus eum Jesus, dilexit eum. Ex quo evidenter monstratur, quod verum dixit, justusque fuit, et bona intentione quæsivit. Et hoc etiam asserit Beda, et innotescit ex subditis. Itaque, Magister bone, quid boni faciam, id est, quid meritorium operabor, quoniam fides sine operibus mortua est, ut habeam vitam æternam pro mercede post vitam hanc temporalem?
paras.en: [[19:16|And behold one came and said to him|Et ecce unus accedens, ait illi]]. This one, according to Matthew, was a young man[[19:20||]][[19:22||]]; and according to Luke he was a ruler[[Luke 18:18||]], that is, noble, rich and powerful, with men under him. [[19:16|Good master|Magister bone]], that is, just and wise, you who do what you teach. For it is not teaching alone but life together with teaching that makes a good master. Hence it was said above: [[Matt 5:19|he that shall do and teach, he shall be called great|Qui fecerit et docuerit, magnus vocabitur]]. According to some, this young man was proud, and asks not with the wish of a learner, that is, with the intention of learning, but of one tempting. But against this seems to be what is told of this young man in Mark, namely that he ran up and, kneeling before Jesus, said what follows[[Mark 10:17||]]; and a little after, when the young man had said that he had kept all the commandments from his youth, it is added: [[Mark 10:21|Jesus, looking on him, loved him|Intuitus eum Jesus, dilexit eum]]. From this it is plainly shown that he spoke the truth, was just, and asked with a good intention. Bede also asserts this, and it is made known by what follows. So: [[19:16|what good shall I do|quid boni faciam]], that is, what meritorious thing shall I do (since [[Jas 2:20|faith without works is dead|fides sine operibus mortua est]][[Jas 2:26||]]), [[19:16|that I may have life everlasting|ut habeam vitam æternam]] as a reward after this temporal life?

paras.t: Qui dixit ei: Quid me interrogas de bono? id est, cur interrogando appellas me bonum? Unus est bonus, Deus, id est, Dominus dumtaxat bonus est. Unde in Marco apertius legitur: Quid me dicis bonum? Nemo bonus, nisi unus Deus.
paras.en: [[19:17|Who said to him: Why askest thou me concerning good|Qui dixit ei: Quid me interrogas de bono]]? That is, why in asking do you call me good? [[19:17|One is good, God|Unus est bonus, Deus]]: that is, the Lord alone is good. Hence in Mark it reads more plainly: [[Mark 10:18|Why callest thou me good? None is good but one, that is God|Quid me dicis bonum? Nemo bonus, nisi unus Deus]].

paras.t: Sed cur Christus arguit adolescentem, quum ipse profecto bonus sit, tanquam verus Deus, et se ipsum bonum appellet apud Joannem: Ego, inquiens, sum pastor bonus; et alibi, An oculus tuus nequam est, quia ego bonus sum? Et respondetur, quod Jesus respondit ad mentem, non ad verba quærentis. Adolescens enim putavit eum hominem purum, idcirco vocavit eum bonum per bonitatis participationem dumtaxat. Jesus vero ostendere volens, quod qui sic de se ipso sentit, non debeat ipsum dicere bonum, loquendo de bono secundum perfectam rationem ipsius, dixit: Quid me interrogas de bono? Est ergo pensandum, quod res dicitur bona dupliciter. Primo, per essentiam, universaliter et perfecte: cui videlicet convenit plenitudo bonitatis quomodolibet atque simpliciter, ita quod bonitas ejus est omniformiter seu in omni nobilitate et beatitudine penitus infinita. Et ita nullus est bonus, nisi Deus verus, quemadmodum nullus dicitur esse vel justus aut sapiens, nisi Deus. Secundo, dicitur aliquid bonum per participationem et in genere: sicque creatura dicitur bona. Vidit enim Deus cuncta quæ fecit, et erant valde bona. Et juxta Apostolum: Omnis creatura Dei bona est. Utroque autem modo fuit et est Dominus Jesus excellentissime bonus: quia secundum naturam divinam, est bonus primo modo, et eadem numero bonitas cum Patre, quemadmodum ait: Ego et Pater unum sumus. Secundum naturam vero humanam, est bonus secundo modo: et sic major est bonitas ejus quam totius universi, non quod ejus humanitas dignior sit humanitate aliorum dignitate naturæ, sed gratiæ. Porro in hac auctoritate Christi qua ait, Nemo bonus, nisi Deus, videtur se fundasse beatissimus theologorum dux, S. Dionysius, asserendo quod bonum sit primum atque potissimum nomen Dei.
paras.en: But why does Christ reprove the young man, since He Himself is truly good, as true God, and calls Himself good in John, saying, [[John 10:11|I am the good shepherd|Ego, inquiens, sum pastor bonus]][[John 10:14||]]; and elsewhere, [[Matt 20:15|Is thy eye evil, because I am good|An oculus tuus nequam est, quia ego bonus sum?]]? The answer is that Jesus answered the mind, not the words, of the questioner. For the young man thought Him a mere man, and therefore called Him good only by participation in goodness. But Jesus, wishing to show that one who thinks so of Him ought not to call Him good, speaking of the good in its perfect sense, said: [[19:17|Why askest thou me concerning good|Quid me interrogas de bono]]? We must consider, then, that a thing is called good in two ways. First, by essence, universally and perfectly: that is, a thing to which the fullness of goodness belongs in every way and simply, so that its goodness is in every form, or in every nobility and beatitude, wholly infinite. And in this way none is good but the true God, just as none is said to be either just or wise except God. Secondly, a thing is called good by participation and within a genus: and so a creature is called good. For [[Gen 1:31|God saw all the things that he had made, and they were very good|Vidit enim Deus cuncta quæ fecit, et erant valde bona]]. And according to the Apostle: [[1 Tim 4:4|every creature of God is good|Omnis creatura Dei bona est]]. In both ways the Lord Jesus was and is most excellently good: for according to the divine nature He is good in the first way, and His goodness is numerically one with the Father's, as He says: [[John 10:30|I and the Father are one.|Ego et Pater unum sumus]]. But according to the human nature He is good in the second way, and so His goodness is greater than that of the whole universe; not that His humanity is worthier than the humanity of others in dignity of nature, but of grace. Moreover, on this saying of Christ, None is good but God, the most blessed leader of theologians, St. Dionysius, seems to have based himself in asserting that Good is the first and chief name of God.

paras.t: Deinde respondet Salvator ad verba adolescentis, qui præinductam responsionem patienter sustinuit. Si vis ad vitam gloriæ ingredi, id est æternam beatitudinem adipisci, serva mandata Decalogi. Tanquam dicat: Hoc requiritur et sufficit ad salutem. Unde in Proverbiis habetur: Serva mandata et legem, quasi pupillam oculi tui; liga eam in digitis tuis, et in tabulis cordis scribe. Et in Ecclesiastico: Si volueris mandata custodire, conservabunt te.
paras.en: Then the Saviour answers the young man's words, he having borne patiently the answer just given. [[19:17|But if thou wilt enter into life|Si … vis ad vitam … ingredi]] of glory, that is, gain eternal beatitude, [[19:17|keep the commandments|serva mandata]] of the Decalogue. As if to say: This is required and is enough for salvation. Hence it is said in Proverbs: [[Prov 7:2|Keep my commandments|Serva mandata]] [[Prov 7:2|and my law as the apple of thy eye|et legem, quasi pupillam oculi tui]]; [[Prov 7:3|Bind it upon thy fingers, write it upon the tables of thy heart.|liga eam in digitis tuis, et in tabulis cordis scribe]]. And in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 15:16|If thou wilt keep the commandments|Si volueris mandata custodire]] [[Ecclus 15:16|they shall preserve thee|conservabunt te]].

paras.t: Dicit ei adolescens: Quæ, scilicet mandata servabo, ut vitam ingrediar? Hoc quærit, quoniam legis præcepta erant triplicia, utpote moralia, judicialia, cærimonialia. Jesus autem dixit, nominando quædam præcepta moralia secundæ tabulæ, quæ ordinant hominem ad proximum: Non homicidium facies, prætermisso ordine juris; alias licitum erat, secundum quod Moyses dixit: Maleficos non patieris vivere. Secundum Joannem, Omnis qui odit fratrem suum, homicida est. Ambrosius quoque: Pasce, inquit, fame periclitantem; si non paveris, occidisti. Judæi autem occiderunt Christum lingua, consilio et consensu. Cain vero occidit Abel propria manu. Omnia ergo homicidia ista prohibita sunt. Non adulterabis; non facies furtum; non falsum testimonium dices; honora patrem et matrem; et diliges proximum tuum sicut te ipsum. Qui enim diligit proximum, legem implevit.
paras.en: [[19:18|He said to him: Which|Dicit ei adolescens: Quæ]]? says the young man: that is, which commandments shall I keep, that I may enter into life? He asks this because the precepts of the Law were of three kinds: moral, judicial and ceremonial. [[19:18|And Jesus said|Jesus autem dixit]], naming certain moral precepts of the second table, which order man towards his neighbour: [[19:18|Thou shalt do no murder|Non homicidium facies]][[Ex 20:13||]], without the order of law, for otherwise it was lawful, as Moses said: [[Ex 22:18|Wizards thou shalt not suffer to live|Maleficos non patieris vivere]]. According to John, [[1 John 3:15|Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer|Omnis qui odit fratrem suum, homicida est]]. Ambrose also says: Feed him who is perishing of hunger; if you have not fed him, you have killed him. The Jews killed Christ by tongue, counsel and consent; but Cain killed Abel with his own hand. All these killings, then, are forbidden. [[19:18|Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not bear false witness|Non adulterabis; non facies furtum; non falsum testimonium dices]][[Ex 20:14||]][[Ex 20:15||]][[Ex 20:16||]]; [[19:19|Honour thy father and thy mother|honora patrem et matrem]][[Ex 20:12||]]: [[19:19|and, Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself|et diliges proximum tuum sicut te ipsum]][[Lev 19:18||]]. For [[Rom 13:8|he that loveth his neighbour hath fulfilled the law|Qui enim diligit proximum, legem implevit]].

paras.t: Dicit illi adolescens: Omnia hæc custodivi a juventute mea, et per consequens alia præcepta moralia hic non expressa. Non enim diligitur proximus, nisi diligatur et Deus. Quid adhuc mihi deest, ut sim perfectus ac tuus discipulus? Ait illi Jesus: Si vis perfectus esse, opera supererogationis faciendo atque evangelica consilia amplectendo, vade, id est, a temporalium rerum affectu recede, et corporaliter perge ad emptores, si opus est, et vende omnia quæ habes, videlicet mobilia et immobilia, et da pauperibus pretia eorum. Majus enim est omnia simul pro Christo relinquere, quam ea paulatim indigentibus communicare, ut sit homo penitus liber et expeditus a cura, affectu et onere temporalium divitiarum, totusque intendat spiritualibus bonis. Et habebis thesaurum, id est copiosam et supereffluentem remunerationem ac possessionem, multo pleniorem quam qui sola præcepta custodiunt, in cælo empyreo, quod est mansio Beatorum. Et veni corporis gressu, mentisque sincero affectu, et sequere me, pauperem vitam ducendo, et perfectionis opera exercendo.
paras.en: [[19:20|The young man saith to him: All these have I kept from my youth|Dicit illi adolescens: Omnia hæc custodivi a juventute mea]], and in consequence the other moral precepts not mentioned here; for one's neighbour is not loved unless God also is loved. [[19:20|what is yet wanting to me|Quid adhuc mihi deest]], that I may be perfect and your disciple? [[19:21|Jesus saith to him: If thou wilt be perfect|Ait illi Jesus: Si vis perfectus esse]], by doing works of supererogation and embracing the evangelical counsels, [[19:21|go|vade]], that is, withdraw from attachment to temporal things, and go in body to the buyers if need be, [[19:21|sell what thou hast|vende omnia quæ habes]], namely movables and immovables, [[19:21|and give to the poor|et da pauperibus]] their price. For it is a greater thing to leave everything at once for Christ than to share it with the needy little by little, so that a man may be wholly free and unencumbered of the care, attachment and burden of temporal riches, and give himself wholly to spiritual goods. [[19:21|and thou shalt have treasure|Et habebis thesaurum]], that is, a plentiful and overflowing reward and possession, much fuller than those who keep the commandments only, [[19:21|in heaven|in cælo]], the empyrean heaven, which is the dwelling of the Blessed. [[19:21|and come|Et veni]] with the steps of the body and the sincere affection of the mind, [[19:21|follow me|sequere me]], leading a poor life and practising the works of perfection.

paras.t: Quum audisset autem adolescens verbum hoc de venditione prædicta, abiit tristis, vel quia doluit se interrogasse, vel quia vidit viam perfectionis esse difficilem, vel quia debebat facere quod audivit. Erat enim habens multas possessiones, hoc est divitias. Ex quo patet, quod licet fuerit justus servando præcepta, caritatem Dei temporalibus omnibus præferendo, non tamen erat perfectus, qui temporalibus aliqualiter inordinate adhæsit, nec tam fervens erat in divino amore, quod pro Deo vellet cuncta relinquere. Tales sunt multi. Nam plures sunt cum custodia præceptorum contenti, nec statum superiorem volunt arripere: quos certum est in ampliori esse periculo.
paras.en: [[19:22|And when the young man had heard this word|Quum audisset autem adolescens verbum]] about the selling just mentioned, [[19:22|he went away sad|abiit tristis]]: either because he was sorry he had asked, or because he saw that the way of perfection was hard, or because he ought to do what he had heard [the margin gives another reading, tædebat: "because it irked him to do"]. [[19:22|for he had great possessions|Erat enim habens multas possessiones]], that is, riches. From this it is clear that, though he was just in keeping the commandments and putting the love of God before all temporal things, he was not perfect, since he clung to temporal things in a somewhat disordered way and was not so fervent in divine love as to be willing to leave all things for God. Many are like this. For many are content with keeping the commandments and do not wish to take up a higher state; and it is certain that they are in greater danger.

paras.t: Jesus autem dixit discipulis suis: Amen dico vobis, quia dives, id est in temporalibus bonis abundans, difficile, id est difficulter, intrabit in regnum cælorum, quod est pauperum, ita ut transeat de divitiis ad divitias. Difficile ergo est, non impossibile, divitem salvari, quoniam difficillimum est in temporalibus abundare, et ea non inordinate amare, esse in divitiis, et non uti deliciis, ab aliis propter divitias honorari, et non extolli, nec mundi vanitates sectari. Ad insinuandum enim quam rarum atque difficile sit locupletem esse justum, non cupidum, dicitur in Ecclesiastico: Beatus dives qui inventus est sine macula, qui post aurum non abiit, nec speravit in pecuniæ thesauris. Quis est hic? et laudabimus eum. Fecit enim mirabilia in vita sua. Verumtamen multi fuerunt ditissimi, et tamen non cupidi, ut Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Booz. Talis fuit et David, qui cunctis divitibus saluberrimum dedit consilium, dicens: Divitiæ si affluant, nolite cor apponere. Et iterum ait: Ego sum vir pauper et tenuis. Dives ergo difficulter salvatur, quia divitiæ sunt spinæ ac tribuli suffocantes verbum Dei. Nec solum dives, sed et divitias appetens, quum tamen facilius sit divitias nondum adeptas quam jam possessas non immoderate amare. Dicit namque Apostolus: Qui volunt divites fieri, incidunt in tentationem et laqueum diaboli. Difficile quoque est diviti implere illud Joannis Baptistæ: Qui habet duas tunicas, id est superfluas, det non habenti; et qui habet escas, similiter faciat.
paras.en: [[19:23|Then Jesus said to his disciples: Amen, I say to you, that a rich man|Jesus autem dixit discipulis suis: Amen dico vobis, quia dives]], that is, one abounding in temporal goods, [[19:23|shall hardly enter into the kingdom of heaven|difficile intrabit in regnum cælorum]], which belongs to the poor[[Matt 5:3||]], so as to pass from riches to riches. It is hard, then, not impossible, for a rich man to be saved: for it is very hard to abound in temporal things and not to love them inordinately, to be among riches and not use them for pleasures, to be honoured by others for one's riches and not be puffed up nor follow the vanities of the world. To suggest how rare and hard it is for a wealthy man to be just and not covetous, it is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 31:8|Blessed is the rich man that is found without blemish: and that hath not gone after gold, nor put his trust in money nor in treasures|Beatus dives qui inventus est sine macula, qui post aurum non abiit, nec speravit in pecuniæ thesauris]]. [[Ecclus 31:9|Who is he, and we will praise him? for he hath done wonderful things in his life.|Quis est hic? et laudabimus eum. Fecit enim mirabilia in vita sua]]. Yet many have been very rich and yet not covetous, as Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Booz. Such too was David, who gave all the rich a most wholesome counsel, saying: [[Ps 61:11|if riches abound, set not your heart upon them|Divitiæ si affluant, nolite cor apponere]]. And again he says: [[1 Kings 18:23|I am a poor man, and of small ability|Ego sum vir pauper et tenuis]]. The rich man, then, is hardly saved, because riches are thorns and briars choking the word of God[[Matt 13:22||]]. And not only the rich man but also the one who craves riches, though it is easier not to love immoderately riches not yet gained than those already possessed. For the Apostle says: [[1 Tim 6:9|they that will become rich fall into temptation and into the snare of the devil|Qui volunt divites fieri, incidunt in tentationem et laqueum diaboli]]. It is hard too for a rich man to fulfil that saying of John the Baptist: [[Luke 3:11|He that hath two coats|Qui habet duas tunicas]], that is, superfluous ones, [[Luke 3:11|let him give to him that hath none; and he that hath meat, let him do in like manner|det non habenti; et qui habet escas, similiter faciat]].

paras.t: Et iterum dico vobis: Facilius est camelum per foramen acus transire: quod naturaliter impossibile est, non tamen omnipotentiæ Dei, quæ posset modicum quid in camelum transsubstantiare, atque per foramen acus transducere; quam divitem intrare in regnum cælorum. Si acceperimus divitem hoc loco sicut in verbo immediate prædicto, oportet fateri quod his verbis non denotatur nisi maxima difficultas salvationis divitis: ita quod dives naturali virtute salvari non valeat, sicut nec camelus per foramen acus transire, et Deus sua omnipotentia mirabilius ac vigorosius utatur salvando divitem, quam ducendo camelum per acus foramen. Sic namque, secundum Augustinum, majus est impium justificare quam mundum creare: cujus creatio non est minoris admirationis, incomprehensibilitatis atque potentiæ, quam transductio cameli per acum. Communiter vero expositores hoc loco accipiunt divitem pro inordinato et cupido divitiarum amatore, qui majorem fiduciam et amorem habet in eis quam in Deo. Talem autem salvari impossibile est, loquendo de potentia Dei ordinata. Huic expositioni favere potest, quod prædictis verbis Christus præmittit apud Marcum: Filioli, inquiens, quam difficile est confidentem in divitiis introire in regnum cælorum! Unde Apostolus ait ad Timotheum: Divitibus hujus sæculi præcipe non sublime sapere, nec sperare in incerto divitiarum. Talis fuit dives et sanctus Job, qui ait: Si putavi aurum robur meum, et obryzo dixi, Fiducia mea; si lætatus sum super divitiis meis.
paras.en: [[19:24|And again I say to you: It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle|Et iterum dico vobis: Facilius est camelum per foramen acus transire]] (which is impossible in nature, though not to the omnipotence of God, which could transubstantiate some small thing into a camel and lead it through the eye of a needle), [[19:24|than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of heaven|quam divitem intrare in regnum cælorum]]. If we take "rich man" here as in the saying just before, we must admit that these words signify only the very great difficulty of a rich man's salvation: so that a rich man cannot be saved by natural power, any more than a camel can pass through the eye of a needle, and God uses His omnipotence more wonderfully and mightily in saving a rich man than in leading a camel through the eye of a needle. For so, according to Augustine, it is greater to justify the wicked than to create the world, whose creation is no less a matter of wonder, incomprehensibility and power than the passing of a camel through a needle. But the commentators commonly take "rich man" here to mean an inordinate and covetous lover of riches, who has more trust in them and love for them than for God. Such a one cannot be saved, speaking of the ordained power of God [that is, God's power as it acts within the order He has decreed, as distinct from His absolute power]. This exposition may be favoured by the fact that in Mark Christ puts before these words: [[Mark 10:24|Children, how hard is it for them that trust in riches to enter into the kingdom of God?|Filioli, inquiens, quam difficile est confidentem in divitiis introire in regnum cælorum!]]! Hence the Apostle says to Timothy: [[1 Tim 6:17|Charge the rich of this world not to be highminded nor to trust in the uncertainty of riches|Divitibus hujus sæculi præcipe non sublime sapere, nec sperare in incerto divitiarum]]. Such a rich man, and a holy one, was Job, who says: [[Job 31:24|If I have thought gold my strength, and have said to fine gold: My confidence:|Si putavi aurum robur meum, et obryzo dixi, Fiducia mea]]; [[Job 31:25|If I have rejoiced over my great riches|si lætatus sum super divitiis meis]].

paras.t: Auditis autem his verbis, omni diviti vehementissime metuendis, discipuli mirabantur valde, propter novitatem et arduitatem hujus doctrinæ toti sæculo prius inauditæ. Novam nempe et supernaturalem doctrinam cælestis magister advexit atque deprompsit. Dicentes ad invicem: Quis ergo poterit salvus esse, si tam arduum est iter ad regnum cæleste? Quasi dicant: Pene nullus, quum multa sint vitia graviora quam amor divitiarum superfluus. Adspiciens autem Jesus pavorem angustiamque ipsorum, dixit illis: Apud homines hoc impossibile est, id est, humana et naturali potestate fieri nequit ut dives salvetur, vel camelus per foramen acus ducatur; apud Deum autem, id est omnipotentiæ Dei, omnia possibilia sunt quibus non repugnat ratio entis, videlicet quæ contradictionem non implicant. Ideo Deus potest hominem in temporalibus abundantem præservare a culpa, potest quoque divitem vitiosum per gratiam immutare, ut bene utatur divitiis et salvetur: gratia enim Dei vita æterna. Mentitur ergo Pelagius, dicens hominem sine gratia posse justificari.
paras.en: [[19:25|And when they had heard this|Auditis autem his]] words, which every rich man should fear most vehemently, [[19:25|the disciples wondered much|discipuli mirabantur valde]], because of the newness and difficulty of this teaching, unheard of before by the whole world: for the heavenly Master brought and set forth a new and supernatural teaching. [[19:25|saying|Dicentes]] to one another: [[19:25|Who then can be saved|Quis ergo poterit salvus esse]], if the way to the heavenly kingdom is so hard? As if to say: Almost no one, since there are many vices more grievous than a superfluous love of riches. [[19:26|And Jesus beholding|Adspiciens autem Jesus]] their fear and distress, [[19:26|said to them: With men this is impossible|dixit illis: Apud homines hoc impossibile est]]: that is, it cannot be done by human and natural power that a rich man be saved, or a camel led through the eye of a needle; [[19:26|but with God|apud Deum autem]], that is, to the omnipotence of God, [[19:26|all things are possible|omnia possibilia sunt]] that are not repugnant to the nature of being, that is, that do not imply a contradiction. So God can keep from sin a man abounding in temporal things; He can also change a vicious rich man by grace, so that he uses his riches well and is saved: for [[Rom 6:23|the grace of God, life everlasting|gratia enim Dei vita æterna]]. Pelagius lies, then, in saying that man can be justified without grace.

paras.t: Tunc, videlicet audita commendatione voluntariæ paupertatis, respondens Petrus in persona omnium Apostolorum, tanquam præcipuus inter eos, dixit ei: Ecce: quæ dictio signum est quod magnum atque notabile sit quod narratur; nos duodecim quos in Apostolos elegisti, reliquimus omnia ista terrena, et secuti sumus te corporis gressu et cordis affectu, assimilationeque vitæ. Hoc tamen de Juda proditore sumi non potest, nisi forte pro certo tempore. Quamvis autem Petrus fuerit pauper, quidam tamen Apostolorum, in quorum persona loquebatur, divites erant, puta Matthæus, Bartholomæus, etc. Ideo congrue ait, Reliquimus omnia. Denique, sicut vidua mittens duo minuta, plus omnibus misit in gazophylacium; sic Petrus pauca relinquens, plus multis reliquit qui pondera auri relinquunt, et tamen aliud sibi reservant, vel non tam prompte et affectuose hoc agunt ut Petrus. Omnia quoque dimisit, qui nihil retinuit sibi, nec sola habita, sed et habenda abjecit pro Christo, ipsum affectum divitiarum eradicando. Quid ergo erit nobis mercedis, et quid redditurus es nobis? Nondum videtur Petrus fuisse perfectus. Perfectus namque amator, de præmio non requirit, sed de dilecto.
paras.en: [[19:27|Then|Tunc]], namely after hearing voluntary poverty commended, [[19:27|Peter answering|respondens Petrus]] in the person of all the Apostles, as the chief among them, [[19:27|said to him: Behold|dixit ei: Ecce]] (a word that is a sign that what is told is great and notable) we twelve whom You chose as Apostles [[19:27|have left all things|reliquimus omnia]] of this earth, [[19:27|and have followed thee|et secuti sumus te]] with the steps of the body, the affection of the heart, and likeness of life. This, however, cannot be taken of Judas the traitor, except perhaps for a certain time. And though Peter was poor, yet some of the Apostles in whose person he spoke were rich, such as Matthew, Bartholomew, etc.; so he fittingly says, We have left all things. Moreover, just as the widow who put in two mites cast in more than all into the treasury[[Mark 12:42||]][[Mark 12:43||]], so Peter, leaving a little, left more than many who leave heaps of gold and yet keep something else back for themselves, or do it less readily and lovingly than Peter. He too left all who kept nothing for himself, and cast away for Christ not only what he had but what he might have had, uprooting the very attachment to riches. [[19:27|what therefore shall we have|Quid ergo erit nobis]] as a reward, and what will You give back to us? Peter does not yet seem to have been perfect; for the perfect lover asks not about the reward but about the beloved.

paras.t: Jesus autem dixit eis, non solum Petro, sed ceteris quoque, in quorum persona loquebatur: Amen dico vobis, quod vos qui secuti estis me, et omnes vestra vestigia sectaturi, omnes videlicet perfecti evangelica observantes consilia, qui figurantur ac designantur per vos. Itaque, Qui secuti estis me, modo prædicto, in paupertate ac ceteris bonis, in regeneratione. Hoc S. Hilarius nectit prædictis, ut sit sensus: Qui secuti estis me, accipiendo Baptismum, qui est spiritualis regeneratio ex aqua et Spiritu Sancto. Hieronymus vero convenientius nectit hoc verbis sequentibus. Eritque sensus: Qui secuti estis me, modo præfato, hanc mercedem habebitis: nam in regeneratione, id est in futura corporum resuscitatione, resurrectione, seu reformatione, quæ terminatur ad esse substantiale secundo collatum restitutumque corpori, propter quod regeneratio nuncupatur, quum sederit Filius hominis in sede majestatis suæ, id est, exercere cœperit manifeste et universaliter suam judiciariam potestatem, dando singulis in anima et corpore quod meruerunt. Sedes hoc loco, corporale solium non designat, sed judiciariam potestatem et usum ipsius, quamvis accipi possit pro loco in quo Christus in die judicii corporaliter erit vel residebit in aere, prout Joel dicit: Consurgant et ascendant gentes in vallem Josaphat, quia ibi sedebit ut judicet omnes gentes in circuitu. Sedebitis et vos super sedes duodecim, id est, in duodenis principalibus thronis, locis, seu soliis, assidebitis, judicantes, judicio assessoriæ dignitatis, atque præcipuæ approbationis, duodecim tribus Israel, quæ vobis credentibus, pro majori parte in incredulitate manserunt, sicque damnabitis eas. Unde superius dixit Salvator Judæis, de Apostolis loquens: Ipsi judices vestri erunt.
paras.en: [[19:28|And Jesus said to them|Jesus autem dixit eis]], not to Peter only but to the others also, in whose person he spoke: [[19:28|Amen I say to you, that you who have followed me|Amen dico vobis, quod vos qui secuti estis me]], and all who will follow in your footsteps, namely all the perfect who observe the evangelical counsels, who are figured and signified by you. So: you who have followed me in the way just said, in poverty and the other good things, [[19:28|in the regeneration|in regeneratione]]. St. Hilary joins this to what goes before, so that the sense is: You who have followed me by receiving Baptism, which is the spiritual regeneration of water and the Holy Spirit[[John 3:5||]]. But Jerome more fittingly joins it to the words that follow, and the sense will be: You who have followed me in the way described will have this reward: for [[19:28|in the regeneration|in regeneratione]], that is, in the future raising, resurrection or re-forming of bodies, which ends in substantial being given a second time and restored to the body, for which reason it is called a regeneration, [[19:28|when the Son of man shall sit on the seat of his majesty|quum sederit Filius hominis in sede majestatis suæ]], that is, shall begin to exercise His power of judgment openly and universally, giving to each in soul and body what he has deserved. The seat here does not signify a bodily throne but the power of judgment and its exercise; though it can be taken for the place where Christ will be in body on the day of judgment, or will be seated in the air, as Joel says: [[Joel 3:12|Let them arise, and let the nations come up into the valley of Josaphat: for there I will sit to judge all nations round about|Consurgant et ascendant gentes in vallem Josaphat, quia ibi sedebit ut judicet omnes gentes in circuitu]]. [[19:28|you also shall sit on twelve seats|Sedebitis et vos super sedes duodecim]], that is, you will sit beside Him on twelve principal thrones, places or seats, [[19:28|judging|judicantes]] with the judgment of the dignity of assessors and of a special approval, [[19:28|the twelve tribes of Israel|duodecim tribus Israel]], which, though you believed, remained for the most part in unbelief; and so you will condemn them. Hence the Saviour said above to the Jews, speaking of the Apostles: [[Matt 12:27|they shall be your judges|Ipsi judices vestri erunt]].

paras.t: Quum inter duodecim Apostolos fuerit Judas proditor unus, quomodo ait Christus, Sedebitis super sedes duodecim, quasi duodecim essent sessuri cum Christo, quorum unum constat esse damnatum? Et respondendum, quod promissio ista quantum ad Judam fuerat conditionalis, videlicet, si perseveraret in bono. Denique per sedes duodecim, significantur solia omnium perfectorum et apostolicorum virorum, qui in die judicii judicabunt cum Christo. Similiter per duodecim tribus Israel, judicandorum universitas declaratur. Præterea advertendum, quod Christus in die judicii, secundum suam divinam naturam, seu Trinitas Deus, judicabit per […] exsecutionem (unde ait: Pater non judicat quemquam, sed judicium omne dedit Filio): Apostoli et viri perfecti, per assessoriam dignitatem, tanquam amici et consiliarii Judicis; ceteri electi, imo omnes boni, per approbationem; minus mali, per comparationem, quemadmodum Ninivitæ, Sodomitæ et regina Saba incredulos Judæos judicaturi dicuntur.
paras.en: Since Judas the traitor was one among the twelve Apostles[[Matt 10:4||]], how does Christ say, [[19:28|you also shall sit on twelve seats|Sedebitis super sedes duodecim]], as though twelve were to sit with Christ, one of whom is known to be damned? The answer is that this promise, as regards Judas, was conditional, namely, if he persevered in good. Moreover, by the twelve seats are signified the thrones of all perfect and apostolic men, who on the day of judgment will judge with Christ; and likewise by the twelve tribes of Israel the whole body of those to be judged is meant. Further, it should be noted that on the day of judgment Christ according to His divine nature, or God the Trinity, will judge by […] [a line of the scan is unreadable here; the sense is presumably "by authority; Christ as man, by"] execution (hence He says: [[John 5:22|neither does the Father judge any man: but hath given all judgment to the Son|Pater non judicat quemquam, sed judicium omne dedit Filio]]); the Apostles and perfect men by the dignity of assessors, as friends and counsellors of the Judge; the rest of the elect, indeed all the good, by approval; the less wicked by comparison, as the Ninivites[[Matt 12:41||]], the Sodomites[[Matt 10:15||]] and the queen of Saba[[Matt 12:42||]] are said to be going to judge the unbelieving Jews.

paras.t: Et omnis qui reliquerit ordinate domum, dando eam vel pretium ejus pro Deo. Etenim in pium usum convertenda sunt temporalia quæ relinquuntur, non penitus conterenda aut destructioni exponenda. Vel fratres, aut sorores, aut patrem, aut matrem. Parentes tamen relinquendi non sunt a filiis aut filiabus si inopes aut debiles sint, nisi eis provideatur de necessariis. Aut filios, vel uxores, aut filias, quæ licet jam non exprimantur, tamen sub prædictis intelliguntur: nam apud Lucam exponitur uxor; aut agros, propter nomen meum, id est finaliter propter me, ut me in æternum conspiciat atque possideat, et ad gloriam meam, ut me in præsenti sæculo perfectius veneretur, contemplando, amando ac serviendo in omnibus. Centuplum accipiet, id est, spiritualibus bonis in præsenti dotabitur, videlicet gratia gratum faciente, caritate divina, consolatione interna, donis Spiritus Sancti: quæ omnia incomparabiliter præstantiora sunt cunctis bonis terrenis. Talis quoque efficitur spiritualis filius, imo et frater, omnium Sanctorum viatorum et comprehensorum, quibus caritate et mystica unitate connectitur. Omnia quoque temporalia ei subduntur, sicut ait Apostolus: Quasi nihil habentes, et omnia possidentes. Et vitam æternam, de qua ait apud Joannem Salvator: Hæc est vita æterna, ut cognoscant te solum Deum, et quem misisti Jesum Christum; possidebit in patria, quando videbit facie ad faciem, id est clare et immediate per speciem. Ecce triplex præmium voluntariorum pauperum, videlicet centupla receptio in […] die novissimo, itemque possessio vitæ æternæ in patria.
paras.en: [[19:29|And every one that hath left house|Et omnis qui reliquerit ordinate domum]] in due order, giving it or its price for God; for the temporal things that are left are to be turned to a holy use, not wholly wasted or given over to destruction; [[19:29|or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother|Vel fratres, aut sorores, aut patrem, aut matrem]]. Parents, however, are not to be left by sons or daughters if they are poor or infirm, unless they are provided with what they need. [[19:29|or children|Aut filios]], or wives, or daughters, which, though they are not expressed here, are understood under what is said (for in Luke wife is expressed[[Luke 18:29||]]); [[19:29|or lands for my name's sake|aut agros, propter nomen meum]], that is, for Me as the end, that he may behold and possess Me for ever, and for My glory, that he may honour Me more perfectly in this present world, contemplating, loving and serving in all things; [[19:29|shall receive an hundredfold|Centuplum accipiet]]: that is, he shall be endowed in the present with spiritual goods, namely sanctifying grace [gratia gratum faciens: the grace that makes the soul pleasing to God], divine charity, inward consolation, and the gifts of the Holy Spirit, all of which are incomparably better than all earthly goods. Such a one also becomes the spiritual son, and indeed the brother, of all the Saints, both wayfarers and those who have attained [the comprehensores, the blessed in heaven], to whom he is joined by charity and mystical unity. All temporal things too are made subject to him, as the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 6:10|as having nothing and possessing all things|Quasi nihil habentes, et omnia possidentes]]. [[19:29|and shall possess life everlasting|et vitam æternam possidebit]], of which the Saviour says in John: [[John 17:3|this is eternal life: That they may know thee, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent|Hæc est vita æterna, ut cognoscant te solum Deum, et quem misisti Jesum Christum]]; he shall possess it in the fatherland, when he shall see [[1 Cor 13:12|face to face|facie ad faciem]], that is, clearly and immediately, by sight. Behold the threefold reward of the voluntarily poor: the hundredfold received in […] [a line of the scan is unreadable here] the last day, and also the possession of eternal life in the fatherland.

paras.t: Multi autem erunt primi novissimi, id est, multi eorum qui modo magnæ sunt reputationis, dignitatis et abundantiæ, erunt in die extremo infimi et abjecti. Multi quoque qui nunc ante alios bona incipiunt, paulatim torpent et deficiunt; et qui tardius inchoant, ferventiores redduntur. Similiter et Judæi, qui erant primi vocatione, ultimi facti sunt salvatione, juxta illud Apostoli: Quum plenitudo gentium intraverit, tunc omnis Israel salvus fiet. Et novissimi primi, id est, qui jam dignitate, potestate vel tempore posteriores sunt, et opprimuntur ac tribulantur a primis seu majoribus hujus sæculi, tunc erunt primi honore et gloria apud Deum. Qui enim humiliatus fuerit, erit in gloria. Et abjecta, infirma ac infima mundi elegit Deus, ut alta, fortia et pomposa condemnet. Propter quod fertur in Psalmo: Suscitans a terra inopem, et de stercore elevans pauperem, ut collocet eum cum principibus populi sui. Ad quod pertinere potest illud Ecclesiastici: Sedes ducum superborum destruxit Deus, et sedere fecit mites pro eis. Hinc quoque Virgo Christifera: Deposuit (inquit) potentes de sede, et exaltavit humiles. Nemo ergo de præsenti sua glorietur in se aut præsumat justitia, vel se aliis præferat, aut quemquam contemnat, quia ab his superari potest in præsenti per gratiam, et in futuro per gloriam, quibus nunc videtur multo perfectior.
paras.en: [[19:30|And many that are first, shall be last|Multi autem erunt primi novissimi]]: that is, many of those who are now of great repute, dignity and wealth will on the last day be lowest and cast down. Many too who now begin good works before others little by little grow sluggish and fail, while those who begin later become more fervent. So too the Jews, who were first in calling, have become last in salvation, according to that saying of the Apostle: [[Rom 11:25|until the fulness of the Gentiles should come in|Quum plenitudo gentium intraverit]], [[Rom 11:26|And so all Israel should be saved|tunc omnis Israel salvus fiet]]. [[19:30|and the last shall be first|Et novissimi primi]]: that is, those who are now later in dignity, power or time, and are oppressed and afflicted by the first or great ones of this world, will then be first in honour and glory with God. For [[Job 22:29|he that hath been humbled, shall be in glory|Qui enim humiliatus fuerit, erit in gloria]]. And God has chosen the abject, weak and lowest things of the world[[1 Cor 1:27||]][[1 Cor 1:28||]], to condemn the high, the strong and the pompous. For which reason it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 112:7|Raising up the needy from the earth, and lifting up the poor out of the dunghill:|Suscitans a terra inopem, et de stercore elevans pauperem]], [[Ps 112:8|That he may place him with princes, with the princes of his people|ut collocet eum cum principibus populi sui]]. To this may belong that saying of Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 10:17|God hath overturned the thrones of proud princes, and hath set up the meek in their stead.|Sedes ducum superborum destruxit Deus, et sedere fecit mites pro eis]]. Hence too the Virgin who bore Christ says: [[Luke 1:52|He hath put down the mighty from their seat and hath exalted the humble.|Deposuit (inquit) potentes de sede, et exaltavit humiles]]. Let no one, then, glory in himself over his present justice or presume on it, or prefer himself to others or despise anyone; for he may be surpassed, now by grace and hereafter by glory, by those than whom he now seems far more perfect.

20.title: Expositio capituli vicesimi: Simile est regnum cælorum homini patrifamilias qui exiit primo mane
20.title_en: Exposition of the twentieth chapter: The kingdom of heaven is like to an householder, who went out early in the morning

paras.t: Statum Ecclesiæ militantis comparat Christus rebus diversis, nobis notis ac corporalibus, quatenus per similitudinem sensibilium et notitiam manifestorum, ad cognitionem mysteriorum Ecclesiæ perducamur, gratiamque ac judicium dispositionis divinæ sciamus. Hinc ergo nunc ait: Simile est regnum cælorum homini patrifamilias. Origenes, per regnum cælorum intelligit Christum: quem si hoc loco per regnum cælorum intellexerimus, plana erit parabola. Quemadmodum enim paterfamilias aliquis diversis horis diei egreditur, ut conducat operarios qui vineam suam operentur seu colant; sic Christus secundum quod Deus, a principio mundi per omnes ætates sæculi hujus exiit, per suæ potentiæ operationem, per suæ veritatis manifestationem, per angelorum missionem, per Patriarcharum ac Prophetarum legationem, ut vocaret quosdam ad ecclesiasticam unitatem, ad fidem et gratiam, ad operandum in domo Dei, quæ est vinea atque Ecclesia Christi. Verumtamen expositores communiter intelligunt hic per regnum cælorum, Ecclesiam militantem, ut sit sensus: Simile est regnum cælorum, id est status seu negotium Ecclesiæ militantis, vel ipsa Ecclesia, ratione sui capitis, scilicet Christi, homini patrifamilias, id est operi seu negotio vel personæ hominis cujuscumque habentis familiam, qui exiit primo mane, id est diluculo, conducere operarios in vineam suam, hoc est ad hoc, quod vitem suam putarent atque excolerent. Sic autem exponendo, quod hic scribitur de patrefamilias difficultatem non habet: sed per patremfamilias spiritualiter figuratur ac designatur Deus Trinitas, seu quælibet divina Persona; per vineam vero, Ecclesia. Sicque in processu exponenda est littera, ita ut Ecclesia comparetur vineæ, quoniam sicut se habet paterfamilias ad vineam suam, sic Deus ad Ecclesiam. De Deo ergo per patremfamilias significato exponentur sequentia. Dicitur autem Deus paterfamilias, tanquam creator et dispensator universorum: de cujus domo scriptum est in Baruch, O Israel, quam magna est domus Dei et ingens locus possessionis ejus! Cujus familia, est congregatio omnium fidelium servientium ei.
paras.en: Christ compares the state of the Church militant to various things, bodily and known to us, so that through the likeness of things of sense and the knowledge of things plain to see we may be led to the knowledge of the Church's mysteries, and learn the grace and judgment of God's ordering. So here He says: [[20:1|The kingdom of heaven is like to an householder|Simile est regnum cælorum homini patrifamilias]]. Origen understands the kingdom of heaven to be Christ; and if we take it so here, the parable will be plain. For just as some householder goes out at various hours of the day to hire labourers to work or till his vineyard, so Christ as God has gone out from the beginning of the world through all the ages of this world, by the working of His power, the showing of His truth, the sending of angels, and the embassy of the Patriarchs and Prophets, to call some to the unity of the Church, to faith and grace, to work in the house of God, which is the vineyard and Church of Christ. But the commentators commonly understand the kingdom of heaven here as the Church militant, so that the sense is: [[20:1|The kingdom of heaven is like|Simile est regnum cælorum]], that is, the state or business of the Church militant, or the Church herself by reason of her Head, Christ, [[20:1|to an householder|homini patrifamilias]], that is, to the doing or business or person of any man who has a household, [[20:1|who went out early in the morning|qui exiit primo mane]], that is, at dawn, [[20:1|to hire labourers into his vineyard|conducere operarios in vineam suam]], that is, to prune and tend his vine. Expounded so, what is written here of the householder has no difficulty; but spiritually the householder figures and signifies God the Trinity, or any divine Person, and the vineyard the Church. And so the letter is to be expounded as it goes on, the Church being compared to a vineyard, since as the householder stands to his vineyard, so God stands to the Church. What follows, then, will be expounded of God, signified by the householder. God is called a householder as the Creator and steward of all things, of whose house it is written in Baruch: [[Bar 3:24|O Israel, how great is the house of God, and how vast is the place of his possession!|O Israel, quam magna est domus Dei et ingens locus possessionis ejus!]]! His household is the gathering of all the faithful who serve Him.

paras.t: Qui exiit, non locum mutando, sed aliquid de novo operando, suamque gratiam effundendo, et suos nuntios emittendo, primo mane, id est in prima mundi ætate, quæ duravit ab Adam usque ad Noe, videlicet ad ingressum in arcam, seu ortum diluvii, conducere, id est per mercedis pollicitationem vocare, operarios, id est homines ad operandum potentes, qui non erant operarii meritorie agendo, antequam vocarentur et ejus gratia prævenirentur, in vineam suam, hoc est ad societatem seu incorporationem Ecclesiæ, quemadmodum ait Apostolus: Eripuit nos de præsenti sæculo nequam, et transtulit in regnum Filii dilectionis suæ. A principio etenim mundi vocavit Deus quosdam ad fidem et caritatem, per quam facti sunt membra Ecclesiæ, et vinea Dei, producendo opera sancta, tanquam optimas uvas. Congregatio ergo fidelium dicitur vinea, sicut per Isaiam asseritur: Vinea Domini Sabaoth, domus Israel est; et per Osee, Vitis frondosa domus Israel. Per hos autem operarios conductos, quidam specialiter intelligunt aliorum doctores, prælatos ac superiores, quos Deus misit in vineam, scilicet Ecclesiam, propter aliorum conversionem seu informationem: quales a principio mundi fuerunt, Adam, Seth, Enoch, Mathusalem.
paras.en: [[20:1|who went out|Qui exiit]], not by changing place but by doing something new, pouring out His grace and sending forth His messengers, [[20:1|early in the morning|primo mane]], that is, in the first age of the world, which lasted from Adam to Noe, namely to the entering of the ark or the beginning of the flood, [[20:1|to hire|conducere]], that is, to call by the promise of a wage, [[20:1|labourers|operarios]], that is, men able to work, who were not labourers working meritoriously before they were called and forestalled by His grace, [[20:1|into his vineyard|in vineam suam]], that is, into the fellowship of the Church or incorporation in it, as the Apostle says: He hath delivered us [[Gal 1:4|from this present wicked world|de præsenti sæculo nequam]], [[Col 1:13|and hath translated us into the kingdom of the Son of his love|et transtulit in regnum Filii dilectionis suæ]]. For from the beginning of the world God called some to faith and charity, through which they became members of the Church and the vineyard of God, bringing forth holy works like the best grapes. The gathering of the faithful, then, is called a vineyard, as is declared through Isaias: [[Is 5:7|the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel|Vinea Domini Sabaoth, domus Israel est]]; and through Osee: [[Osee 10:1|Israel a vine full of branches|Vitis frondosa domus Israel]]. By these hired labourers some understand in particular the teachers, prelates and superiors of others, whom God sent into the vineyard, the Church, for the conversion or instruction of others: such were, from the beginning of the world, Adam, Seth, Enoch, Mathusalem.

paras.t: Conventione autem facta, id est promissione completa, seu pacto inito, cum operariis jam præfatis, ex denario diurno, id est de felicitate æterna eis pro suo labore reddenda. Conventio itaque hæc, est vitæ æternæ promissio, de qua per Jeremiam Dominus ait: Quiescat vox tua a ploratu, et oculi tui a lacrimis, quia est merces operi tuo.
