Poterat namque infra unius milliaris spatium utrique animali sedere, præsertim propter mysticam rationem quæ statim dicetur. Nec apparet cur fecisset asinam sibi adduci, nisi ut super eam veheretur; nec aliter dixisset discipulis, ut dicerent quia Dominus his opus habet. Præterea, ad litteram verisimile est, quod pullus adhuc juvenis fuit ac debilis, quoniam nemo hucusque sedit super eum. Et ideo Christus non diu mansit super pullum.
paras.en: [[21:6|And the disciples going, did as Jesus commanded them|Euntes autem discipuli, fecerunt sicut præcepit illis Jesus]]. [[21:7|And they brought the ass and the colt and laid their garments upon them|Et adduxerunt asinam et pullum, et imposuerunt super eos vestimenta sua]], so that Jesus might sit more softly and becomingly, [[21:7|and made him sit thereon|et eum desuper sedere fecerunt]], on each in turn, as was said. Some seem to assert that Christ did not sit on both animals. So, according to them, the story contains either an impossibility or something unseemly: an impossibility, because in so short a stretch of road He could not have sat on both animals; something unseemly, because it would have been unbecoming for Him to sit on a she-ass. Yet because of the plain authority of the canonical Scripture of both Testaments, it seems we must say as has just been said. For within the space of one mile He could sit on both animals, especially for the mystical reason that will be given at once. Nor does it appear why He would have had the ass brought to Him unless to ride on her; nor why else He told the disciples to say [[21:3|that the Lord hath need of them|quia Dominus his opus habet]]. Moreover, in the letter it is likely that the colt was still young and weak, since no one had yet sat on it; and so Christ did not stay long on the colt.

paras.t: Prædictis insuper consonat quod in Genesi Jacob ait Judæ filio suo de Christo: Ligans ad vineam pullum suum, et ad vitem, o fili mi, asinam suam. Quod enim hoc ad litteram de Christo dicatur, patet ex eo quod immediate præmisit: Non auferetur sceptrum de Juda, donec veniat qui mittendus est; et ipse erit exspectatio gentium.
paras.en: With this agrees, besides, what Jacob says in Genesis to his son Juda about Christ: [[Gen 49:11|Tying his foal to the vineyard, and his ass, O my son, to the vine|Ligans ad vineam pullum suum, et ad vitem, o fili mi, asinam suam]] [Denis's order: "and to the vine, O my son, his ass"]. That this is said of Christ in the letter is clear from what he says immediately before: [[Gen 49:10|The sceptre shall not be taken away from Juda|Non auferetur sceptrum de Juda]], [[Gen 49:10|till he come that is to be sent, and he shall be the expectation of nations|donec veniat qui mittendus est; et ipse erit exspectatio gentium]].

paras.t: Mystice namque per prædictum castellum, designatur totus hic mundus, parvus virtute, magnus pravitate, per modum castelli contra Deum muro impietatis, duritia cordis seu obstinatione munitus. In quem Christus misit discipulos suos, dicens: Ite in mundum universum. In quo Apostoli invenerunt asinam alligatam, id est Synagogam seu populum Judæorum, et pullum, id est gentilitatem. Eratque uterque populus funibus vitiorum obstrictus. Quoniam tamen Synagoga super se tulit onera legis, jugum utique, teste Petro, gravissimum, ideo designatur per asinam subjugalem. Gentiles vero sine servitio legis et fide Dei viventes, lascivi ac vagi, significantur per pullum indomitum a nemine subjugatum. Voluit ergo Christus utrumque animal sibi adduci, quia præcepit Apostolis ut utrumque converterent populum, dicens: Eritis mihi testes in Jerusalem, et in omni Judæa et Samaria, et usque ad ultimum terræ. Sedit quoque super utrumque animal, quoniam utrumque populum sibi subjecit per fidem et cultum divinum. Primo tamen sedit asinæ, quoniam primo venit et discipulos misit ad convertendos Judæos, quemadmodum Paulus ait: Vobis oportebat primum loqui verbum Dei. Quumque discipuli adduxissent asinam et pullum ad Jesum, eum desuper sedere fecerunt, quia quum convertissent quosdam Judæos et gentiles innumerabiles, subjecerunt eos imperio Christi, ut ejus præceptis parerent. Quod vero discipuli posuerunt vestimenta sua super pullum et asinam, hoc designat quod super eos quos converterunt, posuerunt indumenta virtutum, variosque ornatus doctrinarum, gratiam sibi collatam aliis communicando, quemadmodum Petrus hortatur: Unusquisque sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administrantes.
paras.en: In the mystical sense, the castellum signifies this whole world, small in virtue and great in wickedness, fortified against God like a stronghold with the wall of impiety, hardness of heart or obstinacy. Into it Christ sent His disciples, saying: [[Mark 16:15|Go ye into the whole world|Ite in mundum universum]]. In it the Apostles found the ass tied, that is, the Synagogue or the Jewish people, and the colt, that is, the Gentiles; and each people was bound with the cords of vices. But since the Synagogue bore upon itself the burdens of the Law, a yoke indeed most heavy, as Peter testifies[[Acts 15:10||]], it is signified by the ass used to the yoke; while the Gentiles, living without the service of the Law and the faith of God, wanton and wandering, are signified by the untamed colt that no one had broken. So Christ willed both animals to be brought to Him, because He commanded the Apostles to convert both peoples, saying: [[Acts 1:8|you shall be witnesses unto me in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and Samaria, and even to the uttermost part of the earth|Eritis mihi testes in Jerusalem, et in omni Judæa et Samaria, et usque ad ultimum terræ]]. And He sat on both animals, because He subjected both peoples to Himself through faith and divine worship. But He sat first on the ass, because He came first and sent His disciples to convert the Jews, as Paul says: [[Acts 13:46|To you it behoved us first to speak the word of God|Vobis oportebat primum loqui verbum Dei]]. And when the disciples had brought the ass and the colt to Jesus, they [[21:7|made him sit thereon|eum desuper sedere fecerunt]], because when they had converted some Jews and countless Gentiles, they brought them under Christ's rule to obey His commands. That the disciples laid their garments on the colt and the ass signifies that they put on those they converted the clothing of the virtues and the various ornaments of teaching, sharing with others the grace bestowed on themselves, as Peter exhorts: [[1 Pet 4:10|As every man hath received grace, ministering the same one to another|Unusquisque sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administrantes]].

paras.t: Plurima autem turba straverunt, id est extenderunt et supposuerunt, vestimenta sua in via qua erat Christus processurus: alii autem cædebant ramos de arboribus olivarum, et sternebant in via. Hæc omnia fecerunt in signum lætitiæ, et ad reverentiam Salvatoris; itemque, ut ait Hieronymus, ne animal cui Christus sedebat, offenderet in lapidem, ne calcaret in spinam, ne caderet in foveam. Turbæ autem quæ præcedebant Jesum, et quæ sequebantur eum, clamabant, dicentes: Hosanna, id est, obsecro, salva, o fili David, secundum naturam assumptam. Hosanna, est dictio Hebraica, composita ex integro et corrupto, videlicet ab hosi, quod est salva, et anna, quod est dictio optativa. Si autem textus habeat, Hosanna filio David, sensus est: Dicimus filio David, Hosanna, id est, salvifica. Benedictus, id est, laude dignus, sanctus sive laudatus sit, qui venit in nomine Domini, hoc est ex Deo Patre, videlicet secundum voluntatem atque ad gloriam ejus. Unde Salvator ait: Ego veni in nomine Patris mei. Hosanna in altissimis, cælestem beatitudinem conferendo, et ad regna cælorum nos perducendo. Secundum Hieronymum, canticum istud sumptum est ex Psalmographo, qui de Christi adventu conscribens, sic oravit: O Domine, salvum me fac, o Domine, bene prosperare; benedictus qui venit in nomine Domini. Porro hoc canticum consona voce resonabant, utique ex instructione et motione Spiritus Sancti.
paras.en: [[21:8|And a very great multitude spread their garments in the way|Plurima autem turba straverunt, id est extenderunt et supposuerunt, vestimenta sua in via]], spread, that is, stretched out and laid them under, in the way by which Christ was to go: [[21:8|and others cut boughs from the trees|alii autem cædebant ramos de arboribus]] of the olives, [[21:8|and strewed them in the way|et sternebant in via]]. All this they did as a sign of joy and in reverence for the Saviour; and also, as Jerome says, lest the animal on which Christ sat should strike against a stone, tread on a thorn, or fall into a pit. [[21:9|And the multitudes that went before and that followed cried, saying|Turbæ autem quæ præcedebant Jesum, et quæ sequebantur eum, clamabant, dicentes]]: [[21:9|Hosanna|Hosanna]], that is, I beseech, save, O [[21:9|son of David|fili David]] according to the nature You have taken. Hosanna is a Hebrew word, made of one whole word and one shortened, namely hosi, which means "save", and anna, which is a word of wishing. But if the text has "Hosanna to the son of David", the sense is: We say to the son of David, Hosanna, that is, save us. [[21:9|Blessed|Benedictus]], that is, worthy of praise, holy or praised be [[21:9|he that cometh in the name of the Lord|qui venit in nomine Domini]], that is, from God the Father, namely according to His will and to His glory. Hence the Saviour says: [[John 5:43|I am come in the name of my Father|Ego veni in nomine Patris mei]]. [[21:9|Hosanna in the highest|Hosanna in altissimis]], by bestowing heavenly beatitude and leading us to the kingdom of heaven. According to Jerome, this song is taken from the Psalmist, who, writing of Christ's coming, prayed thus: [[Ps 117:25|O Lord, save me: O Lord, give good success|o Domine, bene prosperare]]; [[Ps 117:26|Blessed be he that cometh in the name of the Lord|benedictus qui venit in nomine Domini]]. And they sang this song with one voice, by the teaching and moving of the Holy Spirit.

paras.t: Lucas vero hæc plenius recitat: Quum appropinquaret, inquiens, ad descensum montis Oliveti, cœperunt omnes turbæ descendentium gaudentes laudare Deum voce magna super omnibus quas viderant virtutibus, dicentes: Benedictus qui venit rex in nomine Domini, pax in cælo, et gloria in excelsis. Ut enim in evangelio Joannis legitur: Turba quæ convenit in Jerusalem ad diem festum, quum audisset quod Jesus veniret, exierunt obviam ei cum ramis palmarum.
paras.en: Luke tells these things more fully: [[Luke 19:37|when he was now coming near the descent of Mount Olivet, the whole multitude of his disciples began with joy to praise God with a loud voice, for all the mighty works they had seen|Quum appropinquaret, inquiens, ad descensum montis Oliveti, cœperunt omnes turbæ descendentium gaudentes laudare Deum voce magna super omnibus quas viderant virtutibus]], [[Luke 19:38|Saying: Blessed be the king who cometh in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven and glory on high!|dicentes: Benedictus qui venit rex in nomine Domini, pax in cælo, et gloria in excelsis]]! For, as is read in the Gospel of John: [[John 12:12|a great multitude that was come to the festival day, when they had heard that Jesus was coming|Turba quæ convenit in Jerusalem ad diem festum, quum audisset quod Jesus veniret]], [[John 12:13|went forth to meet him|exierunt obviam ei]] [[John 12:13|Took branches of palm trees|cum ramis palmarum]].

paras.t: Et quum intrasset Jesus Jerosolymam cum processione tam insolita ac solenni, commota est admiratione, indignatione, vel dubitatione, universa civitas, id est major et principalior pars populi habitantis in ea, dicens: Quis est hic, cui tantus honor impenditur? Hoc quidam indignando, quidam dubitando et inquirendo, quidam admirando dixerunt, sicut et angeli Christo ascendente: Quis est iste qui venit de Edom? Et, Quis est iste rex gloriæ? Populi autem, id est turba vulgaris, dicebant: Hic est Jesus propheta. Populus iste confessus fuit in cantico suo, quod ipse esset Christus. Quum igitur asserunt eum esse prophetam, non de qualicumque, sed de summo loquuntur Propheta ac Domino Prophetarum, de quo cecinit Moyses: Prophetam suscitabit vobis Dominus de fratribus vestris, tanquam me. A Nazareth Galilææ, id est de illa civitate oriundus. Conceptus namque atque nutritus fuit in Nazareth, licet in Bethlehem natus sit. Per hoc significatur, quod infirma, abjecta et stulta mundi elegit Deus, ut confundat fortes et sapientes. Sacerdotibus enim, Scribis et Pharisæis non credentibus, populus confitetur.
paras.en: [[21:10|And when he was come into Jerusalem|Et quum intrasset Jesus Jerosolymam]], Jesus, with so unusual and solemn a procession, [[21:10|the whole city was moved|commota est universa civitas]] with wonder, indignation or doubt (the whole city, that is, the greater and chief part of the people living in it), [[21:10|saying: Who is this|dicens: Quis est hic]], to whom such honour is paid? Some said this in indignation, some doubting and inquiring, some in wonder; as the angels too said when Christ ascended: [[Is 63:1|Who is this that cometh from Edom|Quis est iste qui venit de Edom?]]? And: [[Ps 23:8|Who is this King of Glory|Quis est iste rex gloriæ]][[Ps 23:10||]]? [[21:11|And the people said: This is Jesus, the prophet|Populi autem dicebant: Hic est Jesus propheta]]: the people, that is, the common crowd. These people had confessed in their song that He was the Christ. So when they declare Him to be a prophet, they speak not of any prophet but of the supreme Prophet and Lord of the Prophets, of whom Moses sang: [[Deut 18:15|The Lord thy God will raise up to thee a PROPHET of thy nation and of thy brethren like unto me|Prophetam suscitabit vobis Dominus de fratribus vestris, tanquam me]][[Acts 7:37||]]. [[21:11|from Nazareth of Galilee|A Nazareth Galilææ]], that is, coming from that city; for He was conceived and brought up in Nazareth, though He was born in Bethlehem. By this it is signified that [[1 Cor 1:27|the weak things of the world hath God chosen|infirma mundi elegit Deus]], to confound the strong and the wise[[1 Cor 1:28||]]. For while the priests, scribes and Pharisees do not believe, the people confess.

paras.t: Et intravit Jesus in templum Dei: primo, quia in his quæ Patris sui erant, oportuit eum esse; secundo, ut daret nobis exemplum primo intrandi in domum Dei, et quærendi regnum, honorem et gloriam Creatoris; tertio, ut in templo doceret, et errores corrigeret, sicut subjungitur. Et ejiciebat omnes vendentes et ementes in templo. Sacerdotes, qui avarissimi erant, posuerunt in atriis templi quosdam de suis, qui omnium animalium immolaticiorum genera in templo vendebant, ne aliqui, maxime qui de longinquo venerant, possent se excusare, si nihil offerrent in templo, quia a locis remotis non poterant animalia secum adducere. Hos ergo Christus ejecit. Et mensas nummulariorum, hoc est eorum qui pauperibus concedebant sub cautione pecuniam, quatenus nec egeni se excusarent ab immolatione propter defectum pecuniæ, et cathedras vendentium columbas, quæ erant hostiæ pauperum, evertit, pecuniam effundendo. Per hoc præfigurabatur, quod simoniacos et clericos sæcularibus se negotiis implicantes, Christus de Ecclesia sua tanquam indignos repellit, secundum quod ait: Gratis accepistis, gratis date.
paras.en: [[21:12|And Jesus went into the temple of God|Et intravit Jesus in templum Dei]]: first, because [[Luke 2:49|I must be about my father's business|in his quæ Patris sui erant, oportuit eum esse]]; secondly, to give us an example of entering first into the house of God and seeking the kingdom, honour and glory of the Creator; thirdly, to teach in the temple and correct errors, as is added. [[21:12|and cast out all them that sold and bought in the temple|Et ejiciebat omnes vendentes et ementes in templo]]. The priests, who were most avaricious, had placed some of their own people in the courts of the temple, who sold in the temple every kind of animal for sacrifice, so that no one, especially those who had come from far away, could excuse himself if he offered nothing in the temple because he could not bring animals with him from distant places. These, then, Christ cast out. [[21:12|and overthrew the tables of the money changers|Et mensas nummulariorum]], that is, of those who lent money to the poor against security, so that not even the needy could excuse themselves from sacrifice for lack of money, [[21:12|and the chairs of them that sold doves|et cathedras vendentium columbas]], which were the offerings of the poor, pouring out the money. By this it was prefigured that Christ drives out of His Church, as unworthy, simoniacs and clerics who entangle themselves in worldly business, according to His saying: [[Matt 10:8|freely have you received, freely give|Gratis accepistis, gratis date]].

paras.t: Et dicit eis: Scriptum est in Isaia: Domus mea, domus orationis vocabitur, id est, ad orandum deputata erit, et inde nomen habebit, nec esse debet domus negotiationis et cupiditatis. Vos autem fecistis illam esse speluncam latronum, hoc est similem specui seu loco abscondito in quo latrones prædas suas collocant et occultant. Quemadmodum enim in fovea tali ponunt latrones ea quæ rapiunt ab his quos corporaliter necant, sic sacerdotes et eorum familia colligebant in templo pecunias seu pretia eorum quos spiritualiter occiderunt, inducendo eos ad magna peccata, seu pauperum quos excoriaverunt. Et accesserunt ad eum cæci et claudi in templo, ducti vel bajulati ab aliis; et sanavit eos. Per horum operationem miraculorum, Christus confirmavit et verum ostendit præconium sibi a turba exhibitum. Denique, si totum evangelicæ paginæ textum consideremus, inveniemus ubique doctrinæ et verbis Christi mixta et juncta esse miracula, quatenus supernaturalis veritas per supernaturalia opera comprobetur, ut fides nostra, secundum Apostolum, non sit in sermone, sed in ostensione spiritus et virtute.
paras.en: [[21:13|And he saith to them: It is written|Et dicit eis: Scriptum est]] in Isaias: [[21:13|My house shall be called the house of prayer|Domus mea, domus orationis vocabitur]][[Is 56:7||]], that is, it will be set apart for prayer and will take its name from it, and it ought not to be a house of trade and greed. [[21:13|but you have made it a den of thieves|Vos autem fecistis illam esse speluncam latronum]], that is, like a cave or hidden place where robbers stow and hide their plunder. For just as robbers put in such a pit what they take from those they kill in body, so the priests and their household gathered in the temple the money, or the price, of those they killed spiritually by leading them into great sins, or of the poor whom they fleeced. [[21:14|And there came to him the blind and the lame in the temple|Et accesserunt ad eum cæci et claudi in templo]], led or carried by others; [[21:14|and he healed them|et sanavit eos]]. By working these miracles Christ confirmed the praise given Him by the crowd and showed it to be true. Indeed, if we consider the whole text of the Gospel, we shall find miracles everywhere mingled and joined with Christ's teaching and words, so that supernatural truth may be proved by supernatural works, that our faith, according to the Apostle, may be [[1 Cor 2:4|not in the persuasive words of human wisdom. but in shewing of the Spirit and power|non sit in sermone, sed in ostensione spiritus et virtute]][[1 Cor 2:5||]].

paras.t: Videntes autem principes sacerdotum et Scribæ mirabilia quæ fecit, cæcis visum et claudis gressum præstando, et pueros clamantes in templo et dicentes: Hosanna filio David. Parentes namque filios suos secum adduxerant, et sicut pueri audierunt parentes suos ac turbam clamare, sic et ipsi clamabant: nec dubium quin ex influxu Spiritus Sancti, qui movit linguas eorum ad proferendum verba quæ nec ipsi intellexerunt, saltem perfecte. Indignati sunt. Hæc est Judæorum proprietas, ut quanto melius successerit ei quem oderunt, tanto amplius crucientur, et aliquid, si possint vel audeant, opponant. Sic sacerdotes, Scribæ ac Pharisæi, qui contra Christum implacabile odium conceperunt, tanto vehementius affligebantur, indignabantur, et murmurabant ac detrahebant, quanto Christus pluribus miraculis refulgebat, sublimiusque extollebatur a vulgo. Unde apud Joannem dixisse leguntur: Numquid aliquis ex principibus credidit in eum? Sed turba hæc, quæ ignorat legem, maledicti sunt. Et dixerunt ei: Audis quid isti pueri dicunt, te collaudando? id est, si esses tam justus et humilis ut simulas et affirmas, dicendo, Ego non quæro gloriam meam, et claritatem ab hominibus non accipio; non deberes hunc applausum sustinere, sed prohibere. Quia miracula Christi nulla ex parte poterant calumniari, arguunt eum superbiæ vanæque gloriæ.
paras.en: [[21:15|And the chief priests and scribes, seeing the wonderful things that he did|Videntes autem principes sacerdotum et Scribæ mirabilia quæ fecit]], giving sight to the blind and their step to the lame, [[21:15|and the children crying in the temple and saying: Hosanna to the son of David|et pueros clamantes in templo et dicentes: Hosanna filio David]]: for parents had brought their children with them, and as the children heard their parents and the crowd crying out, so they cried too; and no doubt it was by the inflowing of the Holy Spirit, who moved their tongues to utter words which they themselves did not understand, at least not perfectly. [[21:15|were moved with indignation|Indignati sunt]]. This is the way of the Jews: the better things go for one they hate, the more they are tormented, and the more they put up some objection if they can or dare. So the priests, scribes and Pharisees, who had conceived an implacable hatred against Christ, were the more vehemently afflicted, indignant, murmuring and slandering, the more Christ shone with miracles and was exalted by the people. Hence in John they are read to have said: [[John 7:48|Hath any one of the rulers believed in him|Numquid aliquis ex principibus credidit in eum?]]? [[John 7:49|But this multitude, that knoweth not the law, are accursed|Sed turba hæc, quæ ignorat legem, maledicti sunt]]. [[21:16|And said to him: Hearest thou what these say|Et dixerunt ei: Audis quid isti pueri dicunt]], praising you? That is: If you were as just and humble as you pretend and assert, saying, [[John 8:50|I seek not my own glory|Ego non quæro gloriam meam]], and [[John 5:41|I receive not glory from men|claritatem ab hominibus non accipio]], you ought not to put up with this applause but forbid it. Since they could not find fault with Christ's miracles in any respect, they accuse Him of pride and vainglory.

paras.t: Jesus autem dixit eis: Utique audio, et prohibere non debeo. Quod probat auctoritate Scripturæ: Numquid legistis? quasi dicat: Imo legistis, sed non intellexistis, vel non attendistis. Legistis ergo in Psalmo: Ex ore infantium et lactentium perfecisti laudem. Per infantes atque lactentes designantur illitterati ac innocentes. Non enim putandum est, quod pueri isti adeo parvæ ætatis exstiterint, ut adhuc ubera sugerent, et verba proferre non possent. Erant tamen adolescentes, ita ut cum Jeremia dicere possent: A, a, a, Domine Deus, nescio loqui, quia puer ego sum. Nescio (inquit) loqui, prudenter et erudite in lege, videlicet per naturam. Ex ore ergo istorum perfecit, id est, perfecte expressit, Deus laudem de Christo. Non enim ipsi erant qui loquebantur, sed Spiritus Patris eorum.
paras.en: [[21:16|And Jesus said to them: Yea|Jesus autem dixit eis: Utique]], I hear, and I ought not to forbid it. This He proves by the authority of Scripture: [[21:16|have you never read|Numquid legistis]]? As if to say: Indeed you have read it, but you have not understood it, or not paid attention. You have read, then, in the Psalm: [[21:16|Out of the mouth of infants and of sucklings thou hast perfected praise?|Ex ore infantium et lactentium perfecisti laudem]][[Ps 8:3||]]. By infants and sucklings are signified the unlettered and innocent. For we must not think that these children were so young as to be still at the breast and unable to speak words. Yet they were young, so that they could say with Jeremias: [[Jer 1:6|Ah, ah, ah, Lord God: behold, I cannot speak, for I am a child|A, a, a, Domine Deus, nescio loqui, quia puer ego sum]] [Denis: "I know not how to speak"]. "I know not how to speak", he says, wisely and learnedly in the law, that is, by nature. Out of the mouth of these, then, God perfected, that is, perfectly expressed, praise of Christ. For [[Matt 10:20|it is not you that speak, but the spirit of your Father|Non enim ipsi erant qui loquebantur, sed Spiritus Patris eorum]].

paras.t: Et relictis illis invidiosis ac perfidis, qui inde deteriores fiebant, unde emendari et converti debebant, abiit foras extra civitatem Jerusalem, in Bethaniam, viculum Lazari, Marthæ et Mariæ, ibique mansit nocte illa, cum suis discipulis, in domo Marthæ: et probabile est, quod nullus in Jerusalem audebat recipere eum hospitio, propter metum pontificum et conspirationem Scribarum. Bethania autem interpretatur domus obedientiæ. Per hoc ergo quod Christus illos corporaliter dereliquit, Bethaniamque ingressus est, et ibi quievit, figurabatur quod Judæa propter incredulitatem deserta, ad gentes Evangelio obedientes Christus transiret.
paras.en: [[21:17|And leaving them|Et relictis illis]], those envious and faithless men, who were made worse by what should have amended and converted them, [[21:17|he went out of the city into Bethania|abiit foras extra civitatem Jerusalem, in Bethaniam]], out of the city of Jerusalem into Bethania, the little village of Lazarus, Martha and Mary, [[21:17|and remained here|ibique mansit]] that night with His disciples in Martha's house; and it is likely that no one in Jerusalem dared to give Him lodging, for fear of the high priests and because of the conspiracy of the scribes. Bethania means "house of obedience". By Christ's leaving them in body and going into Bethania and resting there, then, it was figured that Christ, forsaking Judea for its unbelief, would pass over to the Gentiles who obey the Gospel.

paras.t: Mane autem diei immediate sequentis, revertens cum discipulis, in civitatem Jerusalem, esuriit, non necessitate, sed voluntate. Et mirum quod Christus tam mane passus est famem, qui de sero in Bethania cœnasse creditur. Non enim in Jerusalem manducasse videtur. Dicunt igitur expositores, quod ista Christi esuries non erat naturalis, sed dispensative assumpta, ad designandum spiritualem esuriem Christi, qua Judæorum ac gentium desideravit salutem. Et videns fici arborem, puta ficulneam, secus viam; venit ad eam, si forte aliquid inveniret in ea, ut dicitur in evangelio Marci; et nihil invenit in ea nisi folia tantum. Et ait illi: Nunquam nascatur ex te fructus, videlicet ficus, in sempiternum. Et arefacta est continuo ficulnea. Quæritur cur Christus, qui utique scivit fructum non esse in arbore illa, præsertim quia non erat tempus ficorum, ut habetur in Marco, quæsivit fructum in ea, et infructuosæ maledixit, quæ in culpa non fuit. Et respondendum, quod Christus famem anticipative assumpsit, et ad ficulneam pro fructu perrexit, propter mysticam rationem. Quemadmodum enim Prophetæ interdum verbis, interdum factis prophetaverunt, sic Christus quandoque sermonibus, quandoque operibus aliquid præsignavit. Accessit ergo ficulneam, quærens in ea fructum, ad insinuandum quod venit ad populum Judæorum, quærens in eis fructum justitiæ. Arbori quoque habenti non fructum sed folia, maledixit, ad innuendum quod sacerdotes, Scribæ, Pharisæi, et ceteri simulatores ac callidi, non veritatem, sed apparentiam sanctitatis habentes, induti vestibus ovium, intus vero pleni hypocrisi, essent divinitus maledicendi. Hieronymus aliam affert rationem, dicens quod ideo maledixit ficulneæ, et arefactam manifestavit discipulis, ut suam eis demonstraret potentiam, quatenus in sua passione fortiores essent, scientes quod ipse poterat adversarios suos dejicere et necare, quemadmodum arefecit ficulneam.
paras.en: [[21:18|And in the morning|Mane autem]] of the very next day, [[21:18|returning into the city|revertens cum discipulis, in civitatem]] of Jerusalem with His disciples, [[21:18|he was hungry|esuriit]], not by necessity but by will. And it is strange that Christ suffered hunger so early, since He is believed to have supped the evening before in Bethania; for He does not seem to have eaten in Jerusalem. So the commentators say that this hunger of Christ was not natural but taken on by design, to signify Christ's spiritual hunger, by which He desired the salvation of Jews and Gentiles. [[21:19|And seeing a certain fig tree by the way side, he came to it|Et videns fici arborem, puta ficulneam, secus viam; venit ad eam]], to see if perhaps He might find anything on it, as is said in the Gospel of Mark[[Mark 11:13||]], [[21:19|and found nothing on it but leaves only|et nihil invenit in ea nisi folia tantum]]. [[21:19|And he saith to it: May no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever|Et ait illi: Nunquam nascatur ex te fructus, videlicet ficus, in sempiternum]] (no fruit, that is, no figs). [[21:19|And immediately the fig tree withered away|Et arefacta est continuo ficulnea]]. It is asked why Christ, who surely knew there was no fruit on that tree, especially since it was not the season for figs, as Mark has it, looked for fruit on it, and cursed a barren tree that was not at fault. The answer is that Christ took on hunger beforehand and went to the fig tree for fruit for a mystical reason. For as the Prophets prophesied sometimes by words and sometimes by deeds, so Christ foreshowed something sometimes by speech and sometimes by works. He went to the fig tree, then, looking for fruit on it, to suggest that He came to the Jewish people looking for the fruit of justice in them. And He cursed the tree that had leaves but no fruit, to hint that the priests, scribes, Pharisees and the other dissemblers and crafty men, who had not the truth but the appearance of holiness, [[Matt 7:15|in the clothing of sheep|induti vestibus ovium]], but [[Matt 23:28|inwardly you are full of hypocrisy|intus vero pleni hypocrisi]], were to be cursed by God. Jerome gives another reason: that He cursed the fig tree and showed it withered to the disciples in order to demonstrate His power to them, so that they might be stronger in His Passion, knowing that He could cast down and kill His adversaries, as He withered the fig tree.

paras.t: Et videntes discipuli ficulneam arefactam, mirati sunt, dicentes: Quomodo continuo aruit a radicibus? quasi dicant: Hoc mirabiliter factum est. Secundum quod in Marco legitur, consideratio, admiratio et collocutio discipulorum de arefactione ficulneæ, non erant statim quando Christus prædicta protulit verba, sed mane diei sequentis: et ita hoc loco non servatur ordo historiæ. Respondens autem Jesus, ait eis: Amen dico vobis, si habueritis fidem certissimam, et non hæsitaveritis, aliquo modo dubitando, non solum de ficulnea facietis quod ego, ut ad verba vestra maledictoria arefiat, sed si monti huic dixeritis, Tolle et jacta te in mare, fiet. Intellectus seu expositio horum verborum patet ex eo quod supra dictum est: Amen dico vobis, si habueritis fidem sicut granum sinapis, dicetis monti huic, Transi hinc, et transibit, et nihil impossibile erit vobis. Hieronymus tamen addit hoc loco, dicens se credere quod Apostoli ad litteram transtulerunt et in mare projecerunt montes, orando seu imperando, quamvis scriptum non sit. Nam ideo, ut ait, scriptum non est, ne daretur infidelibus contradicendi et discredendi major occasio, præsertim quum nec minora signa credant ab Apostolis facta, quæ in Scripturis authenticis fuisse leguntur. Et omnia quæcumque petieritis in oratione credentes, accipietis, id est cum fide idonea, servatis conditionibus ad exaudientiam requisitis, videlicet, ut orent pro se, et perseveranter atque salubriter, utpote in nomine Salvatoris. Hoc et Jacobus monet: Postulet (inquiens) a Deo, et dabitur ei; postulet autem in fide nihil hæsitans. Qui autem hæsitat, similis est fluctui maris qui a vento circumfertur: non ergo æstimet homo ille, quod aliquid accipiat a Deo. Debemus ergo orare in fide cum spe, ut certi simus de veritate eorum quæ cadunt sub fide, et non dubitemus de misericordia Dei: ita quod certitudo spei sit ex parte objecti, videlicet Dei, ex quo nunquam est exauditionis defectus, quum rationabiliter petitur; non ex parte subjecti, seu meritorum sperantis, qui ob culpam suam sæpe non exauditur.
paras.en: [[21:20|And the disciples seeing it wondered, saying: How is it presently withered away|Et videntes discipuli ficulneam arefactam, mirati sunt, dicentes: Quomodo continuo aruit]] from the roots? As if to say: This has been done wonderfully. According to what is read in Mark, the disciples' noticing, wondering at and talking about the withering of the fig tree did not happen immediately when Christ spoke those words, but on the morning of the next day[[Mark 11:20||]]; and so the order of the story is not kept here. [[21:21|And Jesus answering, said to them: Amen, I say to you, if you shall have faith|Respondens autem Jesus, ait eis: Amen dico vobis, si habueritis fidem]], most certain faith, [[21:21|and stagger not|et non hæsitaveritis]], doubting in any way, [[21:21|not only this of the fig tree shall you do|non solum de ficulnea facietis]], as I did, so that it withers at your words of cursing, [[21:21|but also if you shall say to this mountain, Take up and cast thyself into the sea, it shall be done|sed si monti huic dixeritis, Tolle et jacta te in mare, fiet]]. The understanding or exposition of these words is clear from what was said above: [[Matt 17:19|amen I say to you, if you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, you shall say to this mountain: Remove from hence hither, and it shall remove: and nothing shall be impossible to you|Amen dico vobis, si habueritis fidem sicut granum sinapis, dicetis monti huic, Transi hinc, et transibit, et nihil impossibile erit vobis]]. Jerome, however, adds here that he believes the Apostles literally moved mountains and threw them into the sea by praying or commanding, though it is not written. For, as he says, it is not written lest unbelievers be given a greater occasion to contradict and disbelieve, especially since they do not believe even the lesser signs done by the Apostles that are read in the authentic Scriptures. [[21:22|And all things whatsoever you shall ask in prayer believing, you shall receive|Et omnia quæcumque petieritis in oratione credentes, accipietis]]: that is, with fitting faith, the conditions required for being heard being kept, namely that they pray for themselves, and perseveringly and for their salvation, that is, in the name of the Saviour. James too warns of this: [[Jas 1:5|let him ask of God who giveth to all men abundantly and upbraideth not. And it shall be given him|postulet a Deo, qui dat omnibus affluenter, et non improperat: et dabitur ei]]; [[Jas 1:6|But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea, which is moved and carried about by the wind|postulet autem in fide nihil hæsitans. Qui autem hæsitat, similis est fluctui maris qui a vento circumfertur]]. [[Jas 1:7|Therefore let not that man think that he shall receive any thing of the Lord|non ergo æstimet homo ille, quod aliquid accipiat a Deo]]. We ought, then, to pray in faith with hope, so as to be certain of the truth of what falls under faith and not to doubt of God's mercy: so that the certainty of hope is on the side of its object, namely God, in whom there is never any failure to hear when one asks reasonably; not on the side of the subject, or of the merits of the one hoping, who is often not heard because of his own fault.

paras.t: Et quum venisset in templum, die sequenti post Ramos palmarum, accesserunt ad eum docentem populum publice in templo, principes sacerdotum et seniores populi, qui tempore concilii per nomina vocabantur; dicentes: In qua potestate hæc facis, hæc scilicet, quæ te vidimus facere heri et hodie, ejiciendo vendentes de templo, infirmos sanando, et publice prædicando? hoc est, qua auctoritate et cujus ope hæc facis? Quasi dicant: Quum non sis sacerdos, nec legis doctor, quibus solis convenit docere in templo, nec ab imperatore vel senatu licentiam habeas prædicandi et ista agendi, videtur opus tuum usurpatorium esse, et ex præsumptione prodire. Et quis tibi dedit hanc potestatem? tanquam dicant: Quum non habeas eam a principibus sacerdotum nec a Romano imperio, videtur quod virtute et instigatione diaboli facias ista. Simile est, quod alibi dicunt: In principe dæmoniorum ejicit dæmonia. In quo patet intolerabilis cæcitas Judæorum, quasi non esset potestas potestate humana ac diabolica altior, virtus divina, cujus commissione et adjutorio Christus operari potuerit. Denique sancti Prophetæ nonne auctoritate divina docuerunt? Sed et miracula Christi ostenderunt quod divina potestate operabatur, quemadmodum Nicodemus professus est: Scimus, inquiens, quia a Deo venisti magister; nemo enim potest hæc signa facere quæ tu facis, nisi fuerit Deus cum eo.
paras.en: [[21:23|And when he was come into the temple|Et quum venisset in templum]], on the day after Palm Sunday, [[21:23|there came to him, as he was teaching|accesserunt ad eum docentem]] the people publicly in the temple, [[21:23|the chief priests and ancients of the people|principes sacerdotum et seniores populi]], who were called by name at the time of a council, [[21:23|saying: By what authority dost thou these things|dicentes: In qua potestate hæc facis]]: these things, that is, which we saw you do yesterday and today, casting the sellers out of the temple, healing the sick, and preaching publicly? That is, by what authority and by whose help do you do these things? As if to say: Since you are not a priest nor a doctor of the law, to whom alone it belongs to teach in the temple, nor have you leave from the emperor or the senate to preach and do these things, your work seems usurped and to proceed from presumption. [[21:23|And who hath given thee this authority|Et quis tibi dedit hanc potestatem]]? As if to say: Since you do not have it from the chief priests nor from the Roman empire, it seems that you do these things by the power and prompting of the devil. It is like what they say elsewhere: [[Matt 9:34|By the prince of devils he casteth out devils|In principe dæmoniorum ejicit dæmonia]]. In this the intolerable blindness of the Jews is plain, as though there were no power higher than human and diabolical power, namely the divine power, by whose commission and help Christ could work. Did not the holy Prophets, indeed, teach by divine authority? And Christ's miracles showed that He worked by divine power, as Nicodemus confessed: [[John 3:2|we know that thou art come a teacher from God; for no man can do these signs which thou dost, unless God be with him|Scimus, inquiens, quia a Deo venisti magister; nemo enim potest hæc signa facere quæ tu facis, nisi fuerit Deus cum eo]].

paras.t: Consequenter ponitur artificialis et justa evasio Christi, qui poterat istis rationabiliter et doctrinaliter respondere, sed digni non erant. Respondens Jesus, dixit eis: Interrogabo vos et ego unum sermonem: quem si dixeritis mihi responsive, et ego vobis dicam in qua potestate hæc facio. Baptismus Joannis activus, videlicet lotio qua ipse alios abluit in Jordane, de cælo erat, id est ex commissione et auctoritate Dei habitantis in cælo (juxta illud in Psalmo: Dominus in cælo paravit sedem suam; et illud Isaiæ, Cælum mihi sedes est)? an ex hominibus, id est adinventione et confictione humana?
paras.en: Next is set down Christ's skilful and just evasion: He could have answered them reasonably and with teaching, but they were not worthy. [[21:24|Jesus answering, said to them: I also will ask you one word|Respondens Jesus, dixit eis: Interrogabo vos et ego unum sermonem]], [[21:24|which if you shall tell me|quem si dixeritis mihi]] in answer, [[21:24|I will also tell you by what authority I do these things|et ego vobis dicam in qua potestate hæc facio]]. [[21:25|The baptism of John|Baptismus Joannis]] (in the active sense, that is, the washing with which he washed others in the Jordan), [[21:25|whence was it? From heaven|de cælo erat]], that is, by the commission and authority of God, who dwells in heaven (according to that saying in the Psalm: [[Ps 102:19|The Lord hath prepared his throne in heaven|Dominus in cælo paravit sedem suam]]; and that of Isaias: [[Is 66:1|Heaven is my throne|Cælum mihi sedes est]][[Acts 7:49||]])? [[21:25|or from men|an ex hominibus]], that is, by human invention and contrivance?

paras.t: At illi cogitabant intra se, dicentes: Si dixerimus, De cælo esse baptismum Joannis, dicet nobis per increpationem et redargutionem: Quare ergo non credidistis illi Joanni de me testimonium perhibenti (dicendo, Venit fortior me, cujus non sum dignus calceamenta solvere; et iterum, Qui de cælo venit, super omnes est)? Si autem dixerimus, Ex hominibus esse Joannis baptismum, timemus, id est, timere habemus, turbam a Joanne baptizatam, ne interficiat nos tanquam blasphemos. Unde in evangelio Lucæ dicunt: Si dixerimus, Ex hominibus, universa plebs lapidabit nos. In quo patet eorum perversitas, quoniam homines timuerunt magis quam Deum, quum tamen dicat Scriptura: Qui timet hominem, cito corruet. Omnes enim, præsertim vulgares, habebant, id est reputabant, Joannem sicut prophetam. Dictio, Sicut, notat hic veritatem, non similitudinem solam. Noverant enim Joannem vere esse prophetam, ex ejus supernaturali conceptione, patris sui prophetatione, et ceteris quæ in ejus nativitate contigerant; item ex sanctitate et rigore suæ conversationis, efficacia prædicationis, et quia de Christo verbis et factis apertissime prænuntiavit.
paras.en: [[21:25|But they thought within themselves, saying|At illi cogitabant intra se, dicentes]]: [[21:26|If we shall say, from heaven|Si dixerimus, De cælo]] is John's baptism, [[21:26|he will say to us|dicet nobis]] in rebuke and reproof: [[21:26|Why then did you not believe him|Quare ergo non credidistis illi]], John, when he bore witness of me, saying, [[Mark 1:7|There cometh after me one mightier than I, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to stoop down and loose|Venit fortior me, cujus non sum dignus calceamenta solvere]]; and again, [[John 3:31|He that cometh from heaven is above all|Qui de cælo venit, super omnes est]]? [[21:26|But if we shall say, from men|Si autem dixerimus, Ex hominibus]] is John's baptism, [[21:26|we are afraid of the multitude|timemus turbam]], that is, we have to fear the crowd baptized by John, lest they kill us as blasphemers. Hence in the Gospel of Luke they say: [[Luke 20:6|But if we say, of men: the whole people will stone us|Si dixerimus, Ex hominibus, universa plebs lapidabit nos]]. In this their perversity is plain, since they feared men more than God, though Scripture says: [[Prov 29:25|He that feareth man shall quickly fall|Qui timet hominem, cito corruet]]. [[21:26|for all held John as a prophet|omnes enim habebant Joannem sicut prophetam]]: all, especially the common people, held, that is, reckoned, John as a prophet. The word "as" here denotes truth, not mere likeness. For they knew that John was truly a prophet from his supernatural conception, his father's prophesying, and the other things that happened at his birth; and also from the holiness and rigour of his way of life, the power of his preaching, and because he foretold Christ most plainly by words and deeds.

paras.t: Et respondentes Jesu, dixerunt: Nescimus unde erat baptismus Joannis. In hoc mentiebantur: nam in evangelio Lucæ dicunt, Certi sunt, scilicet turba, Joannem prophetam esse. Si ergo noverant turbam de hoc certam esse, etiam ipsi certi fuerunt de hoc: falsum namque non scitur secundum Philosophum. Si itaque agnoverunt Joannem esse prophetam, non ignorabant baptismum ejus esse a Deo. Invidia tamen excæcavit eos in tantum, ut dicerent de Joanne: Dæmonium habet. Ait illis et ipse Jesus: Nec ego vobis dico in qua potestate hæc facio, ne agam contra doctrinam quam dixi: Nolite sanctum dare canibus. Ex prædicta Christi responsione elicitur, quod sæpe liceat uti cautela contra insidiatores, ut clavus clavo repercutiatur et excutiatur: quemadmodum Paulus inter Pharisæos et Sadducæos in malo concordes, discordiam suscitavit. Sic Dominus in libro Josue jussit poni insidias.
paras.en: [[21:27|And answering Jesus, they said: We know not|Et respondentes Jesu, dixerunt: Nescimus]] whence John's baptism was. In this they lied: for in the Gospel of Luke they say, [[Luke 20:6|For they are persuaded that John was a prophet|Certi sunt, scilicet turba, Joannem prophetam esse]], they being the crowd. If, then, they knew that the crowd was certain of this, they themselves were certain of it too; for, according to the Philosopher, what is false is not known. If, therefore, they recognized John to be a prophet, they were not ignorant that his baptism was from God. But envy blinded them so far that they said of John: [[Matt 11:18|He hath a devil|Dæmonium habet]]. [[21:27|He also said to them: Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things|Ait illis et ipse Jesus: Nec ego vobis dico in qua potestate hæc facio]], lest I act against the teaching I gave: [[Matt 7:6|Give not that which is holy to dogs|Nolite sanctum dare canibus]]. From this answer of Christ it is drawn that it is often lawful to use caution against those who lay snares, so that nail may be struck out by nail: as Paul stirred up discord between the Pharisees and Sadducees, who were agreed in evil[[Acts 23:6||]][[Acts 23:7||]]. So too the Lord in the book of Josue ordered an ambush to be laid[[Jos 8:2||]].

paras.t: Consequenter ostendit Christus pravitatem Judæorum per propositionem parabolæ. Quid autem vobis videtur respondendum ad parabolam quam proponam? Homo quidam habebat duos filios, et accedens ad primum, dixit, etc. Juxta litteram parabola ista difficultatem non habet; sed exponenda est secundum id quod per eam designatur. Itaque, Homo quidam, id est Deus Pater omnipotens: qui dicitur homo, non per essentiam, sed proprietatem, quia humanus, benignus, mitis, suavis; habebat duos filios, id est populum gentilem atque Judaicum. Et accedens, per naturalis legis dationem, seu internum instinctum, vel per informationem ab angelis et hominibus sanctis, videlicet Noe et Sem, etc., exhibitam, ad primum, id est populum gentilem, qui fuit a tempore Noe, dixit ei, per instinctum divinum, revelationem angelicam, seu informationem humanam: Fili, ratione creationis et provisionis, quem feci ad imaginem et similitudinem meam, vade hodie, id est tempore peregrinationis istius, operare, servando præcepta moralia, quæ sunt de naturalis dictamine rationis, in vinea mea, id est inter bonos, vel infra Ecclesiam seu gyrum justitiæ. Ille autem respondens, ait contumaciter: Nolo: quia gentiles ad idololatriam declinaverunt. Postea autem, pœnitentia motus de inobedientia sua, videlicet in prædicatione Christi inchoative, et Apostolorum completive, abiit operari in vinea Dei, juste vivendo, et unum Deum colendo.
paras.en: Next Christ shows the wickedness of the Jews by putting forward a parable. [[21:28|But what think you|Quid autem vobis videtur]] should be answered to the parable I shall put to you? [[21:28|A certain man had two sons: and coming to the first, he said|Homo quidam habebat duos filios, et accedens ad primum, dixit]], etc. In the letter this parable has no difficulty; but it is to be expounded according to what it signifies. So: [[21:28|A certain man|Homo quidam]], that is, God the Father almighty, who is called a man not by essence but by property, because He is humane, kind, gentle and sweet, [[21:28|had two sons|habebat duos filios]], that is, the Gentile and the Jewish peoples. [[21:28|and coming|Et accedens]], by giving the natural law, or by inward prompting, or by the instruction given by angels and holy men such as Noe and Sem, etc., [[21:28|to the first|ad primum]], that is, the Gentile people, which existed from the time of Noe, he said to him, by divine prompting, angelic revelation or human instruction: [[21:28|Son|Fili]], by reason of creation and providence, whom I made to my image and likeness[[Gen 1:26||]], [[21:28|go work to day|vade hodie, operare]], that is, in the time of this pilgrimage, by keeping the moral precepts, which belong to the dictate of natural reason, [[21:28|in my vineyard|in vinea mea]], that is, among the good, or within the Church, or the circle of justice. [[21:29|And he answering, said: I will not|Ille autem respondens, ait contumaciter: Nolo]], said stubbornly, for the Gentiles turned aside to idolatry. [[21:29|But afterwards, being moved with repentance, he went|Postea autem, pœnitentia motus, abiit]], repenting of his disobedience, namely by the preaching of Christ in its beginning and of the Apostles in its completion, he went to work in God's vineyard, by living justly and worshipping one God.

paras.t: Accedens autem ad alterum, id est populum Judæorum, qui a tempore Abrahæ cœpit, et per circumcisionem a gentilibus distinguebatur, dixit similiter, scilicet: Fili, vade, operare in vinea mea. Ad hunc enim populum accessit sicut ad primum, maxime quando contulit eis legem per Moysen. At ille respondens Deo, ait: Eo, domine, id est, vado quo jubes, agendo quod præcipis. Hoc dixerunt Judæi in Exodo, loquentes ad Moysen: Omnia quæ præcepit nobis Dominus, faciemus, et erimus obedientes. Et non ivit: quia post pauca, vitulum aureum adoraverunt, et infinita flagitia commiserunt. Huic parabolæ consonat quod Dominus ait in Psalmo de gentilibus et Judæis: Populus quem non cognovi servivit mihi, filii alieni mentiti sunt mihi. Porro, quod dicitur hic de duobus populis, non refertur ad eosdem numero, sed specie. Potest quoque per primum filium intelligi peccator pœnitens, per secundum, justus apostatans.
paras.en: [[21:30|And coming to the other|Accedens autem ad alterum]], that is, the Jewish people, which began from the time of Abraham and was distinguished from the Gentiles by circumcision, [[21:30|he said in like manner|dixit similiter]], namely: Son, go, work in my vineyard. For He came to this people as to the first, above all when He gave them the Law through Moses. [[21:30|And he answering said: I go, Sir|At ille respondens Deo, ait: Eo, domine]], answering God: that is, I go where You bid, doing what You command. This the Jews said in Exodus, speaking to Moses: [[Ex 24:7|All things that the Lord hath spoken, we will do, we will be obedient|Omnia quæ præcepit nobis Dominus, faciemus, et erimus obedientes]]. [[21:30|And he went not|Et non ivit]]: for shortly after they worshipped the golden calf[[Ex 32:4||]] and committed countless crimes. With this parable agrees what the Lord says in the Psalm of the Gentiles and the Jews: [[Ps 17:45|A people which I knew not, hath served me|Populus quem non cognovi servivit mihi]]; [[Ps 17:46|The children that are strangers have lied to me|filii alieni mentiti sunt mihi]]. What is said here of the two peoples refers to them not as the same individuals but as the same kind. By the first son can also be understood the repentant sinner, and by the second the just man who falls away.

paras.t: Quis ex duobus filiis istis fecit voluntatem, id est, exsecutus est præceptum Patris æterni? Dicunt ei: Primus. Nam ille pœnitentia ductus, ivit et fecit quod jusserat Deus: per quod prioris inobedientiæ veniam meruit; alius vero, non eundo, fregit promissum, et prævium perdidit meritum. Dicit illis Jesus, applicando parabolam ad propositum: Amen dico vobis, quia publicani et meretrices, id est pessimi gentilium, præcedent vos in regno Dei, id est, majoris meriti erunt in Ecclesia militanti, ampliorisque gloriæ in triumphanti, quam vos. Designantur enim per filium pœnitentem, vos autem per filium apostatantem: nam verba pulchra habetis, sed facta non consonant. Ideo subditur: Venit enim ad vos Joannes Baptista in via, id est operatione, justitiæ, juste vivendo, recte docendo, Christum annuntiando, peccatores baptizando; et non credidistis ei, sed dixistis: Dæmonium habet. Publicani autem et meretrices crediderunt ei, ad ejus exhortationem peccata sua confitendo, vitam corrigendo, et de Christi adventu credendo. Vos autem videntes fidem et emendationem istorum, vel, videntes miracula mea, quibus patet vera esse quæ ille perhibebat de me, nec pœnitentiam habuistis postea de perfidia vestra et actibus pessimis, ita ut crederetis ei, vel viventi, vel occiso, quia post mortem ejus erat verbis ipsius vehementer credendum, tanquam martyris sancti propter justitiam interfecti: in quo manifestatur obstinatio vestra.
paras.en: [[21:31|Which of the two did the father's will|Quis ex duobus filiis istis fecit voluntatem]], that is, carried out the command of the eternal Father? [[21:31|They say to him: The first|Dicunt ei: Primus]]. For he, led by repentance, went and did what God had ordered, by which he deserved pardon for his former disobedience; but the other, by not going, broke his promise and lost his earlier merit. [[21:31|Jesus saith to them|Dicit illis Jesus]], applying the parable to His purpose: [[21:31|Amen I say to you that the publicans and the harlots|Amen dico vobis, quia publicani et meretrices]], that is, the worst of the Gentiles, [[21:31|shall go into the kingdom of God before you|præcedent vos in regno Dei]], that is, will be of greater merit in the Church militant and of fuller glory in the Church triumphant than you. For they are signified by the son who repented, and you by the son who fell away: for you have fair words, but your deeds do not agree with them. So it is added: [[21:32|For John came to you in the way of justice|Venit enim ad vos Joannes in via justitiæ]] (way, that is, working), by living justly, teaching rightly, announcing Christ and baptizing sinners; [[21:32|and you did not believe him|et non credidistis ei]], but said: [[Matt 11:18|He hath a devil|Dæmonium habet]]. [[21:32|But the publicans and the harlots believed him|Publicani autem et meretrices crediderunt ei]], at his exhortation confessing their sins, amending their lives, and believing in Christ's coming. [[21:32|but you, seeing it|Vos autem videntes]], seeing the faith and amendment of these, or seeing My miracles, by which it is plain that what he testified of Me is true, [[21:32|did not even afterwards repent, that you might believe him|nec pœnitentiam habuistis postea, ut crederetis ei]], repent of your faithlessness and your most wicked deeds: believe him either living or slain, for after his death his words were greatly to be believed, as those of a holy martyr killed for justice. In this your obstinacy is shown.

paras.t: Aliam parabolam audite. Sacerdotes et Scribæ nitebantur sua subtilitate concludere Christum, capiendo eum in verbis propriæ responsionis. Sed non est sapientia, non est prudentia, non est consilium contra Dominum. Propterea Christus eos propria eorum responsione convicit, damnabilesque ostendit, proponens sequentem parabolam. Homo erat paterfamilias, qui plantavit vineam. Per hunc hominem designatur Deus Pater, propter causas præhabitas. Et licet per vineam intelligi possit universalis Ecclesia, tamen hoc loco per eam exprimitur Synagoga: de qua per Jeremiam loquitur Dominus, Pastores multi, inquiens, demoliti sunt vineam meam; et in Isaia, Vinea, inquit, Domini exercituum domus Israel est, et vir Juda germen delectabile ejus. Hanc Deus plantavit corporaliter, collocando Judæos in terra promissionis, et spiritualiter, constituendo eos in fide et gratia. Propter quod ait Psalmista: Vineam de Ægypto transtulisti, ejecisti gentes, et plantasti eam. Et sepem circumdedit ei, id est, angelorum auxilio atque custodia, Patriarcharum et Prophetarum munitione ac meritis, traditione quoque mandatorum ac legis, eam munivit. Vel per sepem, ad litteram intelligitur fortitudo murorum civitatis in Judæa metropolis. Et fodit in ea torcular, id est altare: quod nominatur torcular, quia in eo effundebatur sanguis victimarum, sicut in torculari exprimitur liquor uvarum; et ædificavit turrim, id est templum sublime: de quo exponit Hieronymus illud Michææ prophetæ, Et tu, turris Gregis nebulosa, ad te veniet potestas prima, videlicet Christus, virtus et sapientia Patris, portans omnia verbo virtutis suæ. Et locavit, id est, sub pacto retributionis regendam atque colendam commisit, eam agricolis, id est prælatis et doctoribus: quorum aliqui boni fuerunt, ut Moyses et Aaron; et aliqui mali, de quibus subditur. Unde Isaias insinuans se esse agricolam Synagogæ, ait ad eam: Tritura mea, et filia areæ meæ, quæ audivi a Domino, indicavi tibi. Et peregre profectus est, id est, se quasi absentem exhibuit, dimittendo hominem propriæ voluntati, et ejus pœnitentiam præstolando ac judicium differendo. Porro parabola ista pene sub eisdem verbis habetur in Isaia, in quo legitur: Vinea facta est dilecto, et sepivit eam, et turrim ædificavit in medio ejus, et torcular exstruxit in ea.
paras.en: [[21:33|Hear ye another parable|Aliam parabolam audite]]. The priests and scribes were striving by their subtlety to corner Christ, catching Him in the words of His own answer. But [[Prov 21:30|There is no wisdom, there is no prudence, there is no counsel against the Lord|non est sapientia, non est prudentia, non est consilium contra Dominum]]. So Christ convicted them by their own answer and showed them worthy of condemnation, putting forward the following parable. [[21:33|There was a man, an householder, who planted a vineyard|Homo erat paterfamilias, qui plantavit vineam]]. This man signifies God the Father, for the reasons given before. And though the vineyard can be understood as the universal Church, here it stands for the Synagogue, of which the Lord says through Jeremias: [[Jer 12:10|Many pastors have destroyed my vineyard|Pastores multi, inquiens, demoliti sunt vineam meam]]; and in Isaias: [[Is 5:7|For the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel: and the man of Juda, his pleasant plant|Vinea, inquit, Domini exercituum domus Israel est, et vir Juda germen delectabile ejus]]. God planted it in body, by settling the Jews in the land of promise, and in spirit, by establishing them in faith and grace. Hence the Psalmist says: [[Ps 79:9|Thou hast brought a vineyard out of Egypt: thou hast cast out the Gentiles and planted it|Vineam de Ægypto transtulisti, ejecisti gentes, et plantasti eam]]. [[21:33|and made a hedge round about it|Et sepem circumdedit ei]]: that is, He fortified it with the help and guard of angels, the defence and merits of the Patriarchs and Prophets, and also the giving of the commandments and the Law. Or, in the letter, the hedge means the strong walls of the chief city in Judea. [[21:33|and dug in it a press|Et fodit in ea torcular]], that is, the altar, which is called a press because the blood of victims was poured out on it, as the juice of grapes is pressed out in a winepress; [[21:33|and built a tower|et ædificavit turrim]], that is, the lofty temple, of which Jerome expounds that saying of the prophet Micheas: [[Mich 4:8|And thou, O cloudy tower of the flock|Et tu, turris Gregis nebulosa]], [[Mich 4:8|unto thee shall it come: yea the first power shall come|ad te veniet potestas prima]]: namely Christ, the power and wisdom of the Father[[1 Cor 1:24||]], [[Heb 1:3|upholding all things by the word of his power|portans omnia verbo virtutis suæ]]. [[21:33|and let it out|Et locavit]], that is, entrusted it to be ruled and tilled under a compact of reward, [[21:33|to husbandmen|eam agricolis]], that is, to prelates and teachers, some of whom were good, like Moses and Aaron, and some bad, of whom it goes on to speak. Hence Isaias, hinting that he is a husbandman of the Synagogue, says to her: [[Is 21:10|O my thrashing, and the children of my floor, that which I have heard of the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, I have declared unto you|Tritura mea, et filia areæ meæ, quæ audivi a Domino, indicavi tibi]]. [[21:33|and went into a strange country|Et peregre profectus est]], that is, He showed Himself as it were absent, leaving man to his own will, awaiting his repentance and putting off judgment. This parable is found in almost the same words in Isaias, where it reads: [[Is 5:1|My beloved had a vineyard|Vinea facta est dilecto]] [Denis's text: "A vineyard was made for the beloved"], [[Is 5:2|And he fenced it in|et sepivit eam]], [[Is 5:2|and built a tower in the midst thereof, and set up a winepress therein|et turrim ædificavit in medio ejus, et torcular exstruxit in ea]].

paras.t: Quum autem tempus fructuum appropinquasset, id est post legis lationem, quum Synagoga debuisset opera bona producere, secundum legis præcepta, misit servos suos, sanctos Prophetas priores, ad agricolas, id est sacerdotes, Scribas et principes Synagogæ, ut acciperent fructus ejus, id est, populum Synagogæ ad Deum reducerent, et opera virtuosa in eis invenirent. Et agricolæ apprehensis servis ejus, alium ceciderunt, id est, percusserunt, ut Jeremiam, alium occiderunt, ut Isaiam, alium lapidaverunt, ut Zachariam Joiadæ filium. Iterum misit alios servos plures prioribus, videlicet posteriores Prophetas ac justos agricolis, propter eamdem causam; et fecerunt agricolæ illis similiter, sicut prioribus. Sacerdotes namque, reges et populus Judæorum, diversa tormenta intulerunt sanctis vatibus ad se missis. Propter quod Stephanus ait Judæis: Quem Prophetarum non sunt persecuti patres vestri? Et Apostolus ad Hebræos: Alii, inquit, ludibria et verbera experti, insuper vincula et carceres; lapidati sunt, secti sunt, tentati sunt, in occisione gladii mortui sunt.
paras.en: [[21:34|And when the time of the fruits drew nigh|Quum autem tempus fructuum appropinquasset]], that is, after the giving of the Law, when the Synagogue ought to have brought forth good works according to the precepts of the Law, [[21:34|he sent his servants|misit servos suos]], the earlier holy Prophets, [[21:34|to the husbandmen|ad agricolas]], that is, the priests, scribes and rulers of the Synagogue, [[21:34|that they might receive the fruits thereof|ut acciperent fructus ejus]], that is, that they might lead the people of the Synagogue back to God and find virtuous works in them. [[21:35|And the husbandmen laying hands on his servants, beat one|Et agricolæ apprehensis servis ejus, alium ceciderunt]], that is, struck him, as Jeremias[[Jer 37:14||]], [[21:35|and killed another|alium occiderunt]], as Isaias, [[21:35|and stoned another|alium lapidaverunt]], as Zacharias the son of Joiada[[2 Par 24:21||]]. [[21:36|Again he sent other servants, more than the former|Iterum misit alios servos plures prioribus]], namely the later Prophets and just men, to the husbandmen for the same purpose; [[21:36|and they did to them in like manner|et fecerunt agricolæ illis similiter]], the husbandmen, as to the former. For the priests, kings and people of the Jews inflicted various torments on the holy prophets sent to them. Hence Stephen says to the Jews: [[Acts 7:52|Which of the prophets have not your fathers persecuted|Quem Prophetarum non sunt persecuti patres vestri?]]? And the Apostle to the Hebrews: [[Heb 11:36|And others had trial of mockeries and stripes: moreover also of bands and prisons|Alii, inquit, ludibria et verbera experti, insuper vincula et carceres]]; [[Heb 11:37|They were stoned, they were cut asunder, they were tempted, they were put to death by the sword|lapidati sunt, secti sunt, tentati sunt, in occisione gladii mortui sunt]].

paras.t: Novissime autem, quando videlicet venit temporis plenitudo, et in ultima mundi ætate, quum multo tempore nullus apparuisset Propheta, misit ad eos filium suum, per incarnationem et prædicationem ipsius, quando Verbum caro factum est, et habitavit in nobis. Missio autem Filii intelligi potest, vel ipsa incarnatio Verbi, quæ non fuit localis legatio, sed humanæ naturæ assumptio; vel Verbi jam incarnati corporalis atque localis destinatio, qua Christus Judæos visibiliter accessit et docuit. Dicens, ipse Pater, non assertive, sed indicative, videlicet insinuando quid agricolæ merito facerent, et quod verisimile erat eos esse facturos: Verebuntur, id est, timebunt et honorabunt, filium meum unigenitum et dilectum, mihi consubstantialem, coæternum et coæqualem. Sed ita non fecerunt, ut subditur. Ex hoc loco Hieronymus et Augustinus improbant hæresim Arii atque Eunomii, dicentium Filium Patre minorem et puram creaturam, eo quod dicat se ignorare diem judicii. Ecce hoc loco Pater ait, Verebuntur Filium meum; et in Luca ait, Verebuntur forsitan Filium meum. Numquid et Pater hoc dicit dubitando vel ignorando? Quod ergo illi pro Patre responderint, nos pro Filio respondebimus.
paras.en: [[21:37|And last of all|Novissime autem]], namely when the fulness of time came[[Gal 4:4||]], in the last age of the world, when for a long time no Prophet had appeared, [[21:37|he sent to them his son|misit ad eos filium suum]], by His incarnation and preaching, when [[John 1:14|the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us|Verbum caro factum est, et habitavit in nobis]]. The sending of the Son can be understood either as the incarnation of the Word itself, which was not a sending from place to place but the taking of human nature; or as the bodily and local sending of the Word already incarnate, by which Christ came visibly to the Jews and taught them. [[21:37|saying|Dicens]], the Father Himself, not as asserting but as indicating, namely hinting at what the husbandmen ought rightly to do and what it was likely they would do: [[21:37|They will reverence|Verebuntur]], that is, fear and honour, [[21:37|my son|filium meum]], My only-begotten and beloved, consubstantial, coeternal and coequal with Me. But they did not do so, as is added. From this place Jerome and Augustine refute the heresy of Arius and Eunomius, who said the Son is less than the Father and a mere creature, because He says He does not know the day of judgment. See, here the Father says, They will reverence my son; and in Luke He says: [[Luke 20:13|It may be, when they see him, they will reverence him|Verebuntur forsitan Filium meum]]. Does the Father say this too doubting or not knowing? What they answer, then, for the Father, we will answer for the Son.

paras.t: Agricolæ autem, id est principes sacerdotum, et ceteri sacerdotes ac Scribæ, videntes filium Dei Patris tanta miracula operantem, tamque efficacissime prædicantem, et cetera quæ de Christo prænuntiata fuerunt, in se implentem, dixerunt intra se, id est, cogitaverunt, sed inferioribus non manifestaverunt: Hic est hæres, id est Messias rex Israel, Dominus Synagogæ terræque nostræ. Ex quo videntur Christum cognovisse: quod qualiter verum sit, statim discutietur. Venite, occidamus eum. Collegerunt namque pontifices et Pharisæi concilium, dicentes: Quid facimus, quia hic homo multa signa facit? Et ab illo die cogitaverunt interficere eum. Unde Christus testatur: Super me cogitaverunt consilia, dicentes: Venite, mittamus lignum in panem ejus, et eradamus eum de terra viventium. Et in Psalmo: Adversum me susurrabant omnes inimici mei. Et habebimus hæreditatem ejus, id est, terram et populum Israel possidebimus, sicut hucusque possidebamus. Ad hoc enim moti sunt principes Judæorum occidere Christum, ne possessionem terræ et dominium populi perderent. Unde in evangelio Joannis dicunt: Si dimittimus eum sic, omnes credent in eum; et venient Romani, et tollent locum nostrum et gentem. Denique delectabat eos principatus terrenus, secundum Augustinum: quem viderunt sibi per Christum auferri, qui paupertatem et humilitatem edocuit, et populum ad se convertit. Sed erraverunt. Ideo namque perdiderunt locum et gentem, quoniam Christum interfecerunt: quia in ultionem sanguinis Christi destruxerunt Romani Judæorum urbes ac populum, juxta illud Danielis: Post hebdomades sexaginta duas occidetur Christus, et non erit ejus populus, qui eum negaturus est; et civitatem et sanctuarium dissipabit populus cum duce venturo.
paras.en: [[21:38|But the husbandmen seeing the son|Agricolæ autem videntes filium]], the husbandmen, that is, the chief priests and the other priests and scribes, seeing the Son of God the Father working such miracles, preaching so very powerfully, and fulfilling in Himself the other things foretold of Christ, [[21:38|said among themselves|dixerunt intra se]], that is, thought it, but did not show it to those beneath them: [[21:38|This is the heir|Hic est hæres]], that is, the Messias, the King of Israel, the Lord of the Synagogue and of our land. From this they seem to have recognized Christ; how this is true will be discussed shortly. [[21:38|come, let us kill him|Venite, occidamus eum]]. For [[John 11:47|The chief priests, therefore, and the Pharisees gathered a council and said: What do we, for this man doth many miracles|Collegerunt namque pontifices et Pharisæi concilium, dicentes: Quid facimus, quia hic homo multa signa facit?]]? [[John 11:53|From that day therefore they devised to put him to death|Et ab illo die cogitaverunt interficere eum]]. Hence Christ testifies: [[Jer 11:19|they had devised counsels against me, saying: Let us put wood on his bread, and cut him off from the land of the living|Super me cogitaverunt consilia, dicentes: Venite, mittamus lignum in panem ejus, et eradamus eum de terra viventium]]. And in the Psalm: [[Ps 40:8|All my enemies whispered together against me|Adversum me susurrabant omnes inimici mei]]. [[21:38|and we shall have his inheritance|Et habebimus hæreditatem ejus]], that is, we shall possess the land and people of Israel, as we have possessed them till now. For the rulers of the Jews were moved to kill Christ so as not to lose the possession of the land and the lordship of the people. Hence in the Gospel of John they say: [[John 11:48|If we let him alone so, all will believe in him; and the Romans will come, and take away our place and nation|Si dimittimus eum sic, omnes credent in eum; et venient Romani, et tollent locum nostrum et gentem]]. Indeed, according to Augustine, earthly rule delighted them, and they saw it taken from them by Christ, who taught poverty and humility[[Matt 5:3||]][[Matt 11:29||]] and turned the people to Himself. But they were wrong. For they lost their place and nation precisely because they killed Christ: since in vengeance for Christ's blood the Romans destroyed the cities and people of the Jews, according to that saying of Daniel: [[Dan 9:26|And after sixty-two weeks Christ shall be slain: and the people that shall deny him shall not be his. And a people, with their leader, that shall come, shall destroy the city, and the sanctuary|Post hebdomades sexaginta duas occidetur Christus, et non erit ejus populus, qui eum negaturus est; et civitatem et sanctuarium dissipabit populus cum duce venturo]].

paras.t: Et apprehensum eum, videlicet Filium Dei, ejecerunt agricolæ extra vineam, id est extra urbem Jerusalem Judææ metropolim, in qua erat templum, et occiderunt eum, crucifigentes ipsum in loco Calvariæ. Unde ad Hebræos dicit Apostolus: Jesus ut sanctificaret populum, extra portam passus est.
paras.en: [[21:39|And taking him, they cast him forth out of the vineyard|Et apprehensum eum ejecerunt extra vineam]], namely the Son of God, the husbandmen cast Him out of the vineyard, that is, out of the city of Jerusalem, the chief city of Judea, in which was the temple, [[21:39|and killed him|et occiderunt eum]], crucifying Him on the place of Calvary. Hence the Apostle says to the Hebrews: [[Heb 13:12|Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people by his own blood, suffered without the gate|Jesus ut sanctificaret populum, extra portam passus est]].

paras.t: Quum ergo venerit dominus vineæ, id est, quum Deus cœperit judicare, et judicando ac præmiando visitare Synagogam, vel in morte singulorum, vel quando adduxerit exercitum Romanorum contra Judæam, quid faciet agricolis illis? id est, quam pœnam inferet pro culpis tam magnis? Aiunt illi: Malos agricolas male perdet, id est, dure corripiet et occidet. Perdet enim eos male, loquendo de malo pœnæ, non culpæ, quum tradiderit eos in manus Titi et Romanorum. Et vineam suam, videlicet electos Judæos et primitivam Ecclesiam, locabit aliis, id est agricolis bonis, qui reddant ei fructum temporibus suis. Hoc fecit Deus quando reprobatis Judæorum prælatis, commisit Ecclesiam Apostolis, eorumque successoribus et adjutoribus, qui obtulerunt Deo fructum, id est multos ad fidem conversos, sicut Apostolus ait quibusdam: Opus meum vos estis in Domino; et, In Christo per Evangelium ego vos genui.
paras.en: [[21:40|When therefore the lord of the vineyard shall come|Quum ergo venerit dominus vineæ]], that is, when God begins to judge, and in judging and rewarding to visit the Synagogue, whether in the death of each one or when He brings the army of the Romans against Judea, [[21:40|what will he do to those husbandmen|quid faciet agricolis illis]]? That is, what punishment will He inflict for such great faults? [[21:41|They say to him: He will bring those evil men to an evil end|Aiunt illi: Malos agricolas male perdet]] [literally "He will evilly destroy the evil husbandmen"], that is, He will chastise them harshly and kill them. For He will destroy them evilly, speaking of the evil of punishment, not of guilt, when He hands them over into the hands of Titus and the Romans. [[21:41|and let out his vineyard|et vineam suam locabit]], namely the elect Jews and the primitive Church, [[21:41|to other husbandmen|aliis]], that is, to good husbandmen, [[21:41|that shall render him the fruit in due season|qui reddant ei fructum temporibus suis]]. God did this when, having rejected the prelates of the Jews, He entrusted the Church to the Apostles and their successors and helpers, who offered God fruit, that is, many converted to the faith, as the Apostle says to some: [[1 Cor 9:1|Are not you my work in the Lord|Opus meum vos estis in Domino]]? and: [[1 Cor 4:15|in Christ Jesus, by the gospel, I have begotten you|In Christo per Evangelium ego vos genui]].

paras.t: Sed prædictæ responsioni Judæorum videtur contrarium, quod in Evangelio Lucæ legitur eos dixisse, Absit, videlicet ut malos male perdat, et vineam aliis locet. Et respondendum, quod præinductam responsionem, scilicet, Malos male perdet, Lucas et Marcus describunt, quasi a Christo prolatam; Matthæus vero dicit eam ab aliis datam. Nec tamen est dissonantia in Evangelio veritatis, quia ut Lucas enarrat, Christus dixit parabolam istam ad plebem, quamvis sacerdotes concerneret, qui etiam erant præsentes ac audientes. In plebe vero multi erant qui Christo favebant et crediderant; et isti primo dixerunt, Malos male perdet, ut refert Matthæus. Quorum responsionem Christus approbando repetiit: quo audito, sacerdotes attendentes ad se pertinere parabolam, conscientia remordente, dixerunt, Absit, ut recitat Lucas.
paras.en: But against this answer of the Jews seems to be what is read in the Gospel of Luke, that they said: [[Luke 20:16|God forbid|Absit]], namely that He should destroy the wicked wickedly and let His vineyard out to others. The answer is that Luke and Mark describe the answer quoted, He will destroy the wicked wickedly, as spoken by Christ, while Matthew says it was given by others. Yet there is no discord in the Gospel of truth; for, as Luke relates, Christ spoke this parable to the people[[Luke 20:9||]], though it concerned the priests, who were also present and listening. Among the people there were many who favoured Christ and had believed; and these first said, He will destroy the wicked wickedly, as Matthew reports. Christ repeated their answer, approving it; and on hearing it the priests, seeing that the parable concerned them, their conscience stinging them, said, God forbid, as Luke recounts.

paras.t: Consequenter probat Salvator quod parabolice dixit, allegando scripturam libri Psalmorum. Dicit illis Jesus: Nunquam legistis in Scripturis? tanquam dicat: Imo sæpius in Psalmo legistis: Lapidem, id est Christum, de quo Daniel dicit: Lapis qui abscissus est de monte sine manibus, factus est mons magnus, et implevit universam superficiem terræ. Petra namque est Christus, secundum Apostolum. Quem reprobaverunt ædificantes, id est prædicti agricolæ, sacerdotes et prælati Synagogæ: quorum fuit populum in fide et moribus ædificare; sed sicut solo nomine erant agricolæ, et revera dissipatores, sic solo nomine erant ædificatores, et reipsa destructores. Hic Christus factus est in caput anguli, id est principium seu lapis angularis, in quo conjuncti sunt duo populi, gentiles et Judæi, ad constituendum unam Ecclesiam, sicut in saxo angulari uniuntur duo parietes ad constituendam domum. Unde in Isaia habetur: Hæc dicit Dominus: Ecce ego mittam in fundamentis Sion lapidem, lapidem angularem, probatum, pretiosum, in fundamento fundatum, et qui crediderit in eum non confundetur, vel, non festinet, secundum aliam translationem. A Domino factum est istud, id est, divina virtute et gratia est unio ista duorum populorum in Christo, et Christi ignominiose occisi tanta sublimatio. Propter quod ait Apostolus: In quo et vos coædificamini in habitaculum Dei in Spiritu Sancto. Et est mirabile in oculis nostris interioribus. Quid enim ita mirabile, sicut conversio totius mundi ad hominem crucifixum, qui paulo ante dicere potuit, Ego autem sum vermis et non homo, opprobrium hominum et abjectio plebis?
paras.en: Next the Saviour proves what He said in parable by citing the scripture of the book of Psalms. [[21:42|Jesus saith to them: Have you never read in the Scriptures|Dicit illis Jesus: Nunquam legistis in Scripturis?]]? As if to say: Indeed you have often read in the Psalm[[Ps 117:22||]]: [[21:42|The stone|Lapidem]], that is, Christ, of whom Daniel says: [[Dan 2:34|a stone was cut out of a mountain without hands|Lapis qui abscissus est de monte sine manibus]], [[Dan 2:35|became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth|factus est mons magnus, et implevit universam superficiem terræ]]. For [[1 Cor 10:4|the rock was Christ|Petra namque est Christus]], according to the Apostle. [[21:42|which the builders rejected|Quem reprobaverunt ædificantes]], that is, the husbandmen already spoken of, the priests and prelates of the Synagogue, whose task it was to build up the people in faith and morals; but as they were husbandmen in name only and in reality wasters, so they were builders in name only and in fact destroyers. [[21:42|the same is become the head of the corner|Hic Christus factus est in caput anguli]]: this Christ, that is, the beginning or the corner stone, in which the two peoples, Gentiles and Jews, are joined to make one Church, as two walls are united in a corner stone to make a house. Hence it is said in Isaias: [[Is 28:16|thus saith the Lord God: Behold I will lay a stone in the foundations of Sion, a tried stone, a corner stone, a precious stone, founded in the foundation|Hæc dicit Dominus: Ecce ego mittam in fundamentis Sion lapidem, lapidem angularem, probatum, pretiosum, in fundamento fundatum]], [[Is 28:16|He that believeth|et qui crediderit in eum]] shall not be confounded, or, [[Is 28:16|let him not hasten|non festinet]], according to another translation. [[21:42|By the Lord this has been done|A Domino factum est istud]], that is, it is by divine power and grace that there is this union of the two peoples in Christ, and so great an exaltation of Christ, who was shamefully slain. Hence the Apostle says: [[Eph 2:22|In whom you also are built together into an habitation of God in the Spirit|In quo et vos coædificamini in habitaculum Dei in Spiritu Sancto]]. [[21:42|and it is wonderful in our eyes|Et est mirabile in oculis nostris]], our inward eyes.
