For what is so wonderful as the conversion of the whole world to a crucified man, who a little before could say: [[Ps 21:7|But I am a worm, and no man: the reproach of men, and the outcast of the people.|Ego autem sum vermis et non homo, opprobrium hominum et abjectio plebis?]]?

paras.t: Multi exponunt hanc auctoritatem ad litteram, de quodam lapide magno quem ædificantes templum Salomonis sæpe rejecerunt tanquam inutilem, non invenientes ubi congrue poneretur in ædificio, et tandem inventus est locus conveniens in angulo duorum parietum, ut illic poneretur. Sed istud non videtur conveniens, quia probatio per Scripturam non tenet nisi a sensu litterali, secundum Augustinum. Christus autem per scripturam prædictam probat suum intentum, videlicet se a Judæorum principibus reprobandum. Quod plenius patet in evangelio Lucæ, ubi quum Judæi dixissent, Absit, scilicet, ut malos male perdat, Christus objecit et ait: Quid est ergo quod scriptum est, Lapidem quem reprobaverunt ædificantes, etc.? Tanquam dicat: Hoc aliter non valet impleri nisi per me. Denique nulla Scriptura canonica recitat de lapide tali in templo Salomonis. Sed et Petrus in Actibus Apostolorum loquens de Christo: Hic est (inquit) lapis qui reprobatus est a vobis ædificantibus. De quo et Paulus: Ipso, ait, summo angulari lapide Christo Jesu.
paras.en: Many expound this text in the letter of a certain great stone which the builders of Solomon's temple often rejected as useless, not finding where it could fittingly be placed in the building, until at last a suitable place was found for it at the corner of two walls. But this does not seem fitting, because proof from Scripture holds only from the literal sense, according to Augustine; and Christ proves His point by this scripture, namely that He was to be rejected by the rulers of the Jews. This is plainer in the Gospel of Luke, where, when the Jews had said, God forbid (that is, that He should destroy the wicked wickedly), Christ objected and said: [[Luke 20:17|What is this then that is written, The stone, which the builders rejected|Quid est ergo quod scriptum est, Lapidem quem reprobaverunt ædificantes]], etc.? As if to say: This cannot be fulfilled otherwise than through Me. Indeed, no canonical Scripture tells of such a stone in Solomon's temple. And Peter too, in the Acts of the Apostles, speaking of Christ, says: [[Acts 4:11|This is the stone which was rejected by you the builders|Hic est (inquit) lapis qui reprobatus est a vobis ædificantibus]]. Of whom Paul also says: [[Eph 2:20|Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone|Ipso, ait, summo angulari lapide Christo Jesu]].

paras.t: Ideo dico vobis, quod auferetur a vobis, exigente et operante divina justitia, regnum Dei, id est regnum Ecclesiæ militantis, regnum quoque cæleste, vel sacra Scriptura, secundum Hieronymum, et dabitur genti, per Apostolorum prædicationem credenti, facienti fructus ejus, id est opera virtuosa, per quæ ad regnum Dei pertingitur, et quæ in Scriptura præcipiuntur: de quibus ad Galatas scribit Apostolus, Fructus autem (inquiens) Spiritus, est caritas, gaudium, pax, patientia, longanimitas, etc. Et qui ceciderit super lapidem istum, id est fidelis impie agens, confringetur, id est, spiritualiter destruetur sive lædetur, non penitus conteretur: super quem vero ceciderit lapis iste, id est infidelis cui Christus irruerit per districtionem judicii, conteret eum, id est, penitus condemnabit, atque ab omni bono spirituali comminuet. Tanguntur hic duo peccantium genera, utpote Christianorum et infidelium. Fideles autem, quamvis iniqui, tamen quia in Christo fundantur per fidem, dum peccant dicuntur cadere super Christum, quem offendunt; sed non penitus conteruntur, quoniam sæpe per misericordiam Dei reformantur, fortioresque surgunt, et in peccantibus manet fides, quamvis informis. Infideles vero, qui in Christo nequaquam fundantur, dum peccant, incidunt in manus Dei viventis: sicque lapis iste seu Christus, irruit super eos, et conterit eos, quemadmodum in Judæis videmus impletum. Unde in Jeremia scribitur: Induc super eos diem afflictionis, et duplici contritione contere eos, Domine.
paras.en: [[21:43|Therefore I say to you that the kingdom of God shall be taken from you|Ideo dico vobis, quia auferetur a vobis regnum Dei]], by the demand and working of divine justice: the kingdom of God, that is, the kingdom of the Church militant, and also the heavenly kingdom, or Holy Scripture, according to Jerome; [[21:43|and shall be given to a nation|et dabitur genti]] that believes through the preaching of the Apostles, [[21:43|yielding the fruits thereof|facienti fructus ejus]], that is, virtuous works, by which the kingdom of God is reached, and which are commanded in Scripture, of which the Apostle writes to the Galatians: [[Gal 5:22|But the fruit of the Spirit is, charity, joy, peace, patience|Fructus autem (inquiens) Spiritus, est caritas, gaudium, pax, patientia]], [[Gal 5:22|longanimity|longanimitas]], etc. [[21:44|And whosoever shall fall on this stone|Et qui ceciderit super lapidem istum]], that is, a believer who acts wickedly, [[21:44|shall be broken|confringetur]], that is, shall be spiritually destroyed or harmed, but not wholly crushed; [[21:44|but on whomsoever it shall fall|super quem vero ceciderit]] this stone, that is, the unbeliever upon whom Christ shall rush in the severity of judgment, [[21:44|it shall grind him to powder|conteret eum]], that is, shall condemn him utterly and break him away from every spiritual good. Two kinds of sinners are touched on here, Christians and unbelievers. Believers, though wicked, yet because they are founded on Christ by faith, are said when they sin to fall upon Christ, whom they offend; but they are not wholly crushed, since they are often restored by God's mercy and rise stronger, and faith remains in them while they sin, though unformed [fides informis: faith without charity]. But unbelievers, who are in no way founded on Christ, when they sin [[Heb 10:31|fall into the hands of the living God|incidunt in manus Dei viventis]]: and so this stone, Christ, rushes upon them and crushes them, as we see fulfilled in the Jews. Hence it is written in Jeremias: [[Jer 17:18|bring upon them the day of affliction, and with a double destruction, destroy them|Induc super eos diem afflictionis, et duplici contritione contere eos]], O Lord.

paras.t: Et quum audissent principes sacerdotum et Pharisæi parabolas ejus jam commemoratas, cognoverunt quod de ipsis diceret qui in parabolis denotavit, videlicet quod ipsi essent mali agricolæ, impii ædificatores, et quod viso eo, dixissent, Hic est hæres. Et quærentes eum tenere, id est ad interficiendum comprehendere, tanquam mendacem, vel quia tam dure corripuit eos, timuerunt turbas, ne ab eis resistentiam paterentur, quoniam sicut prophetam eum habebant, id est, turbæ reputaverunt Jesum esse prophetam. Ecce quomodo sacerdotes, Scribæ et Pharisæi, inde deteriores et obstinatiores effecti sunt, scilicet de justa Christi increpatione, unde emendari debebant. Tales sunt qui suam accusationem et redargutionem non dignantur advertere. De quibus ad Timotheum dicit Apostolus: A veritate quidem auditum avertent; et Amos propheta, Odio habuerunt corripientem. Horum nequissimus morbus vocatur, Noli me tangere.
paras.en: [[21:45|And when the chief priests and Pharisees had heard his parables|Et quum audissent principes sacerdotum et Pharisæi parabolas ejus]], the parables just related, [[21:45|they knew that he spoke of them|cognoverunt quod de ipsis diceret]], whom He denoted in the parables, namely that they were the wicked husbandmen and the impious builders, and that on seeing Him they had said, This is the heir. [[21:46|And seeking to lay hands on him|Et quærentes eum tenere]], that is, to seize Him to kill Him, as a liar, or because He had rebuked them so harshly, [[21:46|they feared the multitudes|timuerunt turbas]], lest they should meet resistance from them, [[21:46|because they held him as a prophet|quoniam sicut prophetam eum habebant]], that is, the crowds reckoned Jesus to be a prophet. See how the priests, scribes and Pharisees were made worse and more obstinate by the very thing that should have amended them, namely Christ's just rebuke. Such are those who do not deign to heed their own accusation and reproof, of whom the Apostle says to Timothy: [[2 Tim 4:4|will indeed turn away their hearing from the truth|A veritate quidem auditum avertent]]; and the prophet Amos: [[Amos 5:10|They have hated him that rebuketh|Odio habuerunt corripientem]]. The name of their most wicked disease is: Touch me not [Noli me tangere: the name of an ulcer that grows worse when it is touched].

paras.t: Circa hunc locum opportune quærendum est, an Judæi cognoverunt Jesum esse regem Messiam seu verum Christum in lege promissum. Hæc autem quæstio supra mota atque soluta est; sed nunc diligentius videtur tractanda. Et apparet primo, quod sic, imo auctoritate irrefragabili Salvatoris, qui in isto capitulo perhibet agricolas ipso viso dixisse: Hic est hæres. Quocirca ait Hieronymus: Manifeste probat Dominus his verbis, Judæorum principes, non per ignorantiam, sed per invidiam, Dei Filium crucifixisse. Ambrosius quoque testatur, quod cognoverunt Jesum esse Christum in lege promissum, non tamen quod esset verus Deus. Quam responsionem sequitur Thomas. Idem dicit Glossa hoc loco. Chrysostomus etiam dicit, quod ex omnibus operibus ejus cognoverunt eum esse Filium Dei. Et iterum: Sacerdotes, inquit, omnibus malis repleti, qui jam in Deo sperare non poterant, in ipsum Dominum manus mittebant, non ignorantes eum esse Filium Dei, sed sibi ipsis non parcentes. In oppositum est quod ait Apostolus: Si cognovissent, nunquam Dominum gloriæ crucifixissent; et Petrus, Et nunc, fratres, scio quia per ignorantiam fecistis, sicut et principes vestri. Christus quoque in cruce: Pater, inquit, ignosce illis, quia nesciunt quid faciunt.
paras.en: At this place it is fitting to ask whether the Jews knew that Jesus was the King Messias, or the true Christ promised in the Law. This question was raised and answered above, but it seems it should now be treated more carefully. And first it appears that they did, indeed by the irrefutable authority of the Saviour, who in this chapter declares that the husbandmen, on seeing Him, said: [[21:38|This is the heir|Hic est hæres]]. Hence Jerome says: By these words the Lord plainly proves that the rulers of the Jews crucified the Son of God not through ignorance but through envy. Ambrose too testifies that they knew Jesus was the Christ promised in the Law, but not that He was true God; and Thomas follows this answer. The Gloss says the same here. Chrysostom also says that from all His works they knew Him to be the Son of God; and again: The priests, he says, filled with every evil, who could no longer hope in God, laid hands on the Lord Himself, not ignorant that He was the Son of God, but not sparing themselves. Against this is what the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 2:8|if they had known it, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory|Si cognovissent, nunquam Dominum gloriæ crucifixissent]]; and Peter: [[Acts 3:17|And now, brethren, I know that you did it through ignorance: as did also your rulers|Et nunc, fratres, scio quia per ignorantiam fecistis, sicut et principes vestri]]. And Christ on the cross: [[Luke 23:34|Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do|Pater, inquit, ignosce illis, quia nesciunt quid faciunt]].

paras.t: Respondent quidam, quod Judæi in lege et Prophetis eruditi, videlicet sacerdotes, Scribæ et Pharisæi, noverunt Jesum esse prophetam, et Christum in lege promissum et divinitus missum, non tamen quod esset Deus. Viderunt enim in Christo impleri omnia quæ Scriptura prædixit de signis, loco, tempore atque operibus sui adventus. Signum enim adventus Christi fuit, impletio hebdomadarum de quibus Daniel prophetavit, translatio quoque regni, nativitas in Bethlehem, multaque alia. Vulgares vero ignorantes Scripturam, Christum non cognoverunt, nec quantum ad ejus humanitatem, nec quantum ad ejus divinitatem. Hæc responsio concordat Ambrosio. Quam sequitur Lyra, præter hoc quod responsio hæc ait, eruditos in lege non cognovisse Christum quoad ejus divinitatem. Asserit igitur Lyra, quod majores Judæorum cognoverunt Christum quantum ad utramque ejus naturam: quia sicut Scripturæ assignant signa et modum adventus Christi quantum ad ejus humanitatem; sic de ejus divinitate manifeste loquuntur: ut quum dicitur per Jeremiam, Suscitabo David germen justum; et post pauca, Hoc est nomen quod vocabunt eum, Dominus justus noster: loco cujus in Hebræo habetur nomen Domini tetragrammaton, quod non convenit nisi vero Deo. Et Isaias: Parvulus, inquit, natus est nobis, et vocabitur nomen ejus, Admirabilis, Consiliarius, Deus, Fortis, Pater futuri sæculi, Princeps pacis.
paras.en: Some answer that the Jews learned in the Law and the Prophets, namely the priests, scribes and Pharisees, knew that Jesus was a prophet, and the Christ promised in the Law and sent by God, but not that He was God. For they saw fulfilled in Christ all that Scripture foretold of the signs, place, time and works of His coming. For a sign of Christ's coming was the fulfilment of the weeks of which Daniel prophesied[[Dan 9:24||]], also the passing of the kingdom, the birth in Bethlehem, and much else. But the common people, ignorant of Scripture, did not know Christ, either as to His humanity or as to His divinity. This answer agrees with Ambrose. Lyra follows it, except where this answer says that those learned in the Law did not know Christ as to His divinity. For Lyra asserts that the elders of the Jews knew Christ as to both His natures: because, as the Scriptures give the signs and manner of Christ's coming as to His humanity, so they speak plainly of His divinity; as when it is said through Jeremias: [[Jer 23:5|I will raise up to David a just branch|Suscitabo David germen justum]]; and a little after: [[Jer 23:6|this is the name that they shall call him: The Lord our just one|Hoc est nomen quod vocabunt eum, Dominus justus noster]], in place of which the Hebrew has the four-lettered name of the Lord [the Tetragrammaton], which belongs to none but the true God. And Isaias: [[Is 9:6|For a CHILD IS BORN to us|Parvulus, inquit, natus est nobis]], [[Is 9:6|and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, God the Mighty, the Father of the world to come, the Prince of Peace|et vocabitur nomen ejus, Admirabilis, Consiliarius, Deus, Fortis, Pater futuri sæculi, Princeps pacis]].

paras.t: Sed ista responsio in aliquibus deficit. Primo, quia vulgares, saltem in die Palmarum, noverunt et confessi sunt Jesum esse Salvatorem mundi, regem Israel, seu Christum in lege promissum, dicentes: Hosanna filio David; benedictus qui venit rex in nomine Domini; Hosanna in altissimis. Denique in evangelio Joannis ubertim habetur, quod quidam de turba crediderunt in eum. Similiter in eodem, leguntur Samaritani dixisse mulieri quæ venit ad puteum: Jam non propter tuam loquelam credimus, ipsi enim scimus quia hic est vere Salvator mundi. Denique Lyra sæpe affirmat, quod Judæi carnaliter intellexerunt Scripturas de Christo, idcirco putabant eum in primo suo adventu temporaliter regnaturum, et regnum Judæorum promoturum. Si hoc ita est, nequaquam credebant Jesum esse Christum, quum cernerent eum temporalia cuncta despicere, paupertatem docere, et in omnibus cæleste regnum prædicare. Iterum, quamvis vulgares non noverant Jesum esse Christum ex Scripturis, tamen ex verbis et actibus ejus, id ipsum cognoscere poterant.
paras.en: But this answer falls short in some points. First, because the common people, at least on Palm Sunday, knew and confessed Jesus to be the Saviour of the world, the King of Israel, or the Christ promised in the Law, saying: [[21:9|Hosanna to the son of David|Hosanna filio David]]; [[Luke 19:38|Blessed be the king who cometh in the name of the Lord|benedictus qui venit rex in nomine Domini]]; [[21:9|Hosanna in the highest|Hosanna in altissimis]]. Indeed it is found abundantly in the Gospel of John that some of the crowd believed in Him[[John 7:31||]]. Likewise in the same Gospel the Samaritans are read to have said to the woman who came to the well: [[John 4:42|We now believe, not for thy saying: for we ourselves have heard him and know that this is indeed the Saviour of the world|Jam non propter tuam loquelam credimus, ipsi enim scimus quia hic est vere Salvator mundi]]. Again, Lyra often affirms that the Jews understood the Scriptures about Christ carnally, and so thought He would reign temporally at His first coming and advance the kingdom of the Jews. If this is so, they by no means believed Jesus to be the Christ, since they saw Him despise all temporal things, teach poverty, and in all things preach a heavenly kingdom. Again, though the common people did not know from the Scriptures that Jesus was the Christ, they could know it from His words and deeds.

paras.t: Dicendum ergo, quod Judæi eruditi et multi simplices, noverant Jesum esse Christum aliquantulo tempore, notitia conjecturali atque probabili, non evidenti ac stabili: sic enim et dæmones agnoverunt eum. Postea, prædicante Christo contra vitia sacerdotum, Scribarum ac Pharisæorum, stimulati sunt contra eum invidia, excæcavitque eos malitia eorum: qui excæcati subverterunt fidem simplicium, præsertim in passione. Dum ergo crucifixerunt Jesum, non cognoverunt quod esset Christus, nec sciebant quid faciebant. Quamvis autem scripturæ Prophetarum de Christi divinitate aperte loquebantur, tamen scripturæ hujusmodi satis diversimode solent exponi. Ideo non apparet probabile, quod noverint Jesum esse verum Deum. Imo usque in hodiernum diem, non credunt Messiam suum futurum esse vel fore Deum, sed hominem purum.
paras.en: It must be said, then, that the learned Jews, and many simple ones, knew Jesus to be the Christ for some little time, by a conjectural and probable knowledge, not an evident and stable one; for so the demons too recognized Him. Afterwards, when Christ preached against the vices of the priests, scribes and Pharisees, they were goaded by envy against Him, and [[Wis 2:21|their own malice blinded them|excæcavitque eos malitia eorum]]; and, so blinded, they overturned the faith of the simple, especially in the Passion. When, then, they crucified Jesus, they did not know that He was the Christ, nor did they know what they were doing. And though the writings of the Prophets spoke openly of Christ's divinity, yet such writings are commonly expounded in quite different ways. So it does not seem probable that they knew Jesus to be true God. Indeed, to this day they do not believe that their Messias is to be God, but a mere man.
